Taking 90% of a number 90 gives 81, which equals 9 x 9.
Boiling heats milk enough to kill harmful germs and bacteria and makes it safe to drink and keep for longer.
Pasteurization, named after Louis Pasteur, is the industrial process of heating milk to destroy germs.
Why do parents send their children to school?
Schools provide education, which develops knowledge, skills and character in children.
Education is a fundamental right of children under Article 25-A of the Constitution of Pakistan.
Division comes before addition (BODMAS), so 2/2 = 1 and 2 + 1 = 3.
BODMAS stands for Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.
Out of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What is the percentage of present students?
The absent students are 300, which is 20%.
How many months of the year have 31 days?
The months are January, March, May, July, August, October and December, which makes 7.
February has 28 days (29 in a leap year).
What is the antonym of wild?
Wild describes an animal or place not under human control. Tame means gentle and domesticated, its opposite.
Domestic is another common antonym of wild.
How many faces does a triangular prism have?
A triangular prism has two triangular bases and three rectangular side faces: 2 + 3 = 5 faces.
It also has 9 edges and 6 vertices. Candidates gave different answers (3, 4, 5, 6) because the paper did not name the prism type; the triangular prism is the usual one.
In which year did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations?
Pakistan was admitted to the UN on 30 September 1947, a few weeks after independence.
The UN itself was founded in 1945.
What is one quarter of one tenth of 120?
One tenth of 120 is 12, and a quarter of 12 is 3. Working in the other order gives 30 and then 3.
One quarter of one tenth equals 1/40, so the answer is 120/40.
Out of 500 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
The present students make up 68%, which is the number many people wrongly give.
If yesterday was Sunday, what day will be the day after tomorrow?
If yesterday was Sunday, today is Monday and tomorrow is Tuesday. The day after tomorrow is Wednesday.
The day after tomorrow is always two days after today.
If today is Friday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow?
Tomorrow is Saturday, so the day after tomorrow is Sunday.
The day after tomorrow means two days from today.
What is the national drink (juice) of Pakistan?
Sugarcane juice is regarded as the national juice or drink of Pakistan.
Pakistan is among the world's top producers of sugarcane.
If yesterday was Friday, what day will be the day after tomorrow?
If yesterday was Friday, today is Saturday. The day after tomorrow is Saturday plus 2 days, which is Monday.
The day after tomorrow is always three days after yesterday.
In which year of the Hijri calendar was the Battle of Uhud fought?
The Battle of Uhud was fought in Shawwal 3 AH (625 AD) near Mount Uhud, a year after Badr.
The archers left their post on the hill, which let the Quraish attack from behind.
Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan?
Liaquat Ali Khan became the first Prime Minister of Pakistan on 15 August 1947.
He was assassinated at Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.
Who was the first wife of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
Hazrat Khadija bint Khuwaylid (RA) married the Prophet (PBUH) about 15 years before the first revelation.
The Prophet (PBUH) did not marry again during her lifetime.
If yesterday was Saturday, what day will be the day after tomorrow?
If yesterday was Saturday, today is Sunday and tomorrow is Monday. The day after tomorrow is Tuesday.
Candidates remembered Monday, which is tomorrow, not the day after tomorrow.
What was the relation of Hazrat Hamza (RA) with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
Hazrat Hamza was a son of Abdul Muttalib, so he was a paternal uncle of the Prophet (PBUH). He was also close in age and a foster brother.
Hazrat Hamza was martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH and is called Sayyid-ush-Shuhada.
A pen is bought for Rs 30 and sold for Rs 40. What is the profit percentage?
Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam join the All India Muslim League?
Jinnah formally joined the Muslim League in 1913, at the persuasion of Allama Iqbal, Wazir Hasan and others. He remained a member of the Indian National Congress at the same time.
He left the Congress in 1920 over differences with Gandhi's policies.
1/10 of a number is the same as 10% of it.
Who was the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan?
Sir Muhammad Zafarullah Khan was appointed the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan in 1947 and served until 1954.
He later served as a judge and President of the International Court of Justice.
In which battle was Abu Jahl killed?
Abu Jahl, a leader of the Quraysh, was killed in the Battle of Badr in 2 AH. He was struck down by two young Ansari brothers, Muadh and Muawwidh.
Abu Jahl's real name was Amr ibn Hisham.
In which battle was Hazrat Hamza (RA) martyred?
Hazrat Hamza (RA), uncle of the Prophet (PBUH), was martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH. He was killed by Wahshi, a slave of Jubayr ibn Mut'im.
Hazrat Hamza (RA) is known as Asadullah and Sayyid ush-Shuhada (Chief of the Martyrs).
In which year was the OIC founded?
The OIC was founded in September 1969 at Rabat, Morocco, after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque.
Its headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
Which country lies to the east of Pakistan?
India shares Pakistan's long eastern border.
Pakistan borders Iran to the west, Afghanistan to the north-west, China to the north and India to the east.
What is one third of one tenth of 90?
One tenth of 90 is 9, and one third of 9 is 3. The same value results from taking one tenth of one third of 90 or one third of 10% of 90.
Fractions of a number can be taken in any order because multiplication is commutative.
One tenth is the same as 10 percent.
What is the largest lake of the world by area?
The Caspian Sea, about 371,000 square km, is the largest inland body of water and is classed as a lake.
Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area, and Lake Baikal is the deepest.
What is the longest (largest) river of Asia?
The Yangtze in China is about 6,300 km long, the longest river in Asia.
It is the third longest river in the world.
What is the length of the Indus River according to Pakistani textbooks?
Pakistani textbooks give the length of the Indus as about 3,180 km.
Sources differ: some give about 2,880 km (Britannica) or 2,900 km.
What is the national bird of the USA?
The bald eagle was chosen as the national bird and emblem of the United States.
It appears on the Great Seal of the United States adopted in 1782.
A book is bought for Rs 30 and sold for Rs 40. What is the profit?
Profit = selling price - cost price = 40 - 30 = Rs 10.
Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price.
From whom did Pakistan purchase Gwadar?
Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958 for about 3 million US dollars, and it joined Pakistan on 8 September 1958.
Prime Minister Feroz Khan Noon was in office at the time.
How many pillars of Islam are there?
The five pillars are Shahadah (faith), Salah (prayer), Zakat, Sawm (fasting) and Hajj.
Salah is the pillar performed five times daily.
In which year did Pakistan join the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)?
Pakistan became a member of NAM in 1979 at the Havana summit.
NAM was founded in 1961 at Belgrade.
What is the length of the Canada-United States border?
The border is about 8,891 km (5,525 miles), the longest international land border in the world.
Note that 5,525 is the length in miles, not kilometres.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam become president of the All India Muslim League for the first time?
Jinnah was elected president of the Muslim League at the Lucknow session in December 1916. This was the session at which the Lucknow Pact was agreed.
He later served as president again in the 1920s and 1930s and led the League until Pakistan was created.
Who among the following was a son-in-law of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Hazrat Ali (RA) married the Prophet's daughter Hazrat Fatima (RA).
Hazrat Uthman (RA) was also a son-in-law, having married Hazrat Ruqayyah and later Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA).
Who was the second Governor General of Pakistan?
After the death of Quaid-e-Azam in September 1948, Khawaja Nazimuddin became Governor General of Pakistan. He held the post until 1951.
Nazimuddin was followed as Governor General by Malik Ghulam Muhammad in 1951.
Who wrote the Punjabi romance Heer Ranjha?
Waris Shah wrote the best known version of Heer in 1766.
Earlier versions of the story were written by Damodar Gulati.
How many permanent members does the UN Security Council have?
The permanent members are the USA, UK, France, Russia and China, each holding veto power.
Russia took the Soviet Union's seat in 1991 and China's seat passed from Taiwan to the PRC in 1971.
In which battle did the Muslims dig a trench around Madinah?
The Muslims dug a trench around Madinah in the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab) in 5 AH on the advice of Salman Farsi. It stopped the Quraysh and their allies from attacking the city.
The Battle of Khandaq is also called the Battle of the Confederates (Ahzab).
Which is the highest pass of Pakistan according to most Pakistani textbooks?
Khunjerab Pass, at about 4,693 m on the Pakistan-China border, is the highest pass usually cited for Pakistan.
Sources differ because some lists name Mintaka Pass, also on the China border, as slightly higher; Khunjerab is the highest paved international border crossing.
Which word is a synonym of wild?
Wild means living or growing in nature, not controlled by humans, which is untamed. The other options are its opposites.
Its antonym is tame or domesticated.
Fatima Jinnah trained as a dentist and qualified from the University of Calcutta in 1923. She ran her own dental clinic in Bombay.
She was known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation) and contested the 1965 presidential election against Ayub Khan.
In which district is the Khewra salt mine located?
The Khewra salt mine is in Jhelum district, Punjab, in the Salt Range.
It is among the largest salt mines in the world.
Who was elected Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in October 2025, succeeding Ali Amin Gandapur?
Sohail Afridi of PTI was elected Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in October 2025.

Since 11 October 2026 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has been under governor's rule (Governor Faisal Karim Kundi), so the province has no sitting Chief Minister at the moment. In 2021-22 the answer was Mahmood Khan.
Dividing by 10 moves the decimal point one place left, so 120 becomes 12.
One tenth is the same as 10%.
In which year did Pakistan join SEATO?
Pakistan joined the South-East Asia Treaty Organization in 1954 when the Manila Pact was signed in September 1954.
Some sources give 1955 (ratification), and Pakistan joined the Baghdad Pact (CENTO) in 1955.
In which year was the Indus Waters Treaty signed?
The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960 by Ayub Khan and Nehru, with the World Bank as a party.
It gave Pakistan the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) and India the eastern rivers.
In which year was the Nehru Report presented?
The Nehru Report, drafted by a committee under Motilal Nehru, was presented in 1928.
Jinnah responded with his Fourteen Points in 1929.
In which year was the Pakistan-China border agreement signed?
Pakistan and China signed the boundary agreement on 2 March 1963.
It settled the border in the Karakoram region and led to the Karakoram Highway cooperation.
What is the currency of Armenia?
Georgia uses the lari and Azerbaijan the manat.
What is the currency of Azerbaijan?
Turkmenistan also uses a currency called the manat.
What is the currency of Bangladesh?
Pakistan, India and Nepal use rupees, while Bhutan uses the ngultrum.
Who is the Chief Minister of Punjab?
Maryam Nawaz has been Chief Minister of Punjab since February 2024.
She is the first woman Chief Minister of Punjab; her predecessor in 2021-22 was Usman Buzdar.
Who was the first Governor General of independent India in 1947?
Lord Mountbatten became Governor General of the Dominion of India on 15 August 1947.
Sources differ because Warren Hastings and William Bentinck are also called the first Governor General in earlier British India, but for 1947 it is Mountbatten.
Who wrote the novel Raja Gidh?
Bano Qudsia wrote Raja Gidh, a novel about the concept of haram and halal food and its effect on the mind.
She was married to the writer Ashfaq Ahmed.
The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with which country?
The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway links Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan with Xinjiang in China.
At about 4693 m it is among the highest paved border crossings in the world.
What was the relation of Hazrat Safiyyah (RA) with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
Hazrat Safiyyah bint Abdul Muttalib was a sister of Hazrat Hamza and thus a paternal aunt of the Prophet (PBUH).
She was the mother of Hazrat Zubair ibn al-Awwam (RA).
Hazrat Maryam (AS) was the mother of which prophet?
Hazrat Maryam (AS) was the mother of Hazrat Isa (AS), who was born without a father by Allah's command.
Surah Maryam, the 19th surah of the Quran, is named after her.
How many daughters did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) have?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) had four daughters: Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatima (RA).
All of his daughters except Hazrat Fatima (RA) died during his lifetime.
How many non-permanent members does the UN Security Council have?
The Council has 15 members: 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent members.
Non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms.
In which Hijri year did Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accept Islam?
Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accepted Islam in 8 AH (629 CE), before the conquest of Makkah. Some sources give 7 AH, so sources differ, but 8 AH is the common textbook answer.
He was later given the title Saifullah (Sword of Allah).
On which prophet was the Injeel (Bible) revealed?
The Injeel (Gospel) was revealed to Hazrat Isa (A.S). Zabur was given to Dawood, Taurat to Musa and the Quran to Muhammad.
Hazrat Isa (A.S) is also known as Ruhullah.
On which river is Simly Dam (Simla Dam) built?
Simly Dam near Islamabad is an earthen dam on the Soan River. It supplies water to Islamabad.
It was completed in 1983; Khanpur Dam, by contrast, is on the Haro River.
What is the value of sin 90 degrees?
On the unit circle, the point at 90 degrees is (0, 1) and sine is the y-coordinate, which equals 1.
The value of cos 90 degrees is 0.
On what date was the Nehru Report presented?
The Nehru Report was presented at the All Parties Conference at Lucknow on 28 August 1928.
Motilal Nehru headed the committee that prepared it.
What is the largest district of Pakistan by area?
Chagai in Balochistan covers about 44,748 square km, the largest district of Pakistan by area.
Chagai is where Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in 1998 (Ras Koh hills).
Who was the first child to accept Islam?
Hazrat Ali (RA), the cousin of the Prophet, accepted Islam as a boy of about 10 years old. He was raised in the Prophet's household.
Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the first woman and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) the first free adult man to accept Islam.
Which is the biggest sea of the world by area?
The Philippine Sea covers about 5.7 million square km, the largest sea in the world. The South China Sea is about 3.5 million square km.
The Arabian Sea is the largest of the other options and lies next to Pakistan's coast.
Which wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the daughter of a Jewish leader?
Hazrat Safiyya bint Huyayy was from the Jewish tribe Banu Nadir and married the Prophet (PBUH) after Khaybar.
She accepted Islam before the marriage.
Who was the first Chief Justice of Pakistan?
Sir Abdul Rashid became the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court of Pakistan in 1949.
Muhammad Munir succeeded him as Chief Justice in 1954.
Who wrote the national anthem of Pakistan?
The lyrics of Qaumi Tarana were written by the poet Abul Asar Hafeez Jalandhari. It was officially adopted in 1954.
The music of the national anthem was composed by Ahmed G. Chagla.
How many times has Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup?
Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup four times: 1971, 1978, 1982 and 1994.
Pakistan is the most successful team in Hockey World Cup history.
In which battle was Hazrat Jafar Tayyar (RA) martyred?
Hazrat Jafar ibn Abi Talib (RA) was one of the three commanders martyred in the Battle of Mutah in 8 AH. He is called Tayyar (the flyer) because he is said to have been given wings in Paradise.
The other two commanders at Mutah were Zaid bin Haritha and Abdullah bin Rawaha (RA).
Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan to visit America?
Liaquat Ali Khan visited the United States in May 1950, the first Pakistani Prime Minister to do so.
His visit came after he chose Washington over an invitation from Moscow.
The Khyber Pass connects Pakistan with which country?
The Khyber Pass links Peshawar in Pakistan with Jalalabad and Kabul in Afghanistan.
The Khyber Pass is about 53 km long and has been an invasion and trade route for centuries.
The Dorah Pass connects Pakistan with which country?
The Dorah Pass lies on the Chitral border and leads from Pakistan into Afghanistan (Badakhshan).
Chitral district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is the Pakistani side of the Dorah Pass.
Hazrat Hajra (Hajar) was the mother of which prophet?
Hazrat Hajra was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and gave birth to Hazrat Ismail (AS).
The Sa'i between Safa and Marwa during Hajj commemorates her search for water.
How many original members did the United Nations have when it was founded in 1945?
The UN began in 1945 with 51 original member states (Poland signed later and is counted among them).
How many planets are there in the solar system?
There are eight planets since Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
The planets in order from the Sun start with Mercury and end with Neptune.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam present his Fourteen Points?
Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in March 1929 as the Muslim League reply to the Nehru Report.
They demanded safeguards for Muslims such as separate electorates and a federal system.
Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan are famous players of which sport?
Both Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan of Pakistan were world champions in squash.
Jahangir Khan won the British Open ten times in a row and Jansher Khan won the World Open eight times.
On which prophet was the Zabur (Psalms) revealed?
The Zabur was revealed to Hazrat Dawood (A.S).
Hazrat Sulaiman (A.S) was the son of Hazrat Dawood (A.S).
Swine flu is caused by influenza A viruses, most notably the H1N1 strain.
The 2009 H1N1 pandemic was declared by the WHO in June 2009.
What is the capital of Austria?
Vienna is the capital and largest city of Austria. Canberra is the capital of Australia, not Austria.
Austria and Australia are often confused because of their similar names.
What is the capital of Bulgaria?
Sofia is the capital and largest city of Bulgaria.
Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026.
What is the largest river of Pakistan?
The Indus is the longest and largest river of Pakistan.
It rises near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and falls into the Arabian Sea.
What is the length of the Suez Canal?
The Suez Canal is about 193 km, which is roughly 120 miles.
It connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea and opened in 1869.
Which country is the largest producer of coffee in the world?
Brazil has been the world's largest coffee producer for over 150 years.
Vietnam is the second largest coffee producer.
Which country is the largest producer of tea in the world?
China produces more tea than any other country, with India second.
Kenya and Sri Lanka are the next major producers.
Which is the largest freshwater lake of the world by surface area?
Lake Superior in North America has a surface area of about 82,000 square kilometres, the largest among freshwater lakes.
Lake Baikal is the deepest freshwater lake and holds the most fresh water by volume.
Hazrat Khadija (R.A), wife of the Prophet (PBUH), was the first person and first woman to accept Islam.
Hazrat Sumayya was the first martyr of Islam.
Who was the first president of the All India Muslim League?
Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah Aga Khan III was the first president of the All India Muslim League, founded in Dhaka in 1906.
The League was founded at Dhaka during the All India Muhammadan Educational Conference.
Who wrote the book 'Friends Not Masters'?
'Friends Not Masters: A Political Autobiography' was written by Field Marshal Muhammad Ayub Khan. It was published in 1967.
Ayub Khan was Pakistan's second President and ruled from 1958 to 1969.
Zakat is which pillar of Islam?
The five pillars in order are Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm (fasting) and Hajj, so Zakat is third.
Candidates wrote 4, but in the standard order Zakat comes third.
A bat cannot see; a snake cannot what?
Snakes have no external ears and cannot hear airborne sound well; they sense ground vibrations instead.
Bats find their way by echolocation using high-pitched sounds.
What type of government was set up by the 1962 constitution of Pakistan?
The 1962 constitution concentrated executive power in the President, so it created a presidential form of government.
The 1973 constitution replaced it with a parliamentary system.
How many member states does the European Union (EU) have?
The EU has 27 member states, and the number has not changed since the United Kingdom left on 31 January 2020.
Before Brexit the EU had 28 members; Croatia was the last to join, in 2013.
In which city is the shrine of Hazrat Mian Mir located?
The Sufi saint Hazrat Mian Mir is buried in Lahore, in the Dharampura area.
Mian Mir is said to have laid the foundation stone of the Golden Temple at Amritsar at the invitation of Guru Arjan.
In which month did the 1965 Pakistan-India war take place and how long did it last?
The war began on 6 September 1965 when India crossed the international border at Lahore, and ended with a ceasefire on 23 September 1965, a total of 17 days.
Pakistan celebrates 6 September every year as Defence Day.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam leave the Indian National Congress?
Jinnah left Congress in 1920 over the Nagpur session and its non-cooperation policy.
He joined the Muslim League in 1913.
In which year was the Tashkent Agreement signed?
The Tashkent Declaration ending the 1965 war was signed on 10 January 1966 under Soviet mediation.
It was signed by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri.
Oil wrestling is the national sport of which country?
Oil wrestling (Yagli Gures) is the national sport of Turkey.
The Kirkpinar festival in Edirne, Turkey, is the oldest wrestling competition in the world.
On which river is Warsak Dam built?
Warsak Dam is built on the Kabul River near Peshawar.
Warsak Dam was built in the 1950s with Canadian assistance under the Colombo Plan.
Which is the fifth pillar of Islam?
The five pillars in order are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj, so Hajj is fifth.
Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for those who are able to afford it.
What is the capital of Azad Kashmir?
Muzaffarabad is the capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
Muzaffarabad lies at the confluence of the Jhelum and Neelum rivers.
What is the capital of Belarus?
Minsk is the capital and largest city of Belarus.
Belarus is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe.
What is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan?
Gilgit is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan.
Gilgit-Baltistan is home to K2, the second highest mountain in the world.
What is the capital of Ukraine?
Kyiv (also spelled Kiev) is the capital of Ukraine.
Kyiv sits on the Dnieper river.
What is the currency of Egypt?
What is the currency of Indonesia?
Malaysia uses the ringgit and Thailand the baht.
On what date was the Tashkent Agreement signed?
India and Pakistan signed the Tashkent Declaration on 10 January 1966, ending the 1965 war.
It was signed by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri, who died in Tashkent the next day.
What is the largest lake of Europe?
Lake Ladoga in Russia, about 17,700 square km, is the largest lake entirely within Europe.
The Caspian Sea is larger but is usually not counted as a European lake.
What is the largest river of Afghanistan?
The Helmand River, about 1,150 km, is the longest river wholly within Afghanistan.
The Amu Darya forms part of the northern border and is not entirely within Afghanistan.
What is the length of the Pakistan-India border (including the Line of Control and Working Boundary)?
The combined length of the international boundary, Working Boundary and Line of Control is about 3,323 km.
The Radcliffe Line of 1947 defined the border between the two countries.
What is the national bird of Pakistan?
The chukar partridge is the national bird of Pakistan.
The Shaheen (falcon) is the national symbol of Pakistan's air force and a popular emblem, but not the national bird.
Which word is a synonym of attire?
Attire means clothes or dress, so clothing is the synonym.
Another synonym of attire is apparel.
What is the title of Liaqat Ali Khan?
Liaqat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, was given the title Quaid-e-Millat (Leader of the Nation).
He was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.
In which year was SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) founded?
SAARC was founded at a summit in Dhaka on 8 December 1985. The idea was proposed by Bangladesh's President Ziaur Rahman.
SAARC has its secretariat in Kathmandu, Nepal, and Afghanistan joined as the eighth member in 2007.
In which province is the proposed Kalabagh Dam located (on the Indus, in Mianwali district)?
Kalabagh is in Mianwali district of Punjab, on the Indus near the boundary with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
The dam has never been built because of political opposition from some provinces.
Which country awards the Nobel Prizes (apart from the Peace Prize)?
The Nobel Prizes in physics, chemistry, medicine and literature are awarded in Sweden, in line with Alfred Nobel's will.
The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway.
Which of the following countries is NOT a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
The SCO has ten full members: China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India, Pakistan, Iran and Belarus. Turkey is only a dialogue partner.
Iran joined in 2023 and Belarus in 2024; Afghanistan and Mongolia are observers.
Which is the largest province of Pakistan by population?
Punjab has more than half of Pakistan's population (about 127 million in the 2023 census).
Sindh is the second most populous province.
Which is the last month of the Islamic calendar?
The Islamic year has twelve months and Dhul Hijjah is the twelfth and last.
Hajj is performed in Dhul Hijjah and Muharram is the first month.
Which Sahabi married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Ruqayyah and Hazrat Umm Kulthum?
Hazrat Usman (R.A) married Ruqayyah first and, after her death, Umm Kulthum.
He is known as Dhun-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights.
Which was the first mosque built by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the first mosque of Islam in Madina?
Masjid Quba was built by the Prophet (PBUH) on his arrival near Madina during the Hijrah.
Masjid-e-Nabawi was built soon afterwards in Madina.
Who is the current Chairman of NAB (National Accountability Bureau)?
Lt Gen (retd) Nazir Ahmad became NAB chairman in 2023 and received a three-year extension from March 2026.
Earlier chairmen were Javed Iqbal (2017-22) and Aftab Sultan (2022-23).
Who is the President of Turkey?
Recep Tayyip Erdogan has been President of Turkey since 2014 and was re-elected in 2023.
The capital of Turkey is Ankara.
Who was the brother of Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA)?
Walid bin Walid (RA) was the brother of Khalid bin Waleed (RA) and accepted Islam before him.
Their father Waleed bin Mughirah was a leader of the Banu Makhzum of Quraish.
Who wrote the Punjabi qissa (folk romance) Sohni Mahiwal?
The best-known Punjabi version of Sohni Mahiwal is attributed to Fazal Shah (Sayyid Fazal Shah). Waris Shah is known for Heer Ranjha.
Sources differ on tellers of this tale, but Fazal Shah is the usual textbook answer.
A car travels at 60 km/h and a train at twice that speed (120 km/h). How far does the train travel in 30 minutes?
30 minutes is half an hour, so distance = 120 x 0.5 = 60 km.
Which sea lies between Greece and Italy?
The Ionian Sea lies between southern Italy and western Greece.
The Aegean Sea lies east of Greece, between Greece and Turkey.
A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.
Which country is the second largest in the world by area?
Russia is the largest country and Canada, with about 9.98 million square km, is second.
China and the United States follow closely as third and fourth.
According to the 1962 constitution, how was the President of Pakistan elected?
By an Electoral College of Basic Democrats
By the Governors of the provinces
The 1962 constitution introduced indirect election of the President by an Electoral College made up of the elected Basic Democrats.
The Electoral College initially had 80,000 members, later raised to 120,000 (equally from East and West Pakistan).
Against whom was the Battle of Khyber fought?
The Battle of Khyber (7 AH) was fought by the Muslims against the Jewish tribes living in the fortresses of Khyber.
Hazrat Ali conquered the fort of Qamus in this battle.
Al Jazeera TV channel belongs to which country?
Al Jazeera is an Arabic news channel founded in 1996 and funded by the Qatari state, based in Doha.
Some candidates thought it was Egyptian, but it is Qatari.
Hazrat Ayesha (RA) was the daughter of whom?
Hazrat Ayesha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA).
Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of whom?

How many Khulafa-e-Rashideen (rightly guided caliphs) are there?
They are Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali (RA).

How many sons did Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) have?
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) had two sons who were prophets: Hazrat Ismail (AS) and Hazrat Ishaq (AS).

Pakistan was a founding member of the OIC, which was formed in 1969.

In which year did Quaid-e-Azam die?
Quaid-e-Azam died on 11 September 1948 in Karachi.
He is buried at Mazar-e-Quaid in Karachi.
Kaleemullah is the title of which prophet?
Kaleemullah means the one who spoke with Allah, the title of Hazrat Musa (A.S).

What is the capital of Chile?
Santiago is the capital of Chile.

What is the meaning of the word alter?
To alter means to change something or make it different.

What is the currency of Cuba?
Cuba formerly had a second currency, the convertible peso (CUC), which was abolished in 2021.
What is the currency of Russia?

On what date did the War of Independence of the Subcontinent begin?
The 1857 War of Independence began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.

A mob burned a police station at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh on 4 February 1922.
Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement after this incident.

What is the maximum length of a cricket bat under the laws of cricket?
The Laws of Cricket limit a bat to 38 inches (96.52 cm) in length.
The maximum width of the blade is 4.25 inches.
What is the length of the coastline of Pakistan?
Pakistan's Arabian Sea coastline is officially about 1,046 km.
It is shared between Sindh (about 270 km) and Balochistan (about 770 km).
What is the national tree of Pakistan?
The Deodar (Himalayan cedar) is the national tree of Pakistan.
Its name comes from Sanskrit and means timber of the gods.

Both were sons of Prophet Ibrahim (AS), so they were brothers (half-brothers, by different mothers).

What is the range of the Pakistani surface-to-surface missile Ababeel?

Which word is a synonym of evident?
Evident means clearly seen or understood, which is obvious.
Which word is a synonym of prevalent?
Prevalent means common or existing widely at a given time, which is widespread.
Its opposite is rare or uncommon.
What is the total number of seats of the Provincial Assembly of Punjab?
The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats: 297 general, 66 reserved for women and 8 for non-Muslims.
The National Assembly has 336 seats, of which Punjab has 141 general seats.
Where does the Bay of Pigs invasion of 1961 belong, that is, which country was invaded?
The Bay of Pigs (Bahia de Cochinos) is on the southern coast of Cuba. In April 1961 CIA-backed Cuban exiles landed there to overthrow Fidel Castro and failed.

In which year did Pakistan win the ICC Champions Trophy?
Pakistan beat India by 180 runs in the final at The Oval in London on 18 June 2017 under captain Sarfraz Ahmed.
Pakistan has won the Champions Trophy only once; India won the 2025 edition.

Swat acceded to Pakistan in 1947 but remained a princely state. It was merged fully on 28 July 1969, when the state was abolished.
Swat is now part of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

The first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956 and made Pakistan an Islamic Republic. It was abrogated by Ayub Khan's martial law in October 1958.
23 March was celebrated as Republic Day until the 1962 constitution replaced it.
In which province is Manchar Lake located?
Manchar Lake is in Dadu district of Sindh, west of the Indus.
It is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Pakistan.
In which city is the Shah Jahan Mosque of Pakistan located?
The Shah Jahan Mosque was built in Thatta, Sindh, in the 17th century.
It is famous for its blue tile work and for having no minarets.

Myanmar was the first export customer of the JF-17, signing its deal around 2015 and receiving aircraft from 2018.

Which is the largest country in the world by area?

Ramadan is commonly called the month of Allah in Pakistani textbooks, because fasting is observed in it.

Which prophet was swallowed by a fish and stayed in its belly?
Hazrat Younus (A.S) was swallowed by a large fish and prayed to Allah from within its belly.

Who was the first man to embrace Islam?

Quaid-e-Azam inaugurated the State Bank of Pakistan in Karachi on 1 July 1948.

Who is the national poet of Pakistan?
Allama Muhammad Iqbal is the national poet of Pakistan, called Shair-e-Mashriq.

Nazir Sabir reached the summit of Mount Everest in 1999 as the first Pakistani to do so.

Allama Iqbal wrote this book, which is based on his lectures delivered in 1928-29.

Which is the largest freshwater lake of Pakistan?
Manchar Lake in Sindh is generally regarded as Pakistan's largest freshwater lake.

The absent students are 200, which is 13.33%.

Abdul Qadir was a Pakistani leg-spin bowler famous for his googly and wrist-spin.

The Khilafat Movement began in 1919 after the defeat of the Ottoman Empire in World War I, which threatened the Caliphate.

Asadullah (Lion of Allah) is the title of which Sahabi?
Hazrat Ali (RA) was given the title Asadullah for his bravery. Hazrat Hamza is also called Asadullah.
Khalid bin Waleed is known as Saifullah (Sword of Allah).

Khojak Pass, not Bolan, links Quetta with Chaman and Afghanistan.

Muhammad Ali Jinnah studied at Lincoln's Inn in London and was called to the bar in 1896.

Commonly 86 surahs are counted as Makki (revealed before the Hijrah) and 28 as Madani.

Article 51 of the Constitution reserves 60 seats for women, filled by proportional representation.

The Prophet (PBUH) conquered Makkah peacefully in Ramadan 8 AH (630 CE).

Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai (1689-1752) is the great Sufi poet of the Sindhi language.

India conducted its first nuclear test (Smiling Buddha) at Pokhran in May 1974.

Riyadh is the capital of which country?

Safiullah means the chosen one of Allah and is the title of Hazrat Adam (A.S).

Tirana is the capital of which country?
Tirana is the capital and largest city of Albania in the Balkans.

Tripoli is the capital of which country?
Tripoli is the capital of Libya on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa.

Turkey has the Black Sea to the north, the Aegean to the west and the Mediterranean to the south.

Pakistan is the fifth most populous country, after India, China, the United States and Indonesia.

Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points at Delhi in March 1929, answering the Nehru Report.

Muslim League and the British Government

Where is the Pakistan Navy headquarters?
Naval Headquarters of the Pakistan Navy is in Islamabad.

Who is the President of Iran?

Who led the Quit India Movement of 1942?

Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947.

Pakistan was the runner-up in 1999 and champion in 1992.

With the help of which country was Pakistan Steel Mills built?
Pakistan Steel Mills at Karachi was set up with Soviet technical and financial assistance in the 1970s.

What is the capital of Bhutan?

On what date is Youm-e-Takbeer observed in Pakistan?

Against whom did Shahid Afridi score his record 37-ball century in 1996?
Afridi hit the then fastest ODI century off 37 balls against Sri Lanka at Nairobi in October 1996.
The record stood for 18 years until broken by Corey Anderson in 2014 and then by AB de Villiers.
Against whom was the Battle of Tabuk fought?
In 9 AH the Prophet (PBUH) led an army to Tabuk to face the Byzantine force, but no fighting took place.
It was the last military expedition led by the Prophet (PBUH).
By whom was the Objectives Resolution passed?
It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan and passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan on 12 March 1949.
It later became the preamble of the 1956, 1962 and 1973 constitutions in some form.
By whose hand was Hazrat Hamza martyred in the Battle of Uhud?
Wahshi bin Harb, a slave of Jubayr bin Mutim, killed Hazrat Hamza with a spear on the order of Hind.
The Coastal Highway connects Gwadar with which city?
The Makran Coastal Highway (N-10) runs along the Arabian Sea coast from Karachi to Gwadar.
It is about 653 km long and was completed in 2004.
The Danube is the second longest river of which continent?
The Danube, about 2,850 km long, is the second longest river in Europe after the Volga.
It flows into the Black Sea.
Desert Fox is the title of whom?
Field Marshal Erwin Rommel earned the name Desert Fox for his skilled command of the German Afrika Korps in North Africa.
He was defeated by Montgomery at El Alamein in 1942.
Diphtheria is a disease of which part of the body?
Diphtheria is a bacterial infection that mainly affects the throat and upper airways.
It is prevented by the DPT vaccine.
Fill in the blank: He wasted his time ___ TV.
After the expression waste time, the gerund (-ing form) is used, so watching is correct.
The same pattern is used in spend time doing something.
Fill in the blank: The Pacific is ___ than the Arctic Ocean.
The sentence compares two things and uses than, so the comparative deeper is needed.
The Pacific is the deepest and largest ocean on Earth.
For the Khilafat Movement, Muslims of India migrated towards which country?
During the Hijrat Movement of 1920, thousands of Muslims left India for Afghanistan as a protest against British rule.
The migration failed because the Afghan government could not support so many people.
From which city did the Urdu-Hindi controversy start in 1867?
In 1867 Hindus of Banaras demanded that Hindi in Devanagari script replace Urdu in government offices, starting the controversy.
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan took it as a sign that Hindus and Muslims could not remain together.
The Gulf of Siam, now known as the Gulf of Thailand, mainly lies in which country?
The Gulf of Siam is the old name of the Gulf of Thailand, which borders Thailand mainly, as well as Cambodia, Vietnam and Malaysia.
Sources differ on which country to name, but Thailand is the answer given in most textbooks.
Hafeez Kardar was a player of which sport?
Abdul Hafeez Kardar was a Pakistani cricketer and the first captain of Pakistan in Test cricket.
He captained Pakistan in its first Test victory, at The Oval in 1954.
Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) belonged to which tribe?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) belonged to the Quraish tribe, to its clan Banu Hashim.
Banu Aws and Banu Khazraj were the two main tribes of Madina who became the Ansar.
How many ayats (verses) does Surah Al-Fatiha, the first surah of the Quran, have?
Surah Al-Fatiha has seven ayats, which is why it is also called Sab'a al-Mathani (the seven oft-repeated verses).
Some candidates remembered 5 but the correct number is 7.
How many ayats were revealed in the first revelation (Surah Al-Alaq) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
The first revelation in the Cave of Hira consisted of the first five ayats of Surah Al-Alaq, beginning with Iqra.
The first revelation came in the month of Ramadan.
How many continents are there in the world?
The seven continents are Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia (Oceania).
Asia is the largest continent and Australia the smallest.
How many Hajj did the Holy Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) perform after his migration to Madina?
He performed only one Hajj, in 10 AH, known as Hajjat-ul-Wada (the Farewell Pilgrimage).
He delivered his Farewell Sermon on the plain of Arafat during this Hajj.
How many Muslims were in the army at the Battle of Uhad (Uhud) in the end?
About 1000 set out, but Abdullah bin Ubayy withdrew with about 300 men, leaving about 700 Muslims.
The Quraish army at Uhad numbered about 3000.
How many players are there in a football team on the field?
A football team fields eleven players including the goalkeeper.
A standard football match lasts 90 minutes.
How many ayats are there in total in Surah Al-Baqarah?
Surah Al-Baqarah, the longest surah, has 286 ayats.
It is the second surah of the Quran.
For how many years did the Holy Prophet (SAW) live in Madina after the Hijrah?
He migrated to Madina in 622 AD (1 AH) and passed away there in 632 AD (11 AH), about ten years later.
He lived about 13 years in Makkah after receiving the first revelation.
In how many fields is the Nobel Prize awarded today?
The Nobel Prizes are given in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace and Economics, which is six fields.
Originally there were five; the Economics prize was added in 1969.
Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which rivers were allotted to India?
The 1960 treaty gave the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas and Sutlej) to India and the western rivers to Pakistan.
India announced in April 2025 that it was holding the treaty in abeyance, but the treaty allocation itself is unchanged.
In which city is the historic Bala Hisar Fort located?
Bala Hisar Fort stands in Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It overlooks the old city.
The fort was rebuilt by the Sikhs in the early 19th century.
In which city is the Arfa Karim Tower located?
The Arfa Karim Tower is in Lahore, Punjab, near Gulberg. It is named after the young computer prodigy Arfa Karim.
Arfa Karim was the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional.
In which city was the All India Muslim League founded in 1906?
The All India Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in December 1906 at the Muslim Educational Conference, hosted by Nawab Salimullah Khan.
Its first president was Nawab Viqar-ul-Mulk, and Sir Aga Khan was the first permanent president.
In which country does the Orange River mainly flow?
The Orange River is the longest river in South Africa and flows westward to the Atlantic Ocean. It rises in the mountains of Lesotho.
It forms part of the border between South Africa and Namibia.
In which country is the volcano Mount Etna located?
Mount Etna is on the island of Sicily, Italy. It is one of the most active volcanoes in the world.
It is the highest active volcano in Europe.
In which country were the 2016 Olympic Games held?
The 2016 Summer Olympics were held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
They were the first Summer Olympics held in South America.
In which direction of Pakistan is Iran located?
Iran lies to the west of Pakistan, bordering Balochistan.
Pakistan also shares borders with Afghanistan in the west and north-west and China in the north.
In which Chinese city did the Covid-19 outbreak first appear in December 2019?
The first cases of Covid-19 were reported in Wuhan, the capital of Hubei province, China, in December 2019.
The World Health Organization declared Covid-19 a pandemic in March 2020.
In which game is the agricultural shot played?
The agricultural shot is a cricket stroke in which the batsman swings the bat across the line in a cow-corner heave, like a farmer swinging a scythe.
It is usually aimed towards the cow corner region of the field.
In which Ghazwa did angels come to help the Muslims?
The Quran says that angels helped the Muslims in the Battle of Badr in 2 AH.
About 313 Muslims faced an army of roughly 1,000 Quraysh at Badr.
In which Hijri year was the Battle of Badr fought?
The Battle of Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE).
It was the first major battle between Muslims and the Quraysh.
In which province is the Kharan Desert located?
The Kharan Desert lies in Kharan district of Balochistan.
Pakistan's first nuclear test site, Chagai, is also in Balochistan close to this desert region.
In which quadrant does the point (-2, -3) lie?
Both the x-coordinate (-2) and the y-coordinate (-3) are negative, which is the third quadrant.
In the second quadrant x is negative and y is positive.
In which surah is Ayat-ul-Kursi found?
Ayat-ul-Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah.
Al-Baqarah is the longest surah of the Quran with 286 verses.
In which war was Major Aziz Bhatti martyred?
Major Aziz Bhatti was martyred on 12 September 1965 defending the BRB canal sector near Lahore.
In which year did the Khilafat delegation led by Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar go to England?
The delegation went to England in 1920 to plead the case of the Ottoman Caliphate before Prime Minister Lloyd George.
The Khilafat Movement was launched in 1919.
In which year did the Quit India Movement start?
Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942.
The Muslim League opposed it and its slogan was Divide and Quit.
The Olympic Games were cancelled in which year of World War 1?
The 1916 Berlin Olympics were cancelled because of the war; the games are held every four years, so 1914 was not an Olympic year.
The Olympics were cancelled again in 1940 and 1944 during World War 2.
In which year were the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms enacted as the Government of India Act?
The Government of India Act 1919 implemented the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, which introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
The Government of India Act 1935 later introduced provincial autonomy.
In which year was the first Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences awarded?
The economics prize was first awarded in 1969 to Ragnar Frisch and Jan Tinbergen.
It is funded by the Bank of Sweden and was not one of Alfred Nobel's original five prizes.
In which year were the first Nobel Prizes awarded?
The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in 1901 in the original five categories.
Alfred Nobel died in 1896 and left his fortune to create the prizes.
In which year was the Kargil war fought?
The Kargil conflict between India and Pakistan took place from May to July 1999.
It followed the 1998 nuclear tests of both countries.
In which year was the partition of Bengal annulled?
The partition of Bengal, made in 1905, was annulled in 1911 after Hindu agitation.
The 1911 decision disappointed Muslims of East Bengal.
Into how many equal parts does a diameter divide a circle?
A diameter passes through the centre and splits the circle into two equal semicircles.
The diameter is twice the radius.
Is the sun a star or a planet?
The sun is a star because it produces its own light and heat by nuclear fusion. Planets only reflect light.
The sun is a medium-sized yellow dwarf star at the centre of our solar system.
Which of the following is a city of Libya?
Tripoli is the capital and largest city of Libya. Casablanca is in Morocco, Tunis in Tunisia and Cairo in Egypt.
Benghazi is another major city of Libya.
On what date was CPEC formed?
Candidates and many Pakistani sources give 22 May 2013, when Pakistan and China signed the agreement on the economic corridor during Chinese Premier Li Keqiang's visit.
Sources differ: the 46 billion dollar CPEC package was announced in April 2015 during President Xi Jinping's visit.
On what date was the OIC established?
The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation was established at the Rabat summit on 25 September 1969.
It was set up after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque on 21 August 1969, and its headquarters are in Jeddah.
On which date is Defence Day observed in Pakistan?
Defence Day is observed on 6 September to commemorate the defence of Pakistan in the 1965 war.
The 1965 war with India was fought in September 1965.
Ruble is the currency of which country?
The ruble is the currency of Russia.
Saifullah (Sword of Allah) was the title of whom?
The Prophet (PBUH) gave the title Saifullah to the great general Khalid bin Waleed (R.A).
He commanded the Muslim armies in the conquest of Syria and the battle of Yarmouk.
Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai was a famous poet of which province?
Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai was the great Sufi poet of Sindh. His collection is called Shah Jo Risalo.
His shrine is at Bhit Shah in Sindh.
Sultan Bahu and Bulleh Shah are poets of which language?
Both Sufi poets wrote in Punjabi.
Bulleh Shah is buried in Kasur and Sultan Bahu in Jhang.
Swine flu is caused by what?
Swine flu is caused by influenza viruses, mainly the H1N1 strain.
The H1N1 swine flu pandemic occurred in 2009.
The diameter of a circle is equal to how many radii of the circle?
The diameter is a line through the centre, which is made of two radii. So diameter = 2 x radius.
The circumference of a circle is pi times its diameter.
The Hindu Kush mountain range connects Pakistan with which country?
The Hindu Kush extends from central Afghanistan into northern Pakistan.
Tirich Mir (7708 m), the highest peak of the Hindu Kush, is in Chitral, Pakistan.
The Thomas Cup is associated with which sport?
The Thomas Cup is the men's world team championship of badminton, contested between national teams.
The women's equivalent of the Thomas Cup is the Uber Cup.
The year 1995 was the golden jubilee (50th anniversary) of which international organisation?
The United Nations was founded in 1945, so 1995 marked its 50 years.
The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, now celebrated as United Nations Day.
Which Sahabi was married to two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), earning the title Dhun-Nurayn?
Hazrat Uthman (RA) married Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA) and, after her death, Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA).
Waris Shah is a famous poet of which language?
Waris Shah (1722-1798) wrote the Punjabi romantic epic Heer Ranjha.
Waris Shah is buried in Jandiala Sher Khan, Sheikhupura district.
Warsak Dam, near Peshawar, was completed during the government of which ruler?
Warsak Dam was completed in 1960 under Field Marshal Ayub Khan's government.
It was built on the Kabul River with Canadian help under the Colombo Plan.
How many faraiz does wuzu (ablution) have according to the Hanafi school?
The four faraiz are washing the face, washing the arms up to the elbows, wiping a quarter of the head (masah) and washing the feet up to the ankles.
Schools of thought differ in details of wuzu, and the Hanafi count of four is common in Pakistani textbooks.
What does the word ayat mean?
Ayat is the plural of ayah, meaning a sign, and it is used for the verses of the Quran.
A chapter of the Quran is called a surah.
What does the word Jihad mean?
Jihad comes from the Arabic root j-h-d meaning to strive or exert effort.
Jihad bil nafs means striving against one's own base desires.
OIC stands for Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the collective voice of the Muslim world.
It was called the Organisation of the Islamic Conference until 2011 and is headquartered in Jeddah.
What does Saif mean in Arabic?
Saif is the Arabic word for sword.
The Arabic word for shield is dir.
Zakat literally means purification and growth, as giving it purifies wealth and the soul.
Zakat is the third pillar of Islam and is usually 2.5 percent on savings above nisab.
A diagonal matrix with all diagonal elements equal
A matrix with all elements zero
A matrix with one row only
A matrix whose rows and columns are interchanged
A scalar matrix is a square diagonal matrix in which all the main diagonal elements are the same and all other elements are zero.
A scalar matrix with diagonal elements equal to 1 is the identity matrix.
Which word is a synonym of cleverness?
Cleverness means mental sharpness, so intelligence is the closest in meaning.
Another synonym of cleverness is shrewdness.
Which word is a synonym of constant?
Constant means continuing without change, so steady is the closest in meaning.
In mathematics, a constant is a quantity whose value does not change.
Which word is a synonym of elation?
Elation means great joy or high spirits, so delight is a synonym.
Which word is a synonym of idleness?
Idleness is the state of doing no work, which is laziness.
An island off the Balochistan coast
Astola, also called Haft Talar, is an island in the Arabian Sea off the coast of Balochistan.
It is Pakistan's largest offshore island.
What was the Lucknow Pact of 1916?
An agreement between the Muslim League and Congress accepting separate electorates for Muslims
A treaty between Britain and Afghanistan
An agreement ending the War of Independence 1857
The Lucknow Pact was signed in December 1916 by the All India Muslim League and the Indian National Congress, and Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was called the ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity for his role in it.
What is the National Finance Commission (NFC) used for?
Distributing federal divisible revenue between the federation and the provinces
The NFC Award decides how the divisible pool of federal taxes is shared between the centre and the four provinces.
The 7th NFC Award of 2010 gave the provinces 57.5 percent of the divisible pool.
The way and practice of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
Sunnah literally means path or way, and in Islam it refers to the sayings, actions and approvals of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
Sunnah is the second source of Islamic law after the Quran.
What is the value of tan 45 degrees?
At 45 degrees sin and cos are both 1 over root 2, so tan = sin/cos = 1.
The value of tan 60 degrees is root 3.
What is the antonym of entire?
Entire means whole or complete, so its opposite is partial, meaning only a part.
Whole, complete and total are synonyms of entire.
What is the antonym of persistent?
Persistent means continuing firmly without stopping. Occasional, meaning happening only now and then, is the opposite.
What is the arithmetic mean of x-3 and x+5?
The arithmetic mean of two numbers lies exactly midway between them.
What is the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK)?
Peshawar is the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Quetta, which one candidate wrote, is the capital of Balochistan.
Peshawar is one of the oldest living cities in South Asia.
What is the capital of Sindh?
Karachi is the capital of Sindh province.
Karachi is the largest city of Pakistan.
What is the currency of Albania?
Bulgaria's former lev and Romania's leu are similar-sounding currencies.
What is the currency of Algeria?
Morocco uses the dirham, not the dinar.
What is the currency of Brazil?
Brazil is the largest country in South America.
What is the currency of Bulgaria?
Bulgaria replaced the lev with the euro on 1 January 2026, becoming the 21st eurozone member.
Before 2026 the Bulgarian lev (candidates' 2021-22 answer) was fixed at 1.95583 per euro.
When did the Cripps Mission come to India?
Sir Stafford Cripps reached India in March 1942 with proposals for dominion status after World War II.
The Muslim League and Congress both rejected the proposals.
Which is the deepest known part of the earth's oceans?
Puerto Rico Trench in the Atlantic Ocean
Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean
Java Trench in the Indian Ocean
Tonga Trench in the Atlantic Ocean
The Mariana Trench in the western Pacific holds the deepest point, Challenger Deep. The candidate answer wrongly placed it in the Atlantic.
Challenger Deep is roughly 10,900 metres deep.
What is the first pillar of Islam?
The first pillar is the declaration of faith (Shahada), which affirms Tauheed and the Prophethood of Muhammad (SAW).
The order of the pillars is Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm, Hajj.
What is the graph of a linear equation in two variables?
A linear equation such as y = mx + c has all its solutions on one straight line.
In y = mx + c, m is the slope and c is the y-intercept.
What is the height of K2, the second highest mountain in the world?
K2 is about 8,611 m high (some sources give 8,609 m).
K2 lies in the Karakoram range on the Pakistan-China border and is also called Mount Godwin-Austen.
What is the height of Mount Everest?
The 2020 joint Nepal-China survey gave Everest a height of 8,848.86 m, commonly rounded to 8,849 m.
Before 2020 the accepted height was 8,848 m.
Which is known as the highest battlefield of the world?
Siachen Glacier in the Karakoram, where Pakistani and Indian troops face each other at around 6,000 m, is the highest battlefield.
Siachen is about 76 km long, one of the longest glaciers outside the polar regions.
What is the highest point above sea level in Pakistan?
K2 (8,611 m) is the highest peak in Pakistan.
Nanga Parbat (8,126 m) is the second highest mountain in Pakistan.
What is the kunniyat (kunyah) of the Prophet Muhammad (SAW)?
The Prophet (SAW) was called Abu al-Qasim after his first son Qasim.
His other sons Abdullah and Ibrahim also died in infancy.
What is the largest bird in the world?
The ostrich is the largest and heaviest living bird, up to about 2.7 m tall.
The ostrich cannot fly but is the fastest running bird.
What is the largest city of Sindh by population?
Karachi is the capital of Sindh and the largest city in Pakistan.
Hyderabad is the second largest city of Sindh.
What is the length of a marathon race?
The standard marathon distance is 26 miles 385 yards, which is 42.195 km.
The distance was fixed at the 1908 London Olympics.
What is the literal meaning of the word Hadith?
In Arabic, Hadith means speech, statement, report or narration.
Technically, a Hadith is a report of the words, actions or approvals of the Prophet (SAW).
What is the literal meaning of the word Quran?
That which is recited or read
The word Quran comes from the Arabic root qara'a, meaning to read or recite.
Al-Furqan (the Criterion) and Al-Huda (the Guidance) are other names of the Quran.
What is the lower house of the Parliament of Pakistan called?
The National Assembly is the lower house and its members are directly elected by the people.
The upper house of Pakistan's Parliament is the Senate.
What is the meaning of Al-Feel?
Al-Feel is Arabic for the elephant and is the name of Surah 105 of the Quran.
The surah describes the army of Abraha with elephants that attacked the Kaaba in the year of the Prophet's birth.
What is the meaning of Ayat?
Ayat is the plural of ayah, which means a sign or a verse of the Quran.
The Quran has 114 surahs and 6,236 ayat according to the common count.
What is the meaning of Badr?
Badr in Arabic means the full moon.
The Battle of Badr was fought in 2 AH (624 CE) near a well named Badr.
A flea is a small wingless jumping insect that feeds on the blood of animals.
Fleas can jump many times their own body length.
A place near Makkah where a treaty was signed
Hudaibiya is a place near Makkah where the treaty between the Prophet (PBUH) and the Quraish was signed in 6 AH.
The Treaty of Hudaibiya set a ten-year truce and paved the way for the conquest of Makkah.
What is the meaning of Islam?
Submission to the will of Allah
Islam means submission and obedience to Allah, and the root also gives the sense of peace.
A person who submits to Allah is called a Muslim.
What is the meaning of Maghfirat?
Maghfirat is Arabic for forgiveness or pardon.
Allah's name Al-Ghafoor means the Most Forgiving.
What is the meaning of the word obvious?
Something obvious is easy to see or understand and is clear to everyone.
Its opposite is obscure or hidden.
What is the meaning of Quran?
Quran comes from the Arabic root qara'a, meaning to read or recite, so it means that which is recited.
The Quran was revealed over about 23 years.
What is the meaning of Riba in Islam?
Riba means increase and refers to interest or usury on loans, which Islam prohibits.
The prohibition of riba is stated in Surah Al-Baqarah.
What is the meaning of Zakat?
Zakat means purification and growth, as paying it purifies a person's wealth.
Zakat is paid at 2.5 percent of savings held above the nisab for a year.
What is the most populated city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
Peshawar is the provincial capital and the largest city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by population.
Mardan is among the next largest cities of the province.
What is the multiplicative inverse of a non-zero number A?
The multiplicative inverse of A is the number which gives 1 when multiplied by A. Since A times 1/A = 1, it is 1/A.
Which pamphlet did Chaudhry Rehmat Ali write in 1933?
Chaudhry Rehmat Ali wrote the pamphlet Now or Never; Are We to Live or Perish Forever in 1933.
In it he coined the name Pakistan.
Who was the father of Hazrat Ishaq (AS)?
Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Sarah.
Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
What is the name of Pakistan's unmanned combat aerial vehicle?
Burraq is the armed drone developed by Pakistan and was first used in combat in 2015.
Shahpar is another Pakistani drone used mainly for surveillance.
What is the border line between Pakistan's Punjab and India's Punjab called?
The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947 and divides Punjab between Pakistan and India.
The Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.
What is the name of the parliament of Finland?
The parliament of Finland is called the Eduskunta.
Storting is Norway's parliament and Riksdag is Sweden's.
What is the name of the parliament of Japan?
The national parliament of Japan is called the Diet (Kokkai).
The Diet has two houses, the House of Representatives and the House of Councillors.
What is the national flower of Pakistan?
Jasmine (Chambeli) is the national flower of Pakistan.
Its Latin name is Jasminum officinale.
What is the national fruit of Pakistan?
The mango is the national fruit of Pakistan.
Pakistan is among the largest producers of mangoes in the world.
What is the national game of Canada?
Canada officially declared lacrosse its national summer sport and ice hockey its national winter sport in 1994.
Ice hockey is also an official national sport, so questions may accept either depending on the options.
Constitutional proposals for India drafted by a committee under Motilal Nehru
The Nehru Report of 1928 was a set of constitutional proposals drafted by a committee headed by Motilal Nehru. It rejected separate electorates for Muslims.
Muhammad Ali Jinnah responded with his Fourteen Points in 1929.
What was the old name of Attock city?
Attock city was known as Campbellpur after Sir Colin Campbell.
Its old name was restored to Attock in 1978.
What was the old name of Faisalabad?
Faisalabad was called Lyallpur after Sir James Lyall.
It was renamed in 1979 in honour of King Faisal of Saudi Arabia.
What was the old name of Sri Lanka?
Sri Lanka was known as Ceylon until it was renamed in 1972.
Burma is the old name of Myanmar and Siam of Thailand.
Which is the oldest university of Pakistan?
The University of the Punjab, Lahore was founded in 1882 and is the oldest in Pakistan.
The University of Karachi was founded in 1951.
What is the sign of the product of a positive number and a negative number?
A positive times a negative is always negative, for example 3 x (-2) = -6.
The product of two negative numbers is positive.
What is the real name of Imam Bukhari?
Imam Bukhari's full name was Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari. He compiled the collection Sahih al-Bukhari.
Imam Bukhari was born in 810 CE in Bukhara and his Sahih is regarded as the most authentic hadith collection.
What is the third pillar of Islam?
The five pillars in order are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj. So Zakat is the third.
Zakat is generally 2.5 percent of qualifying savings held for a year.
What is the shape of a basketball court?
A basketball court is a rectangle, 28 m long and 15 m wide in international play.
A basketball team has five players on court at a time.
Which is the shortest surah of the Quran?
Surah Al-Kausar has only 3 verses and 10 words, making it the shortest surah.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah with 286 verses.
What is the smallest bone in the human body?
The stapes in the middle ear is the smallest bone, about 3 mm long.
The femur (thigh bone) is the longest bone in the body.
Which is the smallest planet of the solar system?
Mercury has a diameter of about 4,880 km, the smallest of the eight planets.
Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
What is the sound made by an eagle called?
An eagle's call is described as a screech or shrill cry.
Which word is a synonym of curious?
Curious means eager to know or learn, which is the meaning of inquisitive.
Its opposite is incurious or indifferent.
Which word is a synonym of literal?
Literal means following the exact, word-for-word meaning, so exact is the closest synonym.
Which word is a synonym of possession?
Possession means the state of having or owning something, so ownership is a synonym.
The word can also mean a thing that is owned, such as property.
Which title of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) means Mercy for all the Worlds?
Rahmatul-lil-Alameen means Mercy for the Worlds and is a title of the Prophet (PBUH) taken from the Quran, Surah Al-Anbiya.
Khatam-un-Nabiyyin means Seal of the Prophets.
What is the total number of rukus in the Holy Quran?
The Quran is divided into 558 rukus (sections), a division mainly used in the Indian subcontinent.
The Quran is also divided into 30 paras.
How many months are there in the Islamic calendar?
The Islamic (Hijri) calendar is lunar and has 12 months, starting with Muharram.
It began with the Hijra of the Prophet (PBUH) in 622 CE.
What are the Upper House (Senate) and Lower House (National Assembly) of Pakistan jointly called?
Together with the President, the Senate and the National Assembly form the Parliament, called Majlis-e-Shoora.
The Senate of Pakistan has 96 members.
What is the value of cos 0 degrees?
At 0 degrees the adjacent side equals the hypotenuse, so cos 0 = 1.
Approximately what percentage of the adult human body is water?
Water makes up about 60 percent of an adult's body weight.
Infants have a higher share, around 75 percent.
Which strip of land separates Pakistan from Central Asia (Tajikistan)?
The narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan separates Pakistan from Tajikistan and Central Asia.
The corridor was created as a buffer between British India and Russian Empire in the 19th century.
What type of state did Afghanistan act as for a long time between the British and Russian empires?
Afghanistan stood between British India and Tsarist Russia and served as a buffer state.
The Durand Line was drawn in 1893 as its border with British India.
What was the relation of Hazrat Urwa bin Zubair with Hazrat Ayesha (RA)?
Urwa was the son of Hazrat Zubair bin Awwam and Hazrat Asma, who was the sister of Hazrat Ayesha. This made Urwa her nephew.
Urwa bin Zubair is one of the seven famous jurists of Madina and a major narrator of hadith from his aunt Hazrat Ayesha.
What was the caliphate number of Hazrat Umar (RA) among the Rashidun caliphs?
The order of the Rashidun caliphs is Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali (may Allah be pleased with them). Umar was therefore the second.
Hazrat Umar (RA) ruled from 634 to 644 AD and is called Al-Farooq.
What was the most important event of 8 AH in Islamic history?
The Muslims conquered Makkah peacefully in Ramadan 8 AH (630 AD). The Prophet (PBUH) forgave the people of Makkah and cleansed the Kaaba of idols.
The Battle of Hunain and the siege of Taif followed soon after the conquest of Makkah in the same year.
Which battle of the American Civil War, fought in 1863, was the turning point of the war?
The Battle of Gettysburg was fought in July 1863 in Pennsylvania and ended in a Union victory over the Confederate army of Robert E. Lee. It is widely seen as the turning point of the war.
Abraham Lincoln delivered the famous Gettysburg Address at the battlefield in November 1863.
What was the religion of Najashi, the king of Abyssinia (Habsha) who gave shelter to the early Muslim migrants?
Najashi (Negus) of Abyssinia was a Christian king. He protected the Muslim emigrants and refused to hand them over to the Quraish.
The Muslims made their first migration to Abyssinia in 5th year of the Prophethood.
When was Sindh separated from the Bombay Presidency?
Sindh became a separate province on 1 April 1936 under the Government of India Act 1935. Sir Shah Nawaz Bhutto and others had campaigned for the separation.
The Quaid-e-Azam had included the separation of Sindh in his Fourteen Points of 1929.
In which year did the Khilafat Movement start in India?
The movement started in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Caliph and the Muslim holy places after the First World War. Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Shaukat Ali were its main leaders.
The movement ended after Turkey abolished the caliphate in 1924.
For what purpose is Namaz-e-Istisqa offered?
Istisqa means asking for water. Muslims offer this special prayer when there is drought and ask Allah for rain.
The prayer for a solar or lunar eclipse is called Namaz-e-Kusuf or Khusuf.
In which year was the Cripps Mission sent to India?
Sir Stafford Cripps came to India in March 1942 during the Second World War. He offered dominion status after the war, which the Congress and the Muslim League rejected.
The Cabinet Mission was a different mission that came to India in 1946.
In which year was the first census of Pakistan held?
The first census of Pakistan was held in 1951. Later censuses were held in 1961, 1972, 1981, 1998 and 2017.
The 2017 census was the first one after nearly 19 years since the 1998 census.
When was the All India Muslim League established?
The Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dhaka during the Muhammadan Educational Conference. Nawab Salimullah Khan hosted the meeting.
Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk presided and Sir Agha Khan was the first honorary president.
At what age did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) place the Hajr-e-Aswad (Black Stone) in the Kaaba?
When the Quraish rebuilt the Kaaba, they disputed who would put the Black Stone in place. The Prophet, aged 35, settled the matter by placing it on a cloth carried by all the tribal chiefs.
The Quraish called him Al-Amin (the trustworthy) and accepted his decision.
In which year of the Hijra was the Qibla changed from Bait-ul-Muqaddas (Jerusalem) to the Kaaba?
The command to turn towards the Kaaba came in 2 AH, about sixteen to seventeen months after the Hijra, while the Prophet (PBUH) was leading prayer in Madina.
The mosque where this happened is known as Masjid Qiblatain.
When and where was the Red Cross founded?
The International Committee of the Red Cross was founded in Geneva in 1863 on the initiative of Henry Dunant.
Henry Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.
Where are the Caucasus mountains located?
Between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea
Between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf
Between the Baltic Sea and the North Sea
Between the Mediterranean Sea and the Black Sea
The Caucasus range lies between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea and forms a boundary between Europe and Asia.
Its highest peak is Mount Elbrus in Russia.
Where did Pakistan conduct its nuclear tests on 28 May 1998?
Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Ras Koh hills of Chagai district, Balochistan.
28 May is observed every year as Youm-e-Takbeer.
Which country is the place of origin of the game of squash?
Squash originated in England at Harrow School in the 19th century.
Pakistan dominated world squash through Hashim Khan, Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan.
Lake Saif-ul-Malook is situated in which valley?
Lake Saif-ul-Malook lies near Naran in the Kaghan Valley, Mansehra district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
It is at about 3,200 metres above sea level.
In which city is the Mahabat Khan Mosque located?
The Mahabat Khan Mosque is a Mughal-era mosque in the old walled city of Peshawar, built in the 17th century.
It was built by Mahabat Khan, a governor of Peshawar under Shah Jahan.
Where is the Gulf of Siam (Gulf of Thailand) located?
The Gulf of Siam, now usually called the Gulf of Thailand, is an arm of the South China Sea bordered by Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam and Malaysia.
Bangkok lies at the head of the gulf.
Where is the headquarters of Amnesty International?
Amnesty International has its international secretariat in London.
It was founded in London in 1961 and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977.
Where is the famous Koh-i-Noor diamond kept today?
The Koh-i-Noor is set in a crown that is part of the British Crown Jewels displayed at the Tower of London.
Pakistan, India and others have claimed that it should be returned.
Where is the headquarters of NATO?
NATO has its headquarters in Brussels, Belgium.
NATO was founded in 1949, and its headquarters was in Paris before 1967.
Where is the headquarters of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)?
The OIC secretariat is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
Its intended permanent seat is East Jerusalem once it is liberated.
Where is the shrine of Shah Rukn-e-Alam?
The shrine of Hazrat Shah Rukn-e-Alam is in Multan.
It is famed for its Tughlaq-era architecture.
In which city is the Pakistan Steel Mills located?
Pakistan Steel Mills was built at Pipri near Karachi with Soviet help.
It began production in the early 1980s.
Which angel brought revelation to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
Hazrat Jibrael (Gabriel, AS) conveyed the revelation of the Quran to the Prophet (PBUH).
The first revelation came in the Cave of Hira.
Which province of Pakistan is known as Bab-ul-Islam (Gateway of Islam)?
Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam because Islam first entered the subcontinent there with Muhammad bin Qasim in 712 AD.
The question was asked about a city, but the standard answer is the province Sindh.
Which continent is called the ice desert?
Antarctica receives very little precipitation and is covered in ice, so it is called the ice desert.
It is the coldest, driest and windiest continent.
Which of the following countries is NOT a member of SAARC?
SAARC has eight members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Myanmar is not a member.
SAARC was founded in Dhaka in 1985 and its secretariat is in Kathmandu.
Ban Ki-moon, former Secretary-General of the United Nations, belongs to which country?
Ban Ki-moon is a South Korean diplomat who served as UN Secretary-General from 2007 to 2016.
He was succeeded as Secretary-General by Antonio Guterres of Portugal.
Which country is regarded as the birthplace of modern football (soccer)?
Modern football rules were codified in England in 1863 when the Football Association was formed.
Ancient ball games such as the Chinese cuju existed earlier, so sources differ on the earliest origin.
Which international day is observed on 21 September?
World Peace Day (International Day of Peace)
The UN International Day of Peace is observed on 21 September each year.
World Teachers Day is on 5 October and World Food Day on 16 October.
The United Nations recognises 12 July as which day?
The UN declared 12 July Malala Day in 2013, Malala Yousafzai's birthday.
World Population Day falls on 11 July.
Which is the largest freshwater lake of the world by volume?
Lake Baikal in Russia holds about 20 percent of the world's unfrozen surface freshwater.
Baikal is also the deepest lake in the world.
Which is the deepest lake in the world?
Lake Baikal in Siberia reaches a depth of about 1,642 metres.
Lake Tanganyika is the second deepest lake.
Which is the biggest river of South America?
The Amazon is South America's biggest river and the largest in the world by volume of water.
The Mississippi is a river of North America.
The word follows the rule i before e except after c: chief.
Chef is a different word meaning a professional cook.
Which is the largest bay in the world by area?
The Bay of Bengal, about 2.2 million square km, is generally considered the largest bay in the world.
Hudson Bay is often listed as the second largest.
Which is the longest freshwater lake in the world?
Lake Tanganyika in Africa is about 676 km long, the longest freshwater lake in the world.
Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest lake in the world.
Which is the second largest continent by area?
Asia is the largest and Africa is second largest with about 30.3 million square km.
Africa is also the second most populous continent.
Which of the following countries is a member of SAARC?
Bhutan is one of the eight SAARC members.
SAARC members are Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan.
Which provincial assembly of Pakistan has the most seats?
The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats (297 general, 66 women, 8 non-Muslim), the most of any province.
Sindh has 168, KP 145 and Balochistan 65 seats.
Which surah of the Quran does not begin with Bismillah?
Surah At-Tawbah (Bara'at) is the only surah that does not begin with Bismillah.
Bismillah appears twice in Surah An-Naml, once at the start and once inside verse 30.
Which surah is described in the Quran as Ahsan-ul-Qasas (the best of stories)?
Surah Yusuf tells the story of Hazrat Yusuf (A.S) and Allah calls it the best of stories.
Surah Yusuf is the 12th surah of the Quran.
Which Surah is known as Ash-Shifa (the cure)?
Surah Al-Fatiha is known by many names including Ash-Shifa because it is recited for healing.
It is also called Umm-ul-Kitab and Sab'a al-Mathani.
In which Surah does Allah swear by time?
Surah Al-Asr begins with an oath by time (Wal-Asr).
Surah Al-Asr is the 103rd surah and has three verses.
Which uncle of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is mentioned by name in the Quran?
Abu Lahab is named in Surah Al-Lahab (Al-Masad) which condemns him.
He was the only enemy of the Prophet named in the Quran.
Which wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar Farooq (R.A)?
Hazrat Hafsa bint Umar (R.A) married the Prophet (PBUH) in 3 AH.
Hazrat Aisha was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A).
Who proposed digging the trench in the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab)?
Hazrat Salman Farsi (R.A) suggested digging a trench, a Persian defence method, to protect Madina.
The battle took place in 5 AH.
Who is credited with discovering the photovoltaic effect, the basis of solar energy?
Alexandre Edmond Becquerel observed the photovoltaic effect in 1839, which is the principle behind solar cells.
Albert Einstein won the 1921 Nobel Prize for explaining the photoelectric effect.
Who established the Mughal rule in India?
Babar defeated Ibrahim Lodhi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 and founded the Mughal Empire.
Babar was a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan.
Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah founded Dawn in Delhi in 1941 to voice the Muslim League view.
Dawn moved to Karachi after the creation of Pakistan in 1947.
Who has scored the most ODI runs for Pakistan?
Inzamam-ul-Haq leads Pakistan's ODI run list with 11,701 runs.
Mohammad Yousuf (9,554) and Saeed Anwar (8,824) follow him.
Which country helped Pakistan build the Chashma nuclear power plant?
The Chashma Nuclear Power Plants in Punjab were built with Chinese assistance.
China also built later units such as C-3 and C-4 at Chashma.
Which country helped the USA build relations with China in 1971?
