Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia are leading rubber producers.
Ruh-ul-Qudus is the title of which angel?
Ruh-ul-Qudus (the Holy Spirit) is a title of the angel Hazrat Jibreel (AS), who brought revelation.
Hazrat Jibreel (AS) is also called Ameen.
In which month is Shab-e-Qadr (Laylatul Qadr)?
Laylatul Qadr falls in Ramadan, most likely on an odd night of the last ten days.
The Quran was first revealed on this night, and Surah Al-Qadr describes it as better than a thousand months.
Complete the sentence: She said that she ___ to know.
In reported speech with the past tense verb said, the verb shifts to the past, so wanted is used.
This shifting of tense is called backshift.
Sound travels in the form of what?
Sound is a mechanical (longitudinal) wave that needs a medium such as air to travel.
Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
Stainless steel is an example of what?
Stainless steel is an alloy of iron with chromium and often nickel.
Chromium of at least about 10.5 percent makes it resist rust.
Which country mediated the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 between Pakistan and India?
The Soviet Union under Premier Alexei Kosygin mediated the Tashkent Declaration in January 1966.
Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri died in Tashkent soon after signing.
The Thar desert of Sindh is rich in which mineral resource?
Thar has one of the world's largest lignite coal reserves, about 175 billion tonnes.
Thar coal is being used for power generation at Islamkot.
The Battle of Furqan is the name of which ghazwa?
The Quran calls the day of Badr Yawm al-Furqan, the Day of Distinction between truth and falsehood. So the Battle of Furqan is the Battle of Badr.
Badr was fought in 2 AH (624 CE) and about 313 Muslims faced roughly 1000 Makkan soldiers.
The census of Pakistan is conducted by which organization?
Population and housing censuses in Pakistan are carried out by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics. NADRA and the Election Commission only use the data or registers.
The 2017 and the digital 2023 censuses were both conducted by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics.
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) appointed Hazrat Maaz bin Jabal (RA) as governor of which place?
The Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Maaz bin Jabal to Yemen as governor and teacher of the people.
Hazrat Maaz bin Jabal was known as the most knowledgeable of the Companions in halal and haram.
The Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 was made with the mediation of which organization?
The treaty between Pakistan and India was brokered by the World Bank and signed in Karachi in September 1960.
India announced in April 2025 that it was holding the treaty in abeyance, and Pakistan rejects this move.
The nation of which prophet was destroyed by a rain of stones?
The Quran says the sinful people of Hazrat Loot (AS) were destroyed by a shower of baked clay stones.
The nation of Hazrat Nooh (AS) was destroyed by flood and the people of Aad by a violent wind.
The Panama Canal connects the Pacific Ocean with which ocean?
The canal cuts across Panama and joins the Pacific Ocean with the Atlantic Ocean through the Caribbean Sea.
The Panama Canal was opened in 1914 while the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean with the Red Sea.
Under the Constitution of Pakistan, the President is bound to act on the advice of whom?
Article 48 of the Constitution requires the President to act on the advice of the Prime Minister (or the Cabinet).
Pakistan has a parliamentary system in which the Prime Minister is the real executive head.
The river Amazon is ___ largest river of South America.
A superlative such as largest takes the definite article the.
The Amazon is the largest river in the world by volume of water.
Choose the correct reported speech: The teacher asked, Who is speaking English?
The teacher wanted to know who is speaking English.
The teacher wanted to know who was speaking English.
The teacher wanted to know who has spoken English.
The teacher wanted to know who speaks English was.
In reported speech a present continuous question changes to past continuous, so is speaking becomes was speaking, and the question order becomes a statement.
The reporting verb asked is usually changed to wanted to know or enquired.
The Wakhan Corridor separates Pakistan from which country?
The narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan lies between Pakistan on the south and Tajikistan on the north.
The corridor also touches China at its eastern end.
The word Everyone is what part of speech?
Everyone stands in place of a noun (all people), so it is an indefinite pronoun.
Other indefinite pronouns are someone, anybody and nobody.
Thimphu is the capital of which country?
Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan.
Bhutan is a Himalayan kingdom between China and India.
Through which of these countries does the Tropic of Cancer not pass?
The Tropic of Cancer (23.5 degrees north) crosses India, Bangladesh and Egypt, but Pakistan lies north of it.
It also passes through Mexico, Saudi Arabia, Libya and southern China.
Through which of these countries does the Tropic of Capricorn not pass?
The Tropic of Capricorn (23.5 degrees south) lies in the southern hemisphere, and India is entirely in the northern hemisphere.
It also crosses Chile, Argentina, Namibia, Botswana and Madagascar.
To where did the Muslims first migrate?
In 615 CE (5th year of the Prophethood) a group of Muslims migrated to Abyssinia to escape persecution in Makkah.
The king of Abyssinia, Negus (Najashi), gave them protection.
To which country does Olympic Airlines (now Olympic Air) belong?
Olympic Airlines was the national flag carrier of Greece, founded in 1957 by Aristotle Onassis. It was replaced by Olympic Air in 2009.
Olympic Airways was nationalised in 1975 and ceased operating as the flag carrier in 2009.
To which place did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate in 622 AD?
In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madina (then called Yathrib). This migration is the Hijrat.
The Hijri calendar begins from this migration.
To which tribe did Hazrat Ali (RA) belong?
Hazrat Ali (RA) was born in Makkah into the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraysh tribe. He was the cousin of the Prophet (PBUH).
Aws and Khazraj were the two main tribes of Madina.
Umm Kalsoom (Umm Kulthum) was what of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA) was a daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA).
She married Hazrat Usman (RA) after the death of her sister Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA).
Towards which place was the first Hijrat of the Muslims made?
In 615 AD a small group of Muslims migrated from Makkah to Habsha (Abyssinia) to escape persecution by the Quraysh. Its Christian king, the Negus, gave them protection.
The migration to Madina came about seven years later, in 622 AD.
To whom was the Nishan-e-Haider last awarded?
Havaldar Lalak Jan Shaheed received the award for gallantry in the 1999 Kargil conflict; no later award is recorded.
Lalak Jan belonged to Yasin valley, Gilgit-Baltistan, and is the 11th recipient.
According to the 2023 census, Urdu is the mother tongue of about what percentage of Pakistanis?
The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics 2023 census puts Urdu at about 9.25 percent of the population. Candidates in 2021-22 recalled about 7 percent, which was the 2017 census figure (7.08 percent).
Punjabi is the most common mother tongue, at about 37 percent.
Which are the three largest oceans of the world, in order of size?
By area the Pacific is the largest, then the Atlantic, then the Indian Ocean. The Southern and Arctic Oceans are smaller.
The Pacific Ocean covers about one third of the Earth's surface.
Which day is celebrated on 12 June?
The International Labour Organization observes the World Day Against Child Labour on 12 June each year.
World Environment Day is on 5 June and World Population Day on 11 July.
Thomas Edison developed the first practical long-lasting incandescent electric light bulb in 1879. He also invented the phonograph.
The telephone was patented by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876.
What does the word Al-Fatiha mean?
Al-Fatiha means The Opening, because it opens the Quran and also opens the prayer.
It is also called Umm-ul-Kitab and has seven verses.
What does the Arabic word Ansar mean?
Ansar means helpers. It refers to the people of Madina who sheltered and helped the Muslims migrating from Makkah.
The migrants from Makkah are called Muhajirin.
Uhad (Uhud) is the name of what?
Uhud is a mountain just north of Madina, near which the Battle of Uhud was fought in 3 AH.
The Prophet (PBUH) said that Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it.
A pre-Islamic pact in Makkah to protect the oppressed and uphold justice
A treaty signed between the Muslims and the Quraish in 6 AH
A pact made by the Ansar of Madinah at Aqabah
A trade agreement between Makkah and Syria
Hilf-ul-Fudul was a pledge made by several Makkan clans to help victims of injustice and to see that wrongs were set right. The Prophet (PBUH) took part in it as a young man.
The Prophet (PBUH) said that even after Islam he would respond to a similar call.
What does the term Ijtehad mean in Islamic law?
Independent reasoning to derive rulings from the Quran and Sunnah
Migration for the sake of faith
Ijtehad means exerting one's utmost intellectual effort to find a legal ruling on a new matter from the Quran and Sunnah. A scholar who does this is called a Mujtahid.
Allama Iqbal strongly advocated Ijtehad as the principle of movement in Islam.
What does the Arabic word Mantiq mean?
Mantiq is the Arabic word for logic, the science of correct reasoning. It is taught in Dars-e-Nizami madrassas.
Muslim philosophers such as Al-Farabi and Ibn Sina wrote extensively on Mantiq.
What does NFC stand for in Pakistan's finance system?
NFC stands for National Finance Commission. It decides how federal tax revenue is shared between the federation and the provinces.
The 7th NFC Award of 2010 gave the provinces 57.5 percent of the divisible pool.
What does the abbreviation PSL stand for in Pakistani cricket?
PSL stands for Pakistan Super League, the franchise Twenty20 cricket league of Pakistan. It began in 2016.
The PSL is run by the Pakistan Cricket Board.
What does the word seething mean?
To seethe is to boil or churn, and it is used for a person who is extremely angry but does not show it. So seething means very angry.
Its literal meaning is bubbling as a liquid does when boiling.
Dry ablution with clean earth when water is unavailable
Tayammum is a substitute for wudu or ghusl performed with clean earth or dust when water is not available or cannot be used. It is taught in the Quran in Surah Al-Maidah.
Tayammum is made by striking the hands on clean earth and wiping the face and hands.
What does the Silk Route connect?
China with the Mediterranean and Europe
The Silk Route was an ancient network of trade roads linking China through Central Asia to the Mediterranean world. Silk was a major good carried along it.
The Karakoram Highway in Pakistan follows part of the old Silk Route.
What does the word Akhuwat mean?
Akhuwat is an Arabic and Urdu word meaning brotherhood. It is the name of a Pakistani organisation that gives interest-free loans.
The Akhuwat concept is based on the brotherhood between the Muhajirin and the Ansar of Madinah.
What important event took place in 622 AD?
The Hijrah (migration) of the Prophet (PBUH) from Makkah to Madinah
The Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madinah in 622 AD. This year marks the start of the Islamic Hijri calendar.
The Hijri calendar was introduced in the time of Hazrat Umar (RA).
What is the value of 0! (zero factorial)?
By definition 0! = 1, because there is exactly one way to arrange no objects. This also keeps the formula n! = n x (n-1)! true for n = 1.
The number of ways to choose 0 items from n, nC0, equals 1 for this reason.
What is a period of 100 years also called?
A century is a period of 100 years. A decade is 10 years and a millennium is 1000 years.
A score means 20 years or 20 items.
What is 22 March observed as worldwide?
The United Nations observes 22 March each year as World Water Day. It raises awareness of fresh water and its sustainable use.
World Environment Day is on 5 June and World Health Day on 7 April.
What does the United Nations observe on 24 January?
The UN General Assembly proclaimed 24 January as International Day of Education in December 2018. It was first observed in 2019.
International Literacy Day is on 8 September and World Teachers Day on 5 October.
Subtract the real parts: 3 - 3 = 0. Subtract the imaginary parts: -2i - 2i = -4i, so the answer is -4i.
The product of a complex number and its conjugate is always a real number.
What is an angle of 90 degrees called?
An angle of exactly 90 degrees is called a right angle. Acute angles are smaller and obtuse angles are larger.
What was the relation of A. O. Hume with the Indian National Congress?
He was one of its founders in 1885
He was its first Muslim president
He was the Viceroy who banned it
Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, helped found the Indian National Congress in December 1885. He served as its first general secretary.
The first president of the Congress was W. C. Bonnerjee.
Which word is a synonym of complicated?
Complicated means made of many parts and hard to understand, which is the meaning of complex. Simple, easy and plain are its opposites.
The opposite of complicated is simple.
Which word is a synonym of conceal?
To conceal means to keep something out of sight, which is to hide it. Reveal, show and expose are antonyms.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'dormant'?
Dormant means temporarily inactive or sleeping, as in a dormant volcano.
The opposite of dormant is active.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'evacuate'?
To evacuate is to leave or empty a place, especially because of danger.
Evacuate comes from the Latin word vacuare, meaning to empty.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'exquisite'?
Exquisite describes something extremely beautiful and finely made.
Its opposite could be crude or coarse.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'persistent'?
Persistent means continuing firmly despite difficulty, which is what tenacious means.
Persistent is the antonym of giving up or wavering.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'savage'?
Savage means fierce, wild and untamed.
Savage comes from the Latin silvaticus, meaning of the woods.
What is a zero vector also called?
A vector with zero magnitude and no definite direction is called a null vector.
Adding a null vector to any vector leaves it unchanged.
What is the abscissa of a point in the Cartesian plane?
In a point (x, y), the abscissa is the x-coordinate, the horizontal distance from the y-axis.
The y-coordinate is called the ordinate.
What is Atomic Day (the day of Pakistan's 1998 nuclear tests) called in Pakistan?
Pakistan tested nuclear devices in the Chagai hills in 1998, and the day is observed as Youm-e-Takbeer.
It is observed on 28 May each year.
In statistics, what is the average of a set of numbers also called?
The average is the sum of the values divided by their count, which is the arithmetic mean.
The median is the middle value and the mode is the most frequent value.
Bait ul Muqaddas means the Holy House and refers to Jerusalem and its Masjid al-Aqsa.
It was the first Qibla of Muslims before the change to the Kaaba.
What is Barzakh in Islamic belief?
The period between death and the Day of Judgement
Barzakh is the barrier or intermediate state between a person's death and resurrection.
Barzakh is mentioned in Surah Al-Mu'minun of the Quran.
Which event is commemorated on Kashmir Day (Youm-e-Yakjehti-e-Kashmir) in Pakistan?
Solidarity with the people of Kashmir
Kashmir Day is observed to express support for the Kashmiri right to self-determination.
It is observed on 5 February each year.
What is cot x . sec x equal to?
cot x = cos x / sin x and sec x = 1 / cos x, so the product = 1 / sin x = cosec x.
Cosec x is the reciprocal of sin x.
What is the number of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) among the Khulafa-e-Rashideen?
Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) was the first Rightly Guided Caliph after the Prophet (PBUH).
The order is Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali (RA).
A peace pact of Makkan tribes to protect the oppressed
A treaty between Muslims and Jews of Madinah
Hilful Fudul was a pact formed in Makkah to defend the wronged and help the weak, and the young Prophet (PBUH) took part in it.
The Prophet (PBUH) later said he would still respond to such a pact in Islam.
In vector algebra, what is the value of j . j (dot product of the unit vector j with itself)?
Dot products of different unit vectors such as i . j are 0.
What is Pakistan Standard Time relative to UTC?
Pakistan Standard Time (PST) is five hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time.
Among Muslim-majority countries, what is Pakistan's rank by population?
Indonesia has the largest population among Muslim-majority countries and Pakistan is second.
Which is the most populous district of Punjab, Pakistan?
Lahore has the largest population of any district in Punjab (about 13 million in the 2023 census).
Lahore is also the capital of Punjab.
Stainless steel is mainly an alloy of iron with which metal?
Stainless steel is iron alloyed with at least about 10.5 percent chromium, which resists rust.
Nickel is often added as well.
What is the 15th night of Shaban called?
The night of the 15th of Shaban is known as Shab-e-Barat (night of forgiveness or record).
Shaban is the eighth month of the Islamic calendar and comes just before Ramadan.
Which is the 3rd surah of the Holy Quran?
The order is Al-Fatiha, Al-Baqarah, Ali Imran, so the third is Ali Imran.
Surah Ali Imran has 200 verses and is a Madani surah.
In the commonly taught Pakistani order of the five pillars of Islam (Kalima, Salah, Roza, Zakat, Hajj), which is the 4th pillar?
In this order the pillars run Shahada, Salah, Fasting, Zakat, Hajj, so the fourth is Zakat.
Sources differ: the hadith in Sahih Bukhari lists Hajj before fasting, which makes Hajj fourth.
An acute angle is how large compared with a right angle?
A right angle is 90 degrees and an acute angle is any angle between 0 and 90 degrees, so it is smaller.
An angle larger than 90 and smaller than 180 degrees is called obtuse.
On which date is American Independence Day celebrated?
The US Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776, and that day is celebrated as Independence Day.
The Declaration was mainly drafted by Thomas Jefferson.
An ally is a supporter or friend, and its opposite is an enemy or foe.
The word ally comes from the Latin alligare, meaning to bind to.
To cease means to stop, so its opposite is to continue.
Cease is also often used in the phrase ceasefire.
A chum is a close friend, and the opposite is an enemy.
Chum is an informal word and a synonym of buddy.
To climb is to go up, and the opposite is to descend (go down).
Descend comes from the Latin descendere.
Expansion means growing larger, and its opposite is contraction (becoming smaller).
In economics the opposite phases are expansion and contraction (recession).
To proceed is to go forward, and the opposite is to halt or stop.
Proceed is a synonym of advance, continue and progress.
What is the base of the natural logarithm?
The natural logarithm ln x is the logarithm to base e, where e is approximately 2.71828.
Common logarithms use base 10, and computer science often uses base 2.
What is the value of tan(-x)?
Tangent is an odd function, because sin(-x) = -sin x and cos(-x) = cos x, so tan(-x) = -tan x.
Cosine is an even function, so cos(-x) = cos x.
Which is the biggest continent in the world by area?
Asia covers about 44.6 million square kilometres, which is the largest of all continents.
Asia is also the most populous continent.
In Islam, which is the biggest sin?
The Quran and Hadith describe shirk as the greatest sin, and Allah does not forgive it unless a person repents.
The Quran (Surah An-Nisa 4:48) says that Allah does not forgive shirk but forgives lesser sins.
What is the capital of Bangladesh?
Dhaka is the capital and largest city of Bangladesh.
Bangladesh became independent from Pakistan in 1971.
What is the political capital of Burundi?
Burundi moved its political capital from Bujumbura to Gitega in 2019.
Bujumbura remains the economic capital and the largest city, and was the capital before 2019.
What is the capital of Canada?
Ottawa is the capital of Canada, although Toronto is the largest city.
Ottawa lies on the Ottawa River in the province of Ontario.
What is the capital of Germany?
Berlin is the capital of Germany.
Bonn was the capital of West Germany before reunification in 1990.
What is the capital of Peru?
Lima is the capital and largest city of Peru.
Bogota is the capital of Colombia, Quito of Ecuador and Santiago of Chile.
What is the capital of Australia?
Canberra is the capital of Australia, chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
What is the capital of Azerbaijan?
Baku is the capital of Azerbaijan, on the Caspian Sea.
Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia and Yerevan of Armenia.
What is the capital of Uganda?
Kampala is the capital of Uganda.
Entebbe, near Kampala, hosts Uganda's main international airport.
Which city was the capital of the ancient Gandhara civilization in Pakistani textbooks?
Taxila (Takshashila) is the capital of Gandhara most often given in Pakistani textbooks.
Sources differ: Pushkalavati and later Peshawar (Purushapura) also served as Gandhara capitals.
What is the closest meaning of the word abundant?
Abundant means existing in large quantities. Plentiful is the closest synonym.
The opposite of abundant is scarce.
What is the closest meaning of the word collaboration?
Collaboration means working together with others toward a common goal. Cooperation has the closest meaning.
The word collaborate comes from Latin meaning to labour together.
What is the closest meaning of the word extensive?
Extensive means covering a large area or having a wide range. Widespread is the closest meaning.
The opposite of extensive is limited.
What is the closest meaning of the word juvenile?
Juvenile refers to a young person or something belonging to young people. Youthful is the closest meaning.
A juvenile court deals with offenders below the adult age.
What is the closest meaning of the word slackness?
Slackness means lack of tightness, energy or care. Looseness or laziness fits best.
Slack is the opposite of taut.
What is the closest meaning of the word consent?
Consent means agreement or permission to do something.
The opposite of consent is dissent.
What is the combination of the upper house and lower house of a legislature called?
The legislature made up of the upper and lower houses is called Parliament. In Pakistan it is the Majlis-e-Shoora.
Pakistan's Parliament consists of the National Assembly and the Senate together with the President.
The final consonant n is doubled when adding ing to begin, giving beginning.
Similar doubling occurs in running and swimming.
What is the currency of Belarus?
Belarus uses the Belarusian ruble (code BYN).
The hryvnia is the currency of Ukraine and the zloty that of Poland.
What is the currency of Kenya?
Kenya uses the Kenyan shilling (code KES).
Ethiopia uses the birr and South Africa the rand.
What is the currency of Libya?
Libya uses the Libyan dinar (code LYD).
The Libyan pound was replaced by the dinar in 1971.
What is the currency of Sri Lanka?
Sri Lanka uses the Sri Lankan rupee (code LKR).
The taka is the currency of Bangladesh and the rufiyaa that of the Maldives.
What is the date of America's Independence Day?
The Declaration of Independence of the United States was adopted on 4 July 1776, which is celebrated as Independence Day.
Americans celebrate it every year on 4 July.
On what date did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah die?
Quaid-e-Azam died in Karachi on 11 September 1948, a little over a year after Pakistan was created.
His death anniversary is observed on 11 September every year.
On which date did Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan die?
Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan, known as the father of Pakistan's nuclear programme, died in Islamabad on 10 October 2021.
He was awarded Nishan-e-Imtiaz and Hilal-e-Imtiaz.
What is the derivative of the exponential function e to the power x with respect to x?
x times e to the power (x minus 1)
The function e^x is its own derivative, so d/dx of e^x equals e^x.
The derivative of a to the power x is a^x times ln a.
What is the duty of Hazrat Mikail (AS)?
Hazrat Mikail (AS) is the angel in charge of rain and the provision of sustenance.
Hazrat Jibrail brings revelation, Israfil blows the Trumpet and Azrael takes souls.
According to the Islamic teachings, which question is first asked from a person in the grave?
Munkar and Nakir first ask the deceased: Who is your Lord (Man Rabbuka)? Then they ask about his religion and his Prophet.
Salah is the first deed to be accounted for on the Day of Judgement.
What is the full official name of Pakistan?
Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution names the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
Pakistan was named an Islamic Republic for the first time in the Constitution of 1956.
What is the standard time offset of Pakistan from GMT (UTC)?
Pakistan Standard Time is five hours ahead of GMT, that is UTC+5.
India uses UTC+5:30, so Pakistan is 30 minutes behind India.
Which surah is called the heart (Qalb) of the Quran?
A hadith narrated in the books of Hadith describes Surah Yaseen as the heart of the Quran.
Surah Yaseen is the 36th surah and has 83 verses.
What is the highest court of Pakistan?
The Supreme Court of Pakistan, in Islamabad, is the apex court of the country.
The Federal Shariat Court examines whether laws conform to Islamic injunctions.
What is the highest power of the variable in a polynomial called?
The degree of a polynomial is the largest exponent of its variable. For example, x^3 + 2x has degree 3.
A polynomial of degree 2 is called a quadratic.
What is the integral part of a logarithm called?
A logarithm has two parts: the integer part is the characteristic and the decimal part is the mantissa.
The mantissa of a common logarithm is always kept positive.
Which is the largest bone of the human body?
The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the human body.
The smallest bone is the stapes in the middle ear.
Which is the largest city of Pakistan by population?
Karachi is the most populous city of Pakistan, with over 14 million people at the 2017 census and about 20 million at the 2023 census.
Lahore is the second largest city.
Which is the largest hot desert of the world?
The Sahara in North Africa covers about 9 million square kilometres and is the largest hot desert.
Counting cold deserts, Antarctica is the largest desert in the world.
Which is the largest gulf in the world?
The Gulf of Mexico covers about 1.6 million square kilometres, which is the largest gulf.
The Persian Gulf is much smaller, at about 250,000 square kilometres.
Which is the largest plateau of the world by area?
The Tibetan Plateau covers about 2.5 million square kilometres and is the largest as well as the highest plateau.
It is often called the Roof of the World.
Which is the largest sea of Europe?
The Mediterranean Sea covers about 2.5 million square kilometres, more than any other sea touching Europe.
The Mediterranean connects to the Atlantic Ocean through the Strait of Gibraltar.
What is the upgraded version of the Pakistani missile Hatf-IV (Shaheen-I) called?
Hatf-IV is the Shaheen-I ballistic missile, and its longer-range upgraded variant is called Shaheen-IA.
Shaheen-IA was first test fired in April 2012.
What is the literal meaning of the word Furqan?
The criterion that separates right from wrong
Furqan comes from an Arabic root meaning to separate or distinguish. It therefore means the criterion that distinguishes truth from falsehood.
Al-Furqan is a name of the Holy Quran and the title of the 25th surah.
What is the literal meaning of the word Islam?
Submission and surrender to the will of Allah
Islam comes from the Arabic root s-l-m, meaning submission, surrender and also peace. It means submitting oneself to Allah.
A person who submits to Allah is called a Muslim.
What is the literal meaning of Tayammum?
To intend or aim at something
Tayammum literally means to intend or to aim at something. In Islamic law it means purifying oneself with clean earth when water is unavailable.
Tayammum is allowed in place of wudu or ghusl when water is not available or its use would be harmful.
What is the meaning of the word Al-Noor?
Noor is an Arabic word meaning light, and Al-Noor means The Light.
Surah An-Nur is the 24th surah of the Holy Quran and Al-Nur is one of the names of Allah.
What is the meaning of the word conscious?
Conscious means being awake and aware of oneself or one's surroundings.
What is the meaning of the word gallant?
Gallant means brave and heroic, and also politely attentive to women.
Gallantry awards are given to soldiers for bravery in action.
What is the meaning of Hilf-ul-Fudul?
Hilf-ul-Fudul was a pact made in Makkah by chiefs who promised to defend the oppressed and give justice to all. Its name means the pact of the virtuous.
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) took part in it as a young man before prophethood and praised it later.
What is the meaning of the name Israel?
Israel is a Hebrew name, the title of Hazrat Yaqub (AS), meaning servant of God (Abdullah).
The descendants of Hazrat Yaqub (AS) are called Bani Israel.
What is the meaning of the word oppression?
Cruel or unjust treatment of people
Oppression means the prolonged cruel or unjust use of power over others.
Zulm is the Urdu and Arabic word for oppression.
What is the meaning of Ruku in prayer?
Ruku means to bow, and in salah it is the posture of bowing with hands on the knees.
Sajdah, the prostration, is the posture that follows ruku.
What is the meaning of the word Tanzeel?
Tanzeel comes from an Arabic root meaning to send down, and it is used for the revelation of the Quran.
The Quran says it is a Tanzeel from the Lord of the worlds.
What is the meaning of the word voyage?
A long journey, especially by sea
A voyage is a long journey, especially one made by sea or in space.
Bon voyage is a French phrase wishing someone a pleasant journey.
What is the meaning of the word defer?
To defer means to put off something until a later time.
Another meaning is to yield to someone's opinion, as in defer to the elders.
What is the most abundant organic compound on Earth?
Cellulose forms the cell walls of plants and is the most abundant organic compound on Earth.
Which currency is most used in world trade?
The US dollar is the main currency for invoicing trade and for global reserves.
The euro is the second most used reserve currency.
What is the multiplicative inverse of an identity matrix?
Since I times I equals I, the inverse of an identity matrix is the identity matrix itself.
Multiplying any matrix by the identity matrix leaves it unchanged.
Who was the father of Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Hajra.
Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was his younger half-brother.
What is the boundary line between Pakistan and India in Kashmir called?
The Line of Control (LoC) separates Pakistan-administered and Indian-administered Kashmir.
It was established by the 1972 Simla Agreement, based on the 1949 ceasefire line.
Which continent is known as the Dark Continent?
Africa was called the Dark Continent because its interior was unknown to Europeans for a long time.
The nickname became popular through the explorer Henry Morton Stanley.
What was the name of the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) who was married to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Hazrat Ayesha (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) and a wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA).
What was the name of Pakistan's first satellite?
Badr-1, launched on 16 July 1990 from China, was the first satellite of Pakistan.
Which strait separates Russia and the United States (Alaska)?
The Bering Strait lies between the Chukchi Peninsula of Russia and Alaska in the United States.
It connects the Pacific and Arctic oceans and is about 85 km wide.
What is the national animal of Pakistan?
The Markhor, a wild mountain goat with spiral horns, is the national animal of Pakistan.
The Chukar partridge is the national bird, the Deodar the national tree and Jasmine the national flower of Pakistan.
Which word is nearest in meaning to 'diversity'?
Diversity means a range of different things, which is what variety means. Uniformity and similarity are its opposites.
Its adjective form is 'diverse', meaning varied or different in kind.
What is the new name of the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD)?
RCD, formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey, was renamed the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.
ECO has its secretariat in Tehran.
What is the nisab (minimum threshold) of gold for zakat, in tola?
The nisab of gold is 7.5 tola (about 87.48 grams). The 52.5 tola figure is the nisab of silver.
Zakat on wealth at or above the nisab is 2.5 percent.
What is the rate of ushr (zakat on agricultural produce) on land watered by rain?
Ushr means one tenth, so produce from rain-fed land is charged at 10 percent. Land irrigated at a cost is charged at half of that, 5 percent.
Ushr is due on the harvest itself rather than on yearly savings.
Savage means wild and uncivilized, so its opposite is civilized. Fierce, wild and brutal are similar in meaning to savage.
Savage can also be used as a noun for a brutal person.
Tame means domesticated and not dangerous, so its opposite is wild. Gentle, docile and domestic are close to tame in meaning.
Tame can also describe something dull, such as a tame film.
A report on the Bengal famine
A Muslim League report on the treatment of Muslims under Congress ministries
A report on the partition of Bengal
The Pirpur Report was prepared by a Muslim League committee headed by the Raja of Pirpur. It listed the injustices done to Muslims in Congress-ruled provinces from 1937 to 1939.
The Muslim League also observed a Day of Deliverance in December 1939 when the Congress ministries resigned.
What is the radian measure of a half circle (a straight angle)?
A full circle is 2 pi radians, so half of it is pi radians, which equals 180 degrees.
Hazrat Ali (RA) was related to Hazrat Abu Talib as his:
Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, the uncle of the Prophet (PBUH), who raised Ali's cousin the Prophet.
Ali's mother was Fatima bint Asad, and his brother Jafar was also a son of Abu Talib.
What is the scalar (dot) product of two vectors A and B?
A B sin(theta) as a vector
The scalar product is A.B = |A||B|cos(theta), where theta is the angle between them. The result is a number, not a vector.
The vector (cross) product uses sin(theta) and gives a vector.
What is the other name of the Battle of Ahzab?
The Battle of Ahzab (the Confederates) is also called the Battle of Khandaq (the Trench) because the Muslims dug a trench around Madinah. It was fought in 5 AH.
The trench was dug on the suggestion of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA).
What is the shaving of the head during Hajj called?
Halq is shaving the whole head, and Qasr is trimming the hair. One of them is done to come out of the state of Ihram.
Women only trim a small portion of their hair (Taqsir).
What is the source of the Yellow River (Huang He)?
Bayan Har Mountains in Qinghai, China
The Yellow River rises in the Bayan Har Mountains of Qinghai Province, China. It then flows east into the Bohai Sea.
The river is about 5,464 km long, though sources differ on the exact figure.
Which word is closest in meaning to ADHERENT?
An adherent is a supporter or follower of a person, party or idea.
The verb adhere means to stick to or stay loyal to something.
Which word is closest in meaning to EXCITING?
Exciting means causing great enthusiasm or eagerness, which is thrilling.
The word excite comes from the Latin excitare, meaning to rouse.
Which word is closest in meaning to EXTREMELY?
Extremely means to a very high degree, which is exceedingly.
Words such as utterly and highly are also similar in sense.
Which word is closest in meaning to FLOURISH?
To flourish is to grow and develop in a healthy, successful way, which is to thrive.
Its opposite is to decay or wither.
Which word is closest in meaning to HERITAGE?
Heritage is what is passed down from earlier generations, such as traditions and property, which is a legacy.
UNESCO lists World Heritage Sites such as Moenjodaro and Taxila in Pakistan.
Which word is closest in meaning to HIERARCHY?
A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged in order of rank or importance.
The army rank structure is a typical hierarchy.
Which word is closest in meaning to IMPAIR?
To impair is to damage or weaken something so that it works less well. The candidate answer Ridicule has a different meaning.
Its opposite is to enhance or improve.
Which word is closest in meaning to INDIFFERENCE?
Indifference is a lack of interest or concern, which is apathy.
Its opposite is concern or enthusiasm.
Which word is closest in meaning to LAXITY?
Laxity means lack of strictness or care, which is slackness.
Its opposite is rigour or strictness.
Which word is closest in meaning to LEISURE?
Leisure is time free from work or duties, which is free time.
The word comes from the Old French leisir, meaning to be permitted.
Which word is closest in meaning to MALICIOUS?
Malicious means intending to harm others, which is spiteful.
Which word is closest in meaning to MEDIATE?
To mediate is to step in between two sides in a dispute to settle it, which is to arbitrate.
A mediator is a neutral person who helps two parties reach agreement.
Which word is closest in meaning to OPPRESS?
To oppress is to keep people down by cruel or unjust use of power, which is to persecute.
Which word is closest in meaning to PRECEDING?
Preceding means coming before in time or order, which is previous.
Its opposite is succeeding or following.
Which word is closest in meaning to PREVENT?
To prevent is to stop something from happening, which is to avert.
Hinder and thwart are also close in meaning.
Which word is closest in meaning to PROMINENT?
Prominent means well known or important, which is eminent.
It can also mean easily seen or standing out.
Which word is closest in meaning to RESENTMENT?
Resentment is a feeling of bitter anger about unfair treatment, which is bitterness.
Which word is closest in meaning to SPLENDID?
Splendid means very impressive or excellent, which is magnificent.
Splendid comes from the Latin splendere, to shine.
Which word is closest in meaning to TIMID?
Timid means lacking courage or confidence, which is shy.
Its opposite is bold or daring.
Which word is closest in meaning to TOTALLY?
Totally means in every way or to the full extent, which is completely or entirely.
Utterly and wholly are other close words.
Which word is closest in meaning to TYRANT?
A tyrant is a ruler who uses power in a cruel and unjust way, which is a despot.
Its opposite in sense is a benevolent ruler.
Which is the tallest animal living on land?
An adult giraffe can reach about 5 to 5.5 metres in height. No other land animal is taller.
Giraffes mostly eat leaves from acacia trees.
What is the title (laqab) of Hazrat Adam (AS)?
Hazrat Adam (AS) is called Abul Bashar, the father of mankind. He is also called Safiullah.
He was the first human and the first prophet in Islamic belief.
What is the title of Hazrat Isa (AS)?
Hazrat Isa (AS) is called Ruhullah (Spirit of Allah) and also Al-Masih. Khalilullah is for Ibrahim, Kaleemullah for Musa and Zabihullah for Ismail (AS).
He was born miraculously to Hazrat Maryam (AS) without a father.
What is the title of Hazrat Jibrael (AS)?
Hazrat Jibrael (AS) is called Ruh ul Amin (the Trustworthy Spirit) in the Quran, and also Ruh ul Quds.
He brought revelation to all prophets, including the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
What is the length of the Line of Control (LoC) between Pakistan and India in Kashmir in kilometres, as most commonly given?
The Line of Control was set after the 1971 war and the Simla Agreement of 1972. It is most commonly given as about 740 km.
Sources differ, with some giving up to 776 km.
How many bones are there in the adult human body?
An adult skeleton has 206 bones. A newborn has about 300 which fuse as the child grows.
The femur is the longest bone of the body.
How many landlocked countries are there in the world?
Counting internationally recognised sovereign states with no sea coastline gives 44 landlocked countries.
Counts differ slightly between sources (up to 49) when partially recognised states such as Kosovo are included.
What is the upper house of the Parliament of Pakistan called?
Pakistan's Parliament has two houses, and the upper house is the Senate.
The lower house is the National Assembly.
What is the rate of ushr on crops grown with artificial irrigation (tube wells, canals bought or built at cost)?
Ushr is 10 percent on rain-fed land and half of that, 5 percent, where artificial irrigation involves cost.
Zakat on gold, silver and cash is 2.5 percent.
What is the rate of zakat on gold and silver (above nisab)?
Zakat on gold, silver and cash savings above nisab is one-fortieth, which is 2.5 percent.
Nisab for gold is about 7.5 tola (87.48 grams) and for silver 52.5 tola.
Which is the world's most populous country today?
India overtook China in 2023 to become the most populous country, according to the United Nations.
Before 2023 China was the most populous country.
What is the Yellow River of China also called?
The Yellow River is known in Chinese as the Huang He.
The Yangtze is the longest river in China and Asia.
Uhud is a mountain just north of Madinah where the Battle of Uhud was fought in 3 AH.
The Prophet (PBUH) said that Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it.
Youm-ul-Furqan is the name given to the day of which battle?
The Battle of Badr, fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, is called Youm-ul-Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.
Badr was the first major battle between the Muslims and the Quraish.
Which part of speech is the word 'ouch'?
'Ouch' expresses sudden pain or emotion, which is the job of an interjection.
What technique of defence was used in the Ghazwa Khandaq (Ahzab)?
Muslims dug a trench around the open northern side of Madinah to stop the Quraish cavalry.
The idea was suggested by Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA) in 5 AH.
'The' points to a specific noun, so it is the definite article.
What type of star is the Sun?
The Sun is a G2V main-sequence star, usually called a yellow dwarf.
In about five billion years it will become a red giant.
For what is Hakeem Luqman best known?
Luqman was a sage whose wisdom and advice to his son are praised in the Quran.
Surah Luqman (Surah 31) is named after him.
Regional Cooperation for Development among Pakistan, Iran and Turkey
Regional Council for Defence of Asia
Regional Cooperation for Defence among Muslim states
RCD stood for Regional Cooperation for Development, an economic grouping of Pakistan, Iran and Turkey.
It was replaced by the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.
For what is Sher Shah Suri best known?
Grand Trade Road and administrative reforms
Sher Shah Suri (1540-45) rebuilt the Grand Trade Road, introduced the silver rupee and reformed revenue administration.
He defeated the Mughal emperor Humayun at Chausa and Kannauj.
What was the Bay of Pigs invasion of 1961?
A failed US-backed invasion of Cuba
A US naval battle with Japan
In April 1961 Cuban exiles trained by the CIA landed at the Bay of Pigs and were defeated by Fidel Castro's forces.
It was followed in 1962 by the Cuban Missile Crisis.
A 1942 British mission offering India post-war dominion status
A 1946 plan for a united India
Sir Stafford Cripps came to India in March 1942 with proposals to win Indian support in World War II; both Congress and the Muslim League rejected them.
The Cabinet Mission of 1946 is a different mission.
Which is considered the first book of Hadith compiled?
Imam Malik compiled the Muwatta in Madinah in the 8th century, and it is generally taken as the first book of Hadith.
Some sources mention earlier small collections such as Sahifa Hammam ibn Munabbih.
Which international organization was the predecessor of the United Nations (UNO)?
The League of Nations, founded in 1920 after World War I, failed to prevent World War II and was replaced by the UN in 1945.
The League of Nations was headquartered in Geneva.
In which period did Hazrat Umar (RA) hold the caliphate?
Hazrat Umar (RA) became caliph after Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) in 634 CE and was martyred in 644 CE, ruling about ten and a half years.
His caliphate corresponds to roughly 13 to 23 AH.
What was the Simla Conference of 1945?
A meeting of Wavell with Indian leaders on self-government that failed
The signing of the Pakistan-India peace agreement
The announcement of the Partition Plan
The first session of the Constituent Assembly

The Viceroy Lord Wavell called Indian leaders to Simla in June-July 1945 to discuss an Executive Council. It failed because Congress and the Muslim League could not agree on who nominates Muslim members.
The Wavell Plan was rejected as the Muslim League insisted on being the sole representative of Muslims.
What was the so-called Pig War between the United States and Britain over?
The Pig War of 1859 was a border dispute over San Juan Island; it began after an American farmer shot a British-owned pig. The only casualty was the pig.
The dispute was settled by arbitration in 1872 in favour of the United States.
According to the Hadith, what will a person be asked about first on the Day of Judgement regarding the rights of Allah?
The Prophet (PBUH) said that the first thing a servant will be called to account for on the Day of Judgement is prayer (Salah).
Regarding rights between people, the first matter judged will be bloodshed.
When an ant stings, which acid is injected into the body?
Ant venom contains formic acid, which causes the burning pain of the sting.
Formic acid gets its name from the Latin word formica meaning ant.
When did the COVID-19 (coronavirus) pandemic begin?
The first cases were reported in Wuhan, China, in December 2019.
The WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic on 11 March 2020.
In which year did East Pakistan separate from Pakistan to become Bangladesh?
East Pakistan broke away after the 1971 war, and the Dhaka surrender took place on 16 December 1971.
The Hamoodur Rehman Commission investigated the causes of the 1971 debacle.
In which year of the Hijri calendar did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) perform Umrat-ul-Qaza?
After the Treaty of Hudaibiya the Muslims performed the Umrah they were stopped from in 6 AH. They did it the next year, in 7 AH.
It is called Umrat-ul-Qaza because it made up for the Umrah missed in 6 AH.
In which year of prophethood did Hazrat Umar (RA) embrace Islam, according to most Pakistani textbooks?
Hazrat Umar (RA) accepted Islam in the 6th year of prophethood, after the Prophet's prayer that Allah strengthen Islam through one of the two Umars.
Sources differ slightly, some placing it in the 5th year.
When did India first present the Kashmir issue to the United Nations?
India took the Kashmir dispute to the UN Security Council on 1 January 1948 under Article 35 of the UN Charter.
The UNCIP resolutions of 1948-49 called for a plebiscite in Kashmir.
What was the legislature setup under the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
The 1956 Constitution created a single-house (unicameral) National Assembly with equal representation (parity) for East and West Pakistan.
The 1956 Constitution was abrogated by Ayub Khan's martial law in October 1958.
In which year did India take the Kashmir issue to the UN Security Council?

India lodged its complaint under Article 35 of the UN Charter on 1 January 1948, after tribal and Pakistani forces entered Kashmir. The Security Council then set up the UN Commission for India and Pakistan (UNCIP).
The UN-brokered ceasefire in Kashmir came into effect on 1 January 1949.
In which year did the First World War end?
The armistice with Germany took effect on 11 November 1918, ending the fighting. The Treaty of Versailles followed in 1919.
The First World War began in 1914.
In which year did the Second World War end?
Germany surrendered in May 1945 and Japan surrendered in August and September 1945. The war therefore ended in 1945.
The United Nations was founded in the same year, 1945.
In which year did the Cabinet Mission visit India?
The British Cabinet Mission arrived in India in March 1946 and announced its plan in May 1946. It proposed a loose federation, which the Congress and the Muslim League accepted only briefly.
The Cabinet Mission consisted of Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander.
In which year was the Non-Cooperation Movement launched in India?
Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920, supported by the Khilafat leaders, against British rule. Indians boycotted British courts, schools and goods.
Gandhi suspended the movement in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.
Around which year did the Ottoman Sultanate begin under Osman I?
Osman I founded the Ottoman state in Anatolia around 1299. It lasted until the sultanate was abolished in 1922.
The Ottomans conquered Constantinople in 1453 under Sultan Muhammad II (Mehmed the Conqueror).
On which date is Kashmir Day (Kashmir Solidarity Day) observed in Pakistan?
Pakistan observes Kashmir Solidarity Day on 5 February every year to express support for the people of Indian-held Kashmir.
Kashmiris also observe 27 October as Black Day, the day Indian troops landed in Srinagar in 1947.
In which year did the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College, Aligarh, begin as a college?
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded a school in 1875, which was raised to college level as the MAO College in 1877. Lord Lytton laid its foundation stone in 1877.
The MAO College became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
In which Hijri year was Hajj made obligatory (according to the most commonly taught view)?
Most Pakistani textbooks teach that Hajj became obligatory in 9 AH. The Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Abu Bakr to lead the Hajj that year.
Sources differ, as some scholars give 6 AH or 10 AH; the Prophet (PBUH) performed his only Hajj, the Farewell Hajj, in 10 AH.
In which year was the state of Israel declared?
Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948, as the British Mandate over Palestine ended. The first Arab-Israeli war followed immediately.
The UN General Assembly adopted the Palestine partition plan in November 1947.
In which year was the National Bank of Pakistan (NBP) established?
The National Bank of Pakistan was established in November 1949 to help finance the agricultural sector, notably the jute and cotton crops. It later acted as an agent of the State Bank.
The State Bank of Pakistan began working earlier, on 1 July 1948.
In which Hijri year did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) deliver his Last (Farewell) Sermon?
The Prophet (PBUH) delivered the Last Sermon during the Farewell Hajj on 9 Dhul Hijjah, 10 AH (632 CE), at Arafat. He passed away in 11 AH.
The sermon was delivered at Mount Arafat in the valley of Uranah.
In which year did Choudhary Rahmat Ali write the pamphlet 'Now or Never'?
Choudhary Rahmat Ali and his Cambridge colleagues issued the pamphlet 'Now or Never' in January 1933. It first proposed the name Pakistan for a Muslim homeland.
Rahmat Ali is known as the person who coined the name Pakistan.
In which year was the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) established by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey?
The RCD was formally established in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey to promote economic cooperation. It replaced the earlier CENTO-linked arrangements in the economic field.
The RCD was succeeded by the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.
In which year was the Second Battle of Panipat fought between Akbar's army and Hemu?
The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556, when Akbar's general Bairam Khan defeated Hemu. It secured the Mughal throne for Akbar.
The First Battle of Panipat in 1526 was won by Babur against Ibrahim Lodhi.
On what date was the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan enforced?
The National Assembly passed the Constitution on 10 April 1973, and it was enforced on 14 August 1973. It was authenticated by President Fazal Elahi Chaudhry.
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was the Prime Minister when the Constitution was enacted.
In which year was the World Trade Organization (WTO) established?
The WTO came into being on 1 January 1995, replacing the GATT arrangement.
The WTO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.
At which place did Allama Iqbal deliver his famous Presidential Address of 1930 in which he presented the idea of a separate Muslim state?
Iqbal delivered the Presidential Address at the annual session of the All-India Muslim League held at Allahabad in December 1930.
The Lahore Resolution was passed ten years later, in March 1940.
In which region does the Yellow River (Huang He) of China originate?
The Yellow River rises in the Bayan Har Mountains in Qinghai province on the Tibetan Plateau and flows east to the Bohai Sea.
It is the second longest river in China after the Yangtze.
In which country is Angel Falls, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, located?
Angel Falls (Salto Angel) is in Canaima National Park in Bolivar state, Venezuela.
Lake Superior is the northernmost of the Great Lakes and lies between the USA and Canada in North America.
It is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area.
Where is the MAO College (founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan) located?
The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College was founded in 1875 at Aligarh by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
It later became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
In which city is the Margalla Hills National Park located?
The Margalla Hills form the northern backdrop of Islamabad, the capital of Pakistan.
Faisal Mosque lies at the foot of the Margalla Hills.
Which Indian Ocean water body is the Bay of Bengal part of?
The Bay of Bengal is the northeastern part of the Indian Ocean, bordered by India, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Sri Lanka.
It is the largest bay in the world.
Between which two countries does the Bay of Bothnia lie?
The Gulf or Bay of Bothnia is the northern arm of the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Finland.
It is the northernmost part of the Baltic Sea.
Between which countries does the Gulf (Bay) of Riga lie?
The Gulf of Riga is an inlet of the Baltic Sea bordered by Latvia and Estonia.
Its main port is Riga, the capital of Latvia.
In which country is Shark Bay, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, located?
Shark Bay is on the coast of Western Australia.
It was listed as a World Heritage Site in 1991.
In which region was the ancient Gandhara civilization centred?
Gandhara flourished in the Peshawar valley and Potohar region of northwest Pakistan, with Taxila and Peshawar as major centres.
Gandhara art is famous for Greco-Buddhist sculpture.
Where is the headquarters of SAARC located?
The SAARC Secretariat was established in Kathmandu, Nepal in 1987.
SAARC was founded in 1985 in Dhaka.
Where is the headquarters of the United Nations located?
The UN headquarters is on the east side of Manhattan in New York City, USA.
The UN also has major offices at Geneva, Vienna and Nairobi.
Where is the headquarters of OPEC located?
OPEC moved from Geneva to Vienna, Austria in 1965 and has been headquartered there since.
OPEC was founded in Baghdad in 1960.
In which city or area is Simly Dam located?
Simly Dam is on the Soan River in the Islamabad Capital Territory, about 30 km from the city.
It is a major source of drinking water for Islamabad.
Where is the shrine of Data Ganj Bakhsh (Hazrat Ali Hujwiri) located?
Data Ganj Bakhsh, the author of Kashf-ul-Mahjoob, is buried in Lahore near Bhati Gate. His shrine is one of the most visited in Pakistan.
His death anniversary (Urs) is held every year at the shrine in Lahore.
Where is the tomb of the Punjabi poet Waris Shah located?
Waris Shah, author of the epic Heer Ranjha, is buried at Jandiala Sher Khan in Sheikhupura district, where he died in 1798.
Waris Shah was born in Jandiala Sher Khan and wrote Heer in 1766.
Where is the Zhob River situated?
The Zhob River rises in Balochistan and flows through the Zhob district, joining the Gomal River.
The Gomal River later flows into the Indus River system through Dera Ismail Khan.
Where is the world's largest active volcano, Mauna Loa, located?
Mauna Loa is on the Big Island of Hawaii and is regarded as the largest active volcano on Earth by volume. It erupted in November 2022 for the first time since 1984.
Mount Etna in Italy is Europe's most active volcano.
The Yangtze and the Yellow River are the two longest rivers of which country?
Both the Yangtze and the Yellow River (Huang He) flow through China and empty into the sea on its east coast. The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.
The Yellow River is called the cradle of Chinese civilization.
Where was Benazir Bhutto assassinated in December 2007?
Benazir Bhutto was killed on 27 December 2007 after addressing an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi. She was attacked as she left the venue.
She had been Prime Minister of Pakistan twice, in 1988-90 and 1993-96.
In which city was Pakistan's first Prime Minister, Liaquat Ali Khan, assassinated in 1951?
Liaquat Ali Khan was shot on 16 October 1951 while addressing a public meeting at Company Bagh in Rawalpindi.
Company Bagh was later renamed Liaquat Bagh.
In which city was the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 signed?
The Tashkent Declaration was signed in Tashkent, then in the Soviet Union and now the capital of Uzbekistan.
Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri died in Tashkent the day after the signing.
Where was the atomic test of Pakistan conducted on 28 May 1998?
Pakistan carried out its first nuclear tests in the Ras Koh hills of Chagai district, Balochistan on 28 May 1998.
Where was the Battle of Khaibar fought?
Near Khaibar oasis north of Madinah, Arabia
The Battle of Khaibar was fought in 628-629 AD (7 AH) against the Jewish fortresses at the Khaibar oasis in Arabia. Hazrat Ali (RA) is famous for conquering the fort of Qamus.
The Khyber Pass in Pakistan is a different place with a similar name.
Where did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) receive the first revelation?
The first revelation (the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq) came in the Cave of Hira on Jabal al-Noor near Makkah.
The Prophet (PBUH) was about 40 years old at that time.
Which acid is found in milk?
Sour milk contains lactic acid, formed when bacteria ferment lactose. Fresh milk is only slightly acidic.
Citric acid is found in lemons and oranges.
Which military alliance was formed in 1955 by the Soviet bloc in response to NATO?
The Warsaw Pact was signed in 1955 by the USSR and its eastern European allies as a counter to NATO.
The Warsaw Pact was dissolved in 1991.
Which angel will blow the trumpet (Sur) on the Day of Judgement?
Hazrat Israfil (AS) is the angel appointed to blow the Sur to end the world and again to raise the dead.
Hazrat Azrail (AS) is the angel of death.
Which body regulates electronic media in Pakistan?
The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) regulates private television and radio channels.
Which city is known as the City of Saints (Madinat-ul-Auliya)?
Multan is called the City of Saints because of its many shrines of Sufi saints, such as Bahauddin Zakariya and Shah Rukn-e-Alam.
Multan is also known as the City of Mangoes.
Which commission, headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, drew the boundary line between Pakistan and India in 1947?
The Boundary Commission chaired by Sir Cyril Radcliffe demarcated the Punjab and Bengal borders, and the line is called the Radcliffe Line. The Radcliffe Award was announced on 17 August 1947.
The Radcliffe Award was announced after independence, on 17 August 1947.
Which companion of the Prophet (PBUH) addressed King Najashi of Abyssinia on behalf of the Muslim migrants?
Hazrat Jafar bin Abi Talib was the spokesman of the Muslims who migrated to Abyssinia. He recited verses of Surah Maryam before Najashi.
Najashi later accepted Islam, and the Prophet (PBUH) offered his funeral prayer in absentia.
In which country is the Wakhan Corridor situated?
The Wakhan Corridor is a strip of land in the north-east of Afghanistan in Badakhshan province.
It was created as a buffer between the British and Russian empires in the 19th century.
Which of the following are the Scandinavian countries?
The Scandinavian countries are Norway, Sweden and Denmark.
Finland and Iceland are usually counted with them as Nordic countries.
Which two countries share the border that mostly follows the 49th parallel north?
Much of the border between the contiguous United States and Canada runs along the 49th parallel north.
The 49th parallel was fixed by the Treaty of 1818 and the Oregon Treaty of 1846.
Which country was the first to recognise Pakistan after its creation in 1947, according to most Pakistani textbooks?
Most Pakistani textbooks state that Iran was the first country to recognise Pakistan. Iran also sent the first ambassador.
Sources differ, as some also credit Turkey, and Afghanistan opposed Pakistan's UN membership.
Which country supplied S-400 air defence missile systems to India?
India signed a deal in 2018 with Russia for S-400 Triumf air defence systems. Deliveries began in 2021.
The S-400 is a Russian long range surface to air missile system.
Which country hosted the third modern Olympic Games in 1904?
The third modern Olympics were held in St. Louis, Missouri, USA in 1904. The first was in Athens in 1896 and the second in Paris in 1900.
The 1904 Games were the first Olympics held outside Europe.
Which of the following was NOT a member of the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) formed in 1964?
The RCD was formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey. Afghanistan was never a member.
RCD was replaced by the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.
Which country is known as the Land of the Long White Cloud?
The Maori name Aotearoa is translated as Land of the Long White Cloud and refers to New Zealand.
Wellington is the capital of New Zealand.
Which country is the world's largest producer of chromite (chromium ore)?
According to USGS data, South Africa is by far the largest chromite producer, with about 22.9 million tonnes in 2024. Kazakhstan is second.
South Africa also holds the largest chromite reserves in the world.
Which two countries jointly developed the JF-17 Thunder fighter jet?
The JF-17 Thunder was jointly developed by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex (PAC) Kamra and China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.
Myanmar was the first foreign buyer of the JF-17.
Which cricket league is played in Pakistan?
The Pakistan Super League (PSL) is the professional Twenty20 league of Pakistan. It started in 2016.
Lahore Qalandars won the PSL in 2022 and 2023.
Which cricketer broke Shahid Afridi's record for the fastest century in One Day Internationals?
Afridi scored a century off 37 balls in 1996. Corey Anderson of New Zealand reached a hundred in 36 balls against West Indies in January 2014 and broke it.
AB de Villiers later took the record with a 31-ball century against West Indies in 2015.
Which international day does the United Nations observe on 24 June?
International Day of Women in Diplomacy
The UN General Assembly declared 24 June as the International Day of Women in Diplomacy in 2022. It promotes the participation of women in diplomacy.
World Refugee Day is on 20 June and International Widows Day is on 23 June.
Which famous musician was born in Salzburg, Austria?
Mozart was born in Salzburg on 27 January 1756. Beethoven was born in Bonn, Bach in Eisenach and Schubert in Vienna.
Mozart composed more than 600 works before his death in Vienna in 1791.
Which was the last Ghazwa in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) personally took part?
The Ghazwa of Tabuk in 9 AH was the last military expedition led personally by the Prophet (PBUH).
Tabuk is also called Ghazwa Usrah, the expedition of hardship.
Which authority regulates the oil and gas sector in Pakistan?
OGRA was established in 2002 to regulate the midstream and downstream oil and gas sector. NDMA handles disasters, WAPDA water and power, PEMRA electronic media.
OGRA also recommends the prices of petroleum products and natural gas.
Which is the coldest desert in the world?
The Antarctic Desert is the coldest and largest desert on Earth, with extremely low rainfall and temperatures far below freezing.
The Gobi is the best known cold desert of Asia, but it is much warmer than Antarctica.
The verb profit ends in a single t, and the stress is on the first syllable, so the consonant is not doubled: profited.
The same rule gives benefited and budgeted.
Which is the deepest ocean in the world?
The Pacific Ocean has the greatest average depth and contains the Mariana Trench, the deepest known point.
The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is about 11,000 metres deep.
Which was the first qiblah of the Muslims?
Bait ul Muqaddas (Masjid al-Aqsa) in Jerusalem
Muslims prayed towards Bait ul Muqaddas for about 16 to 17 months after the Hijrah. The qiblah was then changed to the Kaaba.
The change took place in 2 AH in the Masjid Qiblatain in Madinah.
Which is the highest capital city of the world?
La Paz, the seat of government of Bolivia, stands at about 3,640 metres above sea level, higher than any other capital.
Sucre is the constitutional capital of Bolivia, and Quito is the highest official capital.
Which is the highest highway of Pakistan?
The Karakoram Highway reaches about 4,693 metres at the Khunjerab Pass on the China border, the highest paved international road.
It links Hasan Abdal in Pakistan with Kashgar in China.
Which is the highest peak of Pakistan?
K2 (Mount Godwin-Austen) is 8,611 metres high, the highest peak in Pakistan and the second highest in the world.
Nanga Parbat at 8,126 metres is the second highest peak in Pakistan.
Which is the highest polo ground in Pakistan and the world?
The Shandur polo ground at Shandur Pass is about 3,700 metres high and is called the highest polo ground in the world.
A famous polo festival between Chitral and Gilgit-Baltistan is held at Shandur every year.
Which mountain is known as the Killer Mountain?
Nanga Parbat is called the Killer Mountain because many climbers died on it in early attempts.
Nanga Parbat means Naked Mountain and is the ninth highest mountain in the world.
Which is the largest country of Asia by population?
India overtook China in 2023 and is now the most populous country in both Asia and the world, with about 1.45 billion people.
Earlier, China was the most populous country, which was the answer in 2021-22.
Which country is called the largest democracy in the world?
India has the largest electorate and the largest population of any democracy. It is called the world's largest democracy.
India overtook China as the world's most populous country in 2023.
Which is the largest ethnic group of Afghanistan?
Pashtuns form the largest ethnic group of Afghanistan, roughly 40 percent of the population.
Tajiks are the second largest ethnic group of Afghanistan.
Which is the largest lake of East Africa?
Lake Victoria covers about 68,800 square kilometres and is the largest lake in Africa by area.
Lake Victoria is the source of the White Nile.
Which is the largest landlocked country in the world?
Kazakhstan has an area of about 2.72 million square kilometres and no coastline on an ocean. It is the largest landlocked country.
Mongolia is the second largest landlocked country.
Which is the largest man-made lake (reservoir) of Pakistan?
Tarbela Reservoir on the Indus has the largest surface area of any reservoir in Pakistan, about 250 square kilometres.
Tarbela Dam is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.
Which is the largest salt mine of Pakistan?
The Khewra Salt Mine in Jhelum district is the largest salt mine in Pakistan and one of the largest in the world.
Khewra salt is mostly rock salt, known as Himalayan pink salt.
Which is the longest river in the world according to most textbooks?
Most textbooks give the Nile as the longest river, at about 6,650 kilometres.
Some sources measure the Amazon as longer, so sources differ.
Which is the national news agency of Pakistan?
Associated Press of Pakistan (APP) is the state-run national news agency of Pakistan.
APP was nationalised in 1961 and has its headquarters in Islamabad.
Which is the wettest place in the world (the one most commonly named in textbooks)?
Mawsynram in Meghalaya, India, receives the highest average annual rainfall of any inhabited place, over 11,000 mm.
Nearby Cherrapunji was once named the wettest place, so sources differ.
In the Islamic calendar, which is the year called Aam-ul-Huzn (Year of Grief)?
In the 10th year of Prophethood, both Hazrat Khadijah (RA) and Abu Talib passed away, so it is called the Year of Grief.
Soon after, the Prophet (PBUH) travelled to Taif.
Which lines are called parallel lines?
Lines that intersect at a right angle
Lines in the same plane that never meet
Lines that meet at one point
Parallel lines lie in the same plane and stay the same distance apart, so they never meet however far they are extended.
A line that cuts two parallel lines is called a transversal.
Which mountain (peak) lies on the border between China and Pakistan?
K2 in the Karakoram lies on the China-Pakistan border, between Gilgit-Baltistan and Xinjiang.
At 8,611 m, K2 is the second highest mountain in the world.
Which mountain range lies between France and Italy?
The Alps, including Mont Blanc, mark part of the border between France and Italy.
Mont Blanc, at about 4,800 m, is the highest peak in the Alps.
Which mountain range separates Spain and France?
The Pyrenees run between France and Spain.
Andorra lies within the Pyrenees between France and Spain.
Which obligatory act is mentioned in the Quran most often together with Zakat?
The Quran repeatedly pairs the command to establish Salah with the command to pay Zakat.
The phrase 'Aqeemus-Salah wa Atuz-Zakah' occurs many times in the Quran.
Which ocean lies along the coast of Pakistan?
Pakistan's coastline of about 1,046 km is on the Arabian Sea, which is part of the Indian Ocean.
Karachi, Gwadar and Port Qasim are Pakistan's main ports.
Which of the following does not mean big: huge, massive, scrap?
Huge and massive both mean very large, while scrap means a small piece or leftover.
Scrap can also mean to discard something as useless.
Which ancient civilization flourished in Taxila?
Taxila was a major city of the Gandhara civilization and a famed centre of learning.
Taxila was made a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.
Which Pakistani army operation was launched nationwide in February 2017?
Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad was announced on 22 February 2017 after a wave of terror attacks across Pakistan.
Zarb-e-Azb began in June 2014 and Rah-e-Rast in 2009.
Which principal organ of the United Nations is no longer active (suspended operations)?
The Trusteeship Council suspended operations in 1994 after Palau, the last trust territory, became independent.
The other five principal organs are still functioning.
Which organization oversees international civil aviation?
The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), a UN agency, sets global standards for civil aviation.
ICAO is headquartered in Montreal, Canada.
Which Pakistani batter holds the highest individual score in Test cricket for Pakistan?
Hanif Mohammad scored 337 against West Indies at Bridgetown in 1958, still Pakistan's highest Test score.
Younis Khan's 313 against Sri Lanka in 2009 is the second highest by a Pakistani.
Which Pakistani scientist won the Nobel Prize in 1979?
Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics with Sheldon Glashow and Steven Weinberg for the unified electroweak theory.
Abdus Salam is the only Pakistani Nobel laureate in Physics; Malala Yousafzai won the Peace Prize in 2014.
Which planet is named after the Roman equivalent of the Greek god Zeus?
Jupiter is the Roman name of the king of the gods, whom the Greeks called Zeus.
Jupiter is the largest planet of the solar system.
Which planet comes closest to the Earth?
Venus approaches Earth to about 38 million km, closer than any other planet.
Some recent calculations show Mercury is nearest on average over time, but textbooks give Venus.
Which prophet built the ark (boat) at the command of Allah before the great flood?
Allah commanded Hazrat Nuh (AS) to build the ark to save the believers from the flood.
Surah Nuh of the Quran is named after this prophet.
Which Sahabi did the Prophet (PBUH) call the door of knowledge?
A hadith reports the Prophet (PBUH) saying: I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its door.
Hazrat Ali (RA) was the fourth Rightly Guided Caliph.
Which preposition completes the sentence: 'He reminded me ___ my History teacher'?
The verb 'remind' takes 'of' when something resembles or recalls another person or thing.
'Remind someone about' is used for a task or duty, for example remind me about the meeting.
Which preposition is used with 'laugh' when making fun of someone: 'laughed ___ someone'?
To laugh at someone means to mock them; 'laugh at' is the correct phrasal form.
'Laugh with someone' means to share the joke in a friendly way.
Which province of Pakistan has the largest provincial assembly?
The Provincial Assembly of the Punjab has 371 seats, more than the other three assemblies.
Sindh has 168 seats, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 145 and Balochistan 65.
Which surah of the Holy Quran is named after the ant?
Surah Al-Naml (the Ant), the 27th surah, takes its name from the story of the ant that warned its colony about Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) and his army.
Al-Nahl is the surah named after the bee and Al-Ankabut the one named after the spider.
Which two oceans does the Panama Canal connect?
The Panama Canal cuts across the Isthmus of Panama and joins the Atlantic Ocean (via the Caribbean Sea) with the Pacific Ocean. This saves ships the long voyage around South America.
The Panama Canal was opened in 1914.
Which two surahs of the Holy Quran are together called Muawwazatain?
Surah Al-Falaq (113) and Surah Al-Nas (114) both begin with a request to seek refuge (ta'awwuz) with Allah. That is why the pair is called Muawwazatain.
These are the last two surahs of the Quran and are commonly recited for protection.
Which was the first Muslim country to become a nuclear power?
Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998 and became the first Muslim country with nuclear weapons.
Pakistan became the seventh nuclear-armed country in the world, after India's tests earlier in May 1998.
Which defensive technique was used by the Muslims in the Battle of Khandaq (Trench) in 5 AH?
Building a wall of stones around Makkah
Fighting from the hills of Uhud
A night surprise attack on the enemy camp
On the advice of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA), the Muslims dug a long trench across the open side of Madinah. The Quraish and their allies could not cross it and had to retreat.
The battle is also called the Battle of Ahzab (the Confederates).
Who are called Ahl ul Bait?
All the companions of the Prophet (PBUH)
The family members of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)
Ahl ul Bait means the people of the house, that is the family of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), including his wives, daughter Fatimah (RA), Hazrat Ali (RA) and their children.
The Quran addresses the Ahl ul Bait in Surah Al-Ahzab, verse 33.
Which of the following was a daughter of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
The four daughters of the Prophet (PBUH) were Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah (RA). Aisha, Hafsa and Khadija (RA) were his wives.
All the daughters were born to Hazrat Khadija (RA).
Who is called the Hawari (special helper) of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
On the day of Khandaq the Prophet (PBUH) said that every prophet has a Hawari and his Hawari is Zubair (RA), as recorded in Sahih Bukhari.
The word Hawari is also used in the Quran for the disciples of Prophet Isa (AS).
Who broke Shahid Afridi's record for the most sixes in One Day Internationals?
Rohit Sharma hit his 352nd ODI six on 30 November 2025 against South Africa at Ranchi, passing Afridi's 351.
Chris Gayle, with 331 sixes, is third on the all-time ODI list.
Who compiled the hadith collection Sahih Muslim?
Sahih Muslim was compiled by Imam Muslim bin al-Hajjaj al-Naysaburi (died 261 AH).
Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim together are known as the Sahihain.
Who conducts and governs the modern Olympic Games?
The International Olympic Committee, founded in 1894 by Pierre de Coubertin, organises the modern Olympic Games.
The IOC is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.
Who elects the members of the Senate of Pakistan from the provinces?
The members of the Provincial Assemblies
Senators from each province are elected indirectly by the members of that provincial Assembly through the single transferable vote system.
The Senate is a permanent house with half of its members retiring every three years.
Who first raised the Kashmir issue in the United Nations Security Council, and when?
India lodged a complaint under Article 35 of the UN Charter on 1 January 1948, and the Security Council took up the matter.
Pakistan replied with its own complaint on 15 January 1948.
Who founded the technology company Microsoft?
Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft on 4 April 1975.
Microsoft began in Albuquerque, New Mexico, before moving to Washington State.
Who gave the first Azan in Islam?
Hazrat Bilal bin Rabah (RA) was appointed by the Prophet (PBUH) as the first muezzin and called the first Azan in Madinah.
Hazrat Abdullah bin Zaid (RA) saw the words of the Azan in a dream, and the Prophet (PBUH) taught them to Bilal (RA).
Who introduced the fictional spy character James Bond?
Ian Fleming created James Bond in the novel Casino Royale, published in 1953.
Fleming had worked in British naval intelligence during the Second World War.
Who is known as the father of the hydrogen bomb?
Edward Teller, working with Stanislaw Ulam, is credited with the design of the hydrogen bomb, first tested in 1952.
Robert Oppenheimer is known as the father of the atomic bomb; sources sometimes also credit Ulam alongside Teller.
The uncle of the Prophet (PBUH) who opposed him
The leader of the Banu Quraiza
Abu Lahab (Abdul Uzza bin Abdul Muttalib) was an uncle of the Prophet (PBUH) who strongly opposed Islam.
Surah Al-Lahab (Al-Masad) of the Quran was revealed about him.
Who was Baba Farid (Hazrat Fariduddin Ganj Shakar)?
A Sufi saint of the Chishti order
A poet of the Sikh court
Baba Farid (1179-1266) was a famous Punjabi Sufi saint and poet of the Chishti order, and a disciple of Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki.
His shrine is in Pakpattan, and his verses are included in the Guru Granth Sahib.
Who is Pakistan's highest run scorer in One Day Internationals?
Inzamam-ul-Haq scored 11,701 runs in ODIs, the most for Pakistan.
Mohammad Yousuf (9,554) and Saeed Anwar (8,824) follow him on the list.
Which angel is responsible for rain and sustenance according to Islamic belief?
Hazrat Mikaeel (AS) is the angel in charge of rain and provision.
Hazrat Israfeel (AS) will blow the Trumpet on the Day of Judgement.
Who wrote Humayun Nama, an account of the reign of Emperor Humayun?
Gulbadan Begum, a daughter of Babur and aunt of Akbar, wrote Humayun Nama.
Akbar had asked her to record her memories for Abul Fazl's Akbarnama.
Who was the half-brother of Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was a son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) from Hazrat Sarah, while Hazrat Ismail (AS) was his son from Hazrat Hajra, so they were half-brothers.
Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
