Who is the Chief Minister of Balochistan (as of 2026)?
Mir Sarfraz Bugti took office as Chief Minister of Balochistan in March 2024 and was still serving in mid-2026.
His predecessors included Abdul Quddus Bizenjo (2021-2023) and Jam Kamal Khan (2018-2021).
Who is the Chief of the Naval Staff of the Pakistan Navy?
Admiral Naveed Ashraf took over as Chief of the Naval Staff in October 2023 and is the serving chief in 2026.
His predecessors were Admiral Muhammad Zakaullah and, before him, Admiral Muhammad Amjad Khan Niazi.
Who is the Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
Sardar Ayaz Sadiq of the PML-N was elected Speaker on 1 March 2024 and is the current Speaker.
Asad Qaiser, the answer candidates gave in 2021-22, was Speaker from 2018 to 2022.
Who is the Defence Minister of Pakistan?
Khawaja Muhammad Asif of the PML-N is the Federal Minister for Defence in the current government.
Pervez Khattak, the answer candidates gave in 2021-22, was Defence Minister from 2018 to 2022.
Who is the Federal Minister for Interior of Pakistan?
Mohsin Naqvi is the Federal Interior Minister in the current government.
He is also the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board and president of the Asian Cricket Council.
Who is the Speaker of the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab?
Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan of the PML-N has been Speaker of the Punjab Assembly since February 2024.
He is a lawyer from Kasur and was earlier a Special Assistant to the Chief Minister.
Who is the son of Hazrat Hajira (A.S)?
Hazrat Hajira was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S) and the mother of Hazrat Ismail (A.S).
The well of Zamzam sprang up near the infant Ismail (A.S) in Makkah.
Who is known as the Traveler of Islam?
Ibn Battuta, a Moroccan scholar, traveled across much of the Muslim world and beyond for about 30 years and is called the Traveler of Islam.
His travel account is known as the Rihla.
Who is the writer of the book The Spirit of Islam?
The Spirit of Islam (1891) was written by Syed Ameer Ali.
Ameer Ali also wrote A Short History of the Saracens.
Who is the writer of the book Becoming?
Becoming (2018) is the memoir of Michelle Obama, former First Lady of the United States.
It became one of the best-selling memoirs of all time.
Who is the compiler of Tirmizi Sharif (Jami at-Tirmidhi)?
Jami at-Tirmidhi was compiled by Imam Muhammad bin Isa at-Tirmidhi.
It is one of the six major Hadith collections known as the Sihah Sitta.
Who served the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) for ten years in Madinah?
Hazrat Anas bin Malik (R.A) was given to the Prophet (S.A.W) as a boy by his mother and served him for about ten years.
Mark Zuckerberg launched Facebook in 2004 from Harvard University with his college roommates.
The company was renamed Meta Platforms in 2021.
Who is the father of Hazrat Usman (R.A)?
Hazrat Usman (R.A) was the son of Affan bin Abi al-As of the Banu Umayya clan of Quraysh.
Abu Quhafa was the father of Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A) and Khattab the father of Hazrat Umar (R.A).
Who is called the father of modern chemistry?
Antoine Lavoisier is commonly called the father of modern chemistry for his work on oxygen and the law of conservation of mass.
Some sources give this title to Robert Boyle, so sources differ.
Who is regarded as the founder of modern nursing?
Florence Nightingale established modern nursing practice and training after her work in the Crimean War.
She founded the Nightingale School of Nursing in London in 1860, and International Nurses Day is on her birthday, 12 May.
Who mediated between Pakistan and India in the Tashkent Agreement of January 1966?
The Soviet Prime Minister Alexei Kosygin hosted and mediated the talks at Tashkent. The agreement ended the 1965 war.
Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri signed it, and Shastri died in Tashkent the next day.
Who first proposed the name Pakistan?
Choudhry Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge student, coined the name Pakistan in his 1933 pamphlet Now or Never.
Allama Iqbal's 1930 Allahabad address proposed a separate Muslim state but did not use the name Pakistan.
Who refused to accept the Nobel Prize in Literature?
The French writer Jean-Paul Sartre declined the 1964 Nobel Prize in Literature, saying he refused official honours.
Boris Pasternak was forced by Soviet authorities to decline his 1958 Nobel Prize.
Under the Constitution of Pakistan, by whom are the senators of the provinces elected?
The members of the provincial assembly
Senators for each province are elected by the members of that provincial assembly by the single transferable vote.
The Senate has a Chairman who acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent.
Who signed the Simla Agreement of 1972 on behalf of Pakistan?
President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto signed the Simla Agreement with the Indian Prime Minister in July 1972.
The agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 after the 1971 war.
Who started the Non-Cooperation Movement in India in 1920?
Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920, supported by the Khilafat Movement.
It was called off in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.
Who acts as the President of Pakistan when the President is absent or unable to perform the functions of office?
The Speaker of the National Assembly
Under Article 49 of the Constitution, the Chairman of the Senate acts as President. If there is no Chairman, the Speaker of the National Assembly does so.
Muhammad Mian Soomro and Wasim Sajjad are among Senate Chairmen who have acted as President.
Who were the Banu Nadir (Banu Nuzair) in the history of Madina?
A branch of the Aws tribe
Banu Nadir was a Jewish tribe living near Madina. They were exiled in 4 AH after plotting against the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
The other Jewish tribes of Madina were Banu Qainuqa and Banu Quraiza.
Who became the Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan after Yahya Khan in December 1971?
After the fall of Dhaka, Yahya Khan handed power to Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who became President and the first civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator.
Martial law was lifted when the 1973 Constitution came into force.
Who was the husband of Hazrat Ayesha (RA)?
Hazrat Ayesha, daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr, was married to the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
She is known as Umm ul Momineen and narrated over two thousand hadith.
Who was the second Prime Minister of Pakistan?
Liaqat Ali Khan was the first Prime Minister. After his assassination in 1951, Khawaja Nazimuddin became the second.
Nazimuddin had been Governor-General before becoming Prime Minister.
Who was the second President of Pakistan?
Iskander Mirza was the first President under the 1956 Constitution. Ayub Khan removed him in 1958 and became the second.
Counts differ if the Governor-General office is included, but textbooks list Ayub Khan second.
Who was the Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army during the 1965 war with India?
General Muhammad Musa Khan was Commander-in-Chief from 1958 to 1966 and led the army in the 1965 war.
Yahya Khan succeeded him as Commander-in-Chief in 1966.
Who was the closest friend of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) was the Prophet's closest friend and the first man outside his family circle to accept Islam. He is called Siddique and Yar-e-Ghar (companion of the cave).
Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the first caliph of Islam and ruled from 11 AH to 13 AH.
Who was the commander of the Quraysh army in the Battle of Uhud?
Abu Sufyan bin Harb led the Makkan army of about 3,000 in 3 AH, because Abu Jahl had been killed at Badr. Khalid bin Walid commanded the cavalry wing.
Abu Sufyan later accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.
Who was the first Ameer-ul-Momineen (Commander of the Faithful) in Islamic history?
Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was called Khalifa-tu-Rasul Allah, while Hazrat Umar (RA) was the first to be addressed as Ameer-ul-Momineen. Most Islamic history books record this.
The title was adopted by later caliphs such as Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali (RA).
Who was the first caliph of Islam?
After the Prophet (PBUH) passed away in 11 AH, the Muslims chose Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) as their first caliph at Saqifa Bani Saida.
The four Rashidun caliphs ruled in the order Abu Bakr, Umar, Usman and Ali (RA).
Who was the first Pakistani to win a Nobel Prize?
Dr Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg, for the electroweak theory. He was the first Pakistani and the first Muslim Nobel laureate in science.
Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 and is the youngest Nobel laureate.
Who was the first President of Pakistan?
Under the 1956 Constitution, Iskander Mirza became the first President of Pakistan on 23 March 1956. Before this, the head of state was the Governor General.
Quaid-e-Azam and Ghulam Muhammad had served as Governor General, not as President.
Who was the first Pakistani woman to climb K2?
Samina Baig reached the summit of K2 on 22 July 2022, a few hours before Naila Kiani. She was the first Pakistani woman to do so.
Samina Baig had earlier climbed Mount Everest in 2013 and completed the Seven Summits in 2014.
Who was the first woman to travel to space?
Valentina Tereshkova of the Soviet Union flew aboard Vostok 6 in June 1963. She orbited the Earth 48 times.
Sally Ride became the first American woman in space in 1983.
Who was the first woman officer of the Pakistan Army to be promoted to the rank of Lieutenant General (three-star)?

Lt Gen Nigar Johar of the Army Medical Corps was promoted in June 2020 and became the first woman in the Pakistan Army to reach three-star rank. She was also appointed the first female Surgeon General of the Pakistan Army.
She is from Swabi in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
Who was the guarantor and third party that brokered the Indus Waters Treaty between India and Pakistan?
The World Bank mediated the long negotiations and signed the treaty as a party for certain provisions. The treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960.
Some sources describe the World Bank's role as a broker rather than a strict guarantor.
Who was the head of state of Pakistan in 1960?
Ayub Khan took power in the October 1958 coup and was President of Pakistan in 1960. He remained in office until March 1969.
Iskander Mirza, the first President, was removed by Ayub Khan in October 1958.
Who was the false prophet and enemy leader fought by the Muslims in the Battle of Yamama?

The Battle of Yamama in 12 AH was fought against the false claimant to prophethood Musaylima Kazzab and his tribe Banu Hanifa. The Muslim commander was Hazrat Khalid bin Walid (RA), and Musaylima was killed.
Many Huffaz of the Quran were martyred at Yamama, which led to the compilation of the Quran.
Who led the Simla Deputation of 1906 that presented Muslim demands to the Viceroy Lord Minto?
The Simla Deputation of 1 October 1906 was led by Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah, Agha Khan III. It asked for separate electorates for Muslims.
The All India Muslim League was founded a few months later in Dhaka in December 1906.
Who signed the Indus Waters Treaty on behalf of Pakistan in 1960?
President Ayub Khan signed the treaty for Pakistan in Karachi on 19 September 1960. Jawaharlal Nehru signed it for India.
W. A. B. Iliff signed for the World Bank.
Who was the second martial law administrator of Pakistan?
Ayub Khan imposed the first martial law in October 1958. General Yahya Khan imposed the second in March 1969 when Ayub resigned.
General Zia-ul-Haq imposed the third martial law in July 1977.
Why is Hazrat Usman (RA) called Zun-Noorain?
He married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (SAW)
He had two lights on his sword
He was the leader of two armies
He migrated to two countries only
Zun-Noorain means Possessor of Two Lights. He married Ruqayyah (RA) and later Umm Kulthum (RA), both daughters of the Prophet (SAW).
Hazrat Usman (RA) was the third Rightly Guided Caliph and also migrated to Abyssinia with Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA).
Banu Nadir was one of the main Jewish tribes living near Madinah. They were exiled after they broke their agreement with the Muslims.
The other Jewish tribes of Madinah were Banu Qaynuqa and Banu Qurayza.
Which of the following was an uncle of the Holy Prophet (SAW)?
Hazrat Hamza (RA) was a paternal uncle of the Holy Prophet (SAW). Hazrat Ali (RA) was his cousin, while Abu Bakr and Umar were companions.
His other uncles included Abu Talib, Hazrat Abbas (RA) and Abu Lahab.
Who wrote Hayat-e-Javed, the biography of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan?
Hayat-e-Javed, a biography of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, was written by Khawaja Altaf Hussain Hali in 1901.
Hali also wrote the Musaddas, and Dr Javed Iqbal wrote the Iqbal biography Zinda Rood.
Kashf-ul-Mahjoob is the oldest Persian book on Sufism and was written by Hazrat Ali Hujwiri, known as Data Ganj Bakhsh.
Who compiled the hadith book Sunan Nasai?
Sunan Nasai was compiled by Imam Nasai, whose full name was Ahmad ibn Shuayb al-Nasai.
It is one of the six major hadith collections known as Sihah Sittah.
Becoming is the 2018 memoir of Michelle Obama, former First Lady of the United States.
It became one of the best selling memoirs in history.
Who compiled the hadith book Sunan Abu Dawood?
Sunan Abu Dawood was compiled by Imam Abu Dawood Sulayman ibn al-Ashath al-Sijistani.
It is one of the six major hadith collections and focuses on legal rulings.
Who wrote the pamphlet Now or Never (1933)?
Now or Never: Are We to Live or Perish Forever? was written by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.
In it he proposed the name Pakistan for a separate Muslim homeland.
Jami at-Tirmidhi was compiled by Imam Muhammad ibn Isa al-Tirmidhi.
It is one of the six major hadith collections and grades each hadith.
Which of these countries has only a maritime border with Pakistan and no land border?
Pakistan has land borders with Afghanistan, China, India and Iran. Oman has no land border with Pakistan but shares a sea boundary in the Arabian Sea.
The Pakistan-Oman maritime boundary agreement came into force in 2000.
With which Indian prime minister did Pakistan sign the Lahore Declaration in 1999?
The Lahore Declaration of February 1999 was signed by Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
Soon after, the Kargil conflict of 1999 damaged the peace process.
With whom is the theory of relativity associated?
The theory of relativity was developed by Albert Einstein.
He published special relativity in 1905 and general relativity in 1915.
With the help of which country was the KANUPP-1 nuclear power plant at Karachi constructed?
KANUPP-1 is a CANDU heavy water reactor supplied by Canada and started operating in 1972.
Pakistan's later plants at Chashma were built with Chinese help.
Yaum-ul-Furqan is the name of the day of which event?
The Quran calls the day of the Battle of Badr Yaum-ul-Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.
The Battle of Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan, 2 AH.
Y = mx + c is the formula of what?
It is the slope-intercept form of the equation of a straight line, where m is the slope and c is the y-intercept.
The line crosses the y-axis at the point (0, c).
1 degree is equal to how many seconds (of arc)?
1 degree = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds, so 1 degree = 60 x 60 = 3600 seconds.
A full circle is 360 degrees, which equals 1,296,000 seconds of arc.
15 is divisible by which prime numbers?
15 = 3 x 5, and both 3 and 5 are prime numbers.
The number 1 is not a prime number because it has only one divisor.
In 8/7 the numerator 8 is greater than the denominator 7, so it is an improper fraction.
8/7 can be written as the mixed fraction 1 and 1/7.
A boy bought a book for Rs 500 and sold it for Rs 700. What is his profit percentage?
Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price.
Ali is 3 years old and his sister is 4 times his age. When Ali is 8 years old, what will his sister's age be?
Sister's age now = 4 x 3 = 12 years, so she is 9 years older. When Ali is 8 she will be 8 + 9 = 17 years.
Solve age questions by finding the fixed difference first.
Ali is 4 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will his sister's age be when Ali is 11?
Sister's age now = 3 x 4 = 12 years, so she is 8 years older. When Ali is 11 she will be 11 + 8 = 19 years.
The age difference stays constant, here always 8 years.
Ali is 4 years old and Sara is 3 times Ali's age. What will Sara's age be when Ali is 12?
Sara is 3 x 4 = 12 years old now, so she is 8 years older. When Ali is 12 she will be 12 + 8 = 20 years.
Both ages increase by the same number of years.
Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. When Ali is 11 years old, what is his sister's age?
Sister's age now = 3 x 5 = 15 years, so she is 10 years older. When Ali is 11 she will be 11 + 10 = 21 years.
After 6 years both of them are 6 years older: 15 + 6 = 21.
A train travels 60 km in 20 minutes. What is its speed in km/h?
To change km per minute into km per hour, multiply by 60.
A train's speed is 100 km/h. How far does it cover in 1 minute (to two decimal places)?
100 km/h is about 27.8 metres per second.
A helicopter covers 320 km using 40 gallons of fuel. How many gallons are needed to cover 700 km?
Fuel per km = 40/320 = 1/8 gallon. For 700 km: 700/8 = 87.5 gallons.
Fuel used is directly proportional to the distance covered.
A helicopter covers 350 km using 80 gallons of fuel. How many gallons does it need for 700 km?
700 km is twice 350 km, so the fuel needed is twice as much: 2 x 80 = 160 gallons.
In direct proportion, doubling the distance doubles the fuel.
A jet covers 320 km using 50 gallons of fuel. How many gallons will it use to cover 700 km?
Fuel per km = 50/320 = 0.15625 gallon. For 700 km: 700 x 0.15625 = 109.375 gallons.
The same result comes from the proportion 50 x 700 / 320.
A man walks towards north, after some time turns right and then turns left. In which direction is he moving now?
Facing north, a right turn makes him face east. A left turn from east makes him face north again.
A right turn followed by a left turn cancels out.
If the letters of the word BEAUTY are arranged in alphabetical order, which letter will come last?
Alphabetical order of the letters is A, B, E, T, U, Y. The last letter is Y.
Y is the 25th letter of the English alphabet.
Ali and Hasan have 24 apples in total. Ali has 3 times as many apples as Hasan. How many apples does Hasan have?
Let Hasan have x apples, then Ali has 3x. So 4x = 24 and x = 6.
Ali is older than Kashif and Kashif is older than Haris. Who is the oldest and who is the youngest?
Ali is older than Kashif, who is older than Haris, so Ali is the oldest and Haris the youngest.
Such ordering questions are solved fastest by writing the names in a single line from largest to smallest.
Ali is taller than Osama and Osama is taller than Faheem. Who is the tallest of all?
Ali is taller than Osama, who is taller than Faheem, so Ali is the tallest.
Faheem is the shortest in this chain.
Ali is younger than Hassan and Akbar is younger than Ali. Who is the oldest and who is the youngest?
Hassan is older than Ali, who is older than Akbar, so Hassan is the oldest and Akbar the youngest.
Ali is in the middle, so he is neither the oldest nor the youngest.
Ali's sister is three times Ali's age. If Ali is 3 years old, how old will his sister be when Ali is 7 years old?
Sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old when Ali is 3. The age gap is 6 years, so when Ali is 7 she is 7 + 6 = 13.
The difference between two people's ages always stays the same.
Are the numbers 1, 3, 9, 11, 13 even or odd numbers?
Each of these numbers leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2, so they are odd numbers.
Two is the only even prime number.
Arrange these words alphabetically: beauty, leopard. Which comes first?
B comes before L in the alphabet, so beauty comes first and leopard second.
Dictionary order compares words letter by letter from the left.
Complete the alphabet pairs series: AZ, BY, CX, ?
The first letter moves forward (A, B, C, D) while the second moves backward (Z, Y, X, W). The next pair is DW.
Pairs of letters taken from opposite ends of the alphabet always sum to position 27.
Terms at odd places: 115, 170, 235 (adding 55, then 65). Terms at even places: 55, 65, 75 (adding 10 each time).
Series with two interleaved patterns should be split into alternate terms.
Each term is double the previous one, so 16 x 2 = 32.
This is a geometric progression with common ratio 2.
Cows are twice the number of horses and there are 9 goats. If there are 6 cows, how many animals are there in total?
Read carefully which quantity is the base of 'twice'.
The number 3 appears four times, more than any other value (2 and 5 appear twice).
The mode is the most frequent value in a data set.
Find the next term in the coding series: 3Z, 4X, 5U, ?
Numbers rise by 1 (3, 4, 5, 6). Letter positions are Z=26, X=24, U=21, falling by 2, 3, then 4, so next is 17 = Q.
Convert letters to their alphabet positions to see the pattern.
How do you find the midpoint of a line segment joining (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)?
Average the x values and the y values
The midpoint is ((x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2), the average of each coordinate.
The midpoint of a segment divides it into two equal parts.
How many minutes are there in 20 degrees (angle measure)?
One degree = 60 minutes of arc, so 20 x 60 = 1200 minutes.
One minute of arc equals 60 seconds of arc.
What is the maximum number of right angles a triangle can have?
Angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees, so two right angles (180) would leave nothing for the third angle. At most one right angle is possible.
A triangle with one right angle is called a right-angled triangle.
How many vowels are in the letters: DACBIJUHOLEWPSI?
The vowels are A, I, U, O, E, I, which makes 6.
The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.
If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 28th be?
The 28th is 27 days after the 1st. 27 = 3 weeks + 6 days, so Monday + 6 days = Sunday.
The 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th share the same weekday.

Numerically, log 25 to base 10 is about 1.398.
If 20 pens cost Rs 2000, how much will 40 pens cost?
One pen costs 2000 / 20 = Rs 100, so 40 pens cost 40 x 100 = Rs 4000.
Doubling the number of items doubles the cost at a fixed price.
Add 5 to both sides: 3x = 9, so x = 3.
In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the product of extremes equals the product of means (a x d = b x c).

From the 4th to the 12th is 8 days, and 8 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1. Moving 1 day(s) forward from Sunday gives Monday.
Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.
If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day is the 14th day of that month?
From the 1st to the 14th is 13 days, and 13 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6. Moving 6 day(s) forward from Friday gives Thursday.
Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.
A car travels at 90 km per hour. How much distance does it cover in 40 minutes?
40 minutes is 2/3 of an hour, so distance = 90 x 2/3 = 60 km.
Distance = speed x time, with time converted into hours.
If a helicopter needs 340 gallons of fuel to cover 500 km, how much fuel will it need to cover 700 km?
Fuel is proportional to distance: 340 x 700 / 500 = 476 gallons.
Consumption here is 0.68 gallons per km.
If A is a subset of B, then A union B is equal to which set?
Every element of A is already in B, so combining A and B gives just B.
In the same case, A intersection B equals A.
If log x = y (common logarithm, base 10), what is x?
By definition, log x = y with base 10 means x = 10^y.
Natural logarithm uses base e, so ln x = y gives x = e^y.
If U is the universal set and A is a subset of U, what is the set U - A called?
U - A contains all elements of the universal set that are not in A. This set is called the complement of A.
The complement of A is written A' or A^c, and A union A' equals U.
If (x - 1, y + 1) = (0, 0), what are the values of x and y?
Equal ordered pairs have equal components: x - 1 = 0 gives x = 1, and y + 1 = 0 gives y = -1.
Two ordered pairs are equal only when their first and second components are both equal.
If y = 2x + 2 and x = 2, what is the value of y?
The graph of y = 2x + 2 is a straight line with slope 2 and y-intercept 2.
In a class of 400 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of students present?
Candidates remembered 80%, which would mean 320 present.
In a class of 500 students, 240 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
The present percentage here is 48%, and present plus absent always makes 100%.
In a class of 500 boys, 340 are present. How many boys are absent?
Out of 1200 students, 560 are boys. What is the percentage of girls (to two decimal places)?
The boys make up 560 / 1200 x 100 = 46.67% of the students.
Into how many semicircles does a diameter divide a circle?
A diameter passes through the centre and cuts the circle into two equal halves, each called a semicircle.
A semicircle subtends an angle of 180 degrees at the centre.
Multiply the biggest and the smallest of the numbers 7, 4, 3, 6, 5, 2, then subtract the product from the sum of all the numbers. What is the result?
Biggest is 7 and smallest is 2, so the product is 14. The sum is 7+4+3+6+5+2 = 27, and 27 - 14 = 13.
The sum of the first n natural numbers is n(n+1)/2.
Odd one out: Islamabad, Lahore, Quetta, Rawalpindi.
Islamabad is the federal capital, Lahore is the capital of Punjab and Quetta is the capital of Balochistan. Rawalpindi is not a capital.
Rawalpindi is the headquarters of the Pakistan Army and neighbours Islamabad.
P = mc + q is what type of equation?
The variable c appears only to the power one, so the equation is of the form y = mx + c, a linear equation.
The graph of a linear equation is a straight line.
Point out the odd one out: Angle, Rectangle, Square, Hexagon.
Rectangle, square and hexagon are closed plane figures (polygons), while an angle is not a shape but a measure formed by two rays.
Rearrange the letters IAPRS to form a word. What does the word name?
The letters I, A, P, R, S rearranged give PARIS, the capital of France.
Paris stands on the River Seine.
Rearrange the letters RSPAI to get the name of a city.
The letters R, S, P, A, I rearrange to PARIS.
Paris is the capital of France, on the river Seine.
Sheep is to wool as cat is to what?
Wool is the covering that grows on a sheep, and fur is the covering that grows on a cat.
Wool is obtained by shearing sheep.
Speak is to hear as look is to what?
Speaking is matched by hearing, and looking is matched by seeing, the result received.
Hearing is the sense of the ear and seeing is the sense of the eye.
What is the approximate value of the square root of 3?
1.732 x 1.732 is about 3.0, so the square root of 3 is about 1.732.
The square root of 2 is about 1.414 and of 5 is about 2.236.
The cube of unity (1 cubed) is equal to what?
1 x 1 x 1 = 1, so the cube of unity is 1.
The three cube roots of unity are 1 and two complex numbers, each of which also cubes to 1.
The population of a village was 2000 in the year 2000. If it doubled every five years, what was its population in 1980?
From 1980 to 2000 is 20 years, which is 4 doublings. So the 1980 population is 2000 / 2 / 2 / 2 / 2 = 125.
Going back in time, a doubling quantity is halved each period.
In division, the remainder is always less than which number?
If the remainder were equal to or larger than the divisor, the divisor could be taken once more, so the remainder is always smaller than the divisor.
When the remainder is zero, the dividend is exactly divisible by the divisor.
Today is Sunday. What will be the day after tomorrow?
Tomorrow is Monday, so the day after tomorrow is Tuesday.
In Pakistan the working week traditionally runs Monday to Friday.
There are 24 students and 1/4 of them are male. What is the percentage of females?
Males are 1/4 = 25%, so females are 100 - 25 = 75% (18 of 24).
Total students in a class are 1500 and 1200 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
Present and absent percentages add up to 100%.
What are the two square roots of 64?
8 x 8 = 64 and (-8) x (-8) = 64, so the roots are +8 and -8.
Every positive number has two square roots, one positive and one negative.
To find 10% of a number, divide it by 10.
BODMAS: brackets, orders, division and multiplication, then addition and subtraction.
What is the value of 2 + 2 x 2?
BODMAS gives multiplication priority over addition.
Division is done before addition under BODMAS.
What is the value of 2 x 3 + 3 x 6?
Both multiplications are done before the addition.
30% of 20 is 3 times 10% of 20, which is 2.
What is the value of 3 + 3 x 3?
Without BODMAS, one would wrongly compute (3 + 3) x 3 = 18.
60% is the same as 3/5, and 3/5 of 80 is 48.
90% of a number is the number minus 10% of it, so 9 - 0.9 = 8.1.
What is a chord that passes through the centre of a circle called?
A chord through the centre is the longest chord of the circle and is called the diameter.
The diameter is twice the radius.
What is an angle greater than 90 degrees (and less than 180 degrees) called?
An angle between 90 and 180 degrees is obtuse.
An angle of exactly 180 degrees is a straight angle.
What is a matrix whose entries are all zero called?
A matrix with every element equal to zero is called a null (zero) matrix.
Adding a null matrix to any matrix of the same order leaves it unchanged.
What is the value of cos 90 degrees?
On the unit circle, the point at 90 degrees is (0, 1), and its x-coordinate, the cosine, is 0.
What is cos x multiplied by tan x equal to?
Since tan x = sin x / cos x, cos x times tan x = sin x.
Another identity: sin x divided by cos x equals tan x.
Dividing by 10 moves the decimal point one place to the left.
What is the value of tan 0 degrees?
tan 90 degrees is undefined because cos 90 = 0.
What is the 2nd letter of the English alphabet?
The alphabet runs A, B, C, so the second letter is B.
What is the conjugate of a real number?
The conjugate of a + bi is a - bi. For a real number b = 0, so the conjugate is the same number.
A complex number equals its own conjugate only when it is real.
What is the common difference in the series 4, 7, 10, 13?
Such a series is called an arithmetic progression.
What is the distance between the points (-2, 0) and (-2, -3)?
The x-coordinates are equal, so the distance is |0 - (-3)| = 3. By formula: sqrt(0 + 9) = 3.
Points with the same x-coordinate lie on a vertical line.
Which is the distance formula between points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2)?
The distance comes from the Pythagorean theorem applied to the horizontal and vertical differences.
The formula (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1) gives the slope, and the midpoint uses averages.
What is the HCF of 18 and 24?
18 = 2 x 3 x 3 and 24 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3. The common factors are 2 and 3, so HCF = 6.
Their LCM is 72, and HCF x LCM = 18 x 24 = 432.
Division comes first: 2/3. Then 2 + 2/3 = 6/3 + 2/3 = 8/3, which is 2 and 2/3.
In BODMAS, division is performed before addition.
Which word is a synonym of extension?
Extension means an act of making something longer or larger, which is expansion.
The antonym of extension is reduction or curtailment.
Which word is a synonym of severely?
Severely means in a very strict or intense manner, which is harshly.
The antonym of severely is mildly or leniently.
Where does the line y = 3 + 5y lie?
Parallel to the x-axis, so it is neither axis
Rearranging gives -4y = 3, so y = -3/4. This is a horizontal line parallel to the x-axis, not the axis itself.
The x-axis is the line y = 0 and the y-axis is the line x = 0.
What comes next in the series: 1 X 2 Y Y 3 Z Z ?
The numbers 1, 2, 3 are followed by X once, Y twice and Z three times. So one more Z completes 3 ZZZ.
The letters follow the alphabetical order X, Y, Z.
Which comes next in the series: A2, D5, F9, ?
Letters move +3, +2, +1 (A, D, F, G) and numbers add 3, 4, 5 (2, 5, 9, 14). So the next term is G14.
In such series, check the letters and numbers separately.
Which letter comes immediately before W in the English alphabet?
The alphabet runs ... U, V, W, X, so V comes just before W.
W is the 23rd letter of the alphabet.
Which letter comes next: A B C D E F G H ?
The letters are in alphabetical order, and the one after H is I.
I is the 9th letter of the alphabet.
In the series A1, C3, D4, G?, what number follows G?
Each number is the alphabet position of its letter: A=1, C=3, D=4, so G=7.
G is the 7th letter of the alphabet.
Which comes next in the series: A5, B10, C15, ?
Letters move forward one step (A, B, C, D) and numbers increase by 5 (5, 10, 15, 20). So the next is D20.
The number part is the table of 5.
Which of the letters A, H, I, W, M, O, T, U, Y look the same in a mirror (vertical mirror held beside the letter)?
Only A, H, I and O
Only H, I, O and W
Only M, T, U and Y
Every one of these letters is symmetric about a vertical line, so each looks the same when reflected.
Letters like B, C, D, E and K are symmetric only about a horizontal line.
The numbers at odd places (105, 160, 225) rise by 55, then 65, so the next rise is 75: 225 + 75 = 300. The other numbers (55, 65, 75) rise by 10 each time.
Such interleaved series are solved by separating the odd and even places.
Two series are mixed: 115, 170 rise by 55, then 65 more, so 170 + 65 = 235. The other series 55, 65 would continue with 75 afterwards.
Here the added amount is the same as the number that follows each term: 115+55=170, 170+65=235.
Each big number is the previous big number plus the small number after it: 115+55=170, 170+65=235, 235+75=310.
The odd places 115, 225, 335 rise by 110 each time. The even places 55, 65 rise by 10, so the next is 75.
The question asks for the next term, which falls in the even-place series.
The differences are 2, 4, 6, so the next difference is 8. Hence 14 + 8 = 22.
When differences themselves form an arithmetic series, the series is quadratic.
The differences are 3, 6, 12, doubling each time, so the next difference is 24. Hence 45 - 24 = 21.
Series with doubling differences are common in verbal reasoning tests.
Which one is a prime number: 12, 25, 30, 37?
12 and 30 are even, and 25 = 5 x 5. 37 has no divisor other than 1 and itself, so it is prime.
2 is the only even prime number.
Which one is different: A12, B13, D15, E19, C14?
Letter position plus 11 gives the number: A(1)=12, B(2)=13, C(3)=14, D(4)=15. For E(5) it should be 16, but it is 19.
The odd one out breaks the pattern shared by all the others.
A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind, so the units cancel and it is dimensionless. The others all have units.
Velocity is measured in m/s, density in kg/m3 and pressure in pascals.
Which one is different: Cricket, Football, Tennis, Baseball?
Cricket, tennis and baseball are played with a bat or racket, while football is played with the feet and no bat.
Football is the most widely played sport in the world.
Who is the President of Russia?
Vladimir Putin is the President of Russia, in office since 2012 after earlier terms from 2000 to 2008.
He was re-elected in March 2024 for a term of six years.
What is the capital of Nepal?
Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal. It lies in the Kathmandu Valley in the Himalayan region.
Mount Everest, the highest peak in the world, lies on the border of Nepal and China.
Who is the President of the United States in October 2026?
Donald Trump won the 2024 election and was sworn in as the 47th President on 20 January 2025.
Joe Biden was President from January 2021 to January 2025, which is the answer candidates gave in 2022; the USA has a President and no Prime Minister.
What is the capital of Lebanon?
Beirut is the capital and largest city of Lebanon.
Damascus is the capital of Syria.
In which year did the Minto-Morley Reforms (Indian Councils Act) come into effect?
The Indian Councils Act of 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, introduced separate electorates for Muslims. Lord Minto was Viceroy and Lord Morley was Secretary of State for India.
In which country did Pakistan open its first embassy?
Pakistan opened its first embassy in Iran, which was also among the first countries to recognise Pakistan in 1947.
Some sources differ on early diplomatic firsts, but Iran is the answer given in most Pakistani textbooks and tests.
Who is the current President of India?
Droupadi Murmu took oath as the 15th President of India on 25 July 2022.
Her predecessor Ram Nath Kovind, the answer given in 2022, served from 2017 to 2022.
Which one is different: Lahore, Peshawar, Quetta, Karachi, Rawalpindi?
Lahore, Peshawar, Quetta and Karachi are all provincial capitals. Rawalpindi is not a provincial capital, so it is the odd one out.
Islamabad, not Rawalpindi, is the federal capital of Pakistan.
Who wrote the book My Brother, about Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah?
Fatima Jinnah, sister of the Quaid-e-Azam, wrote My Brother, which was published after her death.
Fatima Jinnah is known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).
In which year did Fatima Jinnah die?
Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah died in Karachi on 9 July 1967 and was buried near the mausoleum of Quaid-e-Azam.
She is known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).
Who is the author of the book India of My Dreams?
India of My Dreams is a collection of the writings of Mahatma Gandhi on his vision for India, compiled by R. K. Prabhu.
Gandhi's autobiography is titled The Story of My Experiments with Truth.
What is the capital of the Philippines?
Manila is the capital of the Philippines.
Quezon City is the largest city of the country by population.
Who is the Prime Minister of Sri Lanka (as of October 2026)?
Harini Amarasuriya of the National People's Power became Prime Minister in September 2024 and was reappointed after the November 2024 election.
Earlier answers were Mahinda Rajapaksa (2019 to 2022) and Ranil Wickremesinghe (briefly in 2022).
On which date was the Liaquat-Nehru Pact signed?
The Liaquat-Nehru (Delhi) Pact was signed on 8 April 1950 by Liaquat Ali Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru to protect minorities in both countries.
It is also called the Delhi Pact.
Who is the Prime Minister of France as of October 2026?
Sebastien Lecornu was appointed Prime Minister in September 2025 and reappointed in October 2025, and was still in office in October 2026.
Elisabeth Borne (2022-2024), whom candidates wrote in 2022, was later followed by Attal, Barnier and Bayrou; Emmanuel Macron is the President, not the PM.
Who is the head of state of the United Kingdom?
The UK is a monarchy with no president, and King Charles III is the head of state.
Andy Burnham became Prime Minister in July 2026, and in 2022 candidates named Boris Johnson in this role.
Zabihullah (the one sacrificed for Allah) is the title of which prophet?
Hazrat Ismail (AS) is called Zabihullah because he was offered for sacrifice by his father Ibrahim (AS) in obedience to Allah.
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah and Hazrat Ismail (AS) is the ancestor of the Arab tribes.
Between which two countries was the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 signed?
The Tashkent Declaration was signed by Pakistan and India to end the 1965 war.
The Soviet Union under Premier Kosygin mediated, and Indian PM Shastri died in Tashkent right after signing.
Which region is called the Land of Prophets?
Palestine is called the Land of Prophets because many prophets, including Ibrahim, Dawud, Sulaiman, Isa and others, lived or preached there.
Jerusalem (Al-Quds) in Palestine holds Masjid al-Aqsa, the first qibla of Muslims.
What percentage of the total area of Pakistan is covered by forest?
Pakistan's forest cover is about 4.8 percent of its land area according to commonly quoted figures.
This is low compared with the world average of about 30 percent; sources differ slightly.
Who is the Prime Minister of Japan?
Sanae Takaichi became Japan's first woman Prime Minister in October 2025 and was re-designated after the February 2026 election.
Japan has no president; its head of state is Emperor Naruhito, and Fumio Kishida was PM in 2022.
In a bus of 30 passengers, 2/3 are men and the rest are girls. What is the percentage of girls?
Men = 2/3 x 30 = 20, so girls = 30 - 20 = 10. Percentage of girls = 10/30 x 100 = 33.33%.
Which is the longest railway tunnel in Pakistan?
The Khojak Tunnel, built in 1891 in the Khojak Pass of Balochistan on the Quetta-Chaman line, is about 3.9 km long and is Pakistan's longest railway tunnel.
The Lowari Tunnel in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is longer, but it is a road tunnel, not a railway tunnel.
How old was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) when his grandfather Hazrat Abdul Muttalib passed away?
Abdul Muttalib took care of the Prophet (PBUH) after his mother died and passed away when the Prophet was 8 years old. Afterwards his uncle Abu Talib became his guardian.
The Prophet (PBUH) lost his mother Hazrat Amina at the age of 6.
Who is the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK)?
Faisal Karim Kundi of the PPP has been Governor of KPK since May 2024. He took over from Haji Ghulam Ali.
Shah Farman, the answer given in 2022, was governor from 2019 to 2023.
In which year was the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) founded?
The SCO was formally founded on 15 June 2001 in Shanghai, China, by China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.
Its predecessor was the Shanghai Five of 1996, and Pakistan and India became full members in 2017.
Where were the FIFA World Cup matches of 2022 played?
The 2022 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Qatar from November to December 2022. Argentina won it.
It was the first FIFA World Cup held in an Arab and Muslim-majority country.
In which year was the Indian National Congress founded?
The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A. O. Hume.
The All-India Muslim League was formed later, in 1906 at Dhaka.
Which city is commonly called the heart of Pakistan?
Lahore is popularly called the heart (Dil) of Pakistan because of its culture and history.
Sources differ, as Punjab province is also sometimes described as the heart of Pakistan.
Who is the author of the book India Wins Freedom?
India Wins Freedom is the autobiographical account of the Indian independence struggle by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.
Maulana Azad was the first Education Minister of independent India.
Who is the Chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) as of October 2026?
Mohsin Naqvi was elected PCB chairman unopposed on 6 February 2024 for a three-year term.
Ramiz Raja was PCB chairman from 2021 to December 2022, which was the answer in 2022.
Which city in Pakistan is known as the City of Flowers?
Peshawar is called the City of Flowers because of its many gardens.
Lahore is known as the City of Gardens.
Who is the current Prime Minister of Malaysia (October 2026)?
Anwar Ibrahim became the 10th Prime Minister of Malaysia in November 2022 and is still in office in 2026.
Ismail Sabri Yaakob was PM from 2021 to 2022, when candidates took the test.
Which area is known as the Roof of the World?
The Pamir Plateau in Central Asia is called the Roof of the World because of its great height.
Tibet is also sometimes given this name.
Who was the first Pakistani woman cricketer to take 100 ODI wickets?
Sana Mir became the first Pakistani woman to take 100 ODI wickets in February 2017 against Bangladesh in the World Cup Qualifier.
She finished her ODI career with about 150 ODI wickets, the most by a Pakistani woman, and was inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame.
How many articles does the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan have?
The 1973 Constitution, Pakistan's third constitution, contains 280 articles.
It has 12 parts and 7 schedules and was enforced on 14 August 1973.
In which province of Pakistan is the Reko Diq mine project located?
Reko Diq is a large copper and gold deposit in Chagai district in the west of Balochistan.
Reko Diq is one of the largest undeveloped copper-gold deposits in the world.
What is the official capital of Indonesia?
Jakarta is Indonesia's legal capital. A new capital, Nusantara in East Kalimantan, was planned by a 2022 law, but Jakarta stays the capital until a formal transfer decree is issued.
Nusantara is now planned only as a political capital (target 2028), so candidates who wrote Nusantara in 2022 were anticipating a move that has not formally happened.
Which planet has the largest number of moons?
Saturn has the most confirmed moons of any planet, about 293 as of 2026. Jupiter is second with about 115.
Saturn's count was 83 in 2022 and rose sharply after new discoveries, so older answers differ.
How many wajibat of Namaz are there according to the Hanafi school?
The Hanafi school counts 14 wajibat of Namaz, such as reciting Surah Fatiha and a further surah.
The fard acts of Namaz are 13 in number.
What was the real (original) name of Titu Mir?
Titu Mir, the Bengali leader of the Barasat uprising, was born as Mir Nisar Ali.
He was killed in 1831 by British forces at his bamboo fort in Narkelbaria.
Which companion (Sahabi) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was his adopted son?
Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) was freed and adopted by the Prophet (PBUH) before prophethood, and was known as Zaid bin Muhammad until adoption was abolished.
Zaid is the only companion whose name is mentioned in the Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab).
When did the Al-Khalid main battle tank enter service with the Pakistan Army?
The Al-Khalid (MBT-2000), developed by Pakistan with Chinese help, entered service in 2001.
Some sources mention 2004 for its formal presentation, and the upgraded Al-Khalid-I was inducted in July 2020.
Rough is to smooth as crude is to what?
Rough and smooth are opposites, so the opposite of crude (unrefined) is polished (refined).
Crude oil is oil that has not yet been refined.
In which year was FATA merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
The 25th Constitutional Amendment was passed in May 2018 and merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which was completed after the President signed it.
Candidates often confuse this with 2021, but the merger law was passed in 2018.
In which year was the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP) renamed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
The 18th Amendment passed in April 2010 renamed NWFP as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Pakistan's parliament approved it that year.
The former FATA was merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2018 through the 25th Amendment.
Which letter comes next in the series: B, E, J, Q, ?
The positions are 2, 5, 10, 17. The gaps are 3, 5, 7, so the next gap is 9 and 17 + 9 = 26, which is Z.
The positions are one more than the squares 1, 4, 9, 16, and 25 + 1 = 26.
Who is the Prime Minister of New Zealand (as of October 2026)?
Christopher Luxon of the National Party has been Prime Minister since November 2023 and is still in office in October 2026.
Jacinda Ardern (until January 2023) and Chris Hipkins (until November 2023) held the post earlier; the next election is on 7 November 2026.
What is the antonym of abhor?
To abhor means to hate strongly, so its opposite is to love or admire.
Loathe and detest are synonyms of abhor.
Aleem Dar is a famous umpire of which game?
Aleem Dar, from Lahore, is a famous Pakistani cricket umpire who stood in over 100 Test matches and won the ICC Umpire of the Year award three times in a row (2009-2011).
He served on the ICC Elite Panel of Umpires for many years.
Which bridge in Turkey connects Asia and Europe over the Bosphorus Strait?
The Bosphorus Bridge in Istanbul spans the Bosphorus Strait and joins the European and Asian sides of the city.
It was renamed 15 July Martyrs Bridge in 2016, and Istanbul has other Bosphorus bridges too.
Who is the President of China as of October 2026?
Xi Jinping has been President of China since 2013 and also leads the Communist Party.
The head of government, the Premier, is Li Qiang, so the office of PM is not held by Xi.
What is the height of the Diamer Bhasha Dam?
The Diamer Bhasha Dam on the Indus is 272 metres high, per WAPDA.
It is a roller-compacted concrete dam and one of the tallest of its kind in the world.
On which date did Muhammad Ali Bogra present the Bogra Formula?
Muhammad Ali Bogra presented his constitutional formula on 7 October 1953.
The formula was never implemented because the Constituent Assembly was dissolved in 1954.
What is the relation between Hazrat Musa (AS) and Hazrat Haroon (AS)?
Hazrat Haroon (AS) was the elder brother of Hazrat Musa (AS) and was also a prophet.
Musa (AS) asked Allah to make Haroon (AS) his helper, as mentioned in the Quran.
According to Islamic tradition, who first built the Kaaba?

Islamic tradition says the Kaaba was first built by Hazrat Adam (AS), and later rebuilt by Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) with his son Ismail (AS). Many candidates and sources give this answer for the first building.
Sources differ, and some Pakistani textbooks credit Ibrahim and Ismail (AS) with building it, but they rebuilt it on its old foundations.
Which country is called the Land of the Rising Sun?
Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun; its name Nippon means origin of the sun.
Vienna is the capital of which country?
Vienna is the capital and largest city of Austria on the Danube River.
Budapest, the capital of Hungary, is also on the Danube.
In which surah of the Quran is the name Ahmad (for the Holy Prophet PBUH) mentioned?
The name Ahmad appears in Surah As-Saff (61:6), where Hazrat Isa (AS) gives the good news of a messenger named Ahmad coming after him.
The name Muhammad is mentioned four times in the Quran, in Al-Imran, Al-Ahzab, Muhammad and Al-Fath.
How many articles did the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan have?
The 1956 Constitution, Pakistan's first constitution, had 234 articles.
It was enforced on 23 March 1956 and abrogated in October 1958.
In which year did Pakistan win the IBSF World Snooker Championship for the first time?
Muhammad Yousuf won the world amateur snooker title for Pakistan in 1994.
Muhammad Sajid won the world amateur title in 2006, Pakistan's second.
Which is the last completely revealed surah of the Holy Quran?
Surah An-Nasr is regarded as the last complete surah to be revealed.
Sources differ about the last verse revealed, with Al-Baqarah verse 281 or Al-Maidah verse 3 often mentioned.
Which of the following countries lies in both Europe and Asia?
Turkey is divided by the Bosphorus strait, with a small part in Europe and most of its land in Asia.
Istanbul is the major city that lies on both continents.
Which one is different from the others: Circle, Square, Triangle, Angle?
Circle, square and triangle are closed geometric figures, while an angle is not a closed figure.
An angle is formed by two rays meeting at a common point.
Hazrat Sara (AS), wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), was the mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
Hazrat Hajra (AS) was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS).
Which was the first ghazwa (expedition led personally by the Holy Prophet SAW) of Islam?
The first ghazwa, in Safar 2 AH, was Abwa, also called Waddan, in which the Prophet (SAW) himself went out but no fighting occurred.
The first major battle of Islam was Badr in Ramadan 2 AH.
What is the capital of South Korea?
Seoul is the capital and largest city of South Korea.
Pyongyang is the capital of North Korea.
Malaysia has a king instead of a president. Who is the head of state (Yang di-Pertuan Agong) of Malaysia in 2026?
Malaysia is a constitutional monarchy with no president. Sultan Ibrahim of Johor has been the 17th Agong since 31 January 2024.
His predecessor was Sultan Abdullah of Pahang, who was Agong from 2019 to 2024.
According to the 2023 census, about what percentage of Pakistan's population is Muslim?
The 2023 census recorded Muslims at about 96.35 percent of the population of Pakistan.
The 2017 census figure was 96.47 percent, and candidates often quote 97 percent.
About how many times is the command of Namaz (Salah) mentioned in the Holy Quran, according to common textbooks?
Salah and its related commands are repeated about 700 times in the Quran, showing its great importance.
Sources differ on the exact count, but 700 is the figure given in most Pakistani textbooks.
What is the approximate total length of railway track in Pakistan?
Pakistan Railways reports about 11,881 track kilometres, counting all tracks including double-track sections.
The route length is shorter, about 7,791 km, which is why sources differ.
A third of 90 is ten times a third of 9.
Who was the first civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan?
On 20 December 1971 Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto took over as President and became the first civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator after Yahya Khan stepped down.
Martial law was lifted in Pakistan in 1972 and the 1973 Constitution was adopted under Bhutto.
In the word MANAGEMENT, arranged alphabetically, which letter is second last?
Alphabetical order is A A E E G M M N N T. The last letter is T and the second last is N.
MANAGEMENT has 10 letters, with A, E, M and N each appearing twice.
What was the code name of Pakistan's first nuclear tests of 28 May 1998?
Pakistan's tests of 28 May 1998 at Chagai in Balochistan were code-named Chagai-I.
India's 1974 test was Smiling Buddha and its 1998 tests were Shakti; Pakistan's second test on 30 May 1998 was Chagai-II.
Amsterdam is the capital of which country?
Amsterdam is the constitutional capital of the Netherlands. The government sits in The Hague.
Brussels is the capital of Belgium.
Lima is the capital of which country?
Lima is the capital and largest city of Peru. It lies on the Pacific coast.
Santiago is the capital of Chile.
What is the name of the angel in charge of Hell (Jahannam)?
The Quran (Surah Az-Zukhruf) mentions Malik as the keeper of Hell.
Ridwan is the angel who is the keeper of Paradise.
In which country are the headquarters of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) located?
The ECO secretariat is in Tehran, the capital of Iran.
Pakistan, Iran and Turkey were the founding members of ECO.
Who is the Prime Minister of Israel?
Benjamin Netanyahu has been Prime Minister of Israel since December 2022 and was still in office in October 2026.
Naftali Bennett (2021-2022) was PM when candidates wrote in 2022, and Israel's next general election is scheduled for 27 October 2026.
What is the capital of the Netherlands?
Amsterdam is the constitutional capital of the Netherlands. The government and parliament sit in The Hague.
The International Court of Justice is located in The Hague.
In which year was Bengal partitioned by the British?
Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905 into East Bengal and Assam and the rest of Bengal.
Who is the President of Ukraine?
Volodymyr Zelensky has been President of Ukraine since May 2019 and still holds the office in 2026.
Petro Poroshenko was his predecessor, from 2014 to 2019.
Who announced the partition of Bengal in 1905?
Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, announced the partition of Bengal on 19 July 1905 and it took effect on 16 October 1905, creating a Muslim-majority eastern province.
The partition was annulled in 1911, and the All India Muslim League was formed in 1906 partly in reaction to these events.
Who benefited from the Partition of Bengal in 1905?
The partition created a Muslim-majority province of East Bengal and Assam with Dhaka as its capital, which helped Muslims in education and jobs.
Hindus opposed it strongly and it was annulled in 1911.
In which constitution was the bicameral (two-house) legislature introduced in Pakistan?
The 1973 Constitution created a bicameral Parliament of the National Assembly and the Senate.
The Senate was first formed in 1973 and the 1956 and 1962 constitutions had one house.
On which date was the Pakistan-China boundary agreement signed?
Pakistan and China signed the boundary agreement on 2 March 1963 and settled the border of Gilgit-Baltistan with Xinjiang.
The Karakoram Highway linking the two countries was later built and opened to traffic in 1978.
Which languages were declared official languages in the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
The 1956 Constitution made Urdu and Bengali the state languages of Pakistan.
The Bengali language movement of 1952 forced this recognition.
For how many years is the President of Pakistan elected?
Under the 1973 Constitution the President holds office for a term of five years.
The President is elected by an electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies.
Who was the father of Hazrat Yousuf (AS)?
Hazrat Yousuf (AS) was the son of Hazrat Yaqub (AS), who was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
Hazrat Yaqub (AS) is also known as Israel.
What is the antonym of intimate (adjective)?
Intimate means close and familiar, so the opposite is distant.
Close, familiar and dear are synonyms of intimate.
Who is the President of Sri Lanka (as of October 2026)?
Anura Kumara Dissanayake won the September 2024 presidential election and took office as President.
Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President until 2022 and Ranil Wickremesinghe until 2024.
Between which two countries does the Line of Control (LOC) lie?
The Line of Control is the de facto military border dividing Indian-administered and Pakistan-administered Kashmir.
It was established by the Simla Agreement of 1972.
Who recited verses of the Quran in the court of King Najashi of Abyssinia?
Hazrat Jafar (RA) led the Muslim migrants to Abyssinia and recited the opening verses of Surah Maryam before Najashi. The king was moved and refused to hand the Muslims over to Quraish.
Hazrat Jafar (RA) is also known as Jafar Tayyar and was martyred at the Battle of Mutah.
Which was the second major battle (ghazwa) fought between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah, after the Battle of Badr?
The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was the first major battle of Islam and the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH was the second.
The Battle of Uhud was fought near Mount Uhud, close to Madinah, in Shawwal 3 AH.
On what date did the Australian cricketer Shane Warne die?
Shane Warne died of a suspected heart attack in Koh Samui, Thailand, on 4 March 2022 at the age of 52.
Warne took 708 wickets in Test cricket, a record for a leg-spinner.
The Shimla Agreement between Pakistan and India was signed after which war?
After the 1971 war and the separation of East Pakistan, Pakistan and India met at Shimla in 1972 and signed the agreement.
The 1966 Tashkent Declaration was signed after the 1965 war.
One degree of an angle is equal to how many minutes?
A degree is divided into 60 minutes, and a minute into 60 seconds.
Who was the first woman Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan?
Shamshad Akhtar became the first woman Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan in 2005.
She later served as Caretaker Finance Minister in 2023.
In how many years was the revelation of the Holy Quran completed?
The Quran was revealed gradually to the Prophet (PBUH) over about 23 years, from the first revelation in Hira until shortly before his death.
About 13 years of this period were in Makkah and about 10 years in Madinah.
In which year was the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) established?
ECO was established in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey as the successor of RCD.
RCD (Regional Cooperation for Development) was formed in 1964.
On what date did Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad start?
The Pakistan Army launched Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad on 22 February 2017 against terrorism after a wave of attacks. It was a nationwide operation.
Operation Zarb-e-Azb in 2014 was an earlier operation in North Waziristan.
In which year was the film Jinnah, on the life of Quaid-e-Azam, released?
The film Jinnah, starring Christopher Lee as Jinnah, was released in 1998.
It was directed by Jamil Dehlavi.
Which city is known as the City of Gold?
Johannesburg in South Africa is called the City of Gold because it grew after gold was discovered in the Witwatersrand in 1886.
South Africa has long been one of the largest gold producers in the world, though sources differ on later rankings.
Which plant is commonly named as the fastest growing plant (tree) in the world?
Some bamboo species can grow almost one metre in a single day, which is why bamboo is commonly named the fastest growing plant.
Bamboo is technically a grass, and the Paulownia is often called the fastest growing true tree, so sources differ.
Habba Khatoon was a famous poet of which language?
Habba Khatoon (Zoon) was a 16th century Kashmiri poet known for her lyrical songs.
She is often called the Nightingale of Kashmir.
About what percentage of Antarctica is covered by ice?
About 98 percent of Antarctica is covered by an ice sheet, and only about 2 percent is bare rock. Some sources give 97.6 or 99 percent.
The ice sheet is on average about 2 km thick.
On which date is the International Day to Combat Islamophobia observed?
The UN General Assembly proclaimed 15 March as International Day to Combat Islamophobia in 2022, on a resolution moved by Pakistan on behalf of the OIC.
15 March was chosen as the anniversary of the 2019 Christchurch mosque attacks.
Who is the Pakistani Nobel Prize winner in Physics, and how many Pakistanis have won a Nobel Prize in Physics?
Dr. Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on the electroweak theory. He is the only Pakistani to win a Nobel in Physics.
Pakistan's other Nobel laureate is Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).
The Khyber Pass connects Peshawar with which city of Afghanistan?
The Khyber Pass links Peshawar (Pakistan) with Kabul through the Torkham border crossing and Jalalabad.
The pass lies in the Safed Koh range.
What is the population of Pakistan according to the 2023 census?
The 2023 digital census recorded Pakistan's population as about 241.49 million.
The 2017 census had recorded about 207.7 million, and candidates in 2022 used estimates of about 220 million.
Which was the first private television channel of Pakistan?
Shalimar Television Network, which began in 1990 as People's Television Network, was the first channel to break the monopoly of state-run PTV. It is the answer most textbooks give.
Sources differ on the word private: ARY Digital (2001) and Indus TV (2000) are often called the first fully independent channels.
Who was the first poet of the Punjabi language?
Hazrat Baba Fariduddin Ganjshakar (1188-1266) is regarded as the first poet of Punjabi, and his verses appear in the Guru Granth Sahib.
A quadratic equation is an equation of which degree?
The highest power of the variable in a quadratic equation is 2, so it is a second degree equation.

In which year was SUPARCO, the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, established?
SUPARCO was formally established on 16 September 1961 by an executive order, with Dr Abdus Salam as its first chairman.
Some sources trace a precursor committee to 1961 as well; candidate answers such as 1955 and 1959 are incorrect.
If 1 man writes 5 papers in 5 minutes, how long will 1 man take to write 1 paper?
5 papers take 5 minutes, so 1 paper takes 5 / 5 = 1 minute.
A rate of 1 paper per minute means that 60 papers would take an hour.
Out of 1500 students, 1300 are present. What percentage of the students are absent (to two decimal places)?
The percentage present is 86.67%, which together with 13.33% makes 100%.
According to the 1956 Constitution, what was the minimum age to become President of Pakistan?
The 1956 Constitution required the President to be a Muslim of not less than 40 years of age.
Some candidates remembered 45, but 40 is the age given in the Constitution of 1956.
Who dismissed (abrogated) the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan?
General Yahya Khan took over from Ayub Khan in March 1969, imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution.
The 1962 Constitution had lasted about seven years.

From the 4th to the 19th is 15 days. 15 days is 2 full weeks plus 1 day(s), so the day is 1 day(s) after Friday, which is Saturday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.
If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 26th be?
From the 4th to the 26th is 22 days. 22 days is 3 full weeks plus 1 day(s), so the day is 1 day(s) after Tuesday, which is Wednesday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.
At what age did Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan, the father of Pakistan's nuclear programme, die?
He was born on 1 April 1936 and died on 10 October 2021, which makes him 85 years old.
He died in Islamabad and was buried in the H-8 graveyard.
What is the antonym of sublime?
Sublime means of very high excellence or beauty, so its opposite is ridiculous or lowly.
Magnificent, grand and noble are close in meaning to sublime.
On which side of Pakistan does the Arabian Sea lie?
Pakistan's coastline of about 1,046 km runs along the Arabian Sea in the south, in Sindh and Balochistan.
Iran and Afghanistan lie to the west, China to the north-east and India to the east.
In which province and city is the BRT (Zu Peshawar) transport system located?
The BRT Zu Peshawar is a bus rapid transit system of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It serves the city of Peshawar.
Lahore has the Orange Line Metro Train and Metro Bus, which are different projects.
Which country is the current men's Hockey World Cup champion (2026 edition)?
Germany beat Spain 1-0 in the final on 30 August 2026 in Wavre, Belgium, to retain the title.

What is the derivative of sin x with respect to x?
The standard derivative of sin x is cos x.

On which date was the Lahore Declaration signed by the prime ministers of Pakistan and India?
Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee signed the Lahore Declaration on 21 February 1999 during Vajpayee's bus visit to Lahore.

Approximately how many disbelievers (Quraish) came to fight the Muslims in the Battle of Badr?

Who developed the first successful polio vaccine?
Jonas Salk developed the inactivated polio vaccine, announced in 1955.

Which country hosted the extraordinary session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers on the Afghan crisis in December 2021?

Who is the Prime Minister of Israel (as of October 2026, before the 27 October election)?

Which country has the largest number of lakes in the world?
Canada has the most lakes in the world, with several hundred thousand, more than the rest of the world combined by most estimates.
Finland is known as the land of a thousand lakes but has far fewer lakes than Canada.
Which is the longest river lying entirely within Afghanistan?
The Helmand River, about 1,150 km long, is the longest river that flows wholly in Afghanistan.

Whose motto is Faith, Unity, Discipline?
Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah gave the motto Faith, Unity, Discipline (Iman, Ittehad, Tanzeem) to the nation.

Which letter comes next in the series: L, M, N, ?

L, M, N, O are the 12th to 15th letters of the alphabet.

Asif Ali Zardari is the co-chairperson of the party.
Who started the Reshmi Rumal (Silk Letters) Movement?

The Suez Canal separates Africa from which continent?

Bashar al-Assad ruled Syria from 2000 until his government fell in December 2024.

Who was the first Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan?

Entirely means in every part or fully, the same as completely.

Hazrat Abu Huraira (RA) narrated about 5,374 Ahadith, the highest number among the Companions.

NASA stands for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, a United States government agency.

The partition of Bengal came into effect on 16 October 1905.

Which planet is nearest to the Sun?
Mercury orbits closest to the Sun, at about 58 million km.

1/3 of 120 is 40. A quarter of 40 is 40 divided by 4, which equals 10.

The Chief Justice of the US

What is the capital of China?
Beijing is the capital of the People's Republic of China.

Lat, Manat and Uzza were the three chief idols worshipped by the pagan Arabs before Islam.

Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat soluble and do not dissolve in water. The B vitamins and vitamin C are water soluble.

SUPARCO is the national organization of Pakistan for which field?
SUPARCO stands for Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, Pakistan's national space agency.

The Objective Resolution of 1949 laid down the guiding principles for the constitutions of Pakistan and became their preamble.

Jawaharlal Nehru signed the treaty with Pakistan's President Ayub Khan at Karachi on 19 September 1960.

Hazrat Maryam (AS), the mother of Prophet Isa (AS), is the only woman named in the Quran.

Pakistan issued its first set of four postage stamps on 9 July 1948.

What is the meaning of the word prescribe?

The tune of the national anthem of Pakistan

Its tune was composed by Ahmed G. Chagla in 1949 and the words were written by Hafeez Jalandhari.
What is the walking seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwa during Hajj called?
Sa'i is the ritual walk between Safa and Marwa, commemorating Hazrat Hajra's search for water for Ismail (AS).
The Zamzam well appeared near the Kaaba after this search.
Which animal was with the Ashab-e-Kahf (Companions of the Cave)?
The Quran in Surah Al-Kahf mentions that their dog lay at the entrance of the cave with outstretched paws.
The dog is traditionally named Qitmir.
According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the term of the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies?
Unless dissolved earlier, the National and Provincial Assemblies serve a term of five years from their first meeting.
A Senator's term is six years, with half retiring every three years.
Against whom did the Muslims fight the Battle of Badr?
The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was fought between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.
It was the first major battle of Islam.
What is the antonym of the word biased?
Biased means unfairly favouring one side, so its opposite is impartial.
Unbiased and neutral are other opposites.
What is the border line between Pakistan and India (drawn in 1947) called?
The Radcliffe Line was drawn by the Boundary Commission headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe at the partition of India in 1947.
The Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border and the McMahon Line is the India-China boundary.
In a bus of 24 people, 2/3 are male. What percentage are female?
Males are 2/3 of 24 = 16, so females are 24 - 16 = 8. Percentage = 8/24 x 100 = 33.33 percent.
Females are 1/3 of the bus because the two fractions add up to 1.
How many times did Jahangir Khan win the World Open squash championship?
Jahangir Khan won the World Open six times, the last in 1988.
He also won the British Open ten times in a row from 1982 to 1991.
Which prophet was blessed with a son in his old age?
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) was granted Hazrat Ismail (AS) and later Hazrat Ishaq (AS) in his old age.
Hazrat Zakariya (AS) was also given a son, Hazrat Yahya (AS), in old age.
The circumference of a circle of radius r is equal to
Circumference = 2 x pi x r, which is the same as pi x diameter.
The area of a circle is pi r squared.
What are two circles called that have three points in common?
Three non-collinear points determine exactly one circle. If two circles share three points, they must be the same circle, so they coincide.
Two different circles can meet in at most two points.
What are sets that have no common element called?
Sets with no element in common have an empty intersection, and such sets are called disjoint sets.
Sets that have the same number of elements are called equivalent sets.
Who composed the music of the national anthem of Pakistan?
The tune of the anthem was composed by Ahmed Ghulamali Chagla, while the words were written by Hafeez Jalandhari.
The anthem was officially adopted in 1954.
A. R. Cornelius, a Chief Justice of Pakistan, belonged to which religion?
Justice Alvin Robert Cornelius was a Christian and served as Chief Justice of Pakistan from 1960 to 1968.
He was known for his scholarship and integrity.
Which crop is grown on the largest area in Pakistan?
Wheat is the staple food and covers the largest cropped area, about 9 million hectares.
Cotton is the major cash crop of Pakistan, but it is grown on a smaller area than wheat.
Who is the current Prime Minister of India?
Narendra Modi has been Prime Minister since 2014 and began his third consecutive term in June 2024.
He is the longest-serving Prime Minister of India after Jawaharlal Nehru and Indira Gandhi in total years.
What is a decimal called in which the digits repeat again and again?
A decimal in which a digit or block of digits repeats endlessly, like 0.333..., is called a recurring (repeating) decimal.
Every recurring decimal can be written as a fraction of two integers, so it is a rational number.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam declare in Dhaka that Urdu would be the state language of Pakistan?
On 21 March 1948 at Dhaka, Quaid-e-Azam declared that Urdu alone would be the state language of Pakistan.
Urdu was formally made the national language in the 1973 Constitution, so some sources give a different answer.
A square matrix whose determinant is zero is called what?
A square matrix with determinant equal to zero has no inverse and is called a singular matrix.
A matrix with a non-zero determinant is called non-singular and has an inverse.
On whose advice does the President of Pakistan dissolve the National Assembly under the Constitution as it stands today?
Under Article 58 the President dissolves the National Assembly only on the advice of the Prime Minister.
Before the 18th Amendment of 2010 the President could also dissolve it on his own discretion under Article 58(2)(b).
A train's speed is double that of a car, and the car travels 30 km in 1 hour. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes?
Car speed is 30 km/h, so train speed is 2 x 30 = 60 km/h. In 30 minutes the train covers 60 x 0.5 = 30 km.
Distance equals speed multiplied by time.
What is the term (duration) of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
The National Assembly has a term of five years from its first sitting unless dissolved earlier.
A Senator has a term of six years.
What is the main source of electricity generation in Pakistan today?
Recent data for 2025 show hydel power as the largest single source, around 39 percent in some months. RLNG and nuclear follow.
In earlier decades thermal (oil and gas) plants produced most of Pakistan's electricity.
How many articles are there in the English language?
The English articles are a, an and the. A and an are indefinite and the is definite.
Candidates often wrongly say 2, forgetting that a and an are separate forms.
A train travels twice as fast as a car. If the car covers 30 km in 60 minutes, in what time will the train cover 30 km?
The car's speed is 30 km per hour, so the train's speed is 60 km per hour. The train covers 30 km in 30 / 60 hour = 30 minutes.
Which is the fastest land (terrestrial) animal?
The cheetah is the fastest land animal and can run at about 100 to 110 km per hour in short bursts.
The peregrine falcon is the fastest bird in a dive.
How many agencies were there in the Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA)?
FATA had seven agencies: Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Orakzai, Kurram, North Waziristan and South Waziristan.
There were also frontier regions (FRs) attached to FATA.
In which year was the Bogra Formula presented?
Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra presented the formula in 1953 to solve the constitutional deadlock.
It was announced in the Constituent Assembly in October 1953.
A constitutional proposal for a two-house legislature with parity between East and West Pakistan
A plan to make Urdu the only national language
It proposed a bicameral legislature, with equal representation of the provinces in the upper house and representation by population in the lower house.
It was named after Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra.
In which galaxy does the Earth lie?
Our solar system and the Earth lie in the Milky Way galaxy, a barred spiral galaxy.
The nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way is Andromeda.
The ancient region of Gandhara lay mainly between which two modern cities?
Gandhara covered the Peshawar valley and the Potohar plateau around Taxila, roughly from Peshawar to Rawalpindi in north-west Pakistan.
Sources differ on exact limits, but Taxila and Peshawar are its best-known centres.
In which country do the Golan Heights lie?
The Golan Heights is a rocky plateau in south-western Syria. Most of it has been occupied by Israel since 1967.
Israel annexed the Golan Heights in 1981, but this is not recognised by most of the world.
If Hamza is three times as old as Ali, what will be the age of Hamza when Ali is 7 years old?
Hamza's age is 3 times Ali's age, so 3 x 7 = 21 years.
Age problems are solved by first writing the ratio between the ages.
For how many years did the Quraish of Makkah boycott Banu Hashim?
The Quraish imposed a social and economic boycott on Banu Hashim for about three years in the valley of Shib Abi Talib.
The boycott took place from the 7th to the 10th year of prophethood.
What is the new name of the Kashmir Highway in Islamabad?
In August 2020 Pakistan renamed Islamabad's Kashmir Highway as Srinagar Highway in solidarity with Kashmiris.
The renaming was done on the first anniversary of India's revocation of Article 370 in 2019.
Where was the ICC Men's T20 World Cup of 2021 played?
The 2021 T20 World Cup, officially hosted by the BCCI of India, was moved because of COVID-19 and played in the UAE and Oman in October and November 2021.
Australia won the 2021 final against New Zealand in Dubai.
Which prophet was tested by Allah with a long and severe illness and was known for his patience?
Hazrat Ayub (AS) was tested with loss of wealth, family and a long illness and kept patience, so his name is a proverb for sabr.
Allah cured him after he prayed, as mentioned in the Quran.
What does the adjective intimate mean?
Intimate describes a very close, familiar relationship or a detailed, deep knowledge of something.
Intimate can also be a verb meaning to hint at something indirectly, pronounced differently.
How many gates does Jannah (Paradise) have?
According to authentic hadith, Jannah has eight gates, one of which is Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.
Jahannam, by contrast, has seven gates.
Which fighter jet has Pakistan produced jointly with China?
The JF-17 Thunder is a light multirole fighter built by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex, Kamra, with China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.
Its Chinese designation is FC-1 Xiaolong.
Who wrote the famous biography 'Jinnah of Pakistan'?
Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote 'Jinnah of Pakistan' in 1984.
Fatima Jinnah wrote 'My Brother' and Hector Bolitho wrote 'Jinnah: Creator of Pakistan'.
Which one is different from the others: Karachi, Lahore, Balochistan, Rawalpindi?
Karachi, Lahore and Rawalpindi are cities, while Balochistan is a province.
Balochistan is the largest province of Pakistan by area.
A number that can be written as a ratio of two integers with a non-zero denominator is rational. 5/7 is such a ratio.
Numbers such as pi and the square root of 2 cannot be written as a ratio of integers, so they are irrational.
What is the capital of North Korea?
Pyongyang is the capital and largest city of North Korea.
Seoul is the capital of South Korea.
Which language is the lingua franca (common link language) of Pakistan?
Urdu is understood across all provinces and links people of different mother tongues. It is also the national language.
Punjabi is the most widely spoken mother tongue in Pakistan.
Which letter comes after G in the English alphabet?
The order is F, G, H, I, so H follows G.
Which letter comes after the letter that is followed by M?
The letter followed by M is L, and the letter after L is M.
M is the 13th letter, exactly in the middle of the alphabet.
Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook in 2004 and is the CEO of its parent company Meta.
Facebook was renamed as Meta Platforms in 2021.
On which date did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) arrive in Madina after the Hijrat?
After staying at Quba, the Prophet (PBUH) entered Madina on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, 1 AH (September 622 AD). He had left Makkah a few days earlier.
Some sources give slightly different days for the departure and arrival, but 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal is the common Pakistani textbook date.
