The Rann of Kutch is a large salt marsh in the Thar desert area on the border between Sindh in Pakistan and Gujarat in India. A border dispute there was settled by tribunal in 1968.
The 1965 war began with clashes in the Rann of Kutch in April 1965.
According to the Quran, which religion is accepted by Allah?
The Quran states that the religion with Allah is Islam (Surah Al-Imran 3:19). It also says no other religion will be accepted from anyone.
The Quran was completed with the verse declaring Islam as the chosen religion (Surah Al-Maidah 5:3).
Nankana Sahib is a famous holy site of which religion?
Nankana Sahib is the birthplace of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism. It is in Punjab, Pakistan.
Guru Nanak was born there in 1469.
The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared in response to whose challenge?
Lord Birkenhead, the Secretary of State for India, challenged Indian leaders to draft a constitution acceptable to all communities. The Nehru Report was the Congress-led answer to that challenge.
Quaid-e-Azam rejected the Nehru Report and presented his Fourteen Points in 1929.
Which article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan declares that Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan?
Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution states that Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic to be known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
Article 2 declares Islam to be the State religion of Pakistan.
In which constitution of Pakistan was the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan first used?
The 1956 Constitution, Pakistan's first, named the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956.
The 1962 Constitution changed the name to the Republic of Pakistan, and the 1973 Constitution restored Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
Which country has the largest official gold reserves in the world?
The United States holds about 8,133 tonnes of official gold reserves, roughly double that of second-placed Germany.
Germany is second with about 3,350 tonnes, followed by Italy and France.
In which city did the tribes of Aus and Khazraj reside?
Aus and Khazraj were the two main Arab tribes of Yathrib, later called Madina. They became the Ansar after welcoming the Prophet (PBUH).
The two tribes had long been at war before Islam united them.
On which date was the Pakistan Resolution (Lahore Resolution) presented?

23 March is celebrated as Pakistan Day.
According to the commonly given order of revelation, which Surah was the third to be revealed?
The usual order is Al-Alaq first, Al-Qalam second and Al-Muzzammil third.
Sources differ; some lists place Al-Muddaththir ahead of Al-Muzzammil.
What is the closest meaning of the word reward?
A reward is something given in return for good work or conduct, that is, a recompense.
The opposite of reward is punishment.
Which word is the synonym of rich?
Rich means having a great deal of money, and wealthy has the same meaning.
Affluent is also a synonym of rich.
Which river is the largest in the world by volume of water discharged?
The Amazon carries the greatest volume of water of any river in the world.

The name Punjab means the land of how many rivers?
Punjab is from the Persian words punj (five) and ab (water), meaning five rivers: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.

The Reshmi Romal (Silk Letter) Tehreek was started by Maulana Mahmud Hasan and which colleague?
The Silk Letter Movement of about 1913 to 1920 was organised by Shaikhul Hind Maulana Mahmud Hasan with Maulana Ubaidullah Sindhi.
Letters were written on silk cloth to communicate with allies abroad against British rule.
What is the square root of 196?
14 x 14 = 196, so the square root of 196 is 14.
196 is a perfect square, being 14 squared.
What is the approximate value of the square root of 7?

The square root of 7 is an irrational number, about 2.6458.
How many roots does a quadratic equation have?
A quadratic equation has degree 2, and an equation of degree n has n roots. So it has 2 roots, which may be real or complex.
A quadratic equation has the form ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with a not equal to 0.
In which battle were about 70 Sahaba martyred?
About 70 Sahaba were martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 Hijri.
Only 14 Muslims were martyred at Badr.
In which year did Dr Abdus Salam win the Nobel Prize in Physics?
Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for the electroweak theory.
He was the first Pakistani and first Muslim from Pakistan to win a Nobel Prize.
Which of the following countries is a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) as of 2026?
Iran became a full member in 2023 and Belarus in 2024, bringing the SCO to ten full members. Turkey is only a dialogue partner, while Afghanistan and Mongolia are observers.
The ten full members are China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Iran and Belarus.
Which fruit has its seeds on the outside of its body (on the surface of the skin)?
The tiny seed-like dots on a strawberry are actually separate fruits (achenes) on the outer surface, each containing a seed. The other fruits keep their seeds inside.
The fleshy red part of a strawberry is the swollen receptacle of the flower rather than a true fruit.
Who elects the President of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution?
An Electoral College of the Senate, National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies
Under Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution the President is elected by an Electoral College made up of members of the Senate, the National Assembly and the four Provincial Assemblies.
The President serves a five-year term.
What is the measure of an angle inscribed in a semicircle?
By Thales' theorem, an angle inscribed in a semicircle subtends the diameter and is always a right angle, 90 degrees.
The central angle on a diameter is 180 degrees, which is exactly double the inscribed angle.
Who demanded the separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency in the Muslim proposals of the 1920s?
Jinnah included the separation of Sindh from Bombay in the Delhi Muslim Proposals of 1927 and again in his Fourteen Points of 1929.
Sindh was actually separated from the Bombay Presidency in 1936 and became a separate province.

A treaty with the Jews of Madinah

Where did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) deliver the Last Sermon?
In the valley of Uranah on the plain of Arafat

Choose the correct preposition: She shouted ____ him.
The verb shout takes at when it means to speak angrily to someone, so the correct sentence is She shouted at him.
Shout to someone means to call out so that the person can hear you, with no anger.
What is the meaning of the word 'Siraat' (as in Siraat-e-Mustaqeem)?
'Siraat' is an Arabic word meaning a path or way. In Surah Al-Fatiha, Siraat-e-Mustaqeem means the straight path.

The sister is now 3 x 5 = 15 years old. Adil needs 15 - 5 = 10 more years, so the sister will be 15 + 10 = 25.
The age difference between two people always stays the same (here 10 years).

In which country did the Black Lives Matter slogan and movement first start?
The hashtag and movement began in the USA in 2013 after the acquittal of the man who shot Trayvon Martin.

Who sold the Kashmir valley and to whom?
The British East India Company to Gulab Singh Dogra
By the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) the British East India Company sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh, the Dogra ruler of Jammu.
Gulab Singh became the first Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir.
What is the trivial solution of a homogeneous system of linear equations in three unknowns x, y and z?
In a homogeneous system every right-hand side is 0, so putting every unknown equal to 0 always satisfies it. This is called the trivial solution (0, 0, 0).
A homogeneous system always has at least the trivial solution, so it is never inconsistent.

Subtract x from both sides: 3x - 1 = 2. Add 1: 3x = 3, so x = 1.

Tiananmen Square is situated in which city?
Tiananmen Square lies in the centre of Beijing, the capital of China. It is named after the Gate of Heavenly Peace.
It is one of the largest public squares in the world.
In which city was the first television station of Pakistan set up?
Pakistan Television started its first broadcast from Lahore on 26 November 1964. It was a pilot station.
Karachi and Dhaka stations followed in 1966.
Marvi, the famous folk tale, belongs to which province of Pakistan?
Umar Marvi is one of the seven famous folk heroines of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai's Sindhi poetry. The story belongs to Sindh.
Marvi was a village girl of Tharparkar who refused the offers of the ruler Umar Soomro.

The campaign is also called the Army of Hardship (Jaish-ul-Usrah).

After which event did Hazrat Abu Sufyan (RA) accept Islam?
Abu Sufyan accepted Islam at the time of the Conquest of Makkah in Ramadan 8 AH.

In which Hijri year did Abu Sufyan accept Islam?
Abu Sufyan embraced Islam on the occasion of the Conquest of Makkah, which took place in 8 AH.
Some candidates remember 6 AH, but the Conquest of Makkah was in 8 AH.
Which surah is known as Arus-ul-Quran (the Bride of the Quran)?
Surah Ar-Rahman is called the Bride of the Quran because of its beauty and its repeated refrain.
Surah Yaseen is called the heart of the Quran.
How many surahs of the Holy Quran are named after prophets, according to the commonly given list?
The commonly counted ones are Yunus, Hud, Yusuf, Ibrahim, Nuh and Muhammad, giving six.
Counts differ between sources depending on which names are included.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "evidence"?
Evidence is the facts or signs that show something is true, which is proof.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "negotiate"?
To negotiate is to discuss terms in order to reach agreement, which is to bargain.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "replenish"?
To replenish is to fill up again, which is to refill.
Who is the President of Syria as of October 2026?
Ahmed al-Sharaa became president of the Syrian transitional government in January 2025 after Bashar al-Assad was overthrown in December 2024.
Bashar al-Assad was president from 2000 until December 2024, and the post of prime minister was abolished in March 2025.
What is the other name of the Ghazwa of Tabuk?
Tabuk is also called Ghazwat al-Usrah, the Army of Hardship, because of the heat, distance and shortage of supplies.
It is the last expedition led by the Prophet (SAW) himself.
A man travels towards the north and then turns to his left. In which direction is he now facing?
Facing north, a left turn points to the west.
A right turn from north would point to the east.
Talha is moving towards the north and then turns right. In which direction is he facing now?
Facing north, a right turn points him towards the east.
A left turn from north would point him to the west.
What is the synonym of the word 'tame' (or 'tamed')?
To tame means to make an animal gentle and used to humans, so tame or tamed means domesticated.
Ali is ten years old and his sister is twice his age. When Ali is 20 years old, what will be his sister's age?
The sister is 20 when Ali is 10, so she is 10 years older. When Ali is 20, she is 20 + 10 = 30.
The age difference between two people always stays the same.
What is one third of one tenth of 120?
One tenth of 120 is 12 and one third of 12 is 4.
The order of taking fractions does not change the result: 120 x 1/3 x 1/10 is also 4.
In set theory, what does the letter Z denote?
Z stands for the set of integers, that is, all positive and negative whole numbers and zero (from the German word Zahlen).
N is natural numbers, Q is rational numbers and R is real numbers.
Which pronoun is used for a thing?
'It' is the singular pronoun used for things and animals; he and she are for persons.
What was the real (birth) name of Tipu Sultan?
Tipu Sultan was born as Sultan Fateh Ali Khan Tipu, son of Haider Ali of Mysore.
He was known as the Tiger of Mysore.
Zun-Noon is the title of which prophet?
Zun-Noon means the one of the fish and is the title of Hazrat Yunus (AS).
He was swallowed by a fish and prayed Laa ilaha illa anta subhanaka.
If today is Friday, what day will it be after 12 days?
12 days is 1 week plus 5 days, and 5 days after Friday is Wednesday.
The week has 7 days, so only the remainder after dividing by 7 matters.
If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will be the day after tomorrow?
The 2nd is Friday, so the 3rd is Saturday and the 4th is Sunday. The day after tomorrow means the 4th.
Day after tomorrow means two days after today.
Xinjiang, a province of China, touches which side of Pakistan?
Xinjiang borders Gilgit-Baltistan in the north of Pakistan across the Karakoram.
The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway connects Pakistan with Xinjiang.

From the 4th to the 15th is 11 days. 11 = 7 + 4, so the day is 4 days after Tuesday, which is Saturday.
Counting the difference in dates and taking the remainder after dividing by 7 solves every such day question.

Sister is 3 x 4 = 12 now, so she is 8 years older than Umar. When Umar is 11, she is 11 + 8 = 19.

Who is the current Prime Minister of Ukraine?
Serhii Koretskyi, formerly head of Naftogaz, was confirmed as Prime Minister by the Verkhovna Rada on 16 July 2026.

Who was the first President of Ukraine?
Leonid Kravchuk became the first President of independent Ukraine in December 1991 after the Soviet Union broke up.
He served until 1994, when Leonid Kuchma succeeded him.

Bakar is older than Ali, and Ali is older than Umair, so the order is Bakar, Ali, Umair. Bakar is the oldest and Umair the youngest.

Which uncle of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was martyred in the Battle of Uhud?
Hazrat Hamza (RA), called Asadullah (Lion of Allah), was killed by Wahshi in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH.
He is also known as Sayyid-ush-Shuhada, the chief of the martyrs.
What is a matrix whose number of rows is not equal to its number of columns called?
A matrix with unequal numbers of rows and columns (m x n with m not equal to n) is a rectangular matrix.
If rows and columns are equal, it is a square matrix.
In which city is the International Islamic University (IIUI) located?
The International Islamic University is in Islamabad, the capital of Pakistan.
It was established in 1980 and given its present status in 1985.
Who lives and works in the White House in Washington, D.C.?
The White House is the official residence and workplace of the President of the United States.
The White House has been the residence of every US President since John Adams in 1800.
Al-Lat and Al-Uzza were names of what in pre-Islamic Arabia?
Al-Lat, Al-Uzza and Manat were the three chief idols worshipped by the Arabs before Islam.
Al-Lat was worshipped at Taif and Al-Uzza near Makkah; Manat was worshipped near Madinah.

Multiplying by 1/3 is the same as dividing by 3.

The vowels are A, I, O and U, so there are 4. Y is counted as a consonant here.
The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.
Where is the headquarters of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
The WTO has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.
The WTO was established on 1 January 1995, replacing GATT.
By what other name is Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) known?
Yaqoob (AS) is also called Israel, meaning servant of Allah, and his descendants are the Bani Israel.
Hazrat Yusuf (AS) was the son of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS).
What is the meaning of the word 'zenith' (also its synonym)?
Zenith means the highest point, peak or summit of something.

The 15th is 14 days after the 1st, which is exactly two weeks, so it is also a Friday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.
What is sin(180 - x) equal to?
Angles 180 - x and x lie on the same horizontal level of the unit circle, so they have the same sine: sin(180 - x) = sin x.
In the same way, cos(180 - x) = -cos x.
Who was the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom at the outbreak of the Second World War in 1939?
Neville Chamberlain was Prime Minister from 1937 to May 1940 and declared war on Germany on 3 September 1939.
The UK has no president; Winston Churchill replaced Chamberlain in May 1940, and Boris Johnson (named by a candidate) was PM only in 2019 to 2022.

From 1980 to 2000 is 20 years, which is 4 doublings, so the population in 2000 is 16 times that of 1980. Hence 1600 divided by 16 gives 100.

According to UNHCR, Turkey hosted about 3.6 million refugees in 2019, mostly Syrians, which was the highest in the world.

Absent students are 500 minus 320, which is 180. Then 180 divided by 500 times 100 gives 36 percent.

Girls are 1500 minus 360, which is 1140. Then 1140 divided by 1500 times 100 gives 76 percent.
In a class of 400 students, 360 are boys. What percentage of the students is girls?
Girls are 400 minus 360, which is 40. Then 40 divided by 400 times 100 gives 10 percent.
Who was the 3rd Prime Minister of Pakistan?

Who was the 5th Prime Minister of Pakistan?

What is the transpose of a matrix of order 4x3?
The transpose swaps rows and columns, so a 4x3 matrix becomes a 3x4 matrix.
The transpose of the transpose of a matrix gives back the original matrix.
If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 8th day be?
From the 2nd to the 8th is 6 days. Friday plus 6 days is Thursday.
Six days after any day equals one day before it.
In a school of 3000 students, 2700 are present. What percentage of students are absent?
Present students are 90% of the total.
By which title is Hazrat Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) well known?

Who was Hazrat Abdullah bin Abbas (RA) in relation to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?

General Yahya Khan took over after Ayub Khan resigned and abrogated the 1962 constitution in March 1969 by imposing martial law.

Why did Ali see the thief?
Why had Ali seen the thief?
Why was Ali seeing the thief?

To accept means to receive or agree to something, and its opposite is to reject or refuse.

The sister's age now is 2 x 12 = 24 years. After 8 years she will be 24 + 8 = 32 years.

MI5 is the security agency of which country?

MI6 (the Secret Intelligence Service) handles British foreign intelligence.
MOIS is the intelligence agency of which country?
MOIS is the Ministry of Intelligence of the Islamic Republic of Iran, also known as VAJA.
Pakistan's main intelligence agency is the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI).
Faiq and Ahmad were born in 1970 and 1977 respectively. What are their ages in 1999?

Which is the national airline of Russia?

Lufthansa is from Germany and Emirates from the UAE.
Who is the current Prime Minister of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) as of October 2026?

Who was the President of Azad Jammu and Kashmir before Dr Najeeb Naqi?

Sardar Muhammad Ibrahim Khan became the first President of Azad Kashmir in October 1947 after the Poonch uprising.

Aliya is the name of a person, so it is a proper noun.

The 26 letters have 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, U.
In which country does the world's largest volunteer ambulance service operate?

Boxer Amir Khan, a former world champion, belongs to which country?

Which word is the antonym of anarchy?
Anarchy means a state of disorder and absence of government, so its opposite is order.

How many interior angles does a square have?
A square is a quadrilateral with four corners, so it has four angles, each of 90 degrees.
The four angles of a square add up to 360 degrees.

Who is the Prime Minister of Australia (as of 2026)?

Autonomy means the right or ability of a person, group or region to govern itself and make its own decisions.

The order 5 x 4 means 5 rows and 4 columns. Each column runs down through all the rows, so it has 5 elements.
The total number of elements in a 5 x 4 matrix is 20.
Which letter and number come next in the series: Z1, X3, V5, T7, ?
The letters move back by 2 each time (Z, X, V, T, R) and the numbers increase by 2 (1, 3, 5, 7, 9). So the next term is R9.
Letter series that skip every other letter are common in verbal tests.
To command means to give an authoritative instruction, which is the same as to order.
Command also means control over a unit, as in the command of an army.
The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared in response to which commission?
The Simon Commission of 1927 had no Indian member, and Lord Birkenhead challenged Indians to frame a constitution. The Nehru Report was the Indian reply.
Quaid-e-Azam later put forward his Fourteen Points in 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.
What is common in the series 4, 8, 12, 16?
4 = 4 x 1, 8 = 4 x 2, 12 = 4 x 3 and 16 = 4 x 4, so every term is a multiple of 4 with a common difference of 4.
A series with a constant difference is called an arithmetic progression.
The Partition of Bengal in 1905 gave benefits to which community?
It created the Muslim-majority province of Eastern Bengal and Assam, giving Muslims better chances in education, jobs and politics.
Hindu agitation led the British to annul the partition in 1911.
900 employees work in a company and 480 of them are men. What is the percentage of women?
The percentage of men is 53.33%, and the two percentages add up to 100.
In which year did the East India Company annex the Punjab?
After the Second Anglo-Sikh War, the Punjab was annexed to the Company's territories in 1849.
Maharaja Ranjit Singh had ruled the Punjab until his death in 1839.
Who compiled the hadith collection Musnad Ahmad?
Musnad Ahmad was compiled by Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, founder of the Hanbali school of fiqh.
It contains tens of thousands of hadith arranged by narrator.
What is the largest composite number from 1 to 99?
97 is prime, 98 = 2 x 49 and 99 = 9 x 11 has factors other than 1 and itself. So 99 is the largest composite number.
A composite number has more than two factors.
On what date was the Indian National Congress established?
The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay on 28 December 1885.
Its first president was W. C. Bonnerjee.
Which caliph received the surrender of Jerusalem (Bait-ul-Muqaddas) in 637 AD?
Jerusalem was besieged by Muslim armies under Abu Ubaidah and Amr bin al-As and its people surrendered to Caliph Umar (RA) in person.
Khalid bin Waleed (RA) conquered Damascus region, not Jerusalem.
How many members did the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan originally have?
The first Constituent Assembly formed in 1947 had 69 members.
Its membership was later raised to 79 after the addition of more members.
In which year did the construction of Tarbela Dam begin?
The contract was awarded in May 1968 and main construction ran from 1968 to 1976.
Tarbela Dam is built on the Indus River and is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.
In which year was Rawal Dam built (completed)?
Rawal Dam on the Korang River in Islamabad is listed as completed in 1962.
Some sources give 1962 as the start of construction, so sources differ.
Who performs the duties of the President of Pakistan when the President is absent or unable to act?
Article 49 of the Constitution says the Chairman of the Senate acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent.
If the Chairman is unavailable, the Speaker of the National Assembly acts as President.
Radians = degrees x pi/180 = 60 x pi/180 = pi/3.
Convert to passive voice: He told me about the accident.
I was told about the accident by him.
I am told about the accident by him.
The accident was told by him to me about.
I had told about the accident by him.
The past simple active becomes was/were plus past participle in passive, with the object I becoming the subject.
Passive voice puts the receiver of the action at the start of the sentence.
Which device converts mechanical energy into electrical energy?
A generator (dynamo) turns a coil in a magnetic field and produces electric current from mechanical motion.
An electric motor does the opposite and converts electrical energy into mechanical energy.
Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission
Satellite and Upper Atmosphere Research Corporation
Space Utilization and Planetary Research Commission
Science and Upper Atmosphere Research Council
SUPARCO is Pakistan's national space agency, called the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission.
The Wakhan Corridor connects Pakistan to which province of Afghanistan?
The Wakhan Corridor is a narrow strip in Badakhshan province of north-eastern Afghanistan.
Between which two countries is the longest international border in the world?
The Canada-USA border is about 8,900 km long including the Alaska border, the longest in the world.
It is also the longest undefended border.
A train covers 120 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 15 minutes?
1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes, so the speed is 120 / 100 = 1.2 km per minute. In 15 minutes the train covers 1.2 x 15 = 18 km.
At this speed the train runs at 72 km/h.
A train covers 120 km in one hour. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes?
12 minutes is 1/5 of an hour. So the distance is 120 / 5 = 24 km.
Speed in km per minute is distance in km/h divided by 60, here 2 km per minute.
A train covers 90 km in 1 hour. How much time will it take to cover 120 km?
Time = distance / speed = 120 / 90 = 4/3 hours. 4/3 hours is 1 hour 20 minutes.
The same train covers 1.5 km every minute.
If a car covers 20 km in an hour, what distance does it cover in 30 minutes?
30 minutes is half an hour. So the distance is 20 / 2 = 10 km.
Distance equals speed multiplied by time.
If a car covers 90 km in one hour and 40 minutes, in how many minutes will it cover 1 km?
1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes for 90 km. So 1 km takes 100 / 90 = 10/9 minutes.
Which of the following British reforms introduced separate electorates for the Muslims of the subcontinent?
The Indian Councils Act of 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, granted Muslims separate electorates, which was a key demand of the Simla Deputation of 1906.
The Nehru Report of 1928 rejected separate electorates, while the Cripps Mission came in 1942.
Which is the major rabi (winter) crop of Pakistan?
Wheat is sown in October to December and harvested in April to May, which makes it the main rabi crop.
Cotton, rice and sugarcane are kharif (summer) crops.
On which date is World Red Cross and Red Crescent Day celebrated?
It is observed on 8 May, the birthday of Henry Dunant, the founder of the Red Cross.
Henry Dunant won the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.
After the 2026 tournament, which country or countries will host the next FIFA World Cup in 2030?
FIFA awarded the 2030 World Cup to Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with opening matches in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay to mark the centenary.
The 2026 World Cup was hosted jointly by the United States, Canada and Mexico, and Qatar hosted in 2022.
What is the currency of Belgium (Brussels) and Finland?
Both Belgium and Finland are members of the Eurozone and use the euro.
Belgium used the Belgian franc before adopting the euro in 2002.
What is the currency of Uganda?
Uganda's national currency is the Ugandan shilling.
The capital of Uganda is Kampala.
What is the name of China's currency?
China's official currency is the renminbi, whose main unit is the yuan.
The word renminbi means the people's currency.
Who is the current Director General of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) of Pakistan?
Fuad Asadullah Khan has led the IB since 2022 and in May 2026 the Prime Minister approved a four-year extension for him.
He was the first officer from the intelligence cadre to head the IB.
Who is the current Chancellor of Germany?
Friedrich Merz of the CDU became Chancellor in May 2025 and was still in office in October 2026.
His predecessor was Olaf Scholz (2021 to 2025), and before him Angela Merkel served from 2005 to 2021.
If a circle is divided into 360 equal parts, what is each part called?
A full circle measures 360 degrees, so each of 360 equal parts is one degree.
A quadrant is a quarter of a circle, or 90 degrees.
Which country announced the cutting of funding to the World Health Organization in 2020 and later withdrew from it?
In 2020 President Trump halted US funding to the WHO, and in 2025 the United States started its withdrawal.
The United States had been the largest single donor to the WHO.
In which country is the Khanpur (Kahnpur) Dam located?
Khanpur Dam is on the Haro River near Haripur in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.
Hazrat Asma (R.A), known as Dhat un-Nitaqayn, was the daughter of which Sahabi?
Asma bint Abu Bakr was the elder sister of Hazrat Aisha (R.A) and helped the Prophet (PBUH) during the Hijrah.
She was the mother of Abdullah ibn Zubair (R.A).
Hazrat Umm Kulthum (R.A), who was married to Hazrat Uthman (R.A), was the daughter of whom?
Umm Kulthum was a daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and married Hazrat Uthman after the death of her sister Ruqayyah.
This is why Hazrat Uthman is called Dhun-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights.
Which of the following was a daughter of Hazrat Ali (R.A) and Hazrat Fatima (R.A)?
Hazrat Zainab bint Ali was a daughter of Hazrat Ali and Hazrat Fatima and sister of Hasan and Husain.
Their other daughter was Umm Kulthum bint Ali.
How many days are there in a leap year?
A leap year has an extra day, 29 February, so it has 365 + 1 = 366 days.
A leap year comes every four years, for example 2024 and 2028.
What is the definition of a noun?
A word that describes an action
A word that names a person, place, thing or idea
A word that describes a noun
A word that joins two sentences
A noun is a naming word: it names a person, place, animal, thing or idea.
A verb shows action, an adjective describes a noun, and a conjunction joins words or clauses.
A matrix with equal number of rows and columns
A matrix with only one row
A matrix with all elements zero
A matrix with only one column
A square matrix has the same number of rows as columns, for example 3 by 3.
Only square matrices have determinants and can have inverses.
Which word is a synonym of 'demise'?
Demise means death or the end of something.
In which body were the Basic Democrats of Ayub Khan's system mainly represented?
Electoral college for President and assemblies
Basic Democrats, elected from union councils, formed the electoral college that elected the President and members of the assemblies.
The system was announced in 1959 and used in the 1965 presidential election.
How many Basic Democrats were there in Ayub Khan's system (40,000 in each wing)?
Ayub Khan's Basic Democracies had 80,000 members, 40,000 in East Pakistan and 40,000 in West Pakistan.
The number was later raised to 120,000, but 80,000 was the original figure.
What is the derivative of tan x with respect to x?
d/dx (tan x) = d/dx (sin x / cos x) = (cos^2 x + sin^2 x) / cos^2 x = sec^2 x.
The derivative of cot x is minus cosec squared x.
Which lake is known as the world's largest permanent desert lake?
Lake Turkana in northern Kenya lies in a desert region and is the largest permanent desert lake, nicknamed the Jade Sea.
It is a very alkaline lake in the Great Rift Valley.
What is the determinant of a diagonal matrix?
For a diagonal matrix all off-diagonal entries are zero, so the determinant is the product of the diagonal elements.
The sum of diagonal elements is called the trace.
A square matrix whose off-diagonal elements are all zero
A matrix with all elements equal
A matrix with one row only
A matrix whose determinant is always 1
A diagonal matrix is a square matrix in which every element outside the main diagonal is zero.
Scalar and identity matrices are special diagonal matrices.
If the side of a square is a, what is the length of its diagonal?
By Pythagoras, diagonal = square root of (a^2 + a^2) = a times root 2.
The diagonals of a square are equal and bisect each other at right angles.
What is the diameter of a circle whose radius is 28?
What is the radius of a circle with diameter 52 cm?
Area of this circle is pi x 26 x 26.
Which word comes first in the dictionary?
Compare the third letter: Addidas has d, which comes before i in Adiabatic, Adjust (j) and Adit (i).
Dictionary order compares letters from left to right.
On which date did the singer Lata Mangeshkar die?
Lata Mangeshkar, the Indian playback singer, died in Mumbai on 6 February 2022.
Where was democracy first practised in the world?
Democracy began in the ancient Greek city-state of Athens around the 5th century BC.
The word democracy comes from the Greek words demos (people) and kratos (rule).
The voice of which animal is described in the Holy Quran as the worst of voices?
Surah Luqman says the harshest of voices is surely the voice of the donkey.
The advice is given by Hazrat Luqman to his son in Surah Luqman.
What is the opposite of the word diversity?
Diversity means variety; its opposite is uniformity, meaning sameness.
Diversity is a synonym of variety.
If one dozen pencils cost Rs 60, what is the cost of 5 pencils?
One pencil costs 60 / 12 = Rs 5, so 5 pencils cost 5 x 5 = Rs 25.
If one dozen pencils cost Rs 27, what is the price of 4 pencils?
Four pencils are one third of a dozen, so the cost is 27 / 3 = Rs 9.
What is the national dress of Pakistan?
Shalwar Kameez is worn across all provinces and is recognised as the national dress of Pakistan.
Sherwani is the national dress for formal wear of men and is linked with Quaid-e-Azam.
What is the cutting of hair by a pilgrim at the end of Hajj called?
Halq means shaving the head, and qasr means trimming the hair; one of them is done to leave the state of Ihram.
Women only trim a fingertip length of hair.
What is the measure in degrees of each angle (corner) of a square?
A square has four equal angles and they sum to 360 degrees, so each is 360 / 4 = 90 degrees.
A rectangle also has four right angles.
ECO stands for Economic Cooperation Organization, a regional group of Asian countries.
It succeeded the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) of 1964.
Abdul Sattar Edhi, the famous humanitarian known as the Angel of Mercy, belonged to which country?
Edhi spent his life in Pakistan and founded the Edhi Foundation in Karachi. He is regarded as one of the greatest humanitarians of Pakistan.
Edhi died in Karachi on 8 July 2016.
If one egg takes 2 minutes to boil, how many minutes will 5 eggs take when boiled together in the same pot?
Eggs boil at the same time in the same pot, so the time does not depend on the number of eggs. All 5 eggs take 2 minutes.
This is a classic logic puzzle where the obvious multiplication is wrong.
Akbar is older than Ahmad and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the eldest?
Umair is older than Akbar, and Akbar is older than Ahmad. So the order is Umair, Akbar, Ahmad and Umair is the eldest.
Chain the comparisons to rank all persons.
If Akbar is elder than Ahmad and Adnan is elder than Akbar, then who is the eldest?
Adnan is elder than Akbar, and Akbar is elder than Ahmad. So Adnan is the eldest.
The youngest in this chain is Ahmad.
In which pact were separate electorates for Muslims granted?
Under the Lucknow Pact of 1916 the Congress accepted the Muslim League's demand for separate electorates for Muslims.
Separate electorates were first given in the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.
What is a set that has no element called?
A set with no element is called the null set or empty set and is written as a circle with a slash or as curly brackets with nothing inside.
The empty set is a subset of every set.
What is a set with exactly one element called?
A set containing only one element, such as the set containing 5 alone, is called a singleton set.
A singleton set has exactly two subsets.
If every element of set A is also an element of set B, then A is called what of B?
When all elements of A belong to B, A is a subset of B, written A is contained in B.
B is then called a superset of A.
Which one is different from the rest: cow, snake, elephant, monkey?
Cow, elephant and monkey are mammals, while a snake is a reptile.
Mammals are warm-blooded and feed milk to their young.
What is the meaning of the word 'embellish'?
To make more attractive by adding decoration
Embellish means to decorate or beautify something, or to add extra details to a story.
Adorn and ornament are synonyms of embellish.
When was the partition of Bengal enforced by Lord Curzon?
Lord Curzon divided Bengal into East Bengal and Assam and West Bengal, and the partition took effect on 16 October 1905.
Which of the following are the vowels of the English alphabet?
The five vowel letters of English are A, E, I, O and U.
The English alphabet has 26 letters, so 21 are consonants.
If RAT is coded as TAR (letters reversed), then what is FAT equal to?
RAT becomes TAR by reversing the order of letters. Reversing FAT gives TAF.
Reversal codes are the simplest letter codes.
In trigonometry, what is tan x equal to?
cos x divided by sin x
sin x divided by cos x
Tangent is the ratio of sine to cosine, so tan x equals sin x divided by cos x.
Cot x is the reciprocal of tan x.
What is cosecant x equal to?
sin x divided by cos x
Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine, so cosec x = 1 / sin x.
Sec x = 1 / cos x and cot x = 1 / tan x.
Simplifying gives x - 7 = 0, which has highest power 1 of x, so it is linear and gives x = 7.
A linear equation in one variable has exactly one root.
Who headed the committee for the collection of the Holy Quran in the era of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) appointed Zaid bin Thabit, the Prophet's scribe of revelation, to collect the Quran into one volume.
Zaid also led the committee in the era of Hazrat Usman (RA).
How many end points does a ray have?
A ray starts at one fixed point and extends endlessly in one direction, so it has one end point.
A line segment has two end points and a line has none.
Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was among his bitter enemies?
Abu Lahab (Abdul Uzza) strongly opposed the Prophet (PBUH) and a Surah of the Quran is named after him. Abu Jahal was not his uncle.
Which event did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) take part in after the Harb-e-Fijar?
After the Harb-e-Fijar, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) took part in Hilf-ul-Fudul, a pact formed in Makkah to help the oppressed and protect travellers and the weak. He was a young man at the time.
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) later said that he would still accept such a pact even in Islam.
What is the measure of each external angle of a regular hexagon?
The sum of the external angles of any polygon is 360 degrees. A hexagon has 6 sides, so each external angle is 360 divided by 6 = 60 degrees.
Each internal angle of a regular hexagon is 120 degrees.
What is the measure of each external angle of a regular octagon?
The sum of the external angles of any polygon is 360 degrees. An octagon has 8 sides, so each external angle is 360 divided by 8 = 45 degrees.
Each internal angle of a regular octagon is 135 degrees.
What is meant by Laissez-faire in economics?
Minimum government interference in the economy
Laissez-faire is a French term meaning let do. It is the policy that the government should interfere as little as possible in economic affairs and leave markets free.
Adam Smith is the economist most associated with ideas of free markets.
Which word comes first in the dictionary: False, Fallow, Faithful, Fallable, Falcon?
All words begin with Fa. The third letters are i (Faithful), l (the rest), so Faithful comes first. Then Falcon, Fallable, Fallow and False follow.
Dictionary order compares letters one by one from the left.
Hazrat Ali (RA) belonged to which family (clan) of Quraish?
Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, who was a son of Abdul Muttalib of Banu Hashim. He was thus a cousin of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) also belonged to Banu Hashim.
For what industry is Gaddani in Balochistan famous?
Gaddani, on the coast of Balochistan near Karachi, has one of the largest ship breaking yards in the world, where old ships are dismantled.
For which product is Sialkot famous?
Sialkot is world famous for sports goods, such as footballs, and also for surgical instruments and leather goods.
Footballs made in Sialkot have been used in FIFA World Cups.
For what is Ziyarat in Balochistan famous?
Ziyarat is a hill town famous for the Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Quaid-e-Azam spent his last days in 1948, and for one of the largest juniper forests in the world.
The Residency was damaged by a terrorist attack in 2013 and later rebuilt.
A car travels at 120 km/h and another car travels twice as fast. How far will the second car travel in 30 minutes?
The second car's speed is 2 x 120 = 240 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it travels 240 x 1/2 = 120 km.
Son is to father as nephew is to what?
A son is the child of his father, and a nephew is the child of the brother or sister of an uncle or aunt, so the relation is nephew to uncle.
The female counterpart of a nephew is a niece.
What was the name of the father of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
The father of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was Hazrat Abdullah bin Abdul Muttalib, who died before the Prophet was born.
His mother was Hazrat Amina bint Wahab.
Surah Al-Fatiha is also called by which name?
Surah Al-Fatiha is also called Umm-ul-Kitab (Mother of the Book) and Umm-ul-Quran because it sums up the message of the Quran.
It is also called Sab'a Mathani and is recited in every rakat of Namaz.
For which crime was Fatimah bint Aswad (a woman of Banu Makhzum) punished in the time of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Fatimah bint Aswad of Banu Makhzum was found guilty of theft, and the Holy Prophet (PBUH) ordered the punishment for theft. He refused to let rank or family influence the decision.
He said that nations before them were destroyed because they punished the poor but spared the rich.
Which day is observed in Pakistan on 5th February every year?
Pakistan observes 5 February as Kashmir Solidarity Day to express support for the people of Indian-administered Kashmir.
Pakistan Day is on 23 March and Defence Day on 6 September.
Who was the first Field Marshal of Pakistan?
Muhammad Ayub Khan promoted himself to the rank of Field Marshal in 1959.
Asim Munir was promoted to Field Marshal in May 2025, making him the second.
Subtract x from both sides: 2x - 9 = 7, so 2x = 16 and x = 8.
Cross multiplying gives 14x = 56, which also gives x = 4.
What is the mean of 1, 3, 5 and 6?
The mean is the sum of values divided by the number of values.
Which letter comes after M in the English alphabet?
The alphabet runs L, M, N, so N follows M.
Arrange the letters 'IYTC' to form a meaningful word.
Rearranging I, Y, T, C gives the word CITY.
An anagram uses all the given letters exactly once.
Which is the largest fort of Pakistan?
Ranikot Fort in Sindh has walls about 26 km long and is often called the largest fort in the world.
It is also known as the Great Wall of Sindh.
Between whom was the Ghazwa (Battle) of Badr fought?
The Muslims of Madinah and the Quraish of Makkah
The Muslims and the Jews of Khyber
The Muslims and the Byzantine army
The Muslims and the tribe of Thaqif at Taif
Badr was fought in 2 AH between the small Muslim army led by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and the much larger army of the Quraish of Makkah.
Badr is called Yaum-ul-Furqan, the day that separated right from wrong.
Near which city is the mountain where the Battle of Uhud was fought?
The Battle of Uhud was fought at the foot of Mount Uhud, a few kilometres north of Madinah.
The battle took place in 3 AH between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.
Which fraction comes next in the series: 3/5, 5/8, 8/12, 12/17, ?
Numerators are 3, 5, 8, 12, 17 with differences 2, 3, 4, 5, so the next is 17. Each denominator equals the next numerator, and the denominators 5, 8, 12, 17 continue with 17+6 = 23.
Each fraction's numerator equals the previous fraction's denominator.
What is the currency of France?
France uses the euro, which replaced the French franc in 2002.
The euro is shared by most countries of the European Union eurozone.
If the first day of a month is Friday, which day will the 17th be?
The 15th is 14 days (two full weeks) after the 1st, so it is also a Friday. The 17th is two days later, a Sunday.
A week has 7 days, so dates 7 apart fall on the same weekday.
Change the narration (direct speech) of: He bade farewell to his friends.
He said to his friends that good-bye.
He told his friends, "Farewell to you."
To bid farewell means to say good-bye, so in direct speech it becomes: He said to his friends, "Good-bye."
Similar idioms: bade welcome becomes said, "Welcome", and wished becomes said, "Good luck."
What is the full form of PIA?
PIA stands for Pakistan International Airlines, the national flag carrier of Pakistan.
PIA began as Orient Airways in 1946 and took its present name in 1955.
In which city were the Olympic Games named Tokyo 2020 held?
The 2020 Summer Olympics were awarded to Tokyo, Japan. Because of COVID-19 they were postponed and held in Tokyo from July to August 2021.
How many doors (gates) does the Holy Kaaba have?
The Kaaba has a single door, on its north-east wall, about two metres above ground level.
The door is made of gold-plated material and is opened only on special occasions.
Who served as both Governor General and Prime Minister of Pakistan?
Khawaja Nazimuddin was Governor General from 1948 to 1951 and then Prime Minister from 1951 to 1953.
He became Governor General after the death of Quaid-e-Azam.
Who is the President of Germany?
Frank-Walter Steinmeier has been the Federal President of Germany since March 2017 and was re-elected in 2022. His second term ends in March 2027.
The President is the head of state, while the Chancellor (currently Friedrich Merz) is the head of government.
In which Ghazwa was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) wounded?
In the Battle of Uhad (3 AH) the Prophet (PBUH) was wounded in the face and his blessed tooth was broken.
The Muslim archers left their post on the hill during Uhad, which let the Quraish attack from behind.
What is jute commonly known as?
Jute is called the golden fibre because of its shiny golden-brown colour and its high value as a cash crop.
Bangladesh and India are the largest producers of jute.
Who was the maternal grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
The Prophet's mother was Hazrat Amina bint Wahb, so her father Wahb bin Abd Manaf was his maternal grandfather.
Wahb belonged to the Banu Zuhra clan of Quraish.
The sign greater than or equal to is used in which type of mathematical statement?
The sign for greater than or equal to compares two quantities without saying that they are exactly equal, so it forms an inequality.
The sign for less than or equal to is also used in inequalities.
To which language group does the Sindhi language belong, among the given options?
Sindhi is an Indo-Aryan language that developed from Sanskrit and Prakrit. Of the given options, Sanskrit is the ancestral language group.
Sindhi is the official language of Sindh province and is written in a Perso-Arabic script.
What is the first group of the periodic table called?
Group 1 contains lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium and francium, which are called alkali metals.
Hydrogen sits at the top of Group 1 but is not an alkali metal.
Choose the correct word: They ___ seeds in flowers.
The subject They is plural, so the simple present plural verb grow is needed.
The verb grows is used with singular subjects such as he, she or it.
The old fort of Gwadar/Chabahar region lies on the coast of the Gulf of which?
Gwadar and Chabahar lie on the coast near the Gulf of Oman, at the mouth of the Persian Gulf.
Pakistan bought Gwadar from Oman in 1958.
Which hadith is called Muttafaq Alaih?
A hadith narrated by both Imam Bukhari and Imam Muslim
A hadith narrated by only one companion
A hadith narrated by Imam Tirmidhi
Muttafaq Alaih (agreed upon) is a hadith recorded in both Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.
Such hadith are considered to be of the highest authenticity.
Who received the Nishan-e-Haider for bravery in the Kargil War of 1999?
Captain Karnal Sher Khan Shaheed was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider for his bravery in Kargil.
Havaldar Lalak Jan Shaheed also received the Nishan-e-Haider for Kargil.
What is the straight line that divides a circle into two equal halves called?
A chord passing through the centre of a circle is the diameter and it cuts the circle into two equal semicircles.
The diameter equals twice the radius.
Who is the author of the novel The Pursuit of Happiness (2001)?
The novel The Pursuit of Happiness was written by the author Douglas Kennedy.
Do not confuse it with The Conquest of Happiness by Bertrand Russell.
What is the HCF of 12 and 16?
12 = 2 x 2 x 3 and 16 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2. The common factors are 2 x 2, so the HCF is 4.
Where is the headquarters of the International Labour Organization (ILO) located?
The ILO, a specialised agency of the United Nations, has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.
The ILO was founded in 1919 and became a UN agency in 1946.
Where is the headquarters of the African Union located?
The African Union has its headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
The African Union replaced the Organisation of African Unity in 2002.
According to the Quran, who will be in the lowest depths of the Fire?
Surah An-Nisa says the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire.
Hypocrites outwardly claimed faith while hiding disbelief.
With the help of which country did Pakistan carry out the Saindak project?
The Saindak copper-gold project in Balochistan was developed with Chinese help by the Metallurgical Corporation of China.
Saindak is in Chagai district, Balochistan.

The Prophet (PBUH) is also addressed in the Quran with titles such as Nabi and Rasool.
How many metres are there in 2 km?
What is the midpoint of the points (4, 6) and (2, 6)?
Both points have the same y value, so the segment is horizontal.
What is the meaning of 'broke down' in the sentence: The car broke down one mile away from home?
To break down means a machine or vehicle stops working because of a fault. So the car stopped working one mile from home.
Break down can also mean to lose emotional control or to analyse something in parts.
Which country has the largest number of active military personnel in the world?
China's People's Liberation Army has about two million active personnel, the most in the world. India and the United States follow.
Rankings change slowly, and India has the second-largest active force in most recent lists.
Which of the following is a military alliance?
NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) is a collective defence military alliance founded in 1949. SAARC is regional cooperation, OPEC deals with oil and WTO with trade.
Its Article 5 says an attack on one member is an attack on all.
What is the minimum age to become President of Pakistan?
Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution says the President must be a Muslim, qualified to be a National Assembly member and at least 45 years old.
The President is elected by an electoral college of Parliament and the provincial assemblies.
Who is the Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue of Pakistan?
Muhammad Aurangzeb took charge as Finance Minister in March 2024 and presented the FY2026-27 budget. He is still in office in October 2026.
In 2022 the finance minister was Miftah Ismail, followed by Ishaq Dar.
A train covers 20 km in one hour. About how much distance does it cover in 1 minute?
1 hour is 60 minutes, so distance per minute is 20 divided by 60, which is 0.33 km. This is about 333 metres.
Speed in km/h divided by 60 gives km per minute.
If 1 man writes 5 papers in 5 minutes, how many papers does he write in one minute?
Rate is 5 papers divided by 5 minutes, which is 1 paper per minute.
Rate equals work divided by time.
If 5 men write 5 pages in 1 minute, how much time will 1 man take to write 1 page?
5 men write 5 pages in 1 minute, so each man writes 1 page in 1 minute. One man therefore needs 1 minute for 1 page.
If each worker works at the same rate, work per worker is total work divided by number of workers.
What was the real name of the Bengali freedom fighter Tito Mir?
Tito Mir's real name was Syed Mir Nisar Ali. He led a peasant uprising against landlords and the British in Bengal in 1831.
He built a bamboo fort at Narkelberia and died fighting in 1831.
If a helicopter needs 80 gallons of fuel to move 320 km, how many gallons are needed to cover 400 km?
Fuel per km is 80 divided by 320 = 0.25 gallons. For 400 km, 400 x 0.25 = 100 gallons.
Fuel used is directly proportional to distance.
If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 9th be?
The 9th is 7 days after the 2nd. After a full week the day repeats, so it is Monday.
Any two dates 7 days apart fall on the same weekday.
In which year did Lord Mountbatten arrive in India as the last Viceroy?
Lord Mountbatten arrived in India in March 1947 to oversee the transfer of power. He announced the Partition plan on 3 June 1947.
He later became the first Governor General of independent India.
A train moves at 120 km/h. What distance does it cover in 120 minutes?
120 minutes is 2 hours. Distance = 120 x 2 = 240 km.
Convert minutes to hours by dividing by 60.
A train is moving at a speed of 60 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 10 minutes?
10 minutes is 1/6 hour. Distance = 60 x 1/6 = 10 km.
At 60 km/h a train covers 1 km each minute.
In which year was Islamabad officially made the capital of Pakistan, replacing Rawalpindi as interim capital?
Karachi was first capital, then Rawalpindi served as interim capital while Islamabad was built. Islamabad officially became the capital in 1967.
Sources differ on the exact year, since the decision was taken in 1959-60 and the shift happened in stages.
Who moved the Objective Resolution in the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan in 1949?
Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan moved the Objective Resolution, and it was passed on 12 March 1949.
It later became the preamble of the 1973 Constitution.
Which of the following is one of the Ashra Mubashra?
Hazrat Talha bin Ubaidullah (RA) is among the ten Companions given the glad tidings of Paradise. The others listed are not in the group.
The ten include Abu Bakr, Umar, Usman, Ali, Zubair, Talha, Abdur Rahman bin Auf, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, Saeed bin Zaid and Abu Ubaidah.
What is the relation between multiplication and division?
Division undoes multiplication, so they are inverse operations. For example, 6 x 4 = 24 and 24 / 4 = 6.
Addition and subtraction are also inverse operations.
What is the title of Hazrat Musa (AS)?
Hazrat Musa (AS) is called Kalimullah because Allah spoke to him directly.
Khalilullah is Ibrahim, Safiullah is Adam and Ruhullah is Isa.
Who was the mother of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
The Holy Prophet's mother was Hazrat Amina bint Wahb. Halima Sadia was his wet nurse.
Hazrat Amina passed away when he was about 6 years old.
Which one is different from the following: actor, director, music, producer?
Actor, director and producer are all people who work on a film, while music is a thing, not a person.
Odd-one-out questions are solved by finding the item of a different category.
Who was the Habshi (Abyssinian) king Najashi, who gave shelter to the early Muslim migrants?
Najashi was the title of the Abyssinian king, whose real name was Ashama bin Abjar.
When he died in 9 AH, the Prophet (SAW) offered his funeral prayer in absentia.
An optional prayer offered after sunrise
A prayer offered during an eclipse
Ishraq is an optional (nafl) prayer offered about 15 to 20 minutes after sunrise, after the Fajr prayer.
Namaz-e-Istisqa is the prayer for rain.
Where is the National Museum of Pakistan located?
The National Museum of Pakistan is in Karachi, in the Burnes Garden area.
The Lahore Museum is a separate and older museum.
How many member countries does NATO have at present?
NATO has 32 members, after Finland joined in 2023 and Sweden in 2024.
NATO was founded in 1949 with 12 members.
Is sin x positive or negative in the first quadrant?
In the first quadrant the y-coordinate is positive and sin x equals y divided by r, so it is positive.
In the first quadrant all six trigonometric ratios are positive.
The line x = 3 is ______ to the X axis.
The line x = 3 is a vertical line, and a vertical line meets the horizontal X axis at a right angle.
The line x = 3 is parallel to the Y axis.
Fill in the blank: Mrs. Rehan is not pleased ___ the new servant.
The adjective pleased is followed by the preposition with when it refers to a person. So the correct sentence is: not pleased with the new servant.
Other common adjective and preposition pairs are angry with, good at and afraid of.
What is a bill called after it has been passed by Parliament and approved by the President of Pakistan?
A bill passed by both houses and assented to by the President becomes an Act of Parliament, which is law. An ordinance is a temporary law issued by the President when Parliament is not in session.
Under Article 75 of the Constitution the President has ten days to assent to a bill or return it.
What comes next in the series: 3A, 5C, 7E, ?
The numbers increase by 2 (3, 5, 7, 9) and the letters skip one letter each time (A, C, E, G). So the next term is 9G.
The letters A, C, E, G are the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of the alphabet.
What comes next in the series: 3x+4, 4x+2, ?
The coefficient of x increases by 1 each time (3, 4, 5) and the constant decreases by 2 (4, 2, 0). So the next term is 5x+0 = 5x.
Such a pattern is two arithmetic progressions running together.
What comes next in the series: B2, C3, D4, E5, F?
Each letter moves one step forward and each number increases by 1. F pairs with 6, so the next term is F6.
B is the 2nd letter, C the 3rd, and so on, so each letter pairs with its own position number.
What comes next in the series: 3W, 6X, 9Z, ?
The numbers increase by 3 (3, 6, 9, 12). The letters move forward by 1, then 2, then 3: W to X to Z to C (after Z the alphabet starts again). So the next term is 12C.
In such letter series, the alphabet is treated as a circle, so Z is followed by A.
These are the squares 1x1, 2x2, 3x3, 4x4. The next is 5x5 = 25.
The gaps between squares are the odd numbers 3, 5, 7, 9.
The terms in odd positions go 155, 165 and the terms in even positions go 65, 75, each rising by 10. So the next term is 165 + 10 = 175.
This is an alternating series made of two separate series.
Each number is 2 more than the one before it. So 8 + 2 = 10.
These are the first even natural numbers.
Each number is 3 more than the one before. So 12 + 3 = 15.
Each number is 3 more than the one before. So 9 + 3 = 12.
Each number is 5 more than the one before. So 15 + 5 = 20.
The differences are 3, 6, 12, 24, each double the last. The next difference is 48, so 21 - 48 = -27.
The same series appears as 66, 63, 57, 45, 21 where the next term after 45 is 21.
Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar served as the Governor of which province of Pakistan?
Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar, a leader of the Pakistan Movement, was Governor of Punjab from 1949 to 1951.
Nishtar Medical University in Multan is named after him.
In which Hijri year was Zakat made obligatory?
According to the commonly taught view, Zakat became obligatory in the second year of Hijri, around the time Ramadan fasting was ordained. Some scholars give slightly different years.
Sources differ a little on the exact year of Zakat.
School is a noun. Which pronoun can be used in its place?
A school is a singular, non-living thing, so the pronoun it is used for it.
The plural pronoun for schools is they.
What is the word used in place of a noun called?
A pronoun is used in place of a noun to avoid repeating it, such as he, she, it and they.
Words like he, she and it are personal pronouns.
What is the total number of nuclear-armed countries in the world today?
Nine countries have nuclear weapons: the USA, Russia, the UK, France, China, India, Pakistan, Israel (undeclared) and North Korea.
Pakistan is the only Muslim country with nuclear weapons.
13, 15, 17 and 19 are what type of numbers?
Each of these numbers leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 2, so they are odd numbers.
The only even prime number is 2.
If a set has two elements, how many elements are in its power set?
The power set of a set with n elements has 2 to the power n elements. For n = 2 this is 4: the empty set, two single-element subsets, and the set itself.
A set with 3 elements has a power set of 8 elements.
Which languages were declared official languages of Pakistan by the 1962 constitution?
The 1962 constitution recognised Urdu and Bengali as the national languages of Pakistan.
The 1956 constitution had also named Urdu and Bengali as state languages.
Which is generally regarded as the oldest city of Pakistan according to Pakistani textbooks?
Peshawar is commonly described as the oldest living city of Pakistan, inhabited for over 2,500 years.
Sources differ, as Multan is also claimed to be among the oldest cities in South Asia.
For whom are the Special Olympics held?
The Special Olympics are sports competitions for people with intellectual disabilities.
The Paralympic Games are held for athletes with physical disabilities.
What is the capital of Oman?
Muscat is the capital and largest city of Oman.
Oman is ruled by a Sultan and is located on the south-eastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula.
Change into passive voice: Open the door.
An imperative sentence is changed into the passive using Let + object + be + past participle, giving Let the door be opened.
Imperative sentences express commands, requests or advice.
What does Allama Iqbal Open University mainly promote?
Allama Iqbal Open University in Islamabad provides distance and open education to students who cannot attend regular institutions.
It was established in 1974 as the People's Open University and renamed in 1977.
Fill in the blank: She opened the door ____.
A word describing how an action is done must be an adverb, so slowly is correct.
Most adverbs of manner are formed by adding ly to an adjective.
What is the opposite of contiguous?
Contiguous means sharing a border or touching, so its opposite is separated or detached.
Contiguous comes from the Latin contingere, meaning to touch.
Subtraction is carried out from left to right.
What is the order of a square matrix having n rows?
A square matrix has equal rows and columns, so its order is n x n.
A 3 x 3 matrix is a square matrix of order 3.
What are the coordinates of the origin on a Cartesian graph?
The origin is the point where the x-axis and y-axis cross, so both its x and y values are zero.
The two axes divide the plane into four quadrants that meet at the origin.
Who built the Quba Mosque, the first mosque in Islam?
The Prophet (PBUH) laid the foundation of the Quba Mosque near Madinah on his Hijrah, and the Companions helped build it.
The Quran (Surah At-Tawbah) refers to a mosque founded on piety from the first day, which scholars identify as Quba.
In which period was the first war between Pakistan and India over Kashmir fought?
The first Indo-Pak war over Kashmir began in October 1947 after tribal and Pakistani forces entered the state and India sent troops. It ended with a UN-brokered ceasefire on 1 January 1949.
The ceasefire line later became the Line of Control after the Simla Agreement of 1972.
The Dawn newspaper is owned by which family-run group?
Dawn is published by Dawn Media Group, which is controlled by the Haroon family (with the Saigol family). The Haroon family bought majority shares in 1946.
Dawn was founded by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah in Delhi in 1941.
What was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931?
An agreement that ended the Civil Disobedience Movement and let Gandhi attend the Second Round Table Conference
A pact between Congress and the Muslim League
The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931 between Mahatma Gandhi and the Viceroy Lord Irwin. Congress suspended civil disobedience and the government released political prisoners.
Gandhi then attended the Second Round Table Conference in London in 1931.
Which area of Pakistan is called the Switzerland of Pakistan?
Swat valley is known as the Switzerland of Pakistan for its mountains, rivers and green scenery.
Faisalabad, by contrast, is known as the Manchester of Pakistan.
Under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, which institution is supreme?
The 1973 Constitution set up a parliamentary system in which the Parliament is the supreme law-making body and the Prime Minister heads the government.
In practice the Constitution itself is supreme, and Parliament must act within it.
What is the parliament of Israel called?
The Israeli parliament is called the Knesset and it has 120 members.
On what date was the Indian Independence Act passed by the British Parliament?
The Indian Independence Act received royal assent on 18 July 1947 and created the two dominions of Pakistan and India.
The 3 June 1947 plan was announced by Lord Mountbatten before the Act.
What is the Kunyat (kuniyyat) of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
The Prophet (PBUH) was called Abu al-Qasim after his eldest son Qasim.
Abu Turab was the kunyat of Hazrat Ali (RA), and Abu Hafs of Hazrat Umar (RA).
What is the perimeter of a circle called?
The distance around a circle is called its circumference, equal to 2 x pi x radius.
The diameter is twice the radius.
What is the period of the function sin x?
The sine function repeats its values after every 2 pi radians (360 degrees), so sin(x + 2 pi) = sin x.
The period of tan x is pi.
Aleem Dar is a famous personality in which field?
Aleem Dar is a Pakistani international cricket umpire, who won the ICC Umpire of the Year award three times.
He officiated in more than 130 Test matches.
If 5 persons write 5 papers in 5 days, how many papers will 1 person write in 5 days?
Each person writes 1 paper in 5 days (5 persons write 5 papers in 5 days). So 1 person writes 1 paper in 5 days.
In 25 days, 1 person would write 5 papers.
Which pass connects Peshawar with Afghanistan?
The Khyber Pass, with the Torkham crossing, connects Peshawar with Afghanistan.
The Bolan Pass connects Quetta with Afghanistan and the Khunjerab Pass links Pakistan with China.
Which pillar of Islam is related to the event of Meraj?
Five daily prayers were made obligatory during the Meraj (Night Journey).
Originally 50 prayers were prescribed and were reduced to five.
Badr, where the first major battle of Islam was fought, is the name of what?
A plain with wells near Madinah
Badr is a plain valley with wells about 150 km from Madinah where the Battle of Badr took place in 2 AH.
Mount Uhud, in contrast, is a mountain near Madinah.
Which is the brightest planet in the sky?
Venus is the brightest planet as seen from Earth because it is close and its thick clouds reflect much sunlight.
It is often called the morning or evening star.
Inzamam-ul-Haq is a famous player of which game?
Inzamam-ul-Haq is a former Pakistan cricket captain and batter.
He was a member of the 1992 World Cup winning Pakistan team.
What is the land of the pure people (Sarzamin-e-Pak) a name for?
The name Pakistan means land of the pure, from Urdu pak (pure) and stan (land).
The name was coined by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.
Khushal Khan Khattak is a famous poet of which language?
Khushal Khan Khattak (1613-1689) was a warrior-poet who wrote in Pashto.
He is regarded as the national poet of the Pashtuns.
Baba Fariduddin Ganj Shakar is regarded as the first major poet of which language?
Baba Farid (1173-1266) of Pakpattan is considered the first major poet of the Punjabi language.
Some of his verses are included in the Guru Granth Sahib.
Which of the following points lies on the line y = 6x?
For (2, 12): 6 times 2 = 12, so it satisfies y = 6x. The others do not.
The line y = 6x has slope 6 and passes through the origin.
What is the population of Punjab province according to the 2023 census?
The 2023 census counted about 127.7 million people in Punjab, the most populous province.
Punjab holds roughly half of Pakistan's population.
Which of the following is a major port of Sri Lanka?
Colombo is the largest and busiest port of Sri Lanka.
Hambantota is another important port of Sri Lanka.
When did Pakistan issue its first postage stamps?
Pakistan's first set of postage stamps was issued on 9 July 1948.
Before that, British Indian stamps overprinted with the word Pakistan were used in 1947.
What is the value of x to the power 0 (for x not equal to 0)?
Any non-zero number raised to the power 0 equals 1, because x to the power n divided by x to the power n equals x to the power 0, which equals 1.
The expression 0 to the power 0 is treated as undefined or indeterminate in many contexts.
Which countries hold veto power in the UN Security Council?
The five permanent members of the Security Council (P5) have veto power: USA, UK, France, Russia and China.
A single veto from any permanent member blocks a substantive resolution.
Which regional organization was the predecessor of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO)?
RCD, formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey, was revived and expanded as ECO in 1985.
Pakistan, Iran and Turkey were the founding members of both RCD and ECO.
How many compiled copies of the Quran were prepared in the time of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
Under Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) the Quran was collected into one single compiled copy, kept with him and then with Hazrat Umar and Hazrat Hafsa (RA).
Copies were multiplied and sent to different regions later, during the time of Hazrat Uthman (RA).
Which is the present constitution of Pakistan?
Pakistan is currently governed by the Constitution of 1973, which came into force on 14 August 1973.
It has been amended many times, including the 18th Amendment in 2010.
If the price of 3 eggs is 4 rupees, what is the price of 18 eggs?
18 eggs is 6 times 3 eggs, so the price is 6 times 4 = 24 rupees.
This is a direct proportion problem solved by the unitary method.
Which country produces the most olives in the world?
Spain is the largest producer of olives and olive oil, mainly from the region of Andalusia.
Spain produces roughly half of the world's olive oil in a good year.
What is the value of i x i, where i is the imaginary unit?
The imaginary unit is defined by i squared equals -1, so i x i = -1.
Higher powers repeat in a cycle: i cubed is -i and i to the fourth power is 1.
What is the antonym of the word prohibit?
To prohibit means to forbid something, so its opposite is to permit or allow it.
Prohibit comes from the Latin prohibere, meaning to hold back.
Which word is a synonym of prohibit?
Prohibit means to officially stop something from being done, which is the same as forbid.
Ban and bar are other synonyms of prohibit.
Kharan is a district of which province of Pakistan?
Kharan is a district and town in the west of Balochistan province.
The Kharan Desert, where Pakistan tested nuclear devices in 1998 near Chagai, lies in this region of Balochistan.
How many seats does the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Provincial Assembly have?
After the 25th Amendment merged FATA into KP in 2018, the assembly grew from 124 to 145 seats (115 general, 26 women, 4 non-Muslim).
Before the merger the assembly had 124 seats.
Which word is a synonym of provoke?
To provoke means to stir up a strong reaction, which is the same as to incite.
Instigate and arouse are other synonyms of provoke.
What was the age of Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan at the time of Pakistan's first nuclear tests in May 1998?
Born on 1 April 1936, he was 62 years old on 28 May 1998.
The tests were carried out at Chagai in Balochistan.
From whom did Muhammad bin Qasim conquer Sindh?
Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir, the Hindu ruler of Sindh, in 711-712 AD.
Raja Dahir was defeated near Raor.
Derawar Fort is a large fort in the Cholistan Desert near Ahmedpur East in Bahawalpur district, Punjab.
The fort was built by Rajput Bhatti rulers and is now on Pakistan's tentative UNESCO list.
Where was Masjid Quba, the first mosque in Islam, built?
Masjid Quba was built in the village of Quba on the outskirts of Madinah. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) laid its foundation when he arrived there during the Hijrat.
Masjid Quba is regarded as the first mosque built in Islam.
The Khojak Pass connects Quetta with which Afghan city?
The Khojak Pass in Balochistan lies on the route from Quetta to Chaman and on to Kandahar in Afghanistan. The Khojak Tunnel runs beneath it.
The Bolan Pass links Quetta with Sibi and the plains of Sindh and Punjab.
For how many years did the Quraish of Makkah socially and economically boycott the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Banu Hashim?
The Quraish boycotted Banu Hashim and Banu Muttalib for about three years, and the family stayed in Shib Abi Talib. The boycott ended in the tenth year of prophethood.
Hazrat Abu Talib and Hazrat Khadija (RA) both died soon after the boycott ended.
Who is said to have been the first to memorise the whole Quran (hifz)?
The Quran was revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH), who memorised it as it came and recited it to Hazrat Jibril (AS). He is therefore regarded as the first hafiz.
Among the companions, sources name several early huffaz, so this answer refers to the first hafiz overall.
What is a circle with zero radius called?
If the radius is zero, all points of the circle coincide with the centre, so it is a single point called a point circle.
A circle with radius 1 is called a unit circle.
If my age is 10 years and my brother's age is 2 times my age, what will be the ratio of my age to my brother's age after 10 years?
My brother is 2 x 10 = 20 years old now. After 10 years I will be 20 and he will be 30, so the ratio is 20 : 30 = 2 : 3.
The ratio of ages moves closer to 1 : 1 as both people grow older.
Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) was an organisation of which three countries?
RCD was formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey to promote economic, technical and cultural cooperation.
RCD was later renamed ECO, which expanded in 1992 to include Central Asian states and Afghanistan.
Change into active voice: The book is being read by her.
The passive form is being read becomes the active is reading, and the agent her becomes the subject she. The tense stays present continuous.
In active voice the doer of the action is the subject of the sentence.
Change into passive voice: We are reading a book.
A book was being read by us.
A book is read by us.
A book is being read by us.
A book has been read by us.
Present continuous passive uses is or are being plus the past participle. The object a book becomes the subject and we becomes by us.
Passive voice puts the focus on the action or receiver rather than the doer.
What is the value of the real number -(4! + 6)?
What is the real part of the complex number 7 - 2i?
In a + bi form with a = 7 and b = -2, the real part is 7.
Real numbers are complex numbers whose imaginary part is zero.
Rearrange the letters V I S R E L to make a word. What is the second last letter of that word?
The letters form the word SILVER. Its letters are S, I, L, V, E, R so the second last letter is E.
Silver has the chemical symbol Ag from the Latin argentum.
How many Pakistani Nobel Prize winners have won in the field of physics?
Only Dr Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics, in 1979 for the electroweak theory. Malala Yousafzai won the Peace Prize in 2014.
Abdus Salam shared the 1979 physics prize with Sheldon Glashow and Steven Weinberg.
Which of the following is one of the eight categories of zakat recipients (masarif) mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah?
Surah At-Tawbah (verse 60) lists the fakir, miskin, zakat collectors, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, slaves, debtors, fi sabilillah and travellers. Debtors (Al-Gharimin) are one of them.
Zakat cannot be given to the Prophet's family (Bani Hashim) according to the majority view.
What is dead reckoning in navigation?
Sailing only at night using the stars
Estimating current position from a known starting point, speed, time and direction
Measuring the depth of the sea
Dead reckoning calculates the present position by using a previously known position and adding the distance travelled on a known course. It does not need external signals.
Before GPS, ships and aircraft relied heavily on dead reckoning.
In which year did China recognize Pakistan?
The People's Republic of China was proclaimed in 1949 and Pakistan recognized it in 1950, among the first countries to do so. Diplomatic relations began on 21 May 1951.
Pakistan was among the first Muslim countries to recognize the People's Republic of China.
Where is the Red Sea located?
The Red Sea lies between northeast Africa (Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea) and the Arabian Peninsula (Saudi Arabia, Yemen). It connects to the Mediterranean through the Suez Canal.
The Red Sea joins the Indian Ocean through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.
What was the relation of Hazrat Ali (RA) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, the Prophet's uncle, so he was a cousin. He married the Prophet's daughter Hazrat Fatima (RA).
Hazrat Ali (RA) was the fourth Rightly Guided Caliph.
What is the antonym of reluctant?
Reluctant means unwilling, so its opposite is willing or eager. The other options are synonyms.
Eager and keen are also antonyms of reluctant.
For how many days did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) stay in the Cave of Thawr (Ghar-e-Saur) during the Hijrat?
During the migration to Madinah the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) hid in the Cave of Thawr for three days. They then continued to Madinah.
The cave is near Makkah, south of the city.
According to the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan, what was the minimum age to be a member of the National Assembly?
The 1962 Constitution required a member of the National Assembly to be at least 25 years old.
Sources differ slightly on some qualification details; the minimum age of the President under the 1962 Constitution is commonly given as 35 years.
According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the minimum age required to be elected President of Pakistan?
Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution requires the President to be a Muslim, qualified to be a member of the National Assembly, and not less than 45 years old.
The President is elected by an electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies for a five-year term.
How many seats were reserved for women in the National Assembly under the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
The 1956 Constitution provided a National Assembly of 300 general seats plus 10 seats reserved for women for ten years.
Under the 1973 Constitution today, 60 National Assembly seats are reserved for women.
How many seats are reserved for women in the Punjab Assembly?
The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats: 297 general seats, 66 seats for women and 8 for non-Muslims.
Punjab has the largest provincial assembly in Pakistan.
At which place in Lahore was the Lahore Resolution presented in 1940?
The session of the All India Muslim League was held at Minto Park, now Iqbal Park, where Minar-e-Pakistan stands.
Minar-e-Pakistan was built to commemorate the resolution.
Which gas is mainly responsible for global warming?
Carbon dioxide, released by burning fossil fuels, traps heat in the atmosphere as a greenhouse gas.
Methane is another important greenhouse gas.
What is the meaning of retaliation?
Retaliation means paying back an injury or wrong with a similar action, that is, revenge.
What is the antonym of retaliation?
Retaliation means revenge, so its opposite is forgiveness or pardon.
Revenge, vengeance and reprisal are synonyms of retaliation.
If the letters of the word BEAUTY are written in reverse order, which is the last letter?
BEAUTY reversed is YTUAEB, so the last letter is B.
The first letter of the reversed word is Y.
According to the Hadith Qudsi on fasting, who will Himself give the reward of fasting?
In the Hadith Qudsi Allah says: Fasting is for Me and I shall reward it Myself.
Fasting is the third pillar of Islam in some counts and the fourth in the commonly taught Pakistani order.
In which direction does the sun rise?
The Earth rotates from west to east, so the sun appears to rise in the east.
The sun sets in the west.
Who has scored the most runs in Test cricket?
