Sachin Tendulkar of India scored 15,921 runs in 200 Tests, and no one has passed this total as of October 2026.
Joe Root of England is second, having passed 14,000 Test runs in 2026.
What is the capital of Russia?
Moscow is the capital and largest city of Russia.
Saint Petersburg was the capital of the Russian Empire until 1918.
Saleem is 3 years old and his sister is three times as old as him. How old will his sister be when Saleem is 12?
The sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old now, so she is 6 years older than Saleem. When he is 12, she will be 12 + 6 = 18.
The age difference between two people always stays the same.
What is the synonym of foe?
Foe means an enemy or opponent.
The antonym of foe is friend or ally.
Ali is 3 years old and his sister Sara is 3 times his age. How old will Sara be when Ali is 8 years old?
When Ali is 3, Sara is 3 x 3 = 9, so Sara is 6 years older than Ali. The age gap stays the same, so when Ali is 8, Sara is 8 + 6 = 14.
The difference between two people's ages never changes with time.
Ali is 3 years old and his sister Sara is 3 times his age. How old will Sara be when Ali is 15 years old?
When Ali is 3, Sara is 9, so she is 6 years older. When Ali is 15, Sara is 15 + 6 = 21.
The age gap of 6 years stays fixed for life.
How many seats does the Provincial Assembly of Sindh have in total?
The Sindh Assembly has 168 seats: 130 general seats, 29 reserved for women and 9 reserved for non-Muslims.
The Punjab Assembly is the largest provincial assembly with 371 seats.
How many general seats does Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have in the National Assembly of Pakistan after the 2023 delimitation?
After the merger of FATA and the 2023 delimitation, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has 45 general seats in the National Assembly.
Before the merger of FATA the province had 35 general seats, while Punjab now has 141 general seats.
What is the antonym (opposite) of the word selfless?
Selfless means putting others before oneself, so its opposite is selfish, meaning concerned only with oneself.
Unselfish and altruistic are synonyms of selfless.
Under which Act was Sindh separated from the Bombay Presidency in 1936?
The Government of India Act 1935 created Sindh as a separate province, which came into effect on 1 April 1936.
The demand for separating Sindh from Bombay was part of the Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points of 1929.
How many vowels are there in this sequence: A Q W S T R H J C B D Y K L O?
The only vowels in the sequence are A and O, so the count is 2. Y is treated as a consonant here.
The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.
How many vowels are there in the sequence: a d i u l k m e?
The vowels in the sequence are a, i, u and e, which makes 4.
The English alphabet has five vowels and twenty-one consonants.
The numbers go up by 1 each time and the letters go backwards through the alphabet (z, y, x, w). So the next term is 4w.
Z is the 26th letter and W is the 23rd letter of the alphabet.
Complete the series: a, c, f, ?
The gaps increase by 1: a to c is +2, c to f is +3, so the next is +4. F is the 6th letter and 6 + 4 = 10, which is j.
J is the 10th letter of the English alphabet.
What is the next term in the series: A1, C3, D4, G7, ?
The number is the position of the letter in the alphabet, and the numbers 1, 3, 4, 7 each equal the sum of the two before (3 + 4 = 7). The next number is 4 + 7 = 11, which is K.
The numbers 1, 3, 4, 7, 11 are known as the Lucas numbers.
Fill in the blank: ____ sun sets in the west.
There is only one sun, so the definite article the is used before it.
The definite article is also used with unique things such as the moon, the earth and the sky.
In which year was the Shimla Agreement between Pakistan and India signed?
The Shimla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi.
It converted the ceasefire line of Kashmir into the Line of Control.
Under the Constitution of Pakistan, what is the official name of the Parliament of Pakistan?
Article 50 of the Constitution says the Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses, the National Assembly and the Senate, and it is called Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament).
The two houses of the Majlis-e-Shoora are the National Assembly and the Senate.
In which direction of Pakistan does the port city of Gwadar lie?
Gwadar lies on the Arabian Sea coast in the south-west corner of Pakistan in the province of Balochistan.
Pakistan purchased Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958.
Which type of triangle has all three sides of different lengths?
A scalene triangle has no two sides equal, while an isosceles triangle has two equal sides and an equilateral triangle has three equal sides.
The angles of a scalene triangle are also all different.
Sine is an odd function, so reflecting the angle across the x-axis changes the sign of the sine. Therefore sin(-y) = -sin y.
Cosine is an even function, so cos(-y) = cos y.
Which tense is normally used with the words 'since' and 'for' (for example, 'I have lived here since 2010')?

'Since' and 'for' show how long an action or state has continued up to now, which is expressed by the present perfect (or present perfect continuous) tense. Example: She has worked here for five years.
'Since' is used with a point in time and 'for' with a length of time.
In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan die?
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan died at Aligarh on 27 March 1898.
He was born in 1817, so he lived about 80 years.
Which type of brackets is used to write a solution set?
Sets, including solution sets, are written inside curly brackets, for example {2, 3}.
Round and square brackets are used for intervals.
Solve the proportion 2 : x :: 14 : 28. What is x?
In a proportion the product of extremes equals the product of means: 2 x 28 = x x 14. So 56 = 14x and x = 4.
A proportion a : b :: c : d means a/b = c/d.
Add x and 9 to both sides: 4x = 18, so x = 18/4 = 9/2 = 4.5.
Who was the son of Hazrat Sarah (AS), the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS)?
Hazrat Sarah was the mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS), born when she was very old.
Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Hajra.
The sound of which animal is mentioned in the Quran as the most unpleasant of sounds?
Surah Luqman (31:19) says the harshest of sounds is surely the braying of the donkey.
This verse is part of Luqman's advice to his son to lower his voice.
When was the Soviet Union (USSR) established?
The USSR was formally created on 30 December 1922 by the union of Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian and Transcaucasian republics.
Iqbal's famous 1930 speech at the annual session of the All India Muslim League is known as which address?
Allama Iqbal delivered his Presidential Address at Allahabad in December 1930. In it he proposed a separate Muslim state in north-west India.
The Allahabad Address is considered the intellectual root of the Pakistan idea.
What is the last sermon of the Holy Prophet (SAW) called?
The Prophet (SAW) delivered his final sermon during the Farewell Hajj at Arafat. It is called Khutbah Hajjat-ul-Wida.
The Farewell Hajj took place in 10 AH.
A car runs at 60 km/hr and a train runs at twice the speed of the car. What is the speed of the train?
Train speed = 2 x 60 = 120 km/hr. Speed does not change with the time taken, so it is still 120 km/hr after 30 minutes.
In 30 minutes this train would cover 60 km.
What does OPAC stand for in library science?
OPAC means Online Public Access Catalogue. It is a computerised database that lets users search a library's holdings.
It replaced the traditional card catalogue.
Fill in the blank: She arrived ___ the station.
We use the preposition at with a specific point or place such as a station. So the sentence is: She arrived at the station.
We use arrive in for large places such as cities and countries.
After which battle did the Quraysh stop their attacks on Madina, as the Prophet (SAW) said they would no longer attack?
After the failed siege of Madina in the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab) in 5 AH, the Prophet (SAW) said that the Quraysh would not attack again and the Muslims would march against them.
The Battle of Khandaq was won mainly by the trench dug on the advice of Salman Farsi (RA).
The graphical representation of which type of equation is a straight line?
A linear equation such as y = mx + c has degree one in its variables. Its graph is always a straight line.
A quadratic equation gives a parabola.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'strange'?
Strange means unusual or unexpected, and odd has the same meaning. The other options mean the opposite.
Other synonyms of strange are peculiar and queer.
What is the central subject of the Holy Quran?
The Quran is a book of guidance addressed to mankind. Its main subject is man and his success in this world and the Hereafter.
The Quran has 114 surahs and 30 paras.
Subversion means an attempt to weaken or overthrow an established authority from within. Undermining carries the same sense.
Who was the first Pakistani to reach the summit of K2?
Ashraf Aman reached the summit of K2 in 1977 as part of a Japanese-led expedition.
Nazir Sabir was the first Pakistani to climb Mount Everest, in 2000, and sources differ slightly on the exact K2 summit date in August 1977.
If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 16th of that month?
From the 2nd to the 16th is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. So the 16th falls on the same day as the 2nd, Sunday.
Dates that differ by a multiple of 7 always fall on the same weekday.
What is the meaning of the name of Surah Al-Ankabut?
Ankabut means spider, and the surah is named after the spider's web used as an example in it.
Al-Ankabut is the 29th surah of the Quran.
Which two surahs are known as Muawwazatain?
Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas are called Muawwidhatayn because they seek refuge in Allah.
They are the last two surahs of the Quran, 113 and 114.
What is the capital of Sweden?
Stockholm is the capital and largest city of Sweden.
Sweden is a Scandinavian country in northern Europe.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "abate"?
To abate means to become less intense, which is to subside.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "acquiesce"?
To acquiesce is to accept or go along with something without protest, so comply is closest.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "acquisition"?
An acquisition is something gained or bought, close to purchase.
Companies use the word for takeovers.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "awful"?
Awful means very bad, same as terrible.
The word originally meant inspiring awe.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "brute"?
A brute is a savage or cruel creature, so beast is closest.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "exceptional"?
Exceptional means unusually good or rare, like extraordinary.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "irksome"?
Irksome means causing irritation, so annoying is closest.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "magistrate"?
A magistrate is a civil officer who acts as a judge in lower courts.
In Pakistan, judicial magistrates hear minor criminal cases.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "puzzled"?
Puzzled means confused, the same as perplexed.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "wield"?
To wield is to hold and use something such as a tool or power, so handle is closest.
One can wield a sword or wield influence.
What is the capital of Tajikistan?
Dushanbe is the capital and largest city of Tajikistan.
Tajikistan borders Afghanistan, China, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.
If 1 km takes 100 minutes, how many km can be covered in 12 minutes at the same rate?
Rate is 1/100 km per minute, so in 12 minutes the distance is 12 x 1/100 = 0.12 km.
Distance equals speed multiplied by time.
Which of the following was NOT among the Ashra Mubashra (the ten Companions given glad tidings of Paradise)?
Hazrat Talha is one of the ten given the glad tidings of Paradise, while Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) is not on that list.
The ten include the four Rightly Guided Caliphs, Talha, Zubair, Abdur Rahman bin Auf, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, Saeed bin Zaid and Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah.
Which is the tallest building in Pakistan?
Bahria Icon Tower in Karachi is generally listed as Pakistan's tallest building, though its stated height varies by source (about 273 to 300 metres).
Habib Bank Plaza was long considered the tallest before the Icon Tower was built.
Tarbela Dam is located in which district and province of Pakistan?
Tarbela Dam is built on the River Indus near Tarbela in Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
It is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.
How many farz (obligatory acts) does Tayammum have according to the Hanafi school?
The three farz of Tayammum are making the intention, striking the hands on clean earth and wiping the face, and wiping both arms up to the elbows.
Tayammum is performed when water is not available or cannot be used.
On which date is International Tea Day observed?
The United Nations designated 21 May as International Tea Day, first observed in 2020.
Earlier, tea-producing countries had celebrated an International Tea Day on 15 December.
A soldier's mother ____ her emotions as he left for the front. Choose the correct word.
The phrasal verb 'bottled up' means kept feelings hidden, and 'teared' is not the right form in this sense.
'Bottle up' is the phrasal verb; the past tense is 'bottled up'.
What is 20% of one tenth of 90?
One tenth of 90 is 9, and 20% of 9 is 1.8.
20% is the same as one fifth.
Multiplying by one tenth moves the decimal point one place left.
What is one third of one tenth of 9?
One tenth of 9 is 0.9 and one third of 0.9 is 0.3.
What is cosec theta equal to?
Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine, so cosec theta = 1 / sin theta.
Sec theta is 1 / cos theta and cot theta is 1 / tan theta.
In a right-angled triangle, sin theta is equal to which ratio?
Sine of an angle is the length of the opposite side (perpendicular) divided by the hypotenuse.
Cos theta is base / hypotenuse and tan theta is perpendicular / base.
Which is the third surah of the Holy Quran?
The order is Al-Fatiha, Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, so the third surah is Al-Imran.
A number whose three times is 6 has 2 added to it. What is the result?
If 3 times the number is 6, the number is 2. Adding 2 gives 2 + 2 = 4.
The candidate answer 2 is only the number itself, not the final result.
Through which point does the line y = 6x pass?
Putting x = 0 gives y = 0, so the line passes through the origin (0, 0).
A line of the form y = mx always passes through the origin.
Watch is to time as barometer is to what?
A watch measures time and a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.
A thermometer measures temperature and an anemometer measures wind speed.
What was the approximate age of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at the time of the Fujjar war?
The Fujjar war was fought in the sacred months and the young Prophet (PBUH) took part by handing arrows to his uncles at about the age of 15 years.
Some narrations give an age between 14 and 20 years, so sources differ slightly; 15 is the common textbook answer.
Tipu Sultan was killed defending Seringapatam against the British in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War on 4 May 1799.
The Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792 ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War.
Which title is used for Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA)?
Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) is known by the title Attiq, meaning freed from the fire of Hell, besides Siddiq.
Farooq is the title of Hazrat Umar (RA) and Murtaza of Hazrat Ali (RA).
Habibullah (beloved of Allah) is the title of whom?
Habibullah is a famous title of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
If today is Friday, what day will it be after 14 days?
14 days is exactly 2 weeks, so the day is the same: Friday.
Any multiple of 7 days brings the same weekday.
If today is Monday, what day will it be after 5 days?
Counting 5 days after Monday gives Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday.
Saturday and Sunday form the weekend.
What is the line that touches a circle at exactly one point called?
A tangent touches the circle at exactly one point, while a secant cuts it at two points.
A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
How many tournaments make up the Grand Slam in tennis?
The four Grand Slam tennis tournaments are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open.
Wimbledon is the oldest of the four.
What is the transpose of a row matrix called?
Transposing swaps rows and columns, so a 1 by n row matrix becomes an n by 1 column matrix.
The transpose of a square matrix is also a square matrix.
What was the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) about?
Sale of Kashmir by the British to Gulab Singh
End of the First Anglo-Sikh War handing Punjab to the Mughals
Under the Treaty of Amritsar the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh Dogra for 7.5 million rupees.
It followed the First Anglo-Sikh War and created the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir.
Ali's present age is 3 years and his sister is twice his age. What will be the age of his sister when Ali is 8 years old?
Sister's age now is 2 x 3 = 6, so she is 3 years older than Ali. When Ali is 8, she is 8 + 3 = 11.
The age difference between two people always stays the same.
Salman is 4 years old and Ali is twice the age of Salman. When Salman is 12 years old, what will be the age of Ali?
Ali is 2 x 4 = 8 now, so he is 4 years older than Salman. When Salman is 12, Ali is 12 + 4 = 16.
Do not double the later age; only the present ages are in the ratio 2 to 1.
What type of constitution was the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
The 1956 Constitution, Pakistan's first, set up a federal parliamentary republic with a unicameral National Assembly.
It was abrogated in October 1958 when martial law was imposed.
Beauty is to ugliness as adversity is to what?
Ugliness is the opposite of beauty, and the opposite of adversity (hardship) is prosperity.
Hardship, misfortune and difficulty are synonyms of adversity, not opposites.
Beauty is to ugliness as diversity is to what?
Ugliness is the opposite of beauty, and the opposite of diversity (variety) is uniformity.
Variety, difference and range are close in meaning to diversity.
Unscramble the word SAPIR. Is it the name of a bird, a country or a city?
The letters of SAPIR form PARIS, which is a city, the capital of France.
Paris stands on the River Seine.
In which Hijri year was Hazrat Usman (RA) martyred?
Hazrat Usman (RA), the third caliph, was besieged in his house and martyred in Dhul Hijjah 35 AH (656 CE).
He was succeeded as caliph by Hazrat Ali (RA).
If Y = 4x - 2 and x = 2, what is the value of Y?
Multiplication is done before subtraction in the order of operations.
If y = 2x - 1 and x = 2, what is the value of y?
Substitution means replacing a variable by its given value.
What comes next in the series Z1, Y2, X3, ...?
The letters move backwards through the alphabet (Z, Y, X, W) while the numbers go up by 1 (1, 2, 3, 4). So the next term is W4.
Letter pairs like this often combine a reverse alphabet with an increasing number.
On what date was the Treaty of Versailles signed?
The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919 in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles.
It came into force on 10 January 1920, the same day the League of Nations first met.
What was the Treaty of Versailles?
A peace treaty ending World War I with Germany
A treaty ending World War II
An alliance between Britain and France
A treaty founding the United Nations
The Treaty of Versailles was the peace settlement between Germany and the Allied Powers after World War I.
It forced Germany to accept war guilt, pay reparations and lose territory.
According to the commonly accepted count, how many verses (ayat) does the Holy Quran have?
The Hafs count most widely followed gives 6236 verses across 114 surahs.
Counts differ slightly between recitation traditions; 6666 is a popular but not the standard figure.
Fill in the blank: He was very grateful that he ----- my computer promptly.
The sentence is in the past tense (was grateful), so the past tense repaired is correct.
Tense should stay consistent between the clauses of a sentence.
Who was the last Viceroy of British India?
Lord Mountbatten served as the last Viceroy from March to August 1947 and then became the first Governor-General of independent India.
In which year did Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan make his official visit to the United States?
Liaquat Ali Khan visited the USA in May 1950 at the invitation of President Truman.
This visit is seen as the start of close Pakistan-US relations.
How many vowels are in the letter string AEDIPOUDLEC (Aedipoudlec)?
The vowels are A, E, I, O, U, E, which makes 6.
The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.
How many vowels are in AZPQTVSJFIU?
The vowels are A, I and U, giving 3.
The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.
How many vowels are in AdebccTEvIxyz?
The vowels are A, e, E and I, giving 4.
Capital and small letters count equally.
Which country does India import the largest share of its weapons from, according to SIPRI data?
SIPRI data show Russia as India's largest arms supplier for 2020-24, with about 36 percent of India's imports. France is second.
Russia's share of Indian imports has fallen sharply from about 72 percent in 2010-14.
Choose the correct form of the sentence: Amna will have repair her bike by next week.
Amna will have repaired her bike by next week.
Amna will has repaired her bike by next week.
Amna will have repairing her bike by next week.
Amna will had repair her bike by next week.
The future perfect tense is formed with will have plus the past participle, so repair must become repaired.
The future perfect tense shows an action that will be completed before a stated time in the future.
If 10 men can dig a well in 5 days, how many days will 5 men take to dig it?
Total work = 10 x 5 = 50 man-days. With 5 men, days = 50 / 5 = 10 days.
Fewer workers need proportionally more time, which is called inverse proportion.
In which country is the White House located?
The White House stands at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue in Washington, D.C., United States.
Construction of the White House began in 1792 and it was first occupied by President John Adams in 1800.
Which country is traditionally called the Land of the White Elephant?
Thailand (formerly Siam) is known by this name because white elephants were sacred and symbols of royal power there.
Sources differ slightly, as Myanmar and Laos have also been linked to white elephants, but Thailand is the textbook answer.
Who won the seventh edition of the Pakistan Super League (PSL 7) in 2022?
Lahore Qalandars beat Multan Sultans by 42 runs in the final at Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore, on 27 February 2022.
It was the first PSL title for Lahore Qalandars, who also won PSL 8 in 2023.
Which team won the 2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup?
Australia beat New Zealand by 8 wickets in the final in Dubai in November 2021 to win their first T20 World Cup.
Pakistan won the 2009 ICC T20 World Cup, and it reached the 2021 semi-final.
When are the articles a and an used?
A and an are indefinite articles used before singular countable nouns; a is used before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound.
The article the is the definite article and can be used with singular, plural and uncountable nouns.
What is the work of the angels Munkar and Nakir, according to Islamic belief?
Blowing the trumpet on the Day of Judgement
Questioning a person in the grave
Munkar and Nakir are the two angels who question a person in the grave about his Lord, his religion and his Prophet.
The angels who record deeds are Kiraman Katibin, who sit on each person's shoulders.
In which year did the Holy Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) pass away?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) passed away on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, 11 AH, which corresponds to June 632 CE, in Madina.
He was about 63 years old, and he was buried in the room of Hazrat Ayesha (RA).
If one man writes one paper in 5 minutes, how long does one man take to write one paper?
The question already states that he takes 5 minutes for one paper, so the answer is 5 minutes.
At this rate, he would write 12 papers in one hour.
Which famous book was written by Data Ganj Bakhsh (Hazrat Ali Hujwiri)?
Data Ganj Bakhsh wrote Kashf-ul-Mahjoob, one of the oldest Persian works on Sufism.
In which Hijri year was the Battle of Yamama fought?
The Battle of Yamama was fought against the false prophet Musaylima in 11 AH (632 CE) in the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).
After heavy losses of Quran memorisers in this battle, the Quran was first compiled in book form.
What was the relation of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) to Hazrat Ismail (AS)?
Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Ishaq (AS), who was the younger brother of Ismail (AS), so Yaqoob was Ismail's nephew.
Both Ishaq and Ismail were sons of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).
On which date (day) of Ramadan is Youm-e-Furqan observed?
Youm-e-Furqan marks the Battle of Badr, which was fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH.
Badr is called the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.
Which is the oldest of these heavenly books?
The Taurat was revealed to Hazrat Musa (AS), before the Zabur (Dawood AS), the Injeel (Isa AS) and the Quran (Muhammad PBUH).
The Quran is the last of the heavenly books.
What is the well-known title of Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA)?
Hazrat Zaid (RA) was so dear to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) that he was called Hibb Rasulullah.
He is the only Companion whose name is mentioned in the Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab).
Zenith means the highest point, so its opposite is nadir, the lowest point.
Apex, summit and peak are synonyms of zenith.
Which Indian mathematician is credited with formalising the rules of arithmetic with zero in 628 CE?
Brahmagupta, in his Brahmasphutasiddhanta, gave the first clear rules for using zero in calculations.
Sources differ on who first invented the zero symbol; some credit Aryabhata and earlier Indian scholars.
It has variables and constants joined by operations but no equals or inequality sign, so it is an algebraic expression (it simplifies to -2x + 2).
An equation needs an equals sign, such as 3x - 5x + 2 = 0.
A - B contains the elements of A that are not in B. Only 3 is in A but not in B.
If Y = 4X and X = 2, what is Y?
Here 4 is the coefficient of X.
In the expression 7X + 4, what is 7 called?
The number multiplying the variable X is its coefficient; 4 is the constant term.
X is the variable of the expression.
Subtracting 10 from -10 moves further down the number line to -20.
Two negative numbers added give a larger negative number.
Any non-zero number divided by itself is 1.
Add the like terms: 2x + 3x = 5x, so the result is 5x + 1.
Only like terms can be combined.
Substitute first, then multiply, then subtract.
90% of 91 = 0.9 x 91 = 81.9. Equivalently, 10% of 91 is 9.1, and 91 minus 9.1 = 81.9.
Taking 90% of a number is the same as subtracting 10% of it.
90% of 99 = 0.9 x 99 = 89.1. Equivalently, 10% of 99 is 9.9, and 99 minus 9.9 = 89.1.
90% of 100 is 90, so 90% of 99 is 0.9 less than 90.
In set theory, what is n(A-B) equal to?
A-B contains the elements of A that are not in B. These are all elements of A except those common to both, so n(A-B) = n(A) - n(A intersection B).
The union formula is n(A union B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A intersection B).
What is the capital of Somalia?
Mogadishu is the capital and largest city of Somalia on the Indian Ocean coast.
Hargeisa is the capital of the self-declared Somaliland.
What is the capital of Malta?
Valletta is the capital of Malta and a UNESCO World Heritage city.
Mdina was the old capital of Malta before Valletta.
What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
Astana is the capital of Kazakhstan; it replaced Almaty as capital in 1997.
Astana was renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019 and returned to the name Astana in 2022.
The Khyber Pass connects Peshawar with which town of Pakistan?
The Khyber Pass runs from near Peshawar through Jamrud and Landi Kotal to the Torkham border with Afghanistan.
Landi Kotal is the highest point of the pass and lies close to the Afghan border.
In which year was the first Cricket World Cup held?
The first Cricket World Cup (the Prudential Cup) was played in England and began on 7 June 1975.
West Indies won the first two tournaments, in 1975 and 1979.
Wilhelm Conrad Rontgen, a German physicist, discovered X-rays in 1895 while experimenting with cathode ray tubes.
Rontgen received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 for this discovery.
Which person led the launch of the iPhone, which Apple introduced in 2007?
Steve Jobs, co-founder and then CEO of Apple, unveiled the first iPhone in January 2007. Apple is the company that made it.
Steve Jobs died in 2011 and Tim Cook became Apple's CEO.
Where and in which year were the first Asian Games held?
The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951. Eleven countries took part.
The Asian Games are held every four years under the Olympic Council of Asia.
What does the green colour in the national flag of Pakistan represent?
The dark green field of the flag stands for the Muslim majority of Pakistan, while the white stripe stands for religious minorities.
The crescent symbolises progress and the star symbolises light and knowledge; the flag was adopted on 11 August 1947.
Which of the following countries does NOT share a border with Pakistan?
Pakistan borders India, China, Afghanistan and Iran. Tajikistan is separated from Pakistan by the narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan.
The Wakhan Corridor is only about 14 to 15 km wide at its narrowest point.
Reykjavik is the capital of which country?
Reykjavik is the capital and largest city of Iceland.
Reykjavik is the northernmost capital of a sovereign state in the world.
What is the capital of Ghana?
Accra is the capital and largest city of Ghana, on the Gulf of Guinea coast.
Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from Britain, in 1957.
What is the capital of Latvia?
Riga is the capital and largest city of Latvia.
Latvia is one of the three Baltic states.
Which country won the 2018 FIFA World Cup?
France beat Croatia 4-2 in the final in Moscow in July 2018.
Russia hosted the 2018 tournament, and Argentina won the next one in 2022.
Antonie van Leeuwenhoek first observed bacteria through his handmade microscope in the 1670s. He called them animalcules.
Louis Pasteur proved the germ theory of disease and Robert Koch identified the bacteria causing anthrax and tuberculosis.
Who was the first woman Speaker of the United States House of Representatives?
Nancy Pelosi of California became the first woman Speaker of the US House in January 2007. She held the post again from 2019 to 2023.
Pelosi was succeeded as Speaker by Kevin McCarthy in 2023, and later by Mike Johnson.
Moroni is the capital of which country?
Moroni is the capital of the Union of the Comoros, an island nation in the Indian Ocean.
Comoros lies between Mozambique and Madagascar.
Which country has won the most Cricket World Cup titles?
Australia has won the men's Cricket World Cup six times (1987, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2015 and 2023).
India has won it twice and Pakistan once, in 1992.
Which is the highest peak of the Salt Range?
Sakesar, in district Khushab, is the highest peak of the Salt Range at about 1522 m.
The Salt Range lies between the Jhelum and Indus rivers in Punjab.
Who is credited with discovering the proton?
Ernest Rutherford identified the proton as a particle in 1917-1919.
Thomson discovered the electron and Chadwick discovered the neutron.
Whose slave was Hazrat Bilal (RA) before he accepted freedom through Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
Hazrat Bilal (RA) was the slave of Umayyah ibn Khalaf, who tortured him for accepting Islam. Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) bought and freed him.
Hazrat Bilal (RA) became the first muezzin of Islam.
How many atmospheric layers does the Moon have?
None, it has practically no atmosphere
The Moon is too small and its gravity too weak to hold an atmosphere. It has only an extremely thin exosphere that is almost a vacuum.
Because there is no air, sound cannot travel on the Moon and the sky looks black even in daytime.
James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932 by bombarding beryllium with alpha particles.
Chadwick received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1935 for this discovery.
Which is the smallest ocean in the world?
The Arctic Ocean has an area of about 14 million square kilometres and is the smallest and shallowest ocean.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean.
Which team won the Asia Cup cricket tournament in 2022?
Sri Lanka beat Pakistan by 23 runs in the final in Dubai in September 2022 to win the T20 format Asia Cup.
The 2022 Asia Cup was played in the United Arab Emirates after being moved from Sri Lanka.
In which year was the Suez Canal completed and opened?
The Suez Canal was opened to traffic on 17 November 1869 after about ten years of construction.
It was built under the French engineer Ferdinand de Lesseps and links the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea.
In which surah of the Holy Quran are the faraiz (obligatory acts) of wudu mentioned?
The faraiz of wudu are described in verse 6 of Surah Al-Maidah, which orders washing the face and arms, wiping the head and washing the feet.
The same verse also gives the command for tayammum when water is not available; Surah An-Nisa (4:43) also mentions tayammum.
Ghani Khan, the famous poet and philosopher, wrote mainly in which language?
Ghani Khan (1914-1996) was a well known Pashto poet, painter and philosopher from Charsadda.
He was the son of Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan and wrote the book The Pathans.
Which prophet (AS) was given the ability by Allah to soften and melt iron?
The Quran says Allah made iron soft for Hazrat Dawood (AS), so he could make armour from it. He is the prophet who received the Zabur.
Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) was the son of Hazrat Dawood (AS).
What is the currency of Japan?
Japan's currency is the yen. Its code is JPY.
The Bank of Japan issues the yen.
During which months of 1999 was the Kargil conflict between Pakistan and India fought?
The Kargil conflict began in early May 1999 and ended in late July 1999, after a ceasefire request following talks in Washington.
Kargil lies in the Ladakh region along the Line of Control.
Who is known by the title Quaid-e-Millat?
Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, is known as Quaid-e-Millat (Leader of the Nation).
He was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.
With which neighbouring country does Pakistan share a border of about 2,400 km?
The Pakistan-Afghanistan border, the Durand Line, is about 2,430 km long and is commonly quoted as about 2,400 km.
Pakistan's border with India is about 3,300 km, with Iran about 900 km and with China about 520 km.
Napoleon Bonaparte belonged to which country?
Napoleon Bonaparte was a French general who became Emperor of the French. He was born on the island of Corsica, which was a French territory.
Napoleon was finally defeated at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815.
In the x,y coordinate system, what is the y-coordinate also called?
In a point (x, y), the x-value is called the abscissa and the y-value is called the ordinate.
The point where both coordinates are zero is called the origin.
Where is the shrine of the famous Pashto poet Rehman Baba located?
The mausoleum of Abdur Rehman Mohmand, known as Rehman Baba, is at Hazar Khwani near Peshawar.
Rehman Baba is called the Nightingale of Pashto poetry and lived in the 17th century.
What is the average height of the Potohar Plateau above sea level according to most Pakistani textbooks?
The Potohar Plateau lies between the Indus and Jhelum rivers and has an average height of about 300 to 600 metres.
Sources differ slightly, with some giving the height in feet as about 1000 to 2000 feet.
In which year did Pakistan launch its first satellite, Badr-1?
Pakistan's first satellite, Badr-1, was launched on 16 July 1990 from China by SUPARCO. It was a low-earth-orbit experimental satellite.
Pakistan later launched Badr-B in 2001 and PakSat-1R in 2011.
What is the capital of Zambia?
Lusaka is the capital and largest city of Zambia.
Zambia is a landlocked country in southern Africa that was formerly Northern Rhodesia.
Which is the second highest mountain of Pakistan?
K2 is the highest peak in Pakistan and Nanga Parbat, at about 8,126 m, is the second highest.
Nanga Parbat is nicknamed the Killer Mountain and is in Gilgit-Baltistan.
CPEC stands for China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, a package of infrastructure and energy projects linking Gwadar port with western China.
CPEC was formally launched in 2015 and its flagship port is Gwadar in Balochistan.
In which city is the Air Headquarters of the Pakistan Air Force located?
The Air Headquarters of the Pakistan Air Force is in Islamabad. The PAF Air Command and Staff College is at Karachi.
The Pakistan Air Force Academy is at Risalpur.
In which year was the 18th Amendment to the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan passed?
The 18th Amendment was passed by Parliament in April 2010 and signed by President Zardari. It transferred many powers from the centre to the provinces.
It renamed the North-West Frontier Province as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and removed the President's power to dissolve the National Assembly under 58(2)(b).
What is the antonym of superiority?
Superiority means being higher in quality or rank; the opposite is inferiority.
The terms inferiority complex and superiority complex were popularised by the psychologist Alfred Adler.
Into which sea does the Indus River flow?
The Indus River flows through Pakistan and falls into the Arabian Sea near Karachi in Sindh.
The Indus delta is near Thatta.
What is the approximate maximum height of the Kirthar range (its highest point, Zardak Peak)?
The highest point of the Kirthar range is Zardak Peak at roughly 2,260 metres, or about 7,400 feet.
Sources give slightly different figures, from about 2,260 to 2,267 metres.
What was the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) of Pakistan, Iran and Turkey renamed as in 1985?
The RCD was revived and renamed the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985 by its three founding members.
ECO later expanded in 1992 to include Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.
Which is the busiest sea (ocean) trade route of the world according to standard textbooks?
The North Atlantic sea route links eastern North America with north-western Europe and carries the heaviest volume of ocean trade in most textbooks.
Modern shipping statistics sometimes rank Asian routes through the Strait of Malacca very high, so sources can differ.
Who is traditionally credited in Pakistani textbooks with inventing the telescope?
Galileo Galilei built and used an improved telescope in 1609 to observe the Moon, Jupiter's moons and the planets. Textbooks therefore credit him with the telescope.
Sources differ: the Dutch spectacle maker Hans Lippershey filed the first known patent for a telescope in 1608.
Which is the largest temple in the world?
Angkor Wat in Cambodia covers about 162 hectares and is the largest religious monument in the world.
Angkor Wat was built in the 12th century by King Suryavarman II, first as a Hindu and later a Buddhist temple.
Which is regarded as the first women's university in Pakistan, and in which city is it located?
Kinnaird College for Women University, Lahore
Sardar Bahadur Khan Women's University, Quetta
Fatima Jinnah Women University was founded in 1998 in Rawalpindi and is generally regarded as Pakistan's first women's university. It is named after Fatima Jinnah, the sister of the Quaid-e-Azam.
Some sources call it the first public sector women's university, because Kinnaird College in Lahore was a much older women's college.
What was the code name of Pakistan's nuclear tests conducted in May 1998?
Pakistan's tests at Chagai in Balochistan were named Chagai-I (28 May 1998, five tests) and Chagai-II (30 May 1998, one test).
Pakistan observes 28 May as Youm-e-Takbeer; Smiling Buddha was the code name of India's 1974 test.
In which city is the headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations located?
The FAO has its headquarters in Rome, Italy. It leads international efforts against hunger and works on food and agriculture.
The FAO was founded in 1945 and its World Food Day is observed on 16 October.
Who was the first ambassador of Pakistan to the United States?
Mirza Abol Hassan Ispahani, a close associate of Jinnah, was the first Pakistani ambassador to the USA. He served until 1952.
Sources differ on whether he took up the post in 1947 or 1948; he later served as High Commissioner to Britain.
Tallinn is the capital of which country?
Tallinn is the capital and largest city of Estonia, on the Gulf of Finland.
Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania are the three Baltic states.
What do the five rings of the Olympic flag represent?
Five inhabited continents of the world
The five interlocked rings stand for the five inhabited continents joined by Olympism: Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe and Oceania.
The rings are blue, yellow, black, green and red on a white background, designed in 1913 and first flown in 1920.
The Karakoram mountain range lies between Pakistan and which country?
The Karakoram range runs along the northern border of Pakistan and separates Gilgit-Baltistan from the Xinjiang region of China.
The Karakoram Highway crosses this range through the Khunjerab Pass and links Pakistan with China.
According to the commonly given number in Pakistani textbooks, how many Companions served as Katib-e-Wahi (scribes of revelation) for the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Many Pakistani books state that about 40 Companions wrote down the revelation, including Hazrat Ali, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA).
Sources differ on the exact number, and Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA) is the best known of the scribes.
In which country did noodles originate?
The oldest known noodles, about 4000 years old, were found at the Lajia site in China, and China is generally credited with their origin.
Italy and China have long argued about the origin of pasta and noodles.
The Olympic Games take their name from Olympia and Mount Olympus. In which country did the Olympic Games originate?
The ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia in Greece, and Mount Olympus is also in Greece. The modern Olympics are named after these ancient games.
The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.
On which date was the Battle of Plassey fought?
The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between the British East India Company under Robert Clive and Nawab Siraj ud Daula of Bengal.
The Battle of Plassey is seen as the start of British political rule in India.
The word 'terrorism' was first used in connection with which historical event?
The term came into use in the 1790s for the Reign of Terror of the Jacobins in revolutionary France.
Sources differ on the exact year, with 1794 and 1795 both quoted.
Who wrote the poems Shikwa and Jawab-e-Shikwa?
Allama Muhammad Iqbal wrote Shikwa in 1909 and Jawab-e-Shikwa in 1913.
Both poems were later included in his Urdu collection Bang-e-Dra.
What is the antonym of friendly?
Friendly means kind and welcoming; the opposite is hostile, meaning unfriendly or aggressive.
Hostile comes from the Latin hostis, meaning enemy.
To which country did Winston Churchill, the famous leader of World War II, belong?
Winston Churchill was British and served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1940 to 1945 and again from 1951 to 1955.
Churchill won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1953.
The young Arab general Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh during the Umayyad caliphate. He defeated Raja Dahir.
Sindh is therefore called Bab-ul-Islam, the gateway of Islam, in the subcontinent.
The determinant of the transpose of a square matrix A is equal to what?
Negative of the determinant of A
The inverse of the determinant of A
Interchanging rows and columns does not change the determinant, so det(A transpose) = det(A).
Also det(AB) = det(A) x det(B) for square matrices of the same order.
The speed of a train is double that of a car. If the car's speed is 60 km/h, what is the speed of the train?
Double of 60 km/h is 2 x 60 = 120 km/h.
In which year did the Muslims of the subcontinent get the right of separate electorates?
Separate electorates were granted to the Muslims by the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.
The Lucknow Pact of 1916 later made the Congress accept separate electorates.
What is the average gestation period of a cow?
A cow carries her calf for about 283 days, which is roughly nine months. This is close to the human pregnancy length.
The gestation period of a buffalo is longer, about 310 to 315 days.
Kalimullah (the one who spoke with Allah) is the title of which prophet?
Hazrat Musa (AS) spoke directly with Allah on Mount Tur, so he is called Kalimullah.
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah and Hazrat Isa (AS) is called Ruhullah.
Who has scored the most Test runs for Pakistan?
Younis Khan scored 10,099 runs in Tests and is Pakistan's leading Test run scorer. He was the first Pakistani to pass 10,000 Test runs.
Javed Miandad (8,832) and Inzamam-ul-Haq (8,829) come next.
What does the name Moen jo Daro (Mohenjo-daro) mean?
Mohenjo-daro is a Sindhi name meaning Mound of the Dead. It was a major city of the Indus Valley Civilization.
It is located in Larkana district of Sindh and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Which Islamic Summit of the OIC was held in Pakistan (Lahore) in 1974?
The Second Islamic Summit Conference of the OIC was hosted in Lahore in February 1974. The first summit was held in Rabat in 1969.
The Lahore summit was attended by many Muslim heads of state and led to Bangladesh being recognised by Pakistan.
What is the antonym of the word plentiful?
Plentiful means more than enough, and its opposite is scarce, meaning in short supply.
Other antonyms of plentiful are rare, sparse and insufficient.
On which date was the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) established?
The SCO was formally established in Shanghai on 15 June 2001 by China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.
Pakistan and India became full SCO members in 2017.
SCO stands for Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, a Eurasian political, economic and security grouping.
Its permanent bodies are the Secretariat in Beijing and the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure in Tashkent.
According to the 1973 Constitution, how many seats does Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK) have in the Senate of Pakistan?
After the 2018 merger of FATA and the 2024 changes, KPK has 23 Senate seats: 14 general, 4 women, 4 technocrat and 1 non-Muslim.
Before the merger of FATA, KPK had 22 seats and the Senate had 104 members.
What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word 'utility'?
Utility means the quality of being useful or serving a practical purpose. Usefulness is therefore its closest synonym.
The word 'utilize' means to make practical use of something.
According to the 2017 census, what was the population of Pakistan?
The 6th Population and Housing Census of 2017 counted 207,684,626 people in Pakistan.
The next census, held in 2023, counted about 241.5 million people.
Who made the first solo non-stop flight across the Atlantic Ocean in 1927?
Charles Lindbergh flew the Spirit of St. Louis alone from New York to Paris in May 1927.
Alcock and Brown made the first non-stop transatlantic flight (not solo) in 1919, and Amelia Earhart was the first woman to fly it solo in 1932.
What is the antonym of the word advance?
To advance means to move forward, and its opposite is to retreat or move backward.
Advance can also mean to lend money beforehand, in which case it is a noun meaning a loan paid early.
Who described Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah as the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity?
Sarojini Naidu gave Jinnah this title, praising his work for unity at the time of the 1916 Lucknow Pact. Her 1918 book on him is titled Mohomed Ali Jinnah: An Ambassador of Unity.
Gopal Krishna Gokhale had earlier made a similar remark about Jinnah, so some sources trace the phrase to him.
What is the antonym of fertile?
Fertile land or a fertile mind produces plenty; the opposite is barren, which produces nothing.
Sterile is also accepted as an antonym of fertile, so sources may give either word.
What is the antonym of protect?
To protect is to keep safe from harm; the opposite is to endanger, to put in harm's way.
Defend, guard and shield are synonyms of protect.
What is the baby (young one) of a frog called?
A young frog hatches from an egg as a tadpole, which lives in water and breathes with gills. It later grows legs and lungs and becomes an adult frog.
The change from tadpole to frog is called metamorphosis.
Bani Israel (Children of Israel) are the descendants of which prophet, whose title was Israel?
Israel was the title of Hazrat Yaqub (AS), and his twelve sons formed the twelve tribes of Bani Israel. Hence the people are called Bani Israel.
Hazrat Musa (AS) is the most prominent prophet sent to Bani Israel.
Maputo is the capital of which country?
Maputo, formerly Lourenco Marques, is the capital of Mozambique.
Mozambique gained independence from Portugal in 1975.
There are 24 members in a committee and 5 are men. What is the percentage of women?
The men are 5/24 x 100 = 20.83 percent, and the two percentages add up to 100.
How many nations and territories belong to the Commonwealth Games Federation, which takes part in the Commonwealth Games?
The Commonwealth Games Federation has 74 members (nations and territories), including dependent territories that compete under their own flags.
The Commonwealth of Nations has only 56 member states, and about 72 teams took part in the Glasgow 2026 Games according to some reports.
Who introduced the system of Basic Democracies in Pakistan?
Ayub Khan introduced Basic Democracies through the Basic Democracies Order of 1959. Ordinary citizens elected Basic Democrats from local union councils, who then acted as the electoral college.
The system was ended by General Yahya Khan's government and replaced under the 1973 Constitution.
Diamond is an allotrope of which element?
Diamond is made of carbon atoms joined in a rigid tetrahedral crystal structure.
Graphite is another allotrope of carbon, and diamond is the hardest natural substance.
What is the antonym of "embrace" in the sense of accepting an idea?
To embrace an idea is to accept it eagerly, so its opposite is to reject it.
Embrace also means to hold someone in the arms, and in that sense a synonym is hug.
Sadequain (1930-1987) was a famous Pakistani painter and calligrapher, known for his Quranic calligraphy and murals.
He painted the ceiling mural at the Mangla Dam power house and the Frere Hall murals in Karachi.
What was the relation of Hazrat Fatima (RA) to Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH)?
Hazrat Fatima (RA) was the youngest daughter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA).
She is known as Zahra and Sayyidat Nisa al-Alamin.
The Flemish people are found mainly in which country?
The Flemish are the Dutch-speaking people of Flanders, the northern region of Belgium.
The French-speaking people of southern Belgium are called Walloons.
What is the width (length between the posts) of a standard football goal?
The two posts of a standard football goal are 24 feet (7.32 m) apart.
The goal height is 8 feet (2.44 m).
What is the capital of Iceland?
Reykjavik is the capital and largest city of Iceland. It is the northernmost capital of a sovereign state.
Iceland is a Nordic island country in the North Atlantic Ocean.
In which city is the National Library of Pakistan located?
The National Library of Pakistan is located in Islamabad on Constitution Avenue in the same complex as other national institutions.
It was established in 1951 in Karachi and later moved to Islamabad.
In which year was the construction of Pakistan Steel Mills at Karachi started (established)?
The foundation of Pakistan Steel Mills was laid in 1973 by Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto with Soviet help.
What is the length of the Panama Canal in nautical miles, approximately?
The Panama Canal is about 82 km (51 miles) long. Since 1 nautical mile is 1.852 km, this is about 44 nautical miles.
The canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific oceans and opened in 1914.
Which is generally regarded as the oldest sea port of Pakistan?
Karachi Port is the oldest and busiest port of Pakistan; modern port development there began in the 19th century.
Port Qasim is the second major port and Gwadar is the newest deep-sea port.
How many provinces does Pakistan have?
Pakistan has four provinces: Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.
Islamabad Capital Territory, Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir are not provinces.
Which angel is in charge of rain and provision according to Islamic belief?
Hazrat Mikail (AS) is the angel entrusted with rain, vegetation and sustenance. Jibrail brings revelation, Israfil blows the Trumpet and Izrail takes souls.
Mikail is also spelled Mika'il and is mentioned by name in Surah Al-Baqarah.
Who first suggested the name Pakistan?
Chaudhry Rehmat Ali, a Cambridge student, proposed the name Pakistan in his 1933 pamphlet Now or Never.
The name is made from the letters of Punjab, Afghania, Kashmir, Sindh and Balochistan.
How many main blood groups are there in the ABO system?
The main blood groups are A, B, AB and O, which makes four.
Each group can be Rh positive or Rh negative, giving eight common types.
Who presented the famous Poor Man's (labourer's) Budget in the interim government of British India just before independence?
Liaqat Ali Khan, as Finance Member of the interim government, presented a budget that taxed big business and industrialists to relieve the poor. It was called the Poor Man's Budget.
The budget was presented on 28 February 1947; the interim government itself was formed in September 1946.
To which city did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) migrate in 622 AD?
In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madinah, which was then called Yathrib.
This migration, the Hijrah, marks the start of the Islamic Hijri calendar.
Ahmed is 3 years old and his sister is 4 times his age. What will be the age of his sister after 12 years?
Sister's age now is 3 x 4 = 12 years. After 12 years she will be 12 + 12 = 24 years old.
The age difference between two people always stays the same over time.
What is the antonym of appropriate?
Appropriate means suitable for the situation; the opposite is inappropriate or unsuitable.
Suitable, fitting and proper are synonyms of appropriate.
In which region of Pakistan is Attabad Lake located?
Attabad Lake lies in the Hunza valley of Gilgit-Baltistan near Karimabad. It was formed by a landslide that blocked the Hunza River.
The landslide happened in January 2010 and the lake submerged part of the Karakoram Highway.
The line y = 7 is parallel to which axis?
It is parallel to neither axis
The line y = 7 is horizontal, because every point on it has y equal to 7. A horizontal line is parallel to the x-axis.
The line x = 7 would be vertical and parallel to the y-axis.
What is the antonym of the word breach?
To breach means to break a rule or agreement. Its opposite is compliance or observance, meaning keeping the rule.
Violation, rupture and gap are synonyms or near synonyms of breach, not opposites.
What is the capital of Zimbabwe?
Harare is the capital and largest city of Zimbabwe.
In a circle, what is the distance from the center to any point on the circle called?
The distance from the center to a point on the circle is the radius.
The diameter is twice the radius.
What is the antonym of the word 'comic'?
Comic means funny or amusing, while tragic means sad and causing sorrow, so tragic is the opposite.
Comedy and tragedy are the two classic types of drama.
In which year was the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) institution founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan at Aligarh?
Sir Syed founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental School at Aligarh on 24 May 1875, which later became MAO College.
The school was raised to MAO College in 1877 and became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920; some sources date the college itself to 1877.
How many member countries does the Commonwealth of Nations have?
The Commonwealth of Nations has 56 member states, the latest being Gabon and Togo who joined in June 2022.
In which year was the Communal Award announced by the British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald?
The Communal Award was announced on 16 August 1932 and gave separate electorates to Muslims and other minorities.
Gandhi fasted against the grant of separate electorates to the Depressed Classes, which led to the Poona Pact.
In which city and country is the headquarters of the Asian Development Bank located?
The Asian Development Bank was founded in 1966 and has its headquarters in Mandaluyong City, Metro Manila, in the Philippines.
Japan and the United States are its largest shareholders, and Pakistan is a founding member.
In which direction is China located with respect to Pakistan?
China lies to the north-east of Pakistan and borders Gilgit-Baltistan through the Khunjerab Pass.
The Karakoram Highway links Pakistan and China across the Khunjerab Pass.
Change into indirect speech: Ali said, "I was doing work."
Ali said that he was doing work.
Ali said that he had been doing work.
Ali said that I had been doing work.
Ali said that he has been doing work.
The reporting verb is in the past, so past continuous 'was doing' changes to past perfect continuous 'had been doing', and 'I' becomes 'he'.
Backshift moves each tense one step into the past in indirect speech.
A car moves at 60 km/h and a train is twice as fast. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes?
Train speed = 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 120 x 0.5 = 60 km.
How many vowels are there in the string EAVNJEGFDUI?
The letters are E, A, V, N, J, E, G, F, D, U, I. The vowels are E, A, E, U and I, which makes 5.
The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.
What does Radd-ul-Fasaad, the name of the Pakistan Army operation launched in 2017, mean?
Radd-ul-Fasaad is Arabic and means rejecting or eliminating discord and mischief. The operation was launched in February 2017 to remove the remaining terrorism and strengthen border security.
Operation Zarb-e-Azb (2014) was the earlier major operation in North Waziristan.
Which of the following is a prime number: 7, 9, 18, 21?
7 has only two factors, 1 and 7. 9 = 3 x 3, 18 = 2 x 9 and 21 = 3 x 7 are composite.
2 is the only even prime number.
Electric current is due to the flow of what?
In a metallic conductor, the free electrons drift under a potential difference, and this flow of charge is the electric current.
The SI unit of electric current is the ampere.
What is the closest meaning (synonym) of genuine?
Genuine means real and not imitation. Authentic has the same meaning.
Sincere is also used as a synonym of genuine when talking about feelings.
The Kirthar Hills (Kirthar Range) lie along the border of which two provinces of Pakistan?
The Kirthar Range runs north to south and forms the boundary between Sindh and Balochistan. It is the southern part of the Sulaiman-Kirthar system.
Zardak Peak (about 2,260 m) is generally named as its highest point, though sources differ slightly.
Who was the mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS)?
Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and his wife Hazrat Sarah. He was born when Sarah was very old.
Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
On which date is Labour Day (International Workers' Day) observed?
Labour Day is observed every year on 1 May, including in Pakistan, where it is a public holiday.
The day commemorates the Haymarket affair of Chicago in 1886.
What is the antonym of the word lethal?
Lethal means able to cause death, so its opposite is harmless. Deadly, fatal and poisonous are synonyms or close in meaning.
The word lethal comes from the Latin word letum, meaning death.
Which letter comes next in the series: Z, X, U, Q, ?
The positions are 26, 24, 21, 17 and the differences are 2, 3, 4, so the next difference is 5. 17 minus 5 is 12, which is L.
The differences in this series increase by 1 each time.
The Kirthar Range is regarded as the southern extension of which mountain range?
The Kirthar Range runs north to south along the border of Sindh and Balochistan and is usually described as the southern extension of the Sulaiman Range.
Some sources treat the Kirthar Range as a separate range; its highest point is Kutte Ji Kabar.
What is the approximate length of the River Nile?
The Nile is about 6,650 km (4,130 miles) long. It is traditionally given as the longest river in the world.
Sources differ, and some textbooks give figures near 6,400 to 6,700 km; the Amazon is also claimed as longer by some measurements.
What is the antonym of the word obsolete?
Obsolete means no longer in use or out of date, so its opposite is current or modern.
Outdated and archaic are synonyms of obsolete.
Porto-Novo is the capital of which country?
Porto-Novo is the official capital of Benin in West Africa.
Cotonou is the largest city and seat of government of Benin.
By which process do green plants prepare their food?
Plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide and water to make glucose in photosynthesis.
Oxygen is released as a by-product of photosynthesis.
Who founded the political party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)?
PTI was founded by Imran Khan in April 1996 in Lahore. He has remained its founder and leader since.
Imran Khan became Prime Minister of Pakistan in August 2018 and was removed through a no-confidence vote in April 2022.
Who said that the character of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was the Quran, that is, he was the embodiment of the Quran?
When asked about the character of the Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Aisha (RA) replied that his character was the Quran.
This narration is recorded in Sahih Muslim and the Musnad of Imam Ahmad.
Which is the oldest seaport of Pakistan, as given in Pakistani textbooks?
Karachi Port is generally given as the oldest and main seaport of Pakistan, with the modern port working from the 19th century. Gwadar and Port Qasim are much newer.
Karachi Port Trust was established in 1887; some sources name the ancient port of Banbhore as older.
Which tennis Grand Slam tournament is still played on grass courts?
Wimbledon in London is the only Grand Slam still played on grass.
The French Open is played on clay, while the US Open and Australian Open use hard courts.
What is the synonym of afraid?
Afraid means feeling fear, which is the same as frightened.
Fearless and courageous are antonyms of afraid.
What is the SI unit of temperature?
The kelvin (K) is the base SI unit of temperature. Celsius and Fahrenheit are not SI units.
0 K is called absolute zero, equal to minus 273.15 degrees Celsius.
Transparent means see-through, so its opposite is opaque, which does not let light through.
Wood and metal are opaque materials.
Which type of engine is used in jet aircraft?
Jet aircraft are powered by gas turbine engines such as the turbojet and turbofan. They produce thrust by expelling a fast stream of hot gas backwards.
Frank Whittle of Britain patented the turbojet engine in 1930.
Which major event took place in the 10th year of Hijrah (10 AH)?
Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat-ul-Wida) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)

In 10 AH the Holy Prophet (PBUH) performed his only and last Hajj and delivered the Last Sermon at Arafat. The other events took place in earlier years (Badr 2 AH, Hudaibiya 6 AH, Makkah conquest 8 AH).
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) passed away in 11 AH, a few months after the Farewell Pilgrimage.
Which is the second highest mountain in the world?
K2, at about 8,611 m, is the second highest mountain in the world after Mount Everest.
K2 is the highest mountain of Pakistan and lies in the Karakoram range.
Out of 500 students, 380 are present. What is the percentage of present students?
Find the next number in the series: 55, 579, 65, 580, ?
The series is two interleaved series. The 1st, 3rd and 5th terms go 55, 65, 75 (add 10) and the 2nd and 4th terms go 579, 580, 581 (add 1). The 5th term is 75.
Interleaved series are solved by reading odd and even positions separately.
In which surah of the Holy Quran is Ruh-ul-Amin (the Trustworthy Spirit, Hazrat Jibreel AS) mentioned?
Surah Ash-Shu'ara (26:193) says that the Trustworthy Spirit brought down the Quran upon the heart of the Prophet (PBUH). The Trustworthy Spirit is Hazrat Jibreel (AS).
Jibreel is also called Ruh-ul-Qudus in other verses, for example in Surah Al-Baqarah.
In what amount was the valley of Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh under the Treaty of Amritsar (1846)?
By the Treaty of Amritsar the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh Dogra for 75 lakh Nanakshahi rupees. This began Dogra rule in Kashmir.
The treaty was signed on 16 March 1846 after the First Anglo-Sikh War.
What is the antonym of the word amalgamate?
To amalgamate means to merge or combine into one. The opposite is to separate.
Amalgam is also the name of an alloy of mercury with another metal.
What is the antonym of competent?
Competent means having the ability to do something well; the opposite is incompetent, meaning lacking ability.
Competent and capable are synonyms, so they cannot be the antonym.
What is the antonym of foremost?
Foremost means first in position or importance; the opposite is last (hindmost).
Foremost, leading and chief are all synonyms.
What is the antonym of glory?
Glory means high honour and fame; the opposite is disgrace or shame.
What is the antonym of modern?
Modern means belonging to the present or recent time; the opposite is ancient, meaning belonging to the distant past.
Old-fashioned is another antonym of modern.
In which year was the first Asia Cup cricket tournament held?
The first Asia Cup was played in Sharjah, UAE, in 1984. India won it.
The Asia Cup was started by the Asian Cricket Council founders including Pakistan, India and Sri Lanka.
Who was the father of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA)?
Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the son of Uthman, who was known as Abu Quhafa. He accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah.
Abu Bakr's mother was Salma bint Sakhr, known as Umm-ul-Khair.
What is the base of the common logarithm?
The common logarithm uses base 10, so log 100 = 2 because 10 squared is 100.
The natural logarithm uses base e, which is about 2.718.
In which part of the world do the Bushmen (San people) live?
The Bushmen or San are indigenous hunter-gatherers of southern Africa, living mainly in the Kalahari Desert in Botswana, Namibia and South Africa.
Their languages are known for click sounds.
Accra is the capital of which country?
Accra is the capital and largest city of Ghana, on the Gulf of Guinea.
Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from Britain, in 1957.
Saint John's is the capital of which country?
Saint John's is the capital of Antigua and Barbuda, on the island of Antigua.
Antigua and Barbuda became independent from Britain in 1981.
What is the capital of Greenland?
Nuuk is the capital and largest city of Greenland.
Greenland is an autonomous territory of the Kingdom of Denmark.
What is the capital of Norway?
Oslo is the capital and largest city of Norway.
Norway is not a member of the European Union.
In which years were the Olympic Games cancelled because of World War II?
The 1940 Games (Tokyo/Helsinki) and the 1944 Games (London) were cancelled due to the war.
The Olympics were also cancelled in 1916 because of World War I.
What is the closest meaning of the word 'clumsy'?
A clumsy person moves or handles things in an awkward way and often drops or breaks them.
The opposite of clumsy is graceful or deft.
Change the voice: Were clothes dried by the mother?
Did the mother dry the clothes?
Was the mother drying the clothes?
Had the mother dried the clothes?
Does the mother dry the clothes?
The sentence is passive in the past simple tense, so the active form is 'Did the mother dry the clothes?' with the agent as the subject and the verb in base form after did.
In the past simple, the passive uses was or were plus the past participle.
Which of the following is the synonym of 'contain'?
To contain something means to have it inside or to hold it. 'Hold' is the closest in meaning.
'Contain' can also mean to keep something under control, as in contain a fire.
Which country owes the largest amount of unpaid dues (arrears) to the United Nations?
The United States is the biggest contributor to the UN budget and also has the largest unpaid arrears, over 2 billion US dollars on the regular budget in 2026 plus peacekeeping dues.
China is usually the second largest debtor, often paying its dues late in the year.
In which year and at which city was the Lahore Declaration signed between Pakistan and India?
The Lahore Declaration was signed on 21 February 1999 in Lahore by Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
It was signed a few months before the Kargil conflict of 1999.
What is the antonym of the word development?
Development means growth or advancement, while retrogression means moving backward or declining.
Other opposites of development include decline, regression and deterioration.
Difference means the quality of being unlike. Its opposite is similarity, meaning likeness.
Distinction, variety and contrast are synonyms or near synonyms of difference.
Divided means split apart. Its opposite is united.
Separated, split and broken are synonyms of divided.
What is the closest meaning of 'disgust'?
Disgust is a strong feeling of dislike and sickness at something. Revulsion has the same meaning.
Loathing and repugnance are also synonyms of disgust.
What large sea wave is usually caused by an earthquake under the ocean floor?
A strong undersea earthquake suddenly moves the sea floor and displaces a huge volume of water, which travels as a tsunami.
The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami was caused by a magnitude 9 earthquake near Sumatra.
Who was the first woman elected to the United States Congress?
Jeannette Rankin of Montana was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1916 and took her seat in 1917.
Nancy Pelosi became the first woman Speaker of the US House in 2007.
Which word is closest in meaning to "essential"?
Essential means absolutely needed, which is the meaning of necessary.
Other synonyms are vital and indispensable.
What is the antonym (opposite) of the word 'excuse' used as a verb meaning to forgive?
To excuse means to forgive or let go without blame. Its opposite is to accuse or blame someone.
'Condemn' and 'blame' are also opposites of excuse in this sense.
What is the antonym (opposite) of the word 'exhibit'?
To exhibit means to show openly. Its opposite is to conceal or hide.
An exhibition is a public show of things.
What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word 'exhibit'?
To exhibit means to show something publicly. 'Display' has the same meaning.
'Exhibit' can also be a noun meaning an object shown in a museum or court.
What is the closest meaning of the word 'exponent'?
An exponent is a person who explains or promotes an idea or cause, so an advocate is the closest meaning. An opponent is the opposite.
In mathematics, an exponent is the small raised number that shows the power of a base.
What is the antonym of futility?
Futility means uselessness or having no result. Fruitfulness, meaning being productive and useful, is the opposite.
Uselessness and vanity are synonyms of futility.
Ali is going in the direction of west. He turns left and then turns right. In which direction is Ali going now?
Facing west, a left turn points him south. Then a right turn from south points him west again.
Facing west, his left is south and his right is north.
One hectare is equal to how many square metres?
One hectare is a square of 100 m by 100 m, which is 10,000 square metres.
What is the approximate length of the Himalaya mountain range?
The Himalayas stretch for roughly 2,400 km (about 1,500 miles) from the Indus gorge in the west to the Brahmaputra gorge in the east.
Some sources give 2,400 to 2,500 km; Pakistani textbooks use about 2,400 km.
Which country was the world's largest arms importer in the latest SIPRI data (2021-25)?
SIPRI's March 2026 data for 2021-25 ranks Ukraine first, with about 9.7 percent of global arms imports, followed by India. The USA is a major exporter, not the top importer.
In the 2015-19 and earlier periods India or Saudi Arabia led, and India was second after Ukraine in 2020-24 data as well.
At how many points can two distinct lines in a plane intersect each other?
Two distinct lines meet in at most one point. If they are parallel they do not meet at all.
Two coincident lines share all their points, so they are not distinct.
The followers of Hazrat Isa (AS) are called what?
The followers of Hazrat Isa (Jesus) are called Christians. Christianity is the largest religion in the world by followers.
Which animal did the people of Thamud kill, despite the warning of Prophet Salih (AS)?
The nation of Thamud killed the she-camel sent by Allah as a miracle for Prophet Salih (AS), and was then destroyed.
The people of Thamud lived at Al-Hijr in northern Arabia.
What is the meaning of the word 'kith' (as in 'kith and kin')?
Kith means one's friends, neighbours and acquaintances, while kin means blood relatives.
Candidates often answered relatives, but that is the meaning of kin.
Kith means friends and acquaintances, so its opposite is a stranger.
The phrase 'kith and kin' means friends and relatives.
The word 'Pakistan' means the land of what?
Pakistan means 'Land of the Pure' (Pak means pure and stan means land).
The name was coined by Choudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.
Complete the sentence: The standard of living ____ since his son joined service.
The subject standard is singular and since needs the present perfect tense, so has risen is correct.
Since is followed by a point in time and goes with the present perfect tense.
Change into passive voice: How did you manage it?
How was it managed by you?
How it was managed by you?
How did it managed by you?
How is it managed by you?
A simple past question becomes was or were plus the past participle, so the passive is How was it managed by you?
In the passive voice the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.
On which date was the first martial law imposed in Pakistan?
President Iskander Mirza imposed martial law on 7 October 1958 and General Ayub Khan became the Chief Martial Law Administrator. Ayub Khan then removed Mirza on 27 October 1958.
The second martial law came in 1969 under Yahya Khan and the third in 1977 under Zia-ul-Haq.
Near which city is Mina, the valley where pilgrims stay during Hajj, located?
Mina is a valley about 5 km east of Makkah in Saudi Arabia. Pilgrims stay there and perform the stoning of the Jamarat.
Arafat and Muzdalifah are the other nearby sites of the Hajj rites.
Mogadishu is the capital of which country?
Mogadishu is the capital and largest city of Somalia, on the Indian Ocean coast.
Somalia is located in the Horn of Africa.
Monrovia is the capital city of which country?
Monrovia is the capital and largest city of Liberia in West Africa.
Monrovia is named after the US President James Monroe.
Choose the correct word: When morning ___, the murderer was caught.
The natural phrase is 'when morning came', meaning when daylight arrived.
'Arrive' and 'reach' usually need a place or destination, while 'come' suits time and seasons.
What is the height of Nanga Parbat, the ninth highest mountain in the world?
Nanga Parbat rises to 8,126 metres (26,660 feet) above sea level. It is the ninth highest mountain in the world.
Nanga Parbat is also called Diamer, meaning huge mountain, and is the second highest peak in Pakistan after K2.
What is the antonym of the word obscure?
Obscure means unclear or not well known, so its opposite is clear (or evident).
Synonyms of obscure include vague, unclear and dim.
What was the old name of Thailand?
Thailand was officially known as Siam until 1939, and again briefly from 1945 to 1949. The name was changed to Thailand, meaning land of the free.
The Gulf of Siam is now called the Gulf of Thailand.
Which word is closest in meaning to optional?
Optional means left to choice and not required. Voluntary has the same sense, while the other options mean required.
Compulsory is the antonym of optional.
From which region does the Indus River originate?
The Indus rises in the Tibetan plateau near Mount Kailash and Lake Mansarovar. It then flows through Ladakh and Pakistan into the Arabian Sea.
The Indus enters Pakistan through Gilgit-Baltistan.
The girls are 33 and the boys outnumber the girls by 7. How many boys are there?
The total number of boys and girls here is 73.
Percentage = part divided by whole, multiplied by 100.
According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the term of office of the President of Pakistan?
Article 44 gives the President a term of five years from the day he enters office.
A person cannot hold the office of President for more than two consecutive terms.
What is the synonym of the word plentiful?
Plentiful means existing in large quantities, which is the same as abundant.
Other synonyms of plentiful are ample, copious and bountiful.
In which province of Pakistan is Gwadar Port located?
Gwadar is a coastal city on the Arabian Sea in southwestern Balochistan, and its deep-sea port is there.
Gwadar Port is a key part of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).
Who invented the movable-type printing press in Europe around 1440?
Johannes Gutenberg of Germany developed the movable-type printing press in the mid-1400s.
Movable type had earlier been used in China and Korea, but Gutenberg's press is the textbook answer.
Rearrange the letters RAPIS to form the name of a famous capital city. Which city is it, and of which country is it the capital?
The letters R, A, P, I, S rearrange to make PARIS. Paris is the capital of France.
Paris stands on the River Seine and is the capital of France.
What does RCD stand for in the context of Pakistan, Iran and Turkey?
RCD stands for Regional Cooperation for Development, a 1964 economic cooperation body of Pakistan, Iran and Turkey.
It later became the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO).
Which country joined the United Nations in 2002 after its people approved membership in a referendum?
Swiss voters approved UN membership in a referendum in March 2002, and Switzerland became the 190th member in September 2002.
Switzerland had earlier rejected UN membership in a 1986 referendum.
Which Muslim League leader responded to the Nehru Report (1928) with his famous Fourteen Points in 1929?
The Nehru Report rejected separate electorates and Muslim demands, so Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in March 1929 as the Muslim reply.
Jinnah had earlier put forward his Delhi Muslim Proposals in 1927.
Which word is closest in meaning to seize?
To seize means to take hold of something suddenly and by force, which is to grab.
Capture and snatch are also synonyms of seize.
Who founded the Scientific Society in the subcontinent in 1864?
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Scientific Society at Ghazipur in 1864 to translate Western scientific works into Urdu. It later moved to Aligarh.
The society published the Aligarh Institute Gazette.
For how many years did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) live in Madina after the Hijrat?
The Prophet (PBUH) migrated to Madina in 622 CE and stayed there until his death in 632 CE, about ten years. He migrated at age 53 and passed away at 63.
The first mosque he built in Madina was Masjid Quba, followed by Masjid-e-Nabawi.
Approximately how many princely states existed in British India at the time of the partition in 1947?
At partition about 562 princely states were ruled by local rulers under British paramountcy, and each was to join India or Pakistan.
Sources differ slightly (562 to 565), and some candidates quote 530 or 565.
