The Holy Quran as revealed by Allah consists of which of the following?
The Quran itself is the Arabic text revealed by Allah. Translations and tafseer are human explanations and are not part of the Quran.
The Quran was revealed over about 23 years.
Choose the correct direct speech of: The teacher said that he could not meet all of his students.
The teacher said, "I cannot meet all of my students."
The teacher said, "He could not meet all of his students."
The teacher said, "I could not meet all of your students."
The teacher said, "I did not meet all of my students."
In direct speech the past form could changes back to can and he and his change to I and my.
Reporting words said that is dropped and quotation marks are added in direct speech.
The Dragon's Mouth (Bocas del Dragon) strait lies between Trinidad and which country?
The Dragon's Mouth is a strait between the north-west tip of Trinidad and the Paria Peninsula of Venezuela. It links the Gulf of Paria with the Atlantic Ocean.
Trinidad and Tobago is an island nation in the southern Caribbean.
Which of the following are the three types of blood cells?
Red cells, white cells and platelets
Red cells, white cells and haemoglobin
Blood contains red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets. Plasma is the liquid part, not a cell.
Red blood cells carry oxygen using haemoglobin.
Which of the following is a fard (obligatory) act of wudu according to the Hanafi school?
Washing the hands up to the wrists
The four faraiz of wudu are washing the face, washing both arms up to the elbows, wiping a quarter of the head, and washing both feet up to the ankles. Gargling and rinsing the nose are sunnah.
The four faraiz of wudu are taken from verse 6 of Surah Al-Ma'idah.
Who is the author of the book 'Jinnah of Pakistan'?
Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote 'Jinnah of Pakistan' (1984).
Hector Bolitho wrote another well-known biography titled 'Jinnah: Creator of Pakistan'.
Addition is commutative, so the order of the numbers does not matter.
Out of 1500 students, 1200 are present. How many students are absent?
The percentage of absent students here is 300 / 1500 x 100 = 20%.
Who was the first President under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, taking office in August 1973?
Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto became Prime Minister when the 1973 Constitution came into force on 14 August 1973. Fazal Ilahi Chaudhry became the President at that time.
Bhutto had been President before this, and he became Prime Minister under the new parliamentary system.
Which country became independent in 1994, ending the last United Nations trusteeship?
Palau gained independence on 1 October 1994 and became the last UN Trust Territory to end its trusteeship.
Palau later joined the United Nations in December 1994.
If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 24th be?
From the 2nd to the 24th is 22 days. 22 = 3 weeks and 1 extra days, so count 1 days forward from Friday to reach Saturday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
Which country hosted the largest number of refugees in 2017?
UNHCR reported that Turkey hosted about 3.5 million refugees at the end of 2017, the largest number worldwide.
Turkey stayed at the top of the list for several years because of the Syrian refugee crisis.
Who was the 7th President of the United States?
Andrew Jackson served as the 7th US President from 1829 to 1837, after John Quincy Adams.
Martin Van Buren followed Jackson as the 8th President.
Which is the 6th most populous country in the world?
The ranking is India, China, USA, Indonesia, Pakistan and then Nigeria in sixth place.
Brazil is seventh, and Pakistan is fifth.
If a helicopter uses 50 litres of fuel to travel 200 km, how many litres will it use to travel 350 km?
Fuel per km = 50 / 200 = 0.25 litre. For 350 km: 350 x 0.25 = 87.5 litres.
This is a direct proportion: more distance needs proportionally more fuel.
Out of 400 students, 360 are present. What is the percentage of present students?
Percentage present = 360 / 400 x 100 = 90%. The absent students are 40, which is 10%.
Present and absent percentages add up to 100%.
A helicopter uses 80 gallons of fuel to fly 320 km. How many gallons will it need to fly 800 km?
Fuel per km is 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallon. For 800 km the helicopter needs 800 x 0.25 = 200 gallons.
Problems like this are direct proportion: more distance needs proportionally more fuel.
In a class of 1500 students, 1350 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
Absent students = 1500 - 1350 = 150. Percentage absent = 150 / 1500 x 100 = 10 percent.
Percentage present in the same class is 90 percent, since the two parts add up to 100 percent.
In a class of 500 students, 150 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
Absent students = 500 - 150 = 350. Percentage absent = 350 / 500 x 100 = 70 percent.
The percentage present here is 150 / 500 x 100 = 30 percent.
On which date is Pakistan Air Force Day celebrated?
PAF Day is celebrated on 7 September to honour the PAF's performance in the 1965 war. On that day in 1965 PAF pilots, including M. M. Alam, shot down several Indian aircraft.
Defence Day is observed on 6 September.
In which year did the United States declare its independence?
The Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776. That is why 4 July is celebrated as American Independence Day.
In July 2026 the United States marked 250 years since its Declaration of Independence.
What is the closest meaning of the word annihilate?
To annihilate is to destroy something utterly so that nothing remains. Its closest meaning is to destroy completely.
The word comes from the Latin annihilare, meaning to reduce to nothing.
What is the antonym of the word sumptuous?
Sumptuous means grand and expensive-looking, so its opposite is meagre or poor. Lavish, splendid and rich are synonyms.
Sumptuous is often used for meals, such as a sumptuous feast.
What is the antonym of the word Almighty?
Almighty means having unlimited power. Its opposite is powerless or weak.
Almighty is used for God in Islam and in many other religions.
What is the antonym of coma?
A coma is a state of deep unconsciousness, so its opposite is consciousness (being awake and aware).
The word coma comes from the Greek koma, meaning deep sleep.
What is the antonym of contiguous?
Contiguous means sharing a common border or touching; the opposite is separate or detached.
Pakistan and India are contiguous countries because they share a border.
What is the antonym of divide?
Divide means to split into parts; the opposite is unite, to join together.
Unity is one of the three guiding principles of the Quaid-e-Azam: Unity, Faith and Discipline.
What is the antonym of inaccuracy?
Inaccuracy means lack of correctness; the opposite is precision or accuracy.
Error, mistake and fault are synonyms of inaccuracy.
What is the antonym of isolation?
Isolation means being alone and apart from others; the opposite is companionship or togetherness.
Isolation, seclusion and solitude are close synonyms.
What is the antonym of mild?
Mild means gentle or not severe; the opposite is harsh, meaning severe or rough.
Some candidates remembered tamed here, but tamed is not the standard antonym of mild.
What is the antonym of normally?
Normally means in the usual way; the opposite is abnormally, meaning in an unusual way.
Usually, regularly and commonly are synonyms of normally.
What is the antonym of prosperous?
Prosperous means rich and successful; the opposite is impoverished, meaning poor.
Prosperous, wealthy and thriving are synonyms.
What is the antonym of retrieve?
To retrieve is to get something back; the opposite is to lose it.
Recover and regain are synonyms of retrieve.
What is the antonym of timely?
Timely means happening at the right moment; the opposite is untimely, happening at the wrong moment.
Prompt, punctual and opportune are close synonyms of timely.
What is the antonym (opposite) of apposite?
Apposite means very appropriate or relevant to the matter; the opposite is irrelevant or inapt.
Apposite, apt and pertinent are synonyms.
What is the synonym (closest meaning) of appropriate?
Appropriate means right for a particular situation, which is the meaning of suitable.
Fitting and proper are also synonyms of appropriate.
Which Surah of the Holy Quran was revealed immediately after Surah An-Naml (the Ant) in the commonly given order of revelation?
In the commonly used (Egyptian) order of revelation, Surah An-Naml is the 48th Surah revealed and Surah Al-Qasas follows it.
Sources differ slightly on the exact order of revelation, but both An-Naml and Al-Qasas are Makki Surahs.
Who is the custodian of the House in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
The Speaker presides over the sessions of the National Assembly and is regarded as the custodian of the House. He maintains order and decides points of procedure.
In the Speaker's absence the Deputy Speaker presides over the House.
Where is the headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)?
The IAEA has its headquarters in Vienna, Austria. It promotes peaceful use of nuclear energy.
The IAEA is an independent organization that reports to the UN General Assembly and Security Council.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah pass the matriculation examination of Bombay University?
Most sources state that Jinnah passed the Bombay University matriculation examination at the age of 16 in 1892. He then left for England in early 1893.
Some sources give 1891 for his matriculation because his birth year is itself disputed.
On which date did the Pakistan Army launch Operation Zarb-e-Azb in North Waziristan?
Operation Zarb-e-Azb against militants in North Waziristan began on 15 June 2014. It followed the attack on Karachi airport and the failure of peace talks.
Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad was launched in February 2017 as its follow-up.
How many Muslims were martyred in the Battle of Badr?
Fourteen Muslims were martyred at Badr, six from the Muhajirun and eight from the Ansar. About 70 of the Quraish were killed.
About 70 Sahaba were martyred later in the Battle of Uhud.
Bait-ul-Maqdas (Bait-ul-Muqaddas), the first qibla of the Muslims, is also known by which name?
Bait-ul-Maqdas in Jerusalem is the site of Masjid-e-Aqsa (Al-Aqsa Mosque). The city itself is also called Al-Quds.
The qibla was changed from Bait-ul-Maqdas to the Kaaba in the second year of Hijra.
A barometer is used to measure what?
A barometer measures the pressure of the atmosphere. A falling reading usually warns of bad weather.
Evangelista Torricelli invented the mercury barometer in 1643.
Basic Democracies of Ayub Khan were given constitutional status by which constitution?
The 1962 Constitution made the 80,000 Basic Democrats the electoral college that elected the President and the assemblies.
The 1962 Constitution was abrogated by Yahya Khan in 1969.
In which year was the Berlin Wall built?
East Germany began building the Berlin Wall on 13 August 1961 to stop people leaving for West Berlin.
How many surahs of the Quran begin with Bismillah-ir-Rahman-ir-Rahim?
There are 114 surahs and only Surah At-Tawbah does not begin with Bismillah, so 113 do.
Bismillah occurs twice in Surah An-Naml, once at the start and once inside verse 30.
Why do we boil water before drinking it?
Boiling kills harmful bacteria and other germs that cause waterborne diseases.
Boiling for about one to three minutes is generally advised for unsafe water.

The universal set is usually denoted by U.
What is the complement of the universal set?
The complement of U contains the elements not in U, and there are none, so it is the empty set.
Likewise the complement of the empty set is the universal set.
What is the approximate value of pi?
Pi is the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter, approximately 3.14159. It is commonly written as 3.14 or 22/7.
Pi is an irrational number, so its decimal expansion never ends or repeats.
Vehicle is to tyres as sound is to ___ ?
A vehicle has tyres as a part, and sound is made up of or travels as waves. The analogy links a thing with its essential component.
Sound waves are longitudinal mechanical waves that need a medium.
Which animal uses sound waves (echolocation) to find its way, like eyes?
Bats emit high-frequency ultrasonic sounds and use the returning echoes to locate objects and prey in the dark. This is called echolocation.
Dolphins also use echolocation, and humans copy the idea in sonar.
What does the white band in the flag of Pakistan represent?
The white stripe of the flag stands for the religious minorities of Pakistan, while the green stands for the Muslim majority.
The crescent in the flag represents progress and the star represents light and knowledge.
How many wives did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) have at the time of his death, according to the commonly taught account?
At the time of his death the Holy Prophet (PBUH) had 9 wives living. In total he married 11 wives; Hazrat Khadija (RA) and Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaima (RA) had died before him.
The wives of the Prophet (PBUH) are called Ummahat-ul-Momineen (Mothers of the Believers).
In the sentence 'Wow! This is my book', what part of speech is 'Wow'?
'Wow' expresses a sudden feeling of surprise, and a word that does this is an interjection.
An interjection is usually followed by an exclamation mark.
What is the capital of New Zealand?
Wellington is the capital of New Zealand, although Auckland is its largest city.
New Zealand has no president; its head of state is the British monarch.
The product of a complex number and its conjugate is always a real number.
One third of 20 is 20 divided by 3, which is 20/3 or about 6.67.
A mixed form of 20/3 is 6 and 2/3.
Taking 1/10 of a number just moves the decimal point one place to the left.
What is one third of 25% of 120?
25% is the same as one quarter.
If the 13th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 27th day of that month be?
From the 13th to the 27th is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. So the day is the same, Sunday.
A gap of 7, 14, 21 or 28 days always gives the same weekday.
If the 23rd of a month falls on Friday, what day will the 14th of that month be?
From the 14th to the 23rd is 9 days. 9 = 7 + 2, so the 14th is 2 days before Friday, which is Wednesday.
When going backward, subtract the extra days after removing full weeks.
If the 3rd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 14th be?
From the 3rd to the 14th is 11 days. 11 = 7 + 4, so move 4 days ahead of Friday: Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday. The 14th is Tuesday.
Remove full weeks first, then count the remaining days.
If the 29th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 15th be?
From the 15th to the 29th is 14 days, exactly two weeks, so both are Monday.
Dates that are 14 days apart fall on the same weekday.
If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 15th be?
From the 2nd to the 15th is 13 days. 13 = 7 + 6, so move 6 days ahead of Friday, which gives Thursday.
Thirteen days ahead is the same as one day behind.
If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 17th be?
From the 4th to the 17th is 13 days. 13 = 7 + 6, so the 17th is 6 days after Monday, which is Sunday.
Six days ahead equals one day behind, so Monday becomes Sunday.
If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day is the 17th of the month?
From the 1st to the 17th is 16 days. 16 = 14 + 2, so the 17th is 2 days after Monday, which is Wednesday.
The 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th of a month always share the same weekday.
If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 17th be?
From the 4th to the 17th is 13 days. 13 = 7 + 6, so the 17th is 6 days after Sunday, which is Saturday.
Six days ahead equals one day behind, so Sunday becomes Saturday.
If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 18th of the month be?
From the 2nd to the 18th is 16 days. 16 = 14 + 2, so the 18th is 2 days after Friday, which is Sunday.
Subtract full weeks (multiples of 7) and count only the remainder.
What is one tenth of 10% of 140?
10% and one tenth are the same value, so this is 140 x 0.1 x 0.1 = 1.4.
In a class of 1500 students, 1340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students (to two decimal places)?
The percentage of present students here is 89.33%.
Out of 2000 students, 1600 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
The percentage of present students is 80%.
The population of a city was 1600 in 1960 and it doubles every year. What will the population be in 1967?
From 1960 to 1967 is 7 years, so the population doubles 7 times: 1600 x 2^7 = 1600 x 128 = 204800.
2^7 = 128 and 2^10 = 1024 are useful powers of two to remember.
A car runs at a speed of 180 km/h. How much distance does it travel in 20 minutes?
To convert km/h to m/s multiply by 5/18, so 180 km/h is 50 m/s.
According to the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan, what was the minimum age to be elected President?
The 1962 Constitution required the President to be a Muslim and at least 35 years old.
Under the 1973 Constitution the minimum age for President is 45 years, and the 1956 Constitution required 40 years.
Ali was born in 1974 and Azhar was born in 1970. Bilal is 2 years younger than Azhar. In which year was Bilal born?
Younger by 2 years means born 2 years later, so Bilal was born in 1970 + 2 = 1972.
Born later means younger; born earlier means older.
What position did Pakistan achieve in the 1999 Cricket World Cup?
Pakistan reached the final of the 1999 World Cup in England but lost to Australia at Lord's.
Pakistan won the World Cup once, in 1992.
Akbar was born in 1970 and Ammar in 1977. Bilal is older than Ammar. Who is the youngest of the three?
Bilal is older than Ammar, so Ammar is younger than Bilal. Ammar (1977) is also younger than Akbar (1970), so Ammar is the youngest.
A later birth year means a younger person.
1% of 200 is 2, so 2% is double that.
If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 21st be?
From the 2nd to the 21st is 19 days. 19 = 2 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Sunday to reach Friday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
If the 8th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 21st be?
From the 8th to the 21st is 13 days. 13 = 1 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Tuesday to reach Monday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day will the 21st be?
From the 1st to the 21st is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Friday to reach Thursday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 23rd be?
From the 4th to the 23rd is 19 days. 19 = 2 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Sunday to reach Friday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 23rd be?
From the 3rd to the 23rd is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Monday to reach Sunday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 24th be?
From the 1st to the 24th is 23 days. 23 = 3 weeks and 2 extra days, so count 2 days forward from Monday to reach Wednesday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 24th be?
From the 3rd to the 24th is 21 days. 21 = 3 weeks and 0 extra days, so count 0 days forward from Monday to reach Monday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 24th be?
From the 1st to the 24th is 23 days. 23 = 3 weeks and 2 extra days, so count 2 days forward from Sunday to reach Tuesday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 25th be?
From the 4th to the 25th is 21 days. 21 = 3 weeks and 0 extra days, so count 0 days forward from Monday to reach Monday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
If the 5th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 25th be?
From the 5th to the 25th is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Friday to reach Thursday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
If the 5th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 25th be?
From the 5th to the 25th is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Sunday to reach Saturday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
If the 7th day of a month is Saturday, what day will the 26th be?
From the 7th to the 26th is 19 days. 19 = 2 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Saturday to reach Thursday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 27th be?
From the 1st to the 27th is 26 days. 26 = 3 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Monday to reach Saturday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
If the 7th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 25th be?
From the 7th to the 25th is 18 days. 18 = 2 weeks and 4 extra days, so count 4 days forward from Sunday to reach Thursday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
If the 7th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 12th be?
From the 7th to the 12th is 5 days. 5 = 0 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Monday to reach Saturday.
Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.
The 24th of a month is Friday. What day is the 2nd of the same month?
The 2nd is 22 days before the 24th. 22 = 3 weeks and 1 extra day, so it is one day before Friday, which is Thursday.
Going back exactly 7 days always gives the same weekday.
Which country hosted the largest number of refugees in 2016?
According to UNHCR figures for 2016, Turkey hosted about 2.9 million refugees, mostly Syrians, which was the largest number in the world.
Pakistan was the second largest host in 2016 with about 1.4 million refugees, mostly Afghans.
Which country hosted the 2018 Asian Games?
The 2018 Asian Games were held in Indonesia, in the cities of Jakarta and Palembang.
The 2022 Asian Games, held in 2023, were hosted by Hangzhou in China.
On which date did the 2018 Asian Games begin?
The 18th Asian Games opened in Jakarta on 18 August 2018 and ended on 2 September 2018.
Indonesia's Jakarta and Palembang shared hosting of that edition.
Where were the 2018 Winter Olympic Games held?
The 2018 Winter Olympics took place in Pyeongchang, South Korea, in February 2018.
The 2018 Summer Olympics did not exist: the Summer Games were held in Rio in 2016 and Tokyo in 2021.
Which country hosted the 2018 Asia Cup cricket tournament?
The 2018 Asia Cup was played in the United Arab Emirates, in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, in September 2018.
India won the 2018 Asia Cup by beating Bangladesh in the final.
What is the value of the percentage of absent students if 300 out of 500 students are present?
Percentage present plus percentage absent always equals 100%.
In a class of 1500 students, 300 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
There are 1500 students in a class, 1200 are boys and 300 are girls. What is the percentage of girls?
Out of 1200 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students, to two decimal places?
A helicopter flies at 340 km/h. About how much time does it take to cover 700 km?
Time = distance / speed = 700 / 340 = 2.06 hours, which is about 2 hours 4 minutes.
Speed = distance / time is the basic formula behind such questions.
In a class of 500 students, 360 are present. How many students are absent?
As a percentage, 140 out of 500 is 28%.
A plane uses 80 gallons of fuel to cover 320 miles. How many gallons will 800 miles need?
Fuel per mile = 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallon. For 800 miles: 800 x 0.25 = 200 gallons.
The same method works with kilometres and litres.
A car travels at 78 km/h. How far will it travel in 12 minutes?
To change minutes into hours, divide by 60.
How many elements are there in each row of a matrix of order 4x3?
A matrix of order 4x3 has 4 rows and 3 columns, so each row has 3 elements.
The total number of elements in a 4x3 matrix is 12.
A matrix is of order 4x3. How many rows does it have?
The order of a matrix is written as rows x columns, so a 4x3 matrix has 4 rows.
In which year was the first martial law in Pakistan lifted?
General Ayub Khan imposed martial law in October 1958 and it was lifted on 8 June 1962 when the new constitution came into force.
The 1962 Constitution gave Pakistan a presidential system with Ayub Khan as President.
Which word is the antonym of abrogate?
To abrogate means to repeal or do away with a law. Its opposite is to enact or establish a law.
Repeal, annul and revoke are synonyms of abrogate.
Which word is a synonym of abrogate?
To abrogate means to formally cancel or repeal a law or agreement, so repeal has the same meaning.
The word comes from the Latin abrogare, meaning to repeal a law.
On which date was the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan abrogated?
General Yahya Khan imposed martial law on 25 March 1969 after Ayub Khan resigned, and the 1962 Constitution was abrogated.
Ayub Khan resigned on 25 March 1969 and handed power to the army chief Yahya Khan.
On which date was the first Constitution of Pakistan (1956) adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
The Constituent Assembly adopted the 1956 Constitution on 29 February 1956.
It came into force on 23 March 1956, which is why that day was celebrated as Republic Day.
What is the title of Imam Abu Hanifa's well-known book on beliefs?
Al-Fiqh al-Akbar is the creed work traditionally attributed to Imam Abu Hanifa.
Al-Muwatta is by Imam Malik and Kitab-ul-Umm is by Imam Shafi'i; some scholars debate how much of Fiqh-e-Akbar is by Abu Hanifa himself.
What is the commutative property of addition?
a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c
The commutative property says that changing the order of the numbers being added does not change the sum, so a + b = b + a.
Addition and multiplication are commutative, but subtraction and division are not.
Who was the first black President of South Africa?
Nelson Mandela became South Africa's first black President in May 1994 after the first fully democratic elections.
He spent 27 years in prison and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993 jointly with F. W. de Klerk.
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya (1870) in reply to which book?
A Life of Mahomet by William Muir
Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya was written to answer the objections raised against the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in William Muir's book A Life of Mahomet. Sir Syed wrote it after visiting England in 1869.
Sir Syed's own book on the 1857 war was Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind.
Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya is a work in defence of Islam written by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan. It was published in 1870.
Sir Syed founded the Aligarh Muslim (MAO) College in 1875.
Ahmed is 6 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. When Ahmed is 14 years old, what will be his sister's age?
Sister's age now is 6 x 3 = 18 years, so she is 12 years older than Ahmed. When Ahmed is 14, she is 14 + 12 = 26.
In age problems the difference in ages stays fixed while both ages increase equally.
On which date did Allama Muhammad Iqbal die?
Allama Iqbal died in Lahore on 21 April 1938. He is buried near the Badshahi Mosque.
Iqbal's birth date is 9 November 1877 in Sialkot, which is observed as Iqbal Day.
Complete the analogy: Sailor is to Navy as Airman is to ____.
A sailor serves in the Navy, in the same way an airman serves in the Air Force.
Soldier, sailor and airman are the ranks-and-file terms for the Army, Navy and Air Force.
How many sons did Hazrat Aisha (RA) have?
Hazrat Aisha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), had no children. She is called Ummul Momineen.
She was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) and is known for narrating many hadiths.
On which date was the Jammu and Kashmir State Subject Rule issued?
The State Subject Rule defining who was a permanent resident of Jammu and Kashmir was issued by Maharaja Hari Singh on 20 April 1927. It limited land ownership and state jobs to state subjects.
Maharaja Hari Singh ruled Jammu and Kashmir from 1925 to 1947.
If Ahmad is older than Akbar and Akbar is older than Ali, then Ali is ____.
The order of age is Ahmad, then Akbar, then Ali, so Ali is the youngest. Therefore Ali is younger than Ahmad (and Akbar).
Such statements can be solved by writing the names in order from oldest to youngest.
Is 5x - 4y + 6 = 0 an algebraic expression or an equation?
It has an equals sign with an expression on each side (the right side is 0), so it is an equation. It is a linear equation in two variables.
An algebraic expression, such as 5x - 4y + 6, has no equals sign.
The product of two algebraic expressions is ____ the product of their LCM and HCF.
For any two expressions (or numbers) f and g, f x g = LCM x HCF. So the product is equal to the product of LCM and HCF.
For numbers, 12 x 18 = 216 and LCM 36 x HCF 6 = 216.
What comes next in the series: X3, Y2, Z?
The letters move forward X, Y, Z while the numbers go down 3, 2, 1. So the next term is Z1.
Letter-number series usually move the letters and numbers by fixed steps.
If the letters of the word ARGUMENT are arranged in alphabetical order, which letter is third?
The letters of ARGUMENT in alphabetical order are A, E, G, M, N, R, T, U. The third letter is G.
ARGUMENT has 8 letters and 3 vowels: A, U and E.
By what other name is Pakistan Day, observed on 23 March, also known?
Pakistan Day commemorates the Lahore Resolution (Pakistan Resolution) passed on 23 March 1940, so it is also called Resolution Day. It also marks the adoption of the first constitution in 1956.
Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956 when its first constitution came into force.
Who is the angel of death (Malak-ul-Maut) in Islamic belief?
Hazrat Izrail (AS) is the angel entrusted with taking souls at death. The Quran refers to him as the angel of death in Surah As-Sajdah.
Hazrat Israfil (AS) is the angel who will blow the trumpet on the Day of Judgement.
Two adjacent angles which together form a right angle are called what?
Two angles whose sum is 90 degrees are complementary. Together they make one right angle.
Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees, which is a straight line.
What is the antonym of the word abolish?
To abolish is to put an end to something officially. Its opposite is to establish, meaning to set up.
Abolish, cancel, remove and end are all close in meaning to each other.
What is the antonym of the word accumulated?
Accumulated means gathered together over time. The opposite is dispersed, meaning scattered.
Accumulate is a synonym of amass and collect.
Find the missing number in the analogy 2 : X :: 4 : 16.
Since 4 : 16 shows that 16 is the square of 4 (4 x 4 = 16), the same rule applies to 2, so X = 2 x 2 = 4.
Square numbers are 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 and so on.
Anemia is mainly caused by the deficiency of which element?
Iron is needed to make haemoglobin in red blood cells. Without enough iron the blood cannot carry enough oxygen, which causes anemia.
Area of a parallelogram = base x ______.
The area of a parallelogram is its base multiplied by its perpendicular height, also called its altitude.
The area of a triangle is half of base times altitude.
What is the antonym of despite?
Despite means in spite of something; the opposite idea is because of, which gives a cause.
Despite, in spite of and notwithstanding all mean the same thing.
What is the antonym of eliminated?
Eliminated means removed or left out; the opposite is included or retained.
Eliminate comes from the Latin eliminare, meaning to drive out of doors.
What is the antonym of evidently?
Evidently means in a clear and obvious way; the opposite is obscurely, meaning in an unclear way.
Evidently, obviously and clearly are synonyms of each other.
What is the antonym of foe?
A foe is an enemy; the opposite is a friend.
Foe and enemy are synonyms, as are ally and friend.
What is the antonym of improvement?
Improvement means becoming better; the opposite is deterioration, meaning becoming worse.
Progress and betterment are synonyms of improvement.
What is the antonym of impudent?
Impudent means rude and disrespectful; the opposite is respectful or polite.
Impudent, insolent and cheeky are synonyms.
What is the antonym of multitude?
A multitude is a very large number of people or things; the opposite is a handful, a very small number.
Multitude, crowd and throng are synonyms.
What is the antonym of nourishment?
Nourishment is the food needed for life and growth; the opposite is starvation, the lack of food.
Nutrition and sustenance are synonyms of nourishment.
What is the antonym of pragmatic?
Pragmatic means dealing with things in a practical way; the opposite is idealistic, based on ideals rather than reality.
Pragmatic, practical and realistic are synonyms.
What is the antonym of purification?
Purification means making something clean; the opposite is contamination, making it impure.
Pollution is another antonym of purification.
What is the antonym of recalcitrant?
Recalcitrant means stubbornly resisting authority; the opposite is obedient or compliant.
Candidates remembered willing or ready, which are also close in meaning to obedient.
What is the antonym of refuse?
To refuse is to say no to something offered; the opposite is to accept.
Refuse as a noun means rubbish, but in this question it is the verb.
What is the antonym of shameful?
Shameful means causing shame; the opposite is honourable, deserving respect.
Shameful, disgraceful and scandalous are synonyms.
What is the antonym of strict?
Strict means demanding obedience to rules; the opposite is lenient, meaning easy-going or merciful.
Strict, stern and rigid are synonyms.
What is the antonym of underhand?
Underhand means done in a secret or dishonest way; the opposite is honest or open.
Aboveboard is the usual one-word opposite of underhand.
What is the antonym of virtue?
Virtue means moral goodness; the opposite is vice, meaning immoral behaviour.
The pair virtue and vice is a classic antonym pair.
What is the supreme law (apex law) of Pakistan?
The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, adopted in 1973, is the supreme law of the country and all other laws must conform to it.
The 1973 Constitution was passed under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and has 280 Articles.
What is the arithmetic mean of 24 and 26?
The arithmetic mean of two numbers lies exactly halfway between them.
What is the arithmetic mean of 24 and 36?
The arithmetic mean is the sum of the values divided by how many there are.
What is the arithmetic mean of 8 and 36?
The geometric mean of 8 and 36 is different: it is the square root of 288, about 16.97.
Ten Companions of the Prophet (PBUH) given the glad tidings of Paradise in one lifetime
The ten wives of the Prophet (PBUH)
Ten Muslim commanders of the Battle of Badr
The Ashra-e-Mubashara are ten Companions whom the Prophet (PBUH) named as people of Paradise while they were alive. They include the four Rightly Guided Caliphs.
Their names are listed in a famous hadith narrated by Abdur Rahman bin Awf and Sa'id bin Zaid.
When did the USA drop atom bombs on Japan?
The USA dropped the atom bomb on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945 and on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.
Japan announced its surrender soon afterwards, ending the Second World War.
What is the national game of Australia, as commonly stated?
Cricket is commonly given as the national game of Australia. It is the most popular summer sport there.
Australia has no officially declared national game, so sources differ; Australian rules football is also very popular.
After the Quran, what is the most authentic source of Islamic teachings?
The Hadith and Sunnah, the sayings and actions of the Prophet (PBUH), explain and complete the Quran. They are the second source of Islamic law.
Ijma and Qiyas are usually counted as the third and fourth sources.
What is the average of 23 and 32?
Average equals the sum of values divided by the number of values.
What is the average of 28 and 36?
The average of two numbers lies exactly midway between them.
What is the average of 32 and 20?
Average is also called the arithmetic mean.
What is the y-axis also called in the coordinate plane?
The vertical y-axis is called the ordinate axis and the y-coordinate is the ordinate. The horizontal x-axis is the abscissa axis.
The point where both axes meet is called the origin.
How many times is the name of Hazrat Ayesha (RA) mentioned in the Quran?
The Quran does not mention Hazrat Ayesha (RA) by name. She is referred to indirectly in some verses about the Prophet's household.
The Prophet's wives are addressed as the Mothers of the Believers in Surah Al-Ahzab.
In which Surah was the incident of slander (Ifk) against Hazrat Ayesha (RA) addressed and her innocence declared?
Verses 11 to 20 of Surah An-Nur declare Hazrat Ayesha (RA) innocent of the false accusation. This is known as the incident of Ifk.
The incident took place after the expedition of Banu Mustaliq.
According to the 14 Points of Quaid-e-Azam, what form of government should India have?
A federation with residuary powers vested in the provinces
A unitary system with a strong centre
The 14 Points demanded that the future constitution of India be federal. The residuary powers were to remain with the provinces.
Quaid-e-Azam presented the 14 Points in March 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.
Muslim Bagh in Balochistan is famous for which mineral?
Muslim Bagh in Zhob district of Balochistan is known for its chromite (chromium ore) deposits. Chromite is mined there on a large scale.
Chamalang in Balochistan is known for coal and Saindak for copper and gold.
On which date was the Baghdad Pact first signed between Turkey and Iraq?
Turkey and Iraq signed the Baghdad Pact in Baghdad on 24 February 1955. Britain, Pakistan and Iran joined later in 1955.
After Iraq left in 1959 the pact was renamed CENTO.
Who founded the city of Baghdad?
The Abbasid caliph Al-Mansur founded Baghdad in 762 AD. He made it his capital and named it the City of Peace.
Baghdad reached its golden age under Haroon-ur-Rasheed and Mamun-ur-Rasheed.
What is the approximate area of Balochistan province?
Balochistan covers about 347,190 square km, which is about 44 percent of Pakistan. It is the largest province by area.
Punjab covers about 205,344 square km and Sindh about 140,914 square km.
Which was the first commercial bank of Pakistan, as commonly stated?
Habib Bank Limited (HBL), founded in 1941 and moved to Karachi after 1947, is generally called the first commercial bank of Pakistan.
Sources differ somewhat, but most Pakistani textbooks name Habib Bank.
In which city is the head office of the State Bank of Pakistan located?
The State Bank of Pakistan has its head office on I.I. Chundrigar Road in Karachi. It began operations on 1 July 1948.
The State Bank has a main branch in Islamabad too.
The ruling tribe of Makkah to which the Prophet (PBUH) belonged
Quraysh (Quraish) was the leading tribe of Makkah and the custodian of the Kaaba. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) belonged to its clan Banu Hashim.
Banu Quraiza, Banu Nadir and Banu Qaynuqa were Jewish tribes of Madina.
By what other name is the Sukkur Barrage known?
The Sukkur Barrage on the Indus was opened in 1932 and named the Lloyd Barrage after the Governor of Bombay, Sir George Lloyd.
It irrigates millions of acres in Sindh through seven canals.
The area of a triangle is 24 square cm and its base is 4 cm. What is its height?
Area = (1/2) x base x height, so 24 = (1/2) x 4 x h = 2h. Therefore h = 12 cm.
The height of a triangle is the perpendicular distance from the base to the opposite vertex.
Akbar is 3 times as old as his sister. How old will his sister be when Akbar is 15 years old?
Akbar's age is 3 times his sister's age, so sister = 15 divided by 3 = 5 years.
In ratio questions, divide the larger age by the multiple to get the smaller age.
Ali's sister is 3 times as old as Ali. How old will Ali's sister be when Ali becomes 14 years old?
Sister's age = 3 times Ali's age = 3 x 14 = 42 years.
Here the sister is the older one, so multiply Ali's age by 3.
On which date did Pakistan become an Islamic Republic under the 1956 Constitution?
The first Constitution of Pakistan came into force on 23 March 1956 and the country became the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
23 March is celebrated as Pakistan Day, which also recalls the Lahore Resolution of 1940.
In which year did the revelation (wahi) first begin to descend on Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in the Cave of Hira?
The Prophet (PBUH) was about 40 years old when Angel Jibreel brought the first revelation, in 610 AD during Ramadan.
The first revelation consisted of the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq.
Which countries jointly hosted the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
The 2026 FIFA World Cup was hosted jointly by the United States, Canada and Mexico, from June to July 2026.
The previous World Cup in 2022 was held in Qatar.
Who is the Prime Minister of Belgium as of October 2026?

What did the Fourteen Points of Quaid-e-Azam (1929) demand about electorates?
Separate electorates to continue for Muslims
The Fourteen Points demanded that Muslims keep their separate electorates until they themselves agreed to give them up.
The Fourteen Points were presented in March 1929 as an answer to the Nehru Report.
If sets A and B have no common element, what is n(A union B)?
For any sets n(A union B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A intersection B). With no common element the intersection is empty, so n(A union B) = n(A) + n(B).
Sets with no common element are called disjoint sets.
Where does the Indus River rise and where does it fall?
Rises near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and falls into the Arabian Sea
Rises in the Hindu Kush and falls into the Bay of Bengal
Rises in the Karakoram and falls into the Persian Gulf
Rises in Kashmir and falls into the Arabian Sea at Gwadar
The Indus rises from the Tibetan plateau near Lake Mansarovar, flows through Ladakh and Pakistan and ends in the Arabian Sea near Karachi.
Entirely means completely, and its opposite is partially, which means only in part.
Other opposites are partly and slightly.
What is the equation y = 7x + 7 called?
The highest power of the variables x and y is 1, so it is a linear equation.
The graph of a linear equation in two variables is a straight line.
On what date was the World Health Organization (WHO) established?
The WHO constitution came into force on 7 April 1948, which is why World Health Day is observed every year on 7 April. The WHO was set up as a specialised agency of the United Nations.
The WHO headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland.
On what date was the Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) of Pakistan established?
WAPDA was created by an Act in 1958 and began functioning on 12 February 1958. It was formed to develop Pakistan's water and power resources.
WAPDA was later split so that power distribution moved to separate companies, but it still builds dams such as Tarbela and Mangla.
In which country does Mount Everest, the highest peak in the world, mainly lie?
Mount Everest lies in the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and the Tibet region of China. The main summit is usually described as being in Nepal.
Everest is about 8,849 metres high; Nepal calls it Sagarmatha and Tibet calls it Chomolungma.
On what date did the War of Independence of 1857 begin at Meerut?
The sepoys of the Bengal Army at Meerut revolted on 10 May 1857, and this started the War of Independence. The rebels then marched to Delhi.
The last Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah Zafar, was declared the leader of the rebellion.
Which product is Pakistan's largest export by value?
Textiles, including cotton cloth, yarn, bed linen and readymade garments, make up more than half of Pakistan's exports by value. Rice is the largest food export but is much smaller.
Pakistan is among the top cotton-producing countries in the world.
In which year was Facebook founded?
Mark Zuckerberg launched Facebook on 4 February 2004 from his Harvard University dormitory.
The company was renamed Meta Platforms in 2021.
What is the value of 10! (factorial of 10)?
We need two numbers whose product is -6 and whose sum is +5. These numbers are +6 and -1, so x^2 + 5x - 6 = (x + 6)(x - 1).
The roots of this expression are x = 1 and x = -6.
A farm has 3 goats, 5 cows and 14 hens. What is the total number of legs of these animals?
Goats and cows have 4 legs each: (3 + 5) x 4 = 32 legs. Hens have 2 legs each: 14 x 2 = 28 legs. The total is 32 + 28 = 60.
The count of the farmer's legs is not included.
Who was the first person to fly faster than the speed of sound?
US Air Force pilot Chuck Yeager broke the sound barrier on 14 October 1947 flying the Bell X-1 rocket plane.
The speed of sound at sea level is about 1,235 km/h, called Mach 1.
The former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) became part of which province?
FATA was merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through the 25th Constitutional Amendment, passed in May 2018.
The merged areas were divided into districts such as North Waziristan and South Waziristan.
FATA stands for Federally Administered Tribal Areas, the seven agencies on the Afghan border governed directly by the federal government.
FATA was merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2018.
Where is the headquarters of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) located?
The FATF secretariat is hosted at the OECD headquarters in Paris, France.
The FATF was set up by the G7 in 1989 to fight money laundering and terrorist financing.
What was the name of the father of Hazrat Yunus (AS)?
According to Islamic tradition, Hazrat Yunus (AS) was the son of Matta (Matthew). He was sent to the people of Nineveh.
Hazrat Yunus (AS) is also called Dhun-Nun and Sahib al-Hut because of the incident of the fish.
Who was the father of Hazrat Yaqub (AS)?
Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS) and the grandson of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).
Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the father of Hazrat Yusuf (AS).
In which year was Fatima Jinnah born?
Fatima Jinnah, the sister of Quaid-e-Azam, was born in Karachi in 1893.
Her birth date is given as 30 or 31 July 1893 in different sources, and she died in 1967.
In which city was Fatima Jinnah born?
Fatima Jinnah was born in Karachi in 1893 into the family of Jinnahbhai Poonja.
She was given the title Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).
Surah Al-Fil of the Holy Quran is named after which animal?
Al-Fil means the elephant. The surah describes how Allah destroyed the army of Abraha that came with elephants to demolish the Kaaba.
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in the same Year of the Elephant.
In a class of 33 students, 2/3 are boys. How many are girls?
Girls are 1/3 of the class, which is the same as 33 divided by 3.
To which country did the World War 2 leader Winston Churchill belong?
Winston Churchill was the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom during most of World War 2 (1940-1945).
He also served a second term as Prime Minister from 1951 to 1955.
The ratio 4:12 equals 1:3, so 3:X must also be 1:3. Therefore X = 3 x 3 = 9.
In a proportion a:b :: c:d, the product of extremes equals the product of means (ad = bc).
If the ordered pairs (x, y - 1) and (2, -1) are equal, what are the values of x and y?
Equal ordered pairs have equal coordinates. So x = 2 and y - 1 = -1, which gives y = 0.
Ordered pairs (a, b) and (c, d) are equal only when a = c and b = d.
What is the height of K2 in feet?
K2 is 8,611 metres high. Multiplying by 3.28 gives about 28,251 feet.
K2 is the second highest mountain in the world after Mount Everest at 29,032 feet.
Change into passive voice: It is time to eat food.
It is time that food eats.
Food is time to be eaten.
It is time for food to be eaten.
It was time for food to be eaten.
The active infinitive 'to eat food' becomes 'for food to be eaten' in the passive, with the present tense 'is' kept.
In passive voice the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.
Change into active voice: By whom is the boy being fed?
The passive 'is being fed' (present continuous) becomes 'is feeding' in the active, and 'by whom' becomes 'who'.
The agent after 'by' becomes the subject of the active sentence.
Shoe is to foot as helmet is to what?
A shoe is worn to protect the foot, and a helmet is worn to protect the head.
This is a type of analogy based on an object and the body part it protects.
Which one is different from the rest: square, yard, meter, foot?
Yard, meter and foot are units of length. Square is a geometric shape.
One yard equals three feet, and one meter is about 3.28 feet.
What was the name of the foster sister of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
The Prophet (PBUH) was nursed by Halima Sadia, whose daughter Shaima was his foster sister. She helped to care for him as a child.
Halima Sadia belonged to the tribe of Banu Saad.
What is the closest meaning of the word fostering?
To foster means to encourage the growth or development of something or someone. Nurturing has the closest meaning.
The word foster is also used for caring for a child who is not one's own, as in foster mother.
What is the antonym of fostering?
Fostering means encouraging and caring for growth. Neglecting means failing to care, so it is the opposite.
Nurturing, supporting and promoting are synonyms of fostering.
Where was the Battle (Ghazwa) of Khyber fought?
An oasis north of Madinah inhabited by Jews
Khyber was a fortified oasis about 150 km north of Madinah, home to Jewish tribes. The Muslims fought there in 7 AH.
The famous fort of Khyber was conquered under the leadership of Hazrat Ali (RA).
What is the SI unit of force?
Force is mass times acceleration, so its unit is kg m per second squared, which is called the newton (N).
One newton is the force that gives a mass of 1 kg an acceleration of 1 metre per second squared.
Which country is the fourth most populous country in the world?
The ranking by population is India, China, the United States, then Indonesia. Pakistan is fifth.
Population rankings change over time; India overtook China as the most populous country in 2023.
Who was the fourth Khalifa (Rightly Guided Caliph) of Islam?
The Rightly Guided Caliphs in order were Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali (may Allah be pleased with them).
Hazrat Ali (RA) ruled from 656 to 661 AD.
What is the closest opposite of the word friend?
A foe is an enemy, which is the opposite of a friend. The other options are close in meaning to friend.
Another antonym of friend is enemy.
What is the antonym of fugitive?
A fugitive is a person who has escaped or is running away. A captive is someone held and not free, which is the opposite.
Runaway and escapee are synonyms of fugitive.
What is the synonym of fugitive?
A fugitive is a person who has escaped from custody or is hiding. Runaway has the same meaning.
Fugitive comes from the Latin word fugere, meaning to flee.
What is the synonym of the word full?
Full means containing as much as possible, so complete is a synonym. Empty, hollow and thin are not.
The antonym of full is empty.
If a function is both onto and one-one, what is it called?
A function that is both one-one (injective) and onto (surjective) is called bijective. Such a function has an inverse.
A bijective function matches each element of the domain with exactly one element of the range and covers the whole range.
Which book was written by Mahatma Gandhi as his autobiography?
The Story of My Experiments with Truth
Gandhi wrote his autobiography titled The Story of My Experiments with Truth. It was first written in Gujarati.
The Discovery of India was written by Jawaharlal Nehru and India Wins Freedom by Maulana Azad.
What is the antonym of genuine?
Genuine means real or authentic. Fake means not real, so it is the opposite.
Counterfeit and bogus are also antonyms of genuine.
In a group, 2/3 of the people are men. What percentage of the group is women?
Women = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3 of the group. 1/3 x 100 = 33.33 percent.
The fraction 1/3 equals 33.33 percent as a decimal-percent value.
Change into passive voice: God gives us happiness.
Happiness is given to us by God.
Happiness was given to us by God.
Happiness has been given us by God.
We are given by God happiness.
The sentence is in the simple present tense, so the passive uses is/are plus the past participle: Happiness is given to us by God.
In passive voice the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.
The speed of a train is twice that of a car. What is the speed of the train when the car is going at 30 km/hr?
Speed is distance divided by time, so a train at 60 km/hr covers 60 km in one hour.
When a man asked the Prophet (PBUH) who most deserved his good treatment, whom did the Prophet name first?
In the well known hadith the Prophet (PBUH) said "your mother" three times, and only then "your father".
This hadith is reported in Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.
If Ali is greater than Usama, then Usama is ___ than Ali.
Ali being greater means Usama is lesser, that is smaller, than Ali.
Greater and smaller (or less) are opposite comparisons.
The Karen ethnic group lives mainly in which countries?
The Karen people live mostly in Myanmar (Burma), especially Kayin State, and in western Thailand along the border.
Karen rebels in Myanmar have fought the government since 1949.
In which city is the Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) based?
The NSG has no permanent headquarters, but its secretariat and point of contact work from Vienna, Austria, beside the IAEA.
The NSG was formed in 1974 after India's first nuclear test.
To which clan of the Quraish did Hazrat Hafsa (RA), wife of the Prophet (PBUH), belong?
Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar bin Khattab (RA), who belonged to the Banu Adi clan of the Quraish.
Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was married to the Prophet (PBUH) in 3 AH after the death of her first husband.
What was the Hajr-e-Aswad (Black Stone) incident in the life of the Prophet (PBUH) before prophethood?
He settled the Quraish dispute over who would place the Black Stone by lifting it on a cloak and placing it himself
He destroyed the idols around the Kaaba
He was given the first revelation near the Black Stone
He led the Quraish in a war over the Kaaba
While the Kaaba was being rebuilt, the tribes quarrelled over who would set the Black Stone. The Prophet (PBUH) placed it on a sheet, had the leaders lift it together, and set it in place himself.
The Quraish called him Al-Amin for this wise decision.
Halving a fraction doubles its denominator.
Finger is to hand as leaf is to what?
A finger is a part attached at the end of the hand, just as a leaf is a part attached to a branch.
Analogy questions are solved by finding the relationship between the first pair and applying it to the second.
What is a square matrix called in which all the diagonal elements are one and all other elements are zero?
A square matrix with ones on the main diagonal and zeros elsewhere is the identity matrix.
Multiplying any matrix by the identity matrix leaves it unchanged.
Wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS)
Hazrat Sara (AS) was the first wife of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and the mother of Prophet Ishaq (AS).
Hazrat Hajra (AS) was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS).
What is the HCF of 12 and 24?
12 = 2 x 2 x 3 and 24 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3, so the common factors give 2 x 2 x 3 = 12.
When one number divides the other, the smaller number is the HCF.
Where was the headquarters of the Western European Union (WEU), now dissolved?
The WEU had its headquarters in Brussels, Belgium.
The WEU ended its operations in 2011 after its functions passed to the European Union.
What is the commonly quoted height of Mount Sakesar, the highest peak of the Salt Range?
Mount Sakesar, in district Khushab, is about 4,992 feet (1,522 m) high and is the highest point of the Salt Range.
Some sources give about 1,525 m (5,003 ft), so sources differ slightly.
In which direction was the Hijrat of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) made?
In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madina (then called Yathrib) to escape the persecution of the Quraish.
The Hijri calendar begins from this migration.
Which major expedition of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) took place in 9 Hijri?
The Ghazwa of Tabuk against the Byzantines took place in Rajab 9 AH. This year is also known as the Year of Delegations.
Tabuk was the last Ghazwa in which the Prophet (PBUH) personally led the army.
In which Hijri year was the Ghazwa of Hunain fought?
The Battle of Hunain was fought against the tribes of Hawazin and Thaqif in Shawwal 8 AH, soon after the Conquest of Makkah.
The Muslims were first pushed back by an ambush but then won the battle.
Ali is 4 years old and his sister is twice his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 6 years old?
Sister is 2 x 4 = 8 years now, so the age gap is 4 years. When Ali is 6, sister is 6 + 4 = 10 years.
The age difference between two people stays the same over time.
Ali is 4 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 8 years old?
Sister is 3 x 4 = 12 years now, so the gap is 8 years. When Ali is 8, sister is 8 + 8 = 16 years.
Multiplying the new age by 3 (24) is a common mistake, as the gap stays fixed.
Ali is 4 years old and his sister is 4 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 6 years old?
Sister is 4 x 4 = 16 years now, so the gap is 12 years. When Ali is 6, sister is 6 + 12 = 18 years.
The age gap never changes as both get older at the same rate.
The Himalaya mountain range lies between the Indian subcontinent and which plateau?
The Himalayas separate the Indian plain (India, Nepal, Bhutan) in the south from the Tibetan Plateau of China in the north.
The range crosses five countries: Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bhutan and China.
What is the approximate length of the Hindu Kush mountain range?
The Hindu Kush extends about 800 km (500 miles) from central Afghanistan to northern Pakistan.
Tirich Mir (7,708 m) is its highest peak.
Which is different from the rest: Kangaroo, Horse, Deer, Cow?
The horse, deer and cow are all hoofed land mammals, while the kangaroo is a marsupial that carries its young in a pouch.
Which is different from the rest: Donkey, Zebra, Horse, Giraffe?
Donkey, zebra and horse all belong to the horse family (Equidae), while the giraffe belongs to a different family.
The giraffe is the tallest land animal.
What was the relationship between Hazrat Ishaq (AS) and Hazrat Ibrahim (AS)?
Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Sarah (AS). He was the younger brother of Hazrat Ismail (AS).
Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
Find the value of i(-2i + 3), where i is the imaginary unit.
Multiply out: i(-2i + 3) = -2i squared + 3i. Since i squared = -1, this is 2 + 3i.
The imaginary unit i is defined by i squared = -1.
What is the imaginary part of the complex number 3 + 9i?
In the form a + bi the imaginary part is b. Here b = 9.
IMF stands for International Monetary Fund. It is a UN-linked financial institution that supports global monetary cooperation.
The IMF was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference and is headquartered in Washington DC.
Who was the first Prime Minister of India?
Jawaharlal Nehru became India's first Prime Minister on 15 August 1947 and served until 1964.
Lal Bahadur Shastri was the second Prime Minister of India.
On which date did India's Constituent Assembly adopt the Constitution of India?
The Constituent Assembly adopted the Indian Constitution on 26 November 1949. It came into force on 26 January 1950.
India celebrates 26 January as Republic Day.
On which river is the Bhakra Dam of India built?
The Bhakra Dam is built on the Sutlej River in Himachal Pradesh, India. It forms the Gobind Sagar reservoir.
The Sutlej was allotted to India under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960.
Which institution is responsible for distributing river water among the provinces of Pakistan?
IRSA was set up in 1992 under the Water Apportionment Accord of 1991 to distribute Indus system water among the provinces. WAPDA builds and runs dams and power projects.
The Water Apportionment Accord was signed in 1991 by the four provinces.
What does integration (definite integral) of a function show geometrically?
A definite integral gives the area between the curve and the x-axis over an interval. Slope is given by differentiation.
Integration is the reverse process of differentiation.
Where is the headquarters of the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (UN Human Rights)?
The OHCHR (UN Human Rights) is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. The UN Human Rights Council also meets in Geneva.
The UN Headquarters itself is in New York.
What was the name of the father of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) according to the Holy Quran?
Surah Al-An'am names Ibrahim's father as Azar. Some scholars say Tarikh (Terah) was his given name, so sources differ.
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah, the friend of Allah.
In which year was the first adhesive postage stamp, the Penny Black, introduced?
The Penny Black was issued in Britain on 1 May 1840 and was the world's first adhesive postage stamp. It was introduced by the postal reformer Rowland Hill.
Sindh Dak, issued in 1852 in Sindh, was the first postage stamp of the subcontinent.
In which year was the company Google founded?
Google was incorporated by Larry Page and Sergey Brin on 4 September 1998. The search project began earlier in 1996 at Stanford University.
Candidates often say 1996 because the BackRub research project started that year.
In which year was WhatsApp founded?
WhatsApp was founded in 2009 by Jan Koum and Brian Acton. It started as a status-update app and soon became a messaging service.
In which year was YouTube founded?
YouTube was founded in February 2005 by Chad Hurley, Steve Chen and Jawed Karim. The first video was uploaded in April 2005.
Who is credited with inventing the first compound microscope?
The Dutch spectacle maker Zacharias Janssen is generally credited with the first compound microscope around 1590. Other inventors are sometimes named.
Robert Hooke published Micrographia in 1665 and coined the word cell.
Alexander Graham Bell was granted the first US patent for the telephone in 1876. He is credited as its inventor.
Bell's first successful call was made to his assistant Thomas Watson in 1876.
What is the commonly quoted length of the Pakistan-Iran border?
The Pakistan-Iran border is commonly given as about 909 km. It separates Balochistan from Iran's Sistan and Baluchestan province.
Some sources give about 959 km, so figures differ slightly by source.
What is the currency of Ireland?
Ireland is a member of the Eurozone and uses the euro. It replaced the Irish pound in 2002.
The euro notes and coins entered circulation on 1 January 2002.
The M-1 motorway connects Islamabad with which city?
The M-1 (Peshawar-Islamabad Motorway) links Peshawar with Islamabad. It is about 155 km long.
The M-2 motorway connects Islamabad with Lahore.
In which Islamic month was Pakistan established in 1947?
Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947, which was 27 Ramadan 1366 AH. It was the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) by common belief.
It was also a Friday, the blessed day of the week.
What is the currency of Israel?
Israel's currency is the New Israeli Shekel (ILS). It was introduced in 1985.
The Israeli currency symbol is the sign for the shekel.
Which angel is the guardian of the gate of Jannah (Paradise)?
Ridwan is the angel in charge of Jannah according to Islamic belief. Malik is the keeper of Jahannam.
Jannah is said to have eight gates.
What is the literal meaning of the Arabic word Jannat?
Jannat comes from the Arabic root meaning to hide or cover. It literally means a garden with dense trees.
The Quran uses the word Jannah for Paradise.
Jeddah is a famous port city of which country?
Jeddah is on the Red Sea coast of Saudi Arabia. It is the main gateway for pilgrims travelling to Makkah.
Jeddah is the second largest city of Saudi Arabia after Riyadh.
On which prophet did the angel Hazrat Jibrael (AS) bring the final revelation, the Holy Quran?
Hazrat Jibrael (AS) brought the Holy Quran to the last Prophet, Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH), over about 23 years. The first revelation came in the Cave of Hira.
Jibrael (AS) is also called Ruh-ul-Amin and brought revelation to earlier prophets as well.
On which date of the Islamic calendar did the tragedy of Karbala take place?
Hazrat Imam Hussain (RA) and his companions were martyred at Karbala on 10 Muharram 61 AH (October 680 CE), the day of Ashura.
The tragedy took place during the rule of the Umayyad ruler Yazid.
Who is known as the conqueror of Khaibar (Khyber)?
Hazrat Ali (RA) led the final assault and conquered the fort of Qamus at Khaibar in 7 AH, so he is called Fateh-e-Khaibar.
He is also known as Haidar-e-Karrar and Asadullah.
The Khilafat Movement in India arose mainly because of which event?
The defeat of the Ottoman Empire in the First World War and the threat to the Caliphate
After the First World War the Allies defeated Turkey and threatened the Ottoman Caliph, so Indian Muslims launched the movement to save the Caliphate.
The Nehru Report (1928) came years after the Khilafat Movement (1919-1924).
Who led the Muslim army in the Battle of Khyber?
The Battle of Khyber (7 AH) was fought against the Jews of Khyber and the Muslim army was led by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself.
The main fort Qamus was conquered at the hands of Hazrat Ali (RA).
In mathematics, subtraction is which kind of operator?
Subtraction needs two operands (a - b), so it is a binary arithmetic operator.
The minus sign used with one number, as in -5, acts as a unary operator.
Sikandar (Alexander the Great) was the king of which land?
Alexander the Great was king of Macedonia, a kingdom in northern Greece, and invaded India in 326 BC.
He fought King Porus at the Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum) in present-day Pakistan.
Which country is known as the land of golden fibre?
Jute is called the golden fibre because of its golden colour and high value, and Bangladesh is the world's leading producer of it. So Bangladesh is called the land of golden fibre.
Who was appointed as the first commander of the Muslim army in the Battle of Mu'tah?

The Prophet (PBUH) appointed Hazrat Zayd bin Haritha as commander, with Hazrat Jafar bin Abi Talib and Hazrat Abdullah bin Rawaha next in line. After all three were martyred, Hazrat Khalid bin Walid took command.
The Battle of Mu'tah was fought in 8 AH against the Byzantine forces.
Who founded the All India Muslim League in 1906 at Dhaka, hosting the meeting where it was formed?

The All India Muslim League was formed on 30 December 1906 at Dhaka at a meeting hosted by Nawab Khwaja Salimullah of Dhaka. Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk and Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk were also prominent in its formation.
Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah Aga Khan III was its first president.
Which letter comes next in the series: a, c, d, f, ...?
The positions are 1, 3, 4, 6 and the steps alternate +2 and +1. After 6 the step is +1, giving position 7, which is g.
Which comes next in the series: A3, C5, E7, G9, ?
The letters skip one each time (A, C, E, G, I) and the numbers go up by 2 (3, 5, 7, 9, 11). So the next term is I11.
Letters moving by two places each step are a common pattern in verbal reasoning.
Which comes next in the series: z1, x3, v5, ?
The letters go backwards skipping one (z, x, v, t) and the numbers go up by 2 (1, 3, 5, 7). So the next term is t7.
z is the 26th letter, x the 24th, v the 22nd and t the 20th.
Rearranging the letters AGREMYN gives the name of which country?
The letters A, G, R, E, M, Y, N can be arranged to spell GERMANY, using all seven letters exactly once.
Berlin is the capital of Germany.
Which is the largest flower in the world?
Rafflesia arnoldii, found in the rainforests of Indonesia, has the largest single flower, which can be about one metre across.
It has no leaves, stems or roots and is a parasite on vines.
Change into passive voice: All his friends laughed at him.
He was laughed at by all his friends.
He is laughed at by all his friends.
He had laughed at all his friends.
All his friends were laughed at by him.

Phrasal verbs such as laugh at keep their preposition in the passive voice.
I want a book ___ is not in the library. Fill in the blank.
A relative pronoun for a thing is which, so it correctly links to the book. Who and whom are used for people.
That can also be used here in place of which.

No, because it has a constant

In which month and year did the last US troops leave Afghanistan?
The final US military flights left Kabul airport on 30 August 2021 (31 August in Kabul), ending a war of about twenty years. The Taliban had taken Kabul on 15 August 2021.
The US-led invasion of Afghanistan began in October 2001.
What is the value of log 2 + log 8 (same base)?
By the product rule, log a + log b = log (a x b). So log 2 + log 8 = log 16.
Also log 16 = 4 log 2, because 16 = 2 to the power 4.
What is the value of log 8 divided by log 4?
log 8 = 3 log 2 and log 4 = 2 log 2. So the ratio is 3 log 2 / 2 log 2 = 3/2.
The ratio of two logs of the same base does not depend on the base chosen.
Which country has the longest sea coastline in the world?
Canada has the longest coastline of any country, more than 200,000 km including its islands.
Indonesia, Russia and Australia are usually listed after Canada.
In a class of 30 students, 20 are male. What percentage of the students are female?
Males make up 66.67% of this class.
What is the capital of the Maldives?
Male is the capital and most populous city of the Maldives.
The Maldives is an island nation in the Indian Ocean.
What is the currency of the Maldives?
The Maldivian currency is the rufiyaa.
Taka is the currency of Bangladesh and ngultrum is the currency of Bhutan.
Who invented the printing press with movable type in Europe?
Johannes Gutenberg of Germany invented the movable-type printing press around 1440.
His first major printed work was the Gutenberg Bible.
Which Caliph had copies of the Holy Quran prepared and sent to the major cities of the Islamic state?
Hazrat Usman (RA) had the Quran written in one standard dialect and sent copies to cities such as Kufa, Basra, Damascus and Makkah.
Hazrat Usman (RA) is therefore called Jame-ul-Quran.
What is the name of the native people who live in the highlands of Guatemala?
The Maya people form a large part of the population of the Guatemalan highlands and still speak Mayan languages.
The ancient Maya civilization also built great cities in Guatemala such as Tikal.
What is the magnetic field outside an ideal long solenoid?
In an ideal long solenoid the field is uniform inside and almost zero outside, because the fields of the turns cancel there.
The field inside a solenoid is B = mu0 n I.
What is the SI unit of magnetic induction (magnetic flux density)?
Magnetic flux density is measured in tesla, which equals one weber per square metre.
Gauss is a smaller non-SI unit, with 1 tesla equal to 10,000 gauss.
Which of the following is the meaning of the word marginal?
Marginal means small, slight or of minor importance, or relating to an edge or margin. A marginal gain is therefore a very small gain.
The word comes from the Latin word margo, meaning edge.
Who was the President of Pakistan when the first martial law was imposed in 1958?
Iskander Mirza was President and he himself declared martial law on 7 October 1958 by abrogating the 1956 Constitution. Ayub Khan was Army chief and became the Chief Martial Law Administrator.
Mirza was forced out within three weeks and later went into exile in London.
Who gave the atomic theory of matter in the early nineteenth century?
John Dalton proposed in 1803 that matter is made of tiny indivisible particles called atoms, with atoms of one element being alike. This is called Dalton's atomic theory.
Rutherford later discovered the nucleus and Bohr gave the planetary model of the atom.
Arrange in order: 2, 3, 4, 5, 7. With five values the middle (third) value is 4.
The mean of these numbers is 4.2, which is different from the median.
What is the median of the series 2, 4, 6, 7, 9?
The numbers are already in order and there are five of them, so the middle (third) value is 6.
The mean is 28 / 5 = 5.6, which differs from the median.
What is the meaning of deceit?
Deceit means the act of deceiving, that is, cheating or misleading someone by dishonest behaviour.
What is the meaning of disconnect?
To break the connection or separate
Disconnect means to detach or break the link between two things, for example to cut off a phone line.
What is the meaning of emancipate?
Emancipate means to free someone from legal, social or political restrictions, for example from slavery.
The Emancipation Proclamation of 1863 declared slaves in the Confederate states free in the USA.
What is the meaning of mirth?
Mirth means joyful amusement, especially when shown by laughter.
Its synonyms are merriment and gaiety.
What is the meaning of the word geminate?
To double or arrange in pairs
Geminate means to double something or to occur in pairs. It comes from the Latin gemini, meaning twins.
In linguistics a geminate is a doubled consonant sound.
What is the meaning of the name Anas?
The Arabic name Anas means affection, friendliness or companionship. Hazrat Anas bin Malik (RA) was a famous servant and companion of the Prophet (PBUH).
Anas bin Malik narrated over two thousand hadiths.
In which country was the company Microsoft founded?
Microsoft was founded by Bill Gates and Paul Allen in 1975 in Albuquerque, New Mexico, USA. It later moved to Redmond, Washington.
Microsoft is best known for the Windows operating system and Microsoft Office.
At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate from Makkah to Madina?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in 570 AD and migrated in 622 AD, which is commonly given as 53 years of age in Pakistani textbooks.
Some sources say 52 years because of differences in counting the years.
For which purpose is the Nishan-e-Haider awarded in the Pakistan Armed Forces?
Nishan-e-Haider is the highest military gallantry award of Pakistan. It is given for extraordinary bravery in the face of the enemy.
Captain Raja Aziz Bhatti was among the recipients, for the 1965 war.
Under which ministry do the Pakistan Army, Navy and Air Force work?
The three armed services work under the Ministry of Defence, which handles their administrative and policy matters.
The Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee works for coordination among the services.
Under which federal ministry does the national food department fall in Pakistan?
Ministry of National Food Security and Research
Food policy, wheat and crop matters are handled by the Ministry of National Food Security and Research.
The ministry was earlier called the Ministry of Food and Agriculture.
What is the range of Pakistan's Ra'ad-II cruise missile?
Ra'ad-II is an air-launched cruise missile with a range of about 600 km. It is a nuclear capable weapon.
The original Ra'ad (Hatf-VIII) has a range of 350 km.
What is the mode of the digits 7, 7, 7, 9, 9, 8, 8, 1, 0?
The mode is the value that occurs most often. The digit 7 appears three times, 9 and 8 twice each.
A data set can have more than one mode if values tie for the highest count.
What is the mode of the digits 8, 5, 8, 7, 6, 5, 7, 8, 3, 8?
The digit 8 appears four times, 5 and 7 twice each, and 6 and 3 once. So the mode is 8.
Mean, median and mode are the three measures of central tendency.
Which are the first and the last months of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar?
The Hijri year begins with Muharram and ends with Dhul Hijjah (Zil Hajj), the month of Hajj.
The Hijri calendar starts from the migration of the Prophet (PBUH) to Madina in 622 AD.
What was the main feature of the Minto-Morley Reforms of 1909?
Introduction of separate electorates for Muslims
The Indian Councils Act 1909 (Minto-Morley Reforms) gave Muslims the right to elect their own representatives through separate electorates.
The reforms are named after Lord Minto (Viceroy) and John Morley (Secretary of State for India).
The Faisal Mosque in Islamabad was designed by which architect?
The Faisal Mosque was designed by the Turkish architect Vedat Dalokay and its design is inspired by a Bedouin tent.
It was funded by the Saudi king Faisal bin Abdulaziz and is named after him.
What is the motto of the Pakistan Army?
The motto of the Pakistan Army is Iman, Taqwa, Jihad fi Sabilillah (Faith, Piety, Struggle in the way of Allah).
Faith, Unity, Discipline is the motto given by Quaid-e-Azam to the nation.
In which country is Mount Olympus, the highest mountain in its range and home of the gods in myth, located?
Mount Olympus is located in northern Greece and is its highest mountain.
In Greek mythology it was the home of the twelve Olympian gods.
Table Mountain, a famous flat-topped mountain, is located near which city?
Table Mountain overlooks the city of Cape Town in South Africa.
It is one of the New7Wonders of Nature.
A religious reform movement among the Muslims of Bengal
A political party of the Hindus
The Faraizi Movement was started in Bengal by Haji Shariatullah to make Muslims follow the faraiz (obligations) of Islam and give up un-Islamic customs.
After Haji Shariatullah the movement was led by his son Dudu Miyan.
Ali walks 10 km north, then turns left and then turns right. Which direction is he facing now?
Facing north, a left turn makes him face west; a right turn from west brings him back to face north.
A left turn followed by a right turn cancels out.
Which was the first James Bond film?
Dr. No, released in 1962 with Sean Connery, was the first James Bond film.
James Bond was created by the writer Ian Fleming.
What is 4x multiplied by 4x, plus 2x multiplied by 4x?
4x times 4x = 16 x squared, and 2x times 4x = 8 x squared. Their sum is 24 x squared.
When multiplying terms, the coefficients are multiplied and the powers of x are added.
Fill in the blank: The man was charged ___ murder.
The correct phrase is 'charged with' a crime.
'Accused of' is also correct, but 'charged' takes the preposition 'with'.
Why did Allah send Hazrat Musa (AS) to Pharaoh (Firaun)?
To invite him to Allah and demand freedom for Bani Israel
To fight a war against him
Hazrat Musa (AS) was sent to call Pharaoh to worship one Allah and to free Bani Israel from slavery.
His brother Hazrat Harun (AS) was sent with him to help.
To which place did the Prophet (PBUH) migrate in 622 AD (13 Nabawi)?
In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madina (then called Yathrib).
This migration (Hijrat) is the start of the Hijri calendar.
What gift did Allah give to the Prophet (PBUH) during the Miraj?
During the Miraj the five daily prayers (Salah) were made obligatory for Muslims.
Salah is the only pillar of Islam that was given directly in the heavens.
In which region of Pakistan is Nanga Parbat located?
Nanga Parbat lies in the Diamer district of Gilgit-Baltistan, in the western part of the Himalayas.
It is known as the Killer Mountain because of the many climbers who died on it early on.
A French military leader and Emperor
Napoleon Bonaparte rose through the French army and made himself Emperor of France in 1804.
He was exiled to the island of Saint Helena, where he died in 1821.
Change the narration into indirect speech: He said, "He was playing football."
He said that he is playing football.
He said that he had been playing football.
He said that he was play football.
He said that he will be playing football.
