In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Yathrib, which was later named Madinat-un-Nabi, or Madina.
The Islamic Hijri calendar starts from this migration.
In which year did Pakistan win its first Olympic gold medal?
Pakistan beat India 1-0 in the hockey final at the Rome Olympics of 1960 to win its first gold.
The other golds came in 1968 at Mexico City and 1984 at Los Angeles.
Who is called Shaheed-e-Millat in Pakistan?
Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, was assassinated in Rawalpindi in 1951. He is therefore called Shaheed-e-Millat, the martyr of the nation.
Liaquat Ali Khan was shot at Company Bagh, which was later renamed Liaquat Bagh.
In which city is Bait-ul-Muqaddas (Al-Aqsa Mosque) located?
Bait-ul-Muqaddas is in Jerusalem, in Palestine. It was the first qibla of the Muslims.
The qibla was changed to the Kaaba in the second year of Hijra.
What was the name of the brother of Hazrat Musa (AS)?
Hazrat Haroon (AS) was the elder brother of Hazrat Musa (AS). He was also a prophet and helped Musa (AS) before Pharaoh.
Musa (AS) asked Allah to make Haroon (AS) his helper.
Which term comes next in the series: A88, C76, F52, ?
Letters move forward by 2, 3, 4, so after F comes J. Numbers drop by 12, 24, 36: 88, 76, 52, 16. So the next term is J16.
When differences double or grow in steps, check the differences of the differences.
Who discovered the nucleus of the atom?
Ernest Rutherford discovered the atomic nucleus in 1911 through his gold foil experiment.
James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932 and J. J. Thomson discovered the electron.
Yathrib is the old name of which city?
The city of Yathrib was renamed Madinah-tun-Nabi after the Hijrat of the Prophet (PBUH).
Madinah is also called Madinah Munawwarah.
Making food by green plants using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide
In photosynthesis, plants use chlorophyll in chloroplasts and sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.
Photosynthesis releases the oxygen we breathe.
Who won the Battle of Plassey (1757)?
The East India Company under Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula of Bengal, helped by the betrayal of Mir Jafar.
The victory began British rule in India.
With which surah does the Quran begin in its written order?
The first surah in the Mushaf (written order) is Surah Al-Fatiha, followed by Surah Al-Baqarah.
Surah Al-Fatiha has 7 verses and is recited in every rakat of prayer.
If the diameter of a circle is 56, what is its radius?
Radius is half of the diameter. 56 / 2 = 28.
What is the meaning of the word reasonable?
Reasonable means having good sense and being fair. Its synonym is sensible.
What was the character of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) according to Hazrat Aisha (RA)?
When asked about his character, Hazrat Aisha (RA) replied that his character was the Quran.
This reply is reported in Sahih Muslim.
In a room there are 18 girls and 6 boys. What percentage of the people in the room are boys?
Total people = 18 + 6 = 24. Percentage of boys = 6/24 x 100 = 25 percent.
The percentage of girls in the room is 75 percent.
Fill in the blank: ____ you were sleeping, the telephone rang.
'While' joins two actions that happen at the same time, and here it links a clause with a subject and verb.
'During' is followed by a noun, not by a clause like 'you were sleeping'.
Fill in the blank: Throw the pen ___ the dustbin.
The preposition 'into' shows movement towards the inside of something, so the pen goes into the dustbin.
'In' shows position while 'into' shows movement toward the inside.
Change into indirect speech: She told, "It is a very cold day."
She told that it is a very cold day.
She told that it was a very cold day.
She told that it had been a very cold day.
She told that it will be a very cold day.
The reporting verb is in the past tense, so the present tense "is" changes to the past tense "was". The quotation marks are removed and "that" is added.
In indirect speech, "today" changes to "that day" and "now" changes to "then".
"Trivial" means of little importance, so its opposite is "important" or significant.
Synonyms of trivial include petty, minor and insignificant.
On which date was the One Unit scheme enforced in West Pakistan?
The West Pakistan One Unit scheme was enforced on 14 October 1955, merging the western provinces and states into one unit.
One Unit was abolished by General Yahya Khan on 1 July 1970.
Which Prime Minister of Pakistan was the first to visit China?
Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy visited China in October 1956 and was the first Pakistani Prime Minister to do so.
Pakistan recognised the People's Republic of China in January 1950.
In a group of 24 people, 18 are women. What percentage of the group are men?
The women are 75% of the group.
Choose the correct word: She said to me that she ___ TV.
The reporting verb said is in the past, so the present continuous is watching changes to was watching.
Were is used only with plural subjects or you.
If the 19th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 26th be?
From the 19th to the 26th is 7 days, exactly one week, so the weekday is the same: Sunday.
Dates 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday.
Which session of the All India Muslim League passed the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution on 23 March 1940?
The Lahore Resolution was passed at the 27th annual session of the All India Muslim League held at Minto Park, Lahore, in March 1940.
Quaid-e-Azam presided over this session, held from 22 to 24 March 1940.
In which year was the present Constitution of Pakistan made?
The present Constitution was passed by the National Assembly in April 1973 and enforced on 14 August 1973.
It was drafted under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
Who was the first president of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay in December 1885 under the presidency of W. C. Bonnerjee.
A. O. Hume, the founder of the Congress, was its first general secretary.
What is the antonym of the word abhorrent?
Abhorrent means disgusting or hateful, so its opposite is admirable.
A synonym of abhorrent is detestable.
What is the synonym of the word abhorrent?
Abhorrent means causing strong disgust, which matches detestable.
The related noun is abhorrence, meaning strong hatred.
What is the closest meaning of 'accomplished' when used for a person?
As an adjective, accomplished describes a person who is highly skilled or talented, such as an accomplished pianist.
As a verb form, accomplished also means achieved or completed.
To admonish someone is to warn or scold them firmly. Reprimand and rebuke are its synonyms.
The noun form is admonition, meaning a warning.
Which part of speech describes or modifies a verb?
An adverb tells us how, when, where or how much an action happens. So it describes a verb.
An adverb can also modify an adjective or another adverb.
An aeroplane flies in the air mainly because of which force?
The curved wings make air move faster over the top, creating lower pressure above and an upward force called lift. Lift must be greater than or equal to weight to fly.
The four forces on an aeroplane are lift, weight, thrust and drag.
Which companion narrated the largest number of ahadith?
Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) is reported to have narrated about 5374 ahadith, the most of any companion.
Hazrat Aisha (RA) and Ibn Umar (RA) are also among the major narrators.
At which session of the All India Muslim League was the Lahore Resolution passed?
The Lahore Resolution was passed at the 27th annual session of the All India Muslim League, held at Lahore from 22 to 24 March 1940.
The resolution was moved by A. K. Fazlul Huq on 23 March 1940.
Which word comes first alphabetically in a dictionary: Adidas or Addida?
Both words start with AD. The third letter of Addida is D and of Adidas is I, and D comes before I, so Addida comes first.
Dictionaries compare words letter by letter from the left until the first difference.
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: I always have a problem ____ my laptop.
The correct phrase in English is 'have a problem with' something.
Prepositions are fixed by usage, for example 'good at', 'suffer from' and 'problem with'.
What is the antonym of obnoxious?
Obnoxious means very unpleasant or offensive, so its opposite is pleasant.
Synonyms of obnoxious are odious and objectionable.
What is the antonym of disingenuous?
Disingenuous means not sincere or pretending to know less, so the opposite is candid, meaning frank and honest.
What is the antonym of spirited?
Spirited means full of energy and courage, so the opposite is lifeless or dull.
Wild is not an antonym of spirited, it is the antonym of tame.
What is the meaning of the word astonished?
Astonished means greatly surprised or amazed.
Synonyms of astonished include amazed, stunned and startled.
In which year did the United States attack Afghanistan after the 9/11 events?
The US-led attack on Afghanistan began on 7 October 2001, after the attacks of 11 September 2001.
The US-led forces finally withdrew from Afghanistan in August 2021.
What is the average of the first five natural numbers?
The first five natural numbers are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Their sum is 15 and 15 / 5 = 3.
The average of the first n natural numbers is (n + 1) / 2.
In aviation, in which unit is altitude commonly measured internationally?
International civil aviation standards use feet for altitude and flight levels.
A few countries, such as China and Russia, have used metres for altitude.
In which year did Benazir Bhutto become Prime Minister of Pakistan for the second time?
Her first term was from 1988 to 1990 and her second term started in October 1993 after the 1993 elections.
Her second government was dismissed in 1996.
Rana Bhagwandas, who served as acting Chief Justice of Pakistan, belonged to which religious community?
Rana Bhagwandas was a Hindu from Sindh and became the first non-Muslim to serve as Chief Justice of Pakistan, in an acting capacity in 2007.
He was a judge of the Supreme Court of Pakistan from 1994 until he retired in 2009.
What is the approximate length of the Pakistan-China border according to most Pakistani textbooks?
Most Pakistani textbooks give the length of the border with China as about 523 km, running along the Karakoram range in Gilgit-Baltistan.
Sources differ, and some give about 596 km; the Khunjerab Pass is the only border crossing.
Which angel brought the message (revelation) of Allah to the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.)?
Hazrat Jibrail (A.S.) carried the revelation from Allah to the Prophet (S.A.W.). He is the angel of revelation.
Hazrat Jibrail (A.S.) is also called Ruh-ul-Amin.
If there are 2 cows and the number of camels is twice the number of cows, how many camels are there?
Always read whether the question asks for camels only or for the total animals.
For how many years did Hazrat Abdul Muttalib take care of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) after his mother passed away?
The Prophet (S.A.W.) was 6 when his mother died and 8 when his grandfather died, so Abdul Muttalib cared for him for about 2 years.
After that, his uncle Abu Talib took care of him.
What does the idiom 'to bell the cat' mean?
To take a dangerous task for the benefit of the group
The idiom comes from a fable in which mice wanted someone to tie a bell on the cat. It means to take on a risky task on behalf of others.
The fable is attributed to Aesop.
What is the antonym of the word charming?
Charming means pleasing and attractive. The opposite is unattractive or ugly.
Charming comes from the Latin word carmen, meaning song or spell.
Who was the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan before General Asim Munir?
General Qamar Javed Bajwa served as Chief of Army Staff from November 2016 to November 2022. General Asim Munir then took over from him.
General Raheel Sharif served before Bajwa, from 2013 to 2016.
What is the common difference in the series 2, 6, 10, 14?
Each term is 4 more than the one before: 6 - 2 = 4, 10 - 6 = 4, 14 - 10 = 4.
A series with a constant difference is called an arithmetic progression.
What is the conjugate of the complex number 8 - 3i?
The conjugate of a + bi is a - bi, so the sign of the imaginary part changes: 8 + 3i.
The product of a complex number and its conjugate is always a real number.
What is the idiom to throw cold water on something?
To throw cold water on a plan or idea means to discourage it or show doubt about it.
A similar idiom is to dampen someone's spirits.
In a field there is 1 cow, the donkeys are twice the number of cows, and there are 7 horses. How many animals are in the field?
Donkeys are 2 times 1, which is 2. Total animals are 1 cow plus 2 donkeys plus 7 horses, which is 10.
If the question counted only donkeys and horses, the total would be 9.
What is the derivative of 2x sin x with respect to x?
Use the product rule: d/dx (u v) = u'v + u v' with u = 2x and v = sin x. This gives 2 sin x + 2x cos x.
The product rule is also called Leibniz's rule.
What is the derivative of ln x with respect to x?
The natural logarithm ln x has derivative 1/x for x greater than zero. This is a standard result of calculus.
The derivative of e to the power x is e to the power x itself.
Where is the Kot Diji fort located, in terms of district?
Kot Diji is a town in Khairpur district of Sindh. Its fort was built by the Talpur rulers.
Kot Diji is also an important pre-Harappan archaeological site.
Which of the following is a three-dimensional shape?
A cube has length, width and height, so it is three-dimensional. Square, triangle and circle are flat two-dimensional shapes.
A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.
Which of these antonyms is opposite in meaning to 'disgusting'?
Disgusting means very unpleasant. Delightful is the opposite, meaning very pleasant.
Repulsive and foul are synonyms of disgusting.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'disgusting'?
Disgusting means causing strong dislike or sickness. Revolting has nearly the same meaning.
Other synonyms are repulsive, nasty and foul.
Which group of vitamins does not dissolve in water?
Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. They dissolve in fat and not in water.
Vitamins B-complex and C are water-soluble.
In which division of Balochistan is Gwadar located?
Gwadar district is part of Makran Division in southwestern Balochistan.
Makran division also includes Kech (Turbat) and Panjgur districts.
How many districts does Punjab (Pakistan) have at present?
Punjab has 41 districts grouped into 10 divisions. A claim of 45 districts was officially rejected.
Earlier counts were 36 and then 40 before the newer districts were added.
Which document served as the basis for the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan?
The Objective Resolution of 1949 became the preamble and guiding basis of the constitutions of Pakistan, including 1973.
It was made a substantive part of the constitution by Article 2-A in 1985.
Article 25-A of the Constitution of Pakistan deals with which right?
Article 25-A, added by the 18th Amendment in 2010, gives free and compulsory education to children aged 5 to 16.
The 18th Amendment was passed in April 2010.
For about how long did the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan remain in force?
It was enforced on 23 March 1956 and abrogated in October 1958. This is about two and a half years.
Pakistan became an Islamic Republic under this constitution.
Which of the following lists the elementary row operations of a matrix?
A row can be swapped with another, multiplied by a non-zero constant, or have a multiple of another row added to it.
Elementary row operations do not change the solution set of a linear system.
What is the meaning of the idiom 'to end in smoke'?
The idiom means that a plan or effort fails and produces no result.
A similar idiom is 'to go up in smoke'.
Mount Everest is part of which mountain range?
Mount Everest lies in the Mahalangur sub-range of the Himalayas on the Nepal and China (Tibet) border.
K2, the second highest peak, is in the Karakoram range.
Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still exists today?
The Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt is the only one of the original seven wonders that still stands.
It was built about 2560 BC as a tomb for the pharaoh Khufu.
Ali is 2 years old and Faraz is twice Ali's age. How old is Faraz?
After 2 more years Ali will be 4 and Faraz will be 6.
Which prophet was thrown into fire by Namrood (Nimrod)?
Namrood threw Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) into a big fire, but Allah made it cool and safe for him.
This event is mentioned in Surah Al-Anbiya of the Quran.
What is the synonym of the word fondness?
Fondness means a feeling of liking or love, which is the same as affection.
Other close words for fondness are liking, love and attachment.
What is the antonym of the word fondness?
Fondness means liking, so its opposite is dislike.
Aversion and hatred are also opposites of fondness.
From which ruler did Muhammad bin Qasim conquer Sindh in 712 AD?
Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir, the Brahman ruler of Sindh, in 712 AD.
The conquest began after Arab ships were attacked near Debal, and Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam.
Which city of Pakistan is known as the City of Gardens?
Lahore is called the City of Gardens because of its many Mughal and public gardens such as Shalimar and Jinnah Garden.
Lahore is also called the cultural capital of Pakistan.
Greenland is an autonomous territory of which country?
Greenland is a self-governing territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.
Wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS)
Hazrat Sarah was the first wife of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and the mother of Prophet Ishaq (AS).
Hazrat Hajra (AS), the second wife of Ibrahim (AS), was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS).
What does the Arabic word Hijrat mean?
Hijrat means to leave one's homeland and migrate to another place, especially for the sake of faith.
The Islamic Hijri calendar begins from the Prophet's migration from Makkah to Madina in 622 AD.
What does the idiom "to pick holes" mean?
To pick holes in something means to look for its weak points and criticise it.
A similar phrase is "to find fault with".
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: We are pinning all our hopes ___ the new manager.
The correct phrase is "pin hopes on someone", meaning to depend on that person for success.
The same preposition is used in "pin the blame on someone".
A square matrix with all elements zero
A square matrix with 1 on the main diagonal and 0 elsewhere
A matrix with only one row
A matrix with all elements equal to 1
An identity matrix is a square matrix whose main diagonal elements are all 1 and all other elements are 0.
Multiplying any matrix by the identity matrix of a suitable size leaves it unchanged.
Which famous event took place in 8 Hijri?
The Muslims conquered Makkah peacefully in Ramadan 8 AH.
Battle of Hunain and the Battle of Muta also took place in 8 AH.
What is the main use of insulin in medicine?
Insulin is a hormone that controls blood sugar, so it is given to diabetic patients who cannot make enough of it.
Insulin is made by the beta cells of the pancreas.
The first Governor General of Pakistan
The first Prime Minister of Pakistan
The first Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan
Iskander Ali Mirza became Governor General in 1955 and then the first President of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution.
He was removed by Ayub Khan after the 1958 martial law.
What is the synonym of the word 'indigenous'?
Indigenous means originating in or belonging naturally to a place, which is the meaning of native.
The word comes from the Latin indigena, meaning born in the country.
On what date did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations?
Pakistan was admitted to the United Nations on 30 September 1947, a few weeks after independence.
Pakistan was the 56th member state of the UN.
Pakistan is mainly what kind of country in terms of its economy and land use?
Agriculture is the backbone of Pakistan's economy and a large part of its population depends on it.
The Indus plain of Punjab and Sindh is the main farming region.
Who is the Federal Minister for Law and Justice of Pakistan?
Azam Nazeer Tarar is the Federal Minister for Law and Justice in the present government, as reported in 2026.
Farogh Naseem held the post earlier, in the 2021 government of Imran Khan.
Which letter comes next in the series: Z, Y, X, ?
The letters go backward in the alphabet one place at a time: Z, Y, X, then W.
W is the 23rd letter of the English alphabet.
How many daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) died during his lifetime?
The Prophet (PBUH) had four daughters. Zainab, Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum (RA) died in his lifetime, and only Fatimah (RA) died after him, about six months later.
Hazrat Uthman (RA) married two of the daughters, Ruqayyah and then Umm Kulthum, and is called Dhun-Nurayn.
Who liberated Jerusalem (Bait-ul-Muqaddas) from the Crusaders in 1187 AD?
Salahuddin Ayyubi defeated the Crusaders in the Battle of Hattin in 1187 and then took back Jerusalem. He was the founder of the Ayyubid dynasty.
Jerusalem was first conquered by the Muslims in 637 AD under Hazrat Umar (RA).
Which is the longest river of Pakistan, also called the Sindh river?
The Indus River is about 2,900 km long and is the longest river of Pakistan. It is also called Sindh or Abaseen.
It starts near Mount Kailash in Tibet and falls into the Arabian Sea near Karachi.
Which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was known as Umm-ul-Masakin (Mother of the Poor)?
Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaimah (RA) was famous for feeding and helping the poor, so she was called Umm-ul-Masakin.
She died soon after marriage, during the lifetime of the Prophet (PBUH).
What does the word burgle mean?
To enter a building illegally in order to steal
To burgle means to break into a house or building to steal things, and the person who does it is a burglar.
Burglary is different from robbery, which involves force against a person.
What is the meaning of the word compact?
Closely packed and small in size
Compact means closely and neatly packed together, and taking little space.
A compact disc was named for its small, dense format.
In which year did Pakistan become a member of the World Bank?
Pakistan joined the World Bank and the IMF on 11 July 1950.
The World Bank headquarters is in Washington DC.
In which game has Pakistan won Olympic gold medals?
Pakistan won Olympic gold three times in hockey, in 1960, 1968 and 1984.
Pakistan also won a bronze in Tokyo 1964 in hockey.
What is the commonly quoted range of Pakistan's Babur (Hatf-VII) cruise missile?
The Babur ground-launched cruise missile, first tested in 2005, is commonly given a range of about 700 km. Newer versions are reported with different ranges.
Sources differ because later versions such as Babur-1B and Babur-3 have other stated ranges.
What is the antonym of modesty?
Modesty means not showing off or thinking too highly of oneself. The opposite is arrogance, which is excessive pride.
Vanity is another word opposite to modesty.
Which mountain range lies along the Sindh side of Pakistan, on the border with Balochistan?
The Kirthar Range runs north to south along the Sindh and Balochistan border. Its highest point is Zardak Peak.
The Kirthar Range is the southern extension of the Sulaiman Range.
Which holy book was revealed on Hazrat Musa (AS)?
The Torah (Taurat) was revealed to Hazrat Musa (AS) on Mount Tur.
Zabur was revealed to Dawud (AS) and Injeel to Isa (AS).
What comes next in the series: Z3, W5, T7, ?
The letters go back by 3 each time: Z, W, T, Q. The numbers go up by 2: 3, 5, 7, 9. So the next term is Q9.
Letter series are solved by counting positions in the alphabet.
Where is the headquarters of NASA located?
NASA, the United States space agency, has its headquarters in Washington, D.C.
NATO stands for North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance formed in 1949.
NATO headquarters is in Brussels, Belgium.
Who was Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar?
A leader of the Pakistan Movement and Governor of Punjab
The first Prime Minister of Pakistan
Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar was a senior Muslim League leader and a close associate of Quaid-e-Azam. He later served as Governor of Punjab.
Nishtar Hospital in Multan is named after him.
What is the synonym of the word notorious?
Notorious means widely known for something bad, which is the same as infamous.
Notorious is used for bad fame, while famous is used for good fame.
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: He ___ Lahore by now.
The phrase by now needs the present perfect tense, which is has reached.
Present perfect is formed with has or have plus the past participle.
NWFP stands for North-West Frontier Province, the old name of today's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
The province was renamed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2010.
What is the closest meaning of the word obnoxious?
Obnoxious means extremely unpleasant or offensive.
The word comes from the Latin word obnoxius, meaning exposed to harm.
Into how many parts (quadrants) do the x-axis and the y-axis divide the coordinate plane?
The x-axis and y-axis cross at the origin and divide the plane into four parts called quadrants.
Quadrants are numbered I to IV in the anticlockwise direction starting from the positive x-axis.
What is the ordered triple (three ordered numbers) written as?
A pair has two components, written (a, b). A triple has three ordered components, written (a, b, c).
The first component of an ordered pair is called the abscissa and the second is the ordinate.
What is the meaning of the word overt?
Overt means done or shown openly, not hidden.
The opposite of overt is covert.
What is the antonym of the word pacifist?
A pacifist is a person who opposes war and violence. An aggressive or warlike person is the opposite.
Pacifism means the belief that war and violence are always wrong.
Choose the correct verb: The captain and his team ___ participating.
The captain and his team is a compound (plural) subject, so a plural verb such as were is needed. The singular forms is and is being do not agree.
Two subjects joined by and normally take a plural verb.
There are 30 passengers in a bus and one third of them are men, the rest are women. What is the percentage of women?
Women = 2/3 of the passengers. 2/3 x 100 = 66.67 percent.
Men are 10 of the 30 passengers and women are 20.
10 percent of a number is found by dividing it by 10.
Which tense is used in the sentence 'Girls are playing in the garden'?
The verb phrase 'are playing' is is/am/are plus verb-ing, which shows an action happening now. This is the present continuous tense.
Present continuous is formed as subject plus is/am/are plus verb with -ing.
Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan when Gwadar was handed over to Pakistan by Oman in 1958?
Gwadar was bought from Oman and formally became part of Pakistan on 8 September 1958. Feroz Khan Noon was Prime Minister at that time.
Pakistan paid about 3 million US dollars for Gwadar.
What is the antonym (opposite) of the word 'preceding'?
Preceding means coming before. Its opposite is following, which means coming after.
Succeeding is another word with the opposite meaning of preceding.
A number with exactly two factors, 1 and itself
A prime number is greater than 1 and has only two factors, 1 and itself. For example 7 has only the factors 1 and 7.
The number 1 is neither prime nor composite.
What is the dot product of the unit vectors i and j?
The unit vectors i and j are perpendicular, so i . j = cos 90 degrees = 0.
Also i . i = j . j = k . k = 1.
Which organ of the human body pumps blood throughout the body?
The heart is a muscular organ that contracts regularly and pushes blood through the blood vessels.
A normal adult heart beats about 72 times per minute at rest.
What is the meaning of the idiom 'smell a rat'?
To suspect that something is wrong
The idiom means to sense that something is dishonest or wrong.
The idiom is used when a person becomes suspicious of a plan or person.
11/7 is a ratio of two integers with a non-zero denominator, so it is rational (and also real).
Every rational number is also a real number.
What was the immediate cause of the Second World War in 1939?
Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, and Britain and France then declared war on Germany.
The Treaty of Versailles and the rise of dictators are seen as the deeper causes.
Which angel is responsible for rain and provision according to Islamic belief?
In Islamic tradition Hazrat Mikael (Michael) is the angel in charge of rain and provision.
Hazrat Jibrael brings revelation, Hazrat Israfeel will blow the Trumpet and Hazrat Azrael takes souls.
The square root of a prime number is always what kind of number?
A prime number is not a perfect square, so its square root cannot be written as a fraction of two integers. Hence it is irrational.
For example, the square root of 7 is about 2.6458 and never ends or repeats.
Which of the following Pakistani batters has scored a Test triple century?
Younis Khan scored 313 against Sri Lanka at Karachi in 2009.
Other Pakistani triple centurions are Hanif Mohammad, Inzamam-ul-Haq and Azhar Ali.
What is the capital city of Saudi Arabia?
Riyadh is the capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia.
Jeddah is the main port city on the Red Sea coast.
In which year was SEATO (South East Asia Treaty Organization) established?
SEATO was formed in September 1954 under the Manila Pact.
How many seats did the National Assembly have under the original 1973 Constitution (general plus reserved women seats)?
The 1973 Constitution provided 200 general seats and 10 seats reserved for women, so 210 in all.
The National Assembly now has 336 seats: 266 general seats, 60 reserved for women and 10 for non-Muslims.
If A and B are two sets, what is the set A union B?
The set of elements common to both A and B
The set of all elements in A or in B or in both
The set of elements in A but not in B
The union of A and B (written A U B) contains every element that belongs to A, to B, or to both.
The set of common elements is called the intersection.
Shahzia Sikander, who is well known internationally, is a Pakistani-born what?
Shahzia Sikander, born in Lahore in 1969, is a contemporary visual artist famous for reinventing Indo-Persian miniature painting.
She studied at the National College of Arts, Lahore, and later moved to the United States.
Which prophet is famous for building the ship (ark) that saved the believers from the great flood?
Allah ordered Hazrat Nuh (Noah) AS to build a ship, and he saved the believers and pairs of animals in it from the flood.
According to the Quran, the ark came to rest on Mount Judi.
Your age is 3 years and your sister is twice your age. What will be your sister's age when you are 23 years old?
Your sister is 3 x 2 = 6 now, so she is 3 years older. When you are 23 she will be 23 + 3 = 26.
Age difference stays constant, so add it to the younger person's age.
Sloppy means careless or untidy, so its opposite is neat or careful.
Another opposite of sloppy is meticulous.
Sloppy means done without care or attention, which is the same as careless.
Slovenly and untidy are also close in meaning to sloppy.
In which year of the Hijri calendar does the Islamic calendar start?
The Hijri calendar starts from the migration of the Prophet (PBUH) from Makkah to Madinah. That year is counted as 1 AH.

What is the process of changing water into steam called?
When water is heated it changes from liquid to vapour (steam). This change is called evaporation or vaporization.
The reverse process, steam turning into water, is called condensation.

Eminent means famous and respected, which is prominent.

Fragrant means having a sweet smell, which is aromatic.
A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to frustration?
Frustration is the feeling of being upset when things do not work out, close to disappointment.
A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to refrain?
To refrain is to hold oneself back from doing something, which is to abstain.
A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.
Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to stingy?
Stingy means unwilling to spend money, which is miserly.
A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.
Ali is 12 years old and he is three times as old as his sister. When Ali is 15 years old, how old will his sister be?
Sister's age now = 12 / 3 = 4 years. Ali will be 15 after 3 years, so the sister will be 4 + 3 = 7 years.
The age gap between two people changes, but the number of years that pass is the same for both.
Ali is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will the sister be when Ali is 15 years old?
Sister's age now = 5 x 3 = 15. Ali needs 10 more years to reach 15, so the sister will be 15 + 10 = 25 years.
The sister is always 10 years older than Ali in this problem.
Sara is three times as old as Ali. If Ali is 4 years old, how old will Sara be when Ali is 8 years old?
Sara's age now = 4 x 3 = 12. Ali becomes 8 after 4 years, so Sara will be 12 + 4 = 16 years.
The ratio of ages changes with time, but the difference stays the same (8 years here).
The Battle of the Trench (Khandaq) is connected with which Surah of the Holy Quran?
The events of the Battle of the Trench (also called Ahzab, the Confederates) are described in Surah Al-Ahzab.
The battle was fought in 5 AH.
What is a right angled triangle?
A triangle with all angles less than 90 degrees
A triangle with one angle of 90 degrees
A triangle with one angle more than 90 degrees
A triangle with all sides equal
A right angled triangle has exactly one angle equal to 90 degrees.
The side opposite the right angle is called the hypotenuse.
In an upper triangular matrix, what are the entries below the main diagonal?
All equal to the diagonal entries
A matrix is upper triangular when every entry below the main diagonal is zero, and the nonzero entries lie on or above the diagonal.
In a lower triangular matrix the entries above the diagonal are zero.
What is the synonym (closest meaning) of "trivial"?
"Trivial" means of very little value or importance, which is the same as insignificant.
The noun form is "trivia", meaning unimportant details.
7 can be written as 7/1, a ratio of two integers, so it is a rational number.
7 is also a prime number, a natural number and an odd number.
What does the name Uhud mean?
Uhud means standing alone, as the mountain stands separate from the other hills near Madina.
The Battle of Uhud was fought near this mountain in 3 AH.
Bani Israel (the Ummah of Israel) belonged to which prophet?
Bani Israel were the people to whom Hazrat Musa (AS) was sent, and he led them out of Egypt.
Israel was the title of Hazrat Yaqub (AS), the ancestor of Bani Israel.
What is the antonym of the word undaunted?
Undaunted means fearless, so its opposite is fearful, meaning easily frightened.
Intrepid is another synonym of undaunted.
What is the meaning of the word vague?
Vague describes something that is unclear or lacks precise detail. Its synonyms are unclear and indefinite.
The opposite of vague is clear or precise.
What is the meaning of veto power?
The right to reject or block a decision
The right to call a meeting
The right to join the UN
Veto is Latin for I forbid. It is the power to stop a resolution or decision even if others support it.
In the UN Security Council any one of the five permanent members can block a resolution by veto.
What is the pH value of pure water at room temperature?
Pure water is neutral, so its pH is 7.
Values below 7 are acidic and values above 7 are basic.
Which Pakistani leader was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan to visit China, in 1956?
Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy visited China in October 1956 while he was Prime Minister.
Pakistan and China established diplomatic relations in 1951.
Who wrote the Urdu poetry book Bang-e-Dara?
Bang-e-Dara is the first Urdu poetry collection of Allama Muhammad Iqbal.
What is the result when a real number is divided by zero?
Division by zero has no meaning in mathematics, so the result is undefined.
Zero divided by a non-zero number is zero.
What is 90 / 60 in its simplest form as a decimal?
Divide both by 30 to get 3/2, which equals 1.5.
90/60 as a mixed fraction is 1 and 1/2.
A train covers 100 km in 1 hour. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes at the same speed?
12 minutes is 12/60 = 1/5 of an hour. Distance = 100 x 1/5 = 20 km.
Speed in km per hour times time in hours gives distance in km.
How many inches are equal to 100 meters (to the nearest whole number)?
1 meter is about 39.37 inches. So 100 meters = 100 x 39.37 = 3937 inches.
Multiplying by 100 moves the decimal point two places to the right: 0.001 becomes 0.1.
Multiplying by 10 moves the decimal point one place to the right.
If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 11th be?
From the 1st to the 11th is 10 days. 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Monday + 3 = Thursday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days.
If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day will the 11th be?
From the 1st to the 11th is 10 days. 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Friday + 3 = Monday.
The 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th also fall on Friday in this month.
If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 11th be?
From the 1st to the 11th is 10 days. 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Sunday + 3 = Wednesday.
The 8th, 15th and 22nd of this month are Sundays.
In a class of 1500 students, 1300 are present. How many students are absent?
The percentage absent is 200/1500 x 100 = 13.33 percent.
If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what days will the 12th and the 15th be?
12th: 11 days after Monday, 11 mod 7 = 4, so Friday. 15th: 14 days after Monday is exactly two weeks, so Monday.
The 15th always has the same weekday as the 1st.
If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 17th be?
From the 2nd to the 17th is 15 days. 15 divided by 7 leaves 1, so Friday + 1 = Saturday.
The 9th and 16th of this month are Fridays.
If the 4th day of a month is Thursday, what day will the 18th be?
From the 4th to the 18th is 14 days, exactly two weeks, so the weekday is the same: Thursday.
Dates that differ by 7, 14, 21 or 28 always share the same weekday.
Whom did the British hold mainly responsible for the War of Independence of 1857?
The British blamed the Muslims for the 1857 uprising, since the Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar was its symbolic leader.
After 1857 the British treated Muslims harshly and the Mughal rule formally ended.
Which English letters are the 23rd, 18th, 22nd and 12th letters of the alphabet, in that order?
Counting A=1: 23 is W, 18 is R, 22 is V and 12 is L.
Which political party was in power in the areas that became Pakistan at the time of independence in 1947 and led the movement for Pakistan?
The All India Muslim League led by Quaid-e-Azam formed the first government of Pakistan in 1947.
Liaquat Ali Khan was the first Prime Minister from the Muslim League.
On what date was the Objectives Resolution passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
The Objectives Resolution was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan and passed on 12 March 1949.
It later became the preamble and then Article 2A of the Constitution.
What is the border agreement signed between China and Pakistan in 1963 known as?
On 2 March 1963 Pakistan and China signed the Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement fixing the border in the north.
The Karakoram Highway linking the two countries was built later.
On what date was the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan enforced?
The 1962 Constitution was announced on 1 March 1962 and came into force on 8 June 1962.
It was abrogated on 25 March 1969 when Yahya Khan imposed martial law.
In which year did the First World War start?
The First World War began in 1914 after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.
100% means the whole amount, so 100% of 200 is 200.
If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 23rd be?
From the 1st to the 23rd is 22 days. 22 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so the day is one after Sunday, which is Monday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days.
What is the value of cos 240 degrees?
cos 240 = cos(180 + 60) = -cos 60. Since cos 60 is 1/2, the answer is -1/2.
Cosine is negative in the second and third quadrants.
A train travels 15 km on 1 litre of fuel. How many litres are needed to travel 300 km?
Fuel consumption problems use the formula distance divided by distance per litre.
Any non-zero number divided by itself is 1.
Zero divided by any non-zero number is 0.
If the price of 20 bottles is 800, what is the price of 5 bottles?
One bottle costs 800 divided by 20 = 40. Five bottles cost 5 times 40 = 200.
5 bottles are one fourth of 20 bottles, and one fourth of 800 is 200.
In which valley is Abbottabad located?
Abbottabad lies in the Orash Valley in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, between the Sarban and Shimla hills.
The city is named after Major James Abbott, who founded it in 1853.
What is the full form of the abbreviation HCF?
HCF stands for Highest Common Factor, the largest number that divides two or more numbers exactly.
HCF is also called GCD (Greatest Common Divisor).
In a class of 1500 students, 1360 are present. What is the percentage of absent students, to two decimal places?
Absent students = 1500 - 1360 = 140. Percentage = 140 divided by 1500 times 100 = 9.33%.
In Surah Al-Muzzammil, by what word is the Prophet (PBUH) addressed?
The surah opens with Ya ayyuhal-Muzzammil, meaning O you who are wrapped up in garments. This is how Allah addresses the Prophet (PBUH) there.
Surah Al-Muddaththir, which follows it, opens with a similar address meaning the one covered with a cloak.
What is the meaning of the word 'accomplish'?
To accomplish something means to complete it or achieve it successfully. Its synonyms are achieve and fulfil.
A common antonym of accomplish is fail.
Who is the Supreme Commander of the Pakistan Air Force, as of October 2026?
The Chief of the Air Staff
Under Article 243 of the Constitution, the supreme command of the armed forces is vested in the President. As of 2026 the President is Asif Ali Zardari.
Field Marshal Asim Munir became the first Chief of Defence Forces in December 2025 after the 27th Amendment.
An aircraft uses 80 gallons of fuel to travel 540 km. About how much fuel is needed for 700 km?
Fuel per km is 80 divided by 540. For 700 km: 80 x 700 / 540 = 56000 / 540 = about 103.7 gallons.
Fuel use is directly proportional to distance when the rate is constant.
Who was Ali Bogra in Pakistan's history?
Muhammad Ali Bogra served as the third Prime Minister of Pakistan from 1953 to 1955. He earlier served as ambassador to the USA.
He was succeeded as Prime Minister by Chaudhry Muhammad Ali.
What is the meaning of the idiom 'once for all'?
Once for all (also once and for all) means finally and permanently, so it need not be done again.
Idioms must be learnt as a whole, as their meaning is not the sum of the words.
What is the meaning of the phrase 'all and sundry'?
All and sundry means everyone, whoever they may be.
Sundry on its own means various or several.
Under the Indus Waters Treaty, how many rivers is Pakistan allowed to use as its main share?
The three western rivers, Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, were given to Pakistan. The three eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, went to India.
The treaty was signed in 1960 with World Bank mediation.
Find the next term in the series: a1, b3, c5, ?
The letters go a, b, c, d in order. The numbers go 1, 3, 5, 7, increasing by 2, so the next term is d7.
Odd numbers form an arithmetic series with common difference 2.
Arrange the letters of the word SAID in alphabetical order.
The letters are S, A, I, D. In alphabetical order they are A, D, I, S, so the word is ADIS.
Alphabetical order follows A to Z, so D comes before I and I before S.
How many letters are there in the English alphabet?
The English alphabet runs from A to Z, which makes 26 letters.
The English alphabet has 5 vowels and 21 consonants.
Which triangle has two equal sides and two equal angles?
An isosceles triangle has two equal sides, and the angles opposite those sides are also equal.
An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal and each angle is 60 degrees.
Rearrange the letters of LEAPORD to make the name of an animal.
The letters L, E, A, P, O, R, D can be arranged to spell LEOPARD, which is a big cat.
The leopard is a big cat known for its spotted coat.
What is another name for the Lahore Resolution of 1940?
The Lahore Resolution, passed on 23 March 1940, demanded separate Muslim states and is also called the Pakistan Resolution.
It was moved by A. K. Fazlul Huq at the Muslim League session at Minto Park, Lahore.
Who founded Microsoft and Apple respectively?
Microsoft was founded by Bill Gates (with Paul Allen) in 1975, and Apple was founded by Steve Jobs (with Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne) in 1976.
Microsoft is based in Redmond, Washington, and Apple in Cupertino, California.
In which year was the national anthem of Pakistan first played publicly?
The anthem tune was first played publicly on 13 August 1950 during the visit of the Shah of Iran.
The anthem was officially approved in 1954; Hafeez Jalandhari wrote the words and Ahmed G. Chagla composed the music.
What is the antonym of debatable?
Debatable means open to argument, so the opposite is indisputable, meaning beyond argument.
Another opposite of debatable is undeniable.
What is the antonym of abundance?
Abundance means a very large quantity, and its opposite is scarcity, meaning shortage.
Synonyms of abundance are plenty and profusion.
What is the antonym of acquiesce?
To acquiesce is to accept something without protest, so the opposite is to resist.
Synonyms of acquiesce are consent and comply.
What is the antonym of acquittal?
Acquittal means a court declaring a person not guilty, so the opposite is conviction.
Acquit comes from Old French and means to settle a charge.
What is the antonym of ductile?
A ductile material can be drawn into wire, while a brittle material breaks easily, so brittle is the opposite.
Copper and gold are good examples of ductile metals.
What is the antonym of endow?
To endow is to provide with a quality or gift, so the opposite is to deprive.
Endow also means to give money to an institution.
What is the antonym of exception?
An exception is something that is left out of the general pattern, so the opposite is the rule.
The common saying is that the exception proves the rule.
What is the antonym of malicious?
Malicious means intending to harm, so the opposite is benevolent, meaning kind and well meaning.
Malice means the wish to do harm to others.
What is the antonym of seize?
To seize is to take hold of by force, so the opposite is to release.
What is the antonym of soft?
Soft means easy to press or not firm, and the opposite is hard.
Soft is also the opposite of loud when used for sound.
What is the antonym of vitalise?
To vitalise is to give life or energy to, so the opposite is to weaken.
A British spelling of vitalise is vitalize in American English.
Anwar is older than Ali, and Aslam is younger than Ali. Who is the oldest of the three?
Anwar is older than Ali and Ali is older than Aslam, so the order from oldest is Anwar, Ali, Aslam.
Aslam is the youngest of the three.
Aslam's age is three times Ali's age. After three years Ali's age will be 7 years. What is Aslam's present age?
Ali's present age is 7 - 3 = 4 years. Aslam is three times that, so 3 x 4 = 12 years.
After three years Aslam will be 15 and Ali will be 7.
Choose the correct word: I felt astonished ___ the sad news.
The adjective astonished is normally followed by the preposition at (or by) when it is used with news, so at fits the sentence.
Similar adjectives such as surprised and amazed also commonly take at.
What are the authentic (reliable) Ahadees called?
A hadith with a continuous chain of trustworthy narrators and no defect is called Sahih, meaning authentic.
Other grades of hadith include Hasan (good) and Daif (weak).
What is the total area of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) as given in official Pakistani sources?
Official AJK government publications give the total area of Azad Jammu and Kashmir as 13,297 square kilometres (about 5,134 square miles).
Some foreign sources give a much smaller figure, but 13,297 square kilometres is the official one.
Who was the first Prime Minister of Azad Jammu and Kashmir?
Under the 1974 interim constitution the post of Prime Minister was created, and Abdul Hamid Khan was elected the first Prime Minister of AJK in 1975.
Sardar Muhammad Ibrahim Khan was the first President of AJK, not the first Prime Minister.
Which word comes first in the dictionary: back, racket, biscuit?
Words are arranged by their first letter: b comes before r. Between back and biscuit, the second letters a and i decide it, and a comes first, so the order is back, biscuit, racket.
If the first letters are the same, compare the second letter, then the third, and so on.
What is the main theme of Surah Al-Furqan, whose name means the criterion?
The stories of the earlier nations only
The difference between right and wrong (truth and falsehood)
Furqan means that which separates truth from falsehood. The surah opens by saying Allah sent down the Furqan (the Quran) to distinguish right from wrong.
Surah Al-Furqan is the 25th surah of the Quran.
Near which place was the Battle of Badr fought?
Near the well of Badr, southwest of Madinah
The first major battle of Islam was fought in 2 AH at the wells of Badr, a valley about 150 km southwest of Madinah.
Badr is a valley and a well named after a man of the Banu Ghifar tribe, according to some reports.
Which Mughal emperor built the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore?
The Badshahi Mosque was built by Emperor Aurangzeb Alamgir and completed in 1673.
It was the largest mosque in the world for about 300 years and is among the largest in the world today.
In which year did Pakistan officially recognise Bangladesh as an independent country?
Pakistan recognised Bangladesh in February 1974, before the OIC Islamic Summit held in Lahore.
In which year was the Chashma Barrage on the Indus River completed?
The construction work on Chashma Barrage began after the contract of 1967 and was completed in March 1971.
Chashma Barrage is in Mianwali district and its hydropower station started in 2001.
Which number does not belong in the series: 1, 3, 6, 7, 9?
1, 3, 7 and 9 are all odd numbers, while 6 is the only even number.
An even number is divisible by 2 with no remainder.
What was the date of birth of Major Rashid Minhas Shaheed (Nishan-e-Haider)?
Rashid Minhas was born on 17 February 1951; his family belonged to Kulyana in Jhelum district.
He was martyred on 20 August 1971 while preventing the hijacking of his trainer jet, and is the youngest recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider.
What is the normal pH of human blood?
Human blood is slightly alkaline, with a normal pH range of 7.35 to 7.45.
A pH of exactly 7 is neutral, while stomach acid has a pH of about 1.5 to 3.5.
In which year was Shah Wali Ullah of Delhi born?
Shah Wali Ullah Muhaddith Dehlvi was born in Delhi in 1703 (1114 AH).
He is best known for translating the Holy Quran into Persian and for his book Hujjat Allah al-Baligha.
Fill in the blank: I bought it ____ 10 shillings.
The preposition for is used to show the price paid for something.
We say bought it for a price, but sold it at a price when speaking of rates.
Who bought the valley of Kashmir from the British East India Company in 1846?
Under the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) Gulab Singh Dogra paid 7.5 million rupees to the British and received Kashmir.
His great-grandson Hari Singh was the ruler of Kashmir in 1947.
Where is the famous Golden Gate Bridge located?
The Golden Gate Bridge spans the Golden Gate strait and connects San Francisco with Marin County in California.
It opened in 1937 and is a suspension bridge painted in International Orange.
What is the brother of your mother called in relation to you?
The brother of one's mother is called the maternal uncle, known as Mama in Urdu.
The brother of one's father is called the paternal uncle, known as Chacha.
6/12 divided by 6 on top and bottom gives 1/2, so both fractions have the same value.
Fractions that have the same value are called equivalent fractions.
Which is the largest peninsula in the world?
The Arabian Peninsula, with an area of about 3.2 million square kilometres, is the largest peninsula in the world.
It lies in southwest Asia and includes Saudi Arabia, Yemen and Oman.
Who is the author of the book Zulfi Bhutto of Pakistan: His Life and Times?
Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote Zulfi Bhutto of Pakistan: His Life and Times, published in 1993.
Wolpert also wrote Jinnah of Pakistan.
Which woman of the Makhzum tribe, caught for theft, was brought before the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) for judgement?

A noble woman of Banu Makhzum named Fatima bint Aswad was caught stealing and brought to the Prophet (S.A.W.). He said the law applies equally to all and that even if Fatima, daughter of Muhammad, stole, her hand would be cut.
Some candidates confuse her with Fatima bint Khuwaylid, which is incorrect.
Which of the following is the tallest completed building in Karachi?
Bahria Icon Tower in Karachi has 62 floors and is the tallest completed building in the city. Older towers such as Habib Bank Plaza are shorter.
A taller 82-storey tower called Burj Quaid has been announced in DHA City Karachi but is not yet built.
A is the father of B, but B is not the son of A. What is B to A?
B is a child of A, but not a son, so B must be a daughter.
In blood relation questions, check every possible relation before choosing.
Who were the first and second Caliphs of Islam?
Hazrat Abu Bakr and Hazrat Umar (R.A.)
Hazrat Abu Bakr and Hazrat Ali (R.A.)
Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (R.A.) was the first Caliph and Hazrat Umar Farooq (R.A.) was the second.
The four Rightly Guided Caliphs in order were Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali (R.A.).
What is the capital of Portugal?
Lisbon is the capital and largest city of Portugal.
Porto is the second largest city of Portugal.
What is the capital of Sudan?
Khartoum is the capital of Sudan, at the meeting of the Blue Nile and White Nile.
Juba is the capital of South Sudan.
Which option correctly lists the capitals of Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan in that order?
The provincial capitals are Lahore (Punjab), Karachi (Sindh), Peshawar (KPK) and Quetta (Balochistan).
Islamabad is the federal capital and is not a provincial capital.
Who was the caretaker Chief Minister of Punjab in 2023 to 2024?
Mohsin Naqvi served as caretaker Chief Minister of Punjab from January 2023 until February 2024.
Maryam Nawaz became elected Chief Minister of Punjab in February 2024.
Who was the caretaker Prime Minister of Pakistan in 2023 to 2024?
Anwaar-ul-Haq Kakar led the caretaker government from August 2023 to March 2024.
Shehbaz Sharif became Prime Minister again in March 2024.
What is the main natural source of ultraviolet (UV) rays?
The Sun is the main natural source of UV rays. Most of the harmful UV is absorbed by the ozone layer.
Too much UV exposure can cause sunburn and skin cancer.
Infections are caused by which of the following?
Harmful microorganisms such as bacteria and viruses
Infections are caused by pathogens, which are harmful microorganisms like bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites.
Deficiency diseases, unlike infections, are caused by lack of nutrients.
Who was the companion of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) in the Cave of Thawr during the Hijrat?
Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (R.A.) accompanied the Prophet (S.A.W.) and hid with him in the Cave of Thawr during the migration to Madinah.
Hazrat Ali (R.A.) stayed in Makkah in the Prophet's bed that night.
In which year was the second census of Pakistan held?
Pakistan's censuses were held in 1951, 1961, 1972, 1981, 1998, 2017 and 2023, so the second was in 1961.
The 2023 census was the first digital census of Pakistan.
What is the synonym of the word charming?
Charming means pleasing and delightful, which is close to attractive.
Other synonyms of charming are delightful and appealing.
What is the synonym of the word cherish?
To cherish means to hold something dear, which is the same as to treasure it.
Another synonym of cherish is to value.
What is the total number of squares on a chess board?
A chess board has 8 rows and 8 columns, so 8 x 8 = 64 squares.
Half of the 64 squares are light and half are dark, 32 of each.
The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) was established in which year?
ICAO was established in 1947 after the Chicago Convention on International Civil Aviation was signed in 1944.
ICAO is headquartered in Montreal, Canada, and is a specialized agency of the United Nations.
Which word is closest in meaning to idiom?
An idiom is a fixed expression whose meaning is different from the meanings of its separate words.
For example, the idiom kick the bucket means to die.
Which word is closest in meaning to audacity?
Audacity means a willingness to take bold risks, so boldness is the closest.
Audacity can also mean rude boldness, as in the audacity to lie.
Which word is closest in meaning to coil?
To coil means to wind into a series of loops or rings, like a spiral.
A snake often coils its body when it rests.
Which word is closest in meaning to deeper?
Deeper means going further down or more profound.
The opposite of deeper is shallower.
Which word is closest in meaning to edge?
The edge of something is its outer limit, which means its border or rim.
A synonym of edge is brink, as in the brink of a cliff.
A javelin is a light spear that is thrown, and it is used in athletics.
Javelin throw is an Olympic athletics event, and Arshad Nadeem of Pakistan won gold in it at Paris 2024.
Which word is closest in meaning to rear?
Rear means the back part of something. As a verb it also means to raise a child.
The opposite of rear (as a noun) is front.
Which word is closest in meaning to specific?
Specific means clearly defined and exact, which is precise.
The opposite of specific is general or vague.
Which word is closest in meaning to sustain?
To sustain means to keep something going or support it over time.
Sustainable development means growth that can be kept up without harming the future.
Which word is closest in meaning to conspiracy?
A conspiracy is a secret plan by a group to do something harmful or illegal, which is a plot.
Those who take part in a conspiracy are called conspirators.
Which word is closest in meaning to instructions?
Instructions are details telling someone what to do, which means directions.
Instructions is also a synonym of guidelines.
A translucent object is one that
lets no light pass at all
lets light pass but we cannot see clearly through it
lets light pass so we see perfectly clearly
A translucent object lets some light pass but scatters it, so we cannot see clearly through it. Frosted glass is an example.
A transparent object lets us see clearly, and an opaque object lets no light through.
What is the chemical (Latin) name from which the symbol Au of gold comes?
Gold has the symbol Au, which comes from its Latin name Aurum.
Silver is Ag from Argentum, and iron is Fe from Ferrum.
Where is the head office of the International Energy Agency (IEA)?
The IEA has its headquarters in Paris, France.
The IEA was founded in 1974 after the oil crisis.
In a committee of 24 members, 6 are men. What percentage of the committee is women?
Percentage of men here is 6 / 24 x 100 = 25%.
Who is credited in most Pakistani textbooks with first presenting the Two Nation Theory?
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan first spoke clearly of Hindus and Muslims as two separate nations in the late 1860s and 1870s.
Sources differ: some credit Allama Iqbal (1930 address) for the idea of a separate state, and Quaid-e-Azam gave it its final form.
How many nuclear tests did Pakistan conduct at Chagai on 28 May 1998?
Pakistan conducted five nuclear tests at the Chagai hills on 28 May 1998.
A sixth test was carried out on 30 May 1998 at Kharan, making six in total.
In which year was the 2nd OIC (Islamic Summit) conference held in Lahore?
The second Islamic Summit Conference was held in Lahore in February 1974.
The first Islamic Summit was held in Rabat in 1969.
Which Muslim commander conquered Egypt in the time of Hazrat Umar (RA)?
Hazrat Amr bin Al-As conquered Egypt around 640 AD during the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (RA).
He also founded the city of Fustat, near present Cairo.
In which Ghazwa (battle) with the Prophet (PBUH) were the most companions martyred?
About 70 companions were martyred in the Battle of Uhud, the highest number among the battles fought with the Prophet (PBUH) present.
Only about 14 Muslims were martyred at Badr.
With which tribe did the Muslims fight in the Battle of Badr?
The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was fought between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.
Badr is known as Youm-ul-Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.
What is a collection of well defined distinct objects called?
In mathematics a well defined collection of distinct objects is called a set.
The objects in a set are called its elements or members.
In which year was Warsak Dam, on the Kabul River near Peshawar, completed?
Warsak Dam was built in the 1950s and early 1960s under the Colombo Plan with Canadian help. Its first phase, including the dam and four 40 MW units, was completed in 1960.
Sources differ on when construction began (1949 or 1951), but 1960 is the commonly given completion year.
On which river is Rawal Dam, which supplies water to Rawalpindi and Islamabad, constructed?
Rawal Dam is an earth-fill dam built on the Korang River in Islamabad. It stores water for the twin cities.
Rawal Lake, formed by the dam, lies near Islamabad and was completed in 1962.
Iceland is an island nation in the North Atlantic Ocean. It is counted as part of Europe.
The capital of Iceland is Reykjavik.
If 7 pairs of shoes cost Rs. 3500, what is the cost of one pair?
Cost of one pair equals 3500 divided by 7, which is 500.
Cost of 10 such pairs would be Rs. 5000.
A train covers 120 km in 1 hour. How many km will it cover in 12 minutes?
Speed is 120 km/h, which is 2 km per minute. In 12 minutes it covers 2 times 12, which is 24 km.
12 minutes is one fifth of an hour, and one fifth of 120 is 24.
A train moves at twice the speed of a car. If the car covers 120 km in 60 minutes, in how many minutes will the train cover 120 km?
Car speed is 120 km/h, so train speed is 240 km/h. Time for 120 km is 120 divided by 240, which is half an hour, or 30 minutes.
When speed doubles, the time for the same distance is halved.
You have five cows and 3 times as many goats. How many animals do you have in total?
Goats are 3 times 5, which is 15. Total is 5 plus 15, which is 20.
The goats alone are three times the number of cows.
Approximately how long is the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) route from Kashgar to Gwadar?
CPEC links Kashgar in western China with Gwadar Port in Balochistan. The most commonly quoted length is about 3000 km.
Some sources give lower figures such as 2600 to 2800 km, depending on what is counted.
What is the cube root of 196, correct to two decimal places?
5.81 cubed is about 196.1, and 5.8 cubed is about 195.1, so the cube root of 196 is about 5.81. It is not a perfect cube.
The nearest perfect cubes are 125 (cube of 5) and 216 (cube of 6).
What is the cube root of 1?
1 times 1 times 1 equals 1, so the cube root of 1 is 1.
Besides 1, the number 1 also has two complex cube roots.
What is the currency of Afghanistan?
The official currency of Afghanistan is the Afghani (AFN). It is divided into 100 puls.
The Afghani replaced the older Afghani in 2002 with new banknotes after the fall of the Taliban government.
Which currency has the highest value per unit in the world?
The Kuwaiti Dinar (KWD) is worth more than any other currency unit, over 3 US dollars each. Its strength comes from Kuwait's oil wealth and tight currency policy.
The Bahraini Dinar and Omani Rial are the next most valuable currency units.
Who is the current President of Pakistan (as of October 2026)?
Asif Ali Zardari was sworn in as the 14th President of Pakistan on 10 March 2024 and still holds the office. The President is elected by an electoral college of Parliament and provincial assemblies.
Zardari's predecessor was Dr Arif Alvi, who served from 2018 to 2024.
In which direction from Karachi is Mohenjo-daro located?
Mohenjo-daro is near Larkana in northern Sindh, which lies north-east of Karachi. It is on the right bank of the Indus river.
Mohenjo-daro was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.
On which date was Liaquat Ali Khan assassinated?
Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, was shot at a public meeting in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951. The assassin Said Akbar was killed on the spot.
The place of the assassination, Company Bagh, was later renamed Liaquat Bagh.
Which law or principle states that a body immersed in a fluid experiences an upward force equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces?
This is the statement of Archimedes' principle. The upward force is called buoyant force and explains why ships float.
Archimedes is said to have discovered the principle while taking a bath in ancient Greece.
In which year was the Babri Mosque in Ayodhya demolished?
The Babri Mosque was demolished by Hindu extremist mobs on 6 December 1992. The event led to widespread riots in India.
In 2019 the Indian Supreme Court gave the disputed site for a Hindu temple.
Evaporation of water does NOT depend upon which of the following?
Evaporation happens at the surface, so it depends on temperature, surface area, humidity and wind. The depth of the water does not change the rate.
Evaporation is faster in hot, dry and windy conditions.
In which part of the world is the Gobi Desert located?
The Gobi is a large cold desert in East Asia. It covers parts of southern Mongolia and northern China.
The Gobi is known for fossil finds, including dinosaur eggs.
Which nation, associated with the city of Iram in the Quran, was destroyed after rejecting Hazrat Hud (AS)?
The people of Aad, who lived in Iram of the pillars, rejected Hazrat Hud (AS). They were destroyed by a violent windstorm.
The people of Thamud were the nation of Hazrat Saleh (AS).
What is the determinant of a non-square matrix?
Equal to its number of rows
A determinant can be found only for a square matrix, with equal rows and columns. For a non-square matrix it does not exist.
A square matrix with determinant zero is called a singular matrix.
In which year did Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk die?
Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk (Mushtaq Hussain) died in January 1917.
He was a founding member of the All India Muslim League in 1906.
What is the common difference in the numbers of the series A4, B8, C12?
The numbers are 4, 8, 12 and the letters go A, B, C. The number difference is 8 - 4 = 4 and 12 - 8 = 4.
The next term would be D16.
Which term is different in this series: A3, C5, E7, G9, I12?
Letters move by 2 (A, C, E, G, I) and numbers also move by 2 (3, 5, 7, 9, 11). The last term should be I11, so I12 is wrong.
Such questions test both letter and number patterns together.
Sidra is 5 years old and her brother is twice her age. How old is her brother?
Twice her age is 2 x 5 = 10 years. So the brother is 10 years old.
The age difference between them is 5 years.
Dishonest means not truthful. Honest is its opposite.
The prefix dis- often makes the opposite meaning.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'dishonest'?
Dishonest means untruthful or cheating. Deceitful has the same sense.
Fraudulent is another synonym of dishonest.
What is the distance between the points (4, 0) and (3, 0)?
Both points are on the x-axis, so the distance is the difference of x values: 4 - 3 = 1.
The distance formula is the square root of the sum of squared differences.
In which district of Balochistan is the Gwadar port located?
The port lies in Gwadar district, whose headquarters is Gwadar city.
Gwadar was bought from Oman in 1958.
Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: The doctor gives him medicine ___ his cough.
We use 'for' to show the purpose or the illness being treated. So it is 'medicine for his cough'.
We also say 'a cure for' a disease.
Horse is to mare as dog is to what?
A mare is a female horse. The female dog is called a bitch.
A young dog is a puppy.
What is the domain of the function tan x?
All real numbers except odd multiples of pi/2
All real numbers except multiples of pi
tan x = sin x / cos x, which is undefined where cos x = 0. That happens at odd multiples of pi/2.
The range of tan x is all real numbers.
Under Article 25A of the 1973 Constitution, education is free and compulsory for children of which age group?
Article 25A says the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children from five to sixteen years.
This article was added by the 18th Amendment in 2010.
The photoelectric effect is explained on the basis of which nature of light?
Einstein explained that light comes in packets of energy called photons, and one photon ejects one electron.
Einstein received the Nobel Prize in 1921 for this explanation.
In which year was Allama Iqbal elected President of the All India Muslim League?
Iqbal presided over the Allahabad session of the Muslim League in 1930.
In that address he presented the idea of a separate Muslim state in the north-west of India.
J.J. Thomson discovered the electron in 1897 using cathode ray experiments.
Rutherford discovered the nucleus and Chadwick discovered the neutron.
How many types of elementary row operations are there for a matrix?
The three types are interchanging two rows, multiplying a row by a non-zero number, and adding a multiple of one row to another row.
These operations are used in Gaussian elimination.
Seven boxes of powder weigh 49 kg in total, and one empty box weighs 1 kg. What is the weight of the powder in one box?
Each filled box weighs 49 / 7 = 7 kg. Taking out the 1 kg empty box leaves 6 kg of powder.
The total powder in all boxes is 42 kg.
Making friends is more rewarding than to make enemies.
Making friend is more rewarding than making enemies.
Making friends is more rewarding than making enemies.
Make friends is more rewarding than making enemies.
Both parts of the comparison should have the same form, so both use the gerund: making friends and making enemies. Friends must also be plural.
This rule is called parallel structure.
Pakistan is to Asia as England is to what?
Pakistan is a country in the continent Asia, and England is a country in the continent Europe.
England is part of the United Kingdom.
What is the currency of England?
England uses the pound sterling, the currency of the United Kingdom.
The pound is one of the oldest currencies still in use.
Which event made the USA enter World War 2?
Japan attacked the US naval base at Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941, and the USA declared war the next day.
The USA dropped atom bombs on Japan in August 1945.
Through which province of present-day Pakistan did Islam enter the subcontinent?
Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711 AD, so Islam spread into the subcontinent from Sindh.
Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam; some sources note Arab traders reached the south Indian coast earlier.
The speed of light in a conductor
The average velocity of free electrons in a conductor under an electric field
The speed of a charged particle in vacuum
The random speed of electrons without a field
Free electrons move randomly, but an electric field gives them a small net average velocity along the conductor. This is called drift velocity.
Drift velocity is very small, of the order of millimetres per second.
What does the idiom 'to drive home' mean?
To travel back to one's house
To emphasise a point so that it is clearly understood
To drive home a point means to make it very clear by stressing it strongly.
Example: The teacher drove home the importance of discipline.
In a point (x, y) on the Cartesian plane, if y is called the ordinate, what is x called?
In coordinate geometry the x-coordinate is called the abscissa and the y-coordinate is called the ordinate.
The abscissa measures distance along the x-axis, and the ordinate measures distance along the y-axis.
In mathematics, ln x stands for which logarithm?
Logarithm of x to the base e (natural logarithm)
Logarithm of x to the base 10
Logarithm of x to the base 2
Logarithm of x to the base 1
The symbol ln means the natural logarithm, which is the logarithm to the base e.
The number e is approximately 2.718, and log with base 10 is called the common logarithm.
Which term does the standard equation of a circle (x^2 + y^2 = r^2) NOT involve?
The equation of a circle with centre at the origin has only x^2, y^2 and r^2. There is no product term xy.
A conic section equation containing an xy term represents a rotated curve.
The equation y = 2x is called what type of equation?
Both x and y have power 1, so y = 2x is a linear equation, and its graph is a straight line.
This line passes through the origin because y = 0 when x = 0.
In which year was the European Union formally established by the Maastricht Treaty?
The Maastricht Treaty came into force on 1 November 1993 and created the European Union.
Its forerunner, the European Economic Community, was formed by the Treaty of Rome in 1957.
Evaporation of water mainly takes place because of which of the following?
Heat gives water molecules enough energy to escape from the liquid surface as vapour.
Evaporation is faster with higher temperature, larger surface area, wind and low humidity.
What is the exact words of a speaker, quoted inside inverted commas, called in grammar?
Direct speech repeats the speaker's exact words in quotation marks.
Indirect (reported) speech gives the meaning in the reporter's own words, without quotation marks.
What is the value of 6! (factorial of 6)?
The product of two numbers is 91 and one of them is 13. What is the other number?
The prime factors of 91 are 7 and 13.
Who was the first man to accept Islam (embrace faith) among adult men?
Most Pakistani textbooks say Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) was the first adult free man to accept Islam.
Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the first woman, Hazrat Ali (RA) the first child and Hazrat Zaid (RA) the first freed slave, according to common textbooks.
A train moves twice as fast as a car. If the car moves at 90 km/h, how far will the train go in 30 minutes?
Speed of the train = 2 x 90 = 180 km/h. Distance in 30 minutes (half an hour) = 180 x 1/2 = 90 km.
Ali and Farooq are brothers. Ali is three times as old as Farooq, and Farooq is now 4 years old. How old will Farooq be when Ali is 13 years old?
Ali's age now = 3 x 4 = 12. Ali will be 13 after 1 year, when Farooq will be 4 + 1 = 5.
The difference between their ages always stays 8 years.
Farooq is 10 years old and his sister is 4 times his age. How old will his sister be when Farooq is 20?
Sister's age now = 4 x 10 = 40. Farooq needs 10 more years to reach 20, so she will be 40 + 10 = 50.
The age gap of 30 years never changes.
Out of 1500 people, 1200 are male. What is the percentage of females?
Males are 1200 / 1500 x 100 = 80%, so the two percentages add up to 100%.
Which is the biggest natural gas field of Pakistan?
The Sui gas field in Balochistan is the largest natural gas field in Pakistan.
Sui gas was discovered in 1952 and has supplied gas to the country for decades. Sources differ: the Mari gas field is also very large, but Pakistani textbooks name Sui as the biggest.
In which city is the headquarters of FIFA located?
FIFA, the world football governing body, has its headquarters in Zurich, Switzerland.
FIFA was founded in 1904 in Paris, but its headquarters moved to Zurich in 1932.
Between which two groups of countries was World War 1 (1914-1918) mainly fought?
World War 1 was fought between the Allied Powers (Britain, France, Russia and later the USA) and the Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire and Bulgaria).
The war ended on 11 November 1918 and the Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919.
Naha, the capital of Okinawa Prefecture, is in which country?
Naha is the capital city of Okinawa Prefecture, which is part of Japan.
Okinawa is the largest island of the Ryukyu Islands and hosts several US military bases.
Choose the correct preposition: Stand ____ your friend in a critical situation.
To stand by someone means to support them, especially in difficulty.
The phrase stand by also means to be ready to act.
Which type of energy is stored in fruits?
Fruits store energy in food molecules such as sugars, which is chemical energy released during digestion.
Plants make this energy from sunlight through photosynthesis.
What was Hilf-ul-Fudul, in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) took part before prophethood?
A peace pact to help the oppressed and the weak
A treaty with the Jews of Madina
Hilf-ul-Fudul was a pact made by several Makkan tribes to protect the rights of the oppressed and the travellers.
It was formed after the Harb-e-Fijar, and the Prophet (PBUH) later said he would still accept such a pact in Islam.
Who gets the benefit of the NFC Award?
The federal government and the provinces
The National Finance Commission Award decides how the divisible tax revenue is shared between the federal government and the provinces.
The 7th NFC Award of 2010 gave the provinces 57.5 percent of the divisible pool.
For what are the people of ancient Gandhara famous?
Gandhara is famous for Gandhara art, a style of Buddhist sculpture that mixed Greek and Indian influences.
Taxila and Peshawar were main centres of Gandhara.
Mahatma Gandhi is famous for what?
Leading the Indian freedom movement through non-violence
Gandhi led the Indian independence struggle against British rule with non-violent civil disobedience.
He was known as Mahatma, meaning great soul, and was assassinated in 1948.
Which of the following are greenhouse gases?
Carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and water vapour trap heat in the atmosphere and cause the greenhouse effect.
Oxygen and nitrogen make up about 99 percent of dry air but are not greenhouse gases.
Which type of spectrum do monoatomic gases give?
Excited atoms emit light only at fixed wavelengths, so monoatomic gases give line (atomic) spectra.
Molecules give band spectra, and hot solids give continuous spectra.
How many general seats does the Provincial Assembly of Sindh have?
The Sindh Assembly has 168 seats in total: 130 general seats, 29 reserved for women and 9 for non-Muslims.
Punjab has the largest provincial assembly in Pakistan.
Fill in the blank: Ali gets angry very soon. He takes ____ his father.
To take after someone means to resemble them in character or looks.
Take up means to start a hobby, and take over means to assume control.
Who is the current Governor of Gilgit-Baltistan (as of October 2026)?
Syed Mehdi Shah has been Governor of Gilgit-Baltistan since August 2022 and swore in the new Chief Minister in July 2026.
His predecessor as governor was Raja Jalal Hussain Maqpoon (2018 to 2022).
Who is the current Governor of Punjab (as of October 2026)?
Sardar Saleem Haider Khan of the PPP took oath as Governor of Punjab on 10 May 2024 and still holds the post.
Before him the governor was Baligh-ur-Rehman, and earlier Chaudhry Muhammad Sarwar.
Girl is to boy as woman is to what?
A girl is a young female and a boy is a young male. In the same way a woman is an adult female and a man is an adult male.
Analogy questions test the same relationship in both pairs, here female and male.
Which one is the odd one out: mango, guava, apple, potato?
Mango, guava and apple are fruits that grow on trees, while potato is a vegetable (an underground tuber).
