Potato is a stem tuber that grows under the soil.
What is the approximate total length of the Great Wall of China, according to the 2012 Chinese survey?
A Chinese state survey in 2012 measured all its wall sections at 21,196 km.
Other sources give lower figures, depending on which sections are counted.
What is the name of the hadith book of Imam Bukhari (RA)?
Imam Bukhari compiled the collection called Al-Jami al-Sahih, known as Sahih al-Bukhari.
It is regarded as the most authentic book of hadith after the Quran.
What is another name of the Khutba Hajjatul Wada?
Hajjatul Wada means the Farewell Pilgrimage, so the khutba is called the Last or Farewell Sermon.
The Prophet (PBUH) delivered it at Arafat in 10 AH.
For about how many years did General Zia ul Haq rule Pakistan?
Zia ul Haq took power on 5 July 1977 and remained in power until his death in a plane crash on 17 August 1988, which is about 11 years.
He was followed by Ghulam Ishaq Khan as President after his death.
Who, as Viceroy of India, introduced separate electorates for Muslims through the reforms of 1909?

Lord Minto was Viceroy in 1909 and, with Secretary of State Lord Morley, brought the Morley-Minto Reforms that gave Muslims separate electorates. The demand had been made by the Simla Deputation of 1906.
Because of this, Lord Minto is often called the Father of Communal Electorates.
What is the meaning of the idiom "to hit the nail on the head"?
To say or do exactly the right thing
The idiom means to describe a problem or give an answer that is exactly right. The usual form is "hit the nail on the head".
An idiom is a phrase whose meaning is different from the meanings of its separate words.
Fill in the blank: As I was hot, I ___ my coat.
Being hot, a person would remove the coat, and the phrasal verb for removing clothes is "took off". The past tense is needed because of "was".
The opposite phrasal verb is "put on".
Which place in Pakistan is famous for its natural hot springs?
Tatta Pani in Kotli district of Azad Kashmir is well known for its hot water springs. Its name means hot water in Urdu.
Tatta Pani is also the name of another hot spring site near Gilgit-Baltistan.
Which is the hottest desert in the world?
The Sahara in Africa is the largest hot desert and is generally called the hottest desert of the world.
The Sahara covers about 9 million square kilometres of North Africa.
According to the Holy Quran, for what purpose did Allah divide mankind into nations and tribes?
So that they may fight each other
So that they may know one another
So that some may rule others
Surah Al-Hujurat (49:13) says Allah made people into nations and tribes so that they may know one another.
The same verse says the most honoured before Allah is the one who is most righteous.
Which gas in the air is essential for human breathing?
Humans need oxygen for respiration, which releases energy from food in the body cells.
Oxygen makes up about 21 percent of the air.
Which country hosted the first ICC Cricket World Cup in 1975?
The first Cricket World Cup was played in England in June 1975 with 60-over matches.
England also hosted the 1979, 1983 and 1999 editions and the 2019 edition.
Which team won the first ICC Cricket World Cup in 1975?
West Indies beat Australia in the 1975 final at Lord's, led by Clive Lloyd.
West Indies also won the second World Cup in 1979.
Identify the tense of the sentence: They are playing cricket.
The sentence uses "are" with the verb ending in -ing, which is the form of the present continuous tense.
Present continuous is used for actions happening now.
What is the determinant of an identity matrix?
The determinant of a diagonal matrix is the product of its diagonal elements. For an identity matrix this is 1 x 1 x ... x 1 = 1.
The identity matrix is its own inverse.
What does the idiom "out and out" mean?
"Out and out" means complete or total, as in "an out and out liar".
It is used before a noun to stress that something is complete.
What does the idiom "to cry wolf" mean?
To cry wolf is to give a false warning so that people do not believe you when real danger comes.
The idiom comes from Aesop's fable The Boy Who Cried Wolf.
Which river is regarded as the most important river of Pakistan?
The Indus is the longest river of Pakistan and the main source of water for its agriculture and for the country's irrigation system.
The Indus flows from Tibet through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.
What is the main purpose of zakat in Islam?
To increase the wealth of the rich
To reduce poverty and help the needy
Zakat is a compulsory share of wealth given to the poor and needy, which reduces the gap between rich and poor.
Zakat is the third pillar of Islam and is 2.5 percent on savings above nisab.
Impoverished means very poor, and destitute has the same meaning.
Needy and penniless are also synonyms.
In which province of Pakistan was the Sui gas field discovered and developed?
Sui is in the Dera Bugti district of Balochistan, and its gas field began supplying the country in the 1950s.
Sui is the largest natural gas field of Pakistan.
Where is the headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) located?
ICAO, a specialised agency of the United Nations, has its headquarters in Montreal, Canada.
ICAO was established in 1944 under the Chicago Convention.
Who invented the first practical photocopy (xerography) process?
Chester Carlson, an American inventor, made the first photocopy by the dry process called xerography in 1938.
The Xerox company later made his process commercially famous.
Who is credited with inventing the radio (wireless telegraphy)?
Guglielmo Marconi developed practical wireless radio communication in the 1890s and is commonly credited as its inventor.
Marconi shared the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics for this work.
What is the multiplicative inverse of 3?
The multiplicative inverse of a number is the number that gives product 1 with it. Since 3 times 1/3 equals 1, the inverse is 1/3.
Zero is the only real number with no multiplicative inverse.
What is x^i times x^i, where i is iota (the square root of minus one)?
When the bases are the same, the powers are added: i + i = 2i, so the result is x^(2i).
Note that i squared equals minus 1, which would be needed only if the powers were multiplied.
Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the ___ of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS), who was himself the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).
Yaqoob (AS) is also called Israel, and his twelve sons formed the tribes of Bani Israel.
In which direction is Karachi located from Islamabad?
Islamabad is in the north (about 33.7 N, 73 E) and Karachi is far to the south and west (about 24.9 N, 67 E), so Karachi lies south-west of Islamabad.
The two cities are roughly 1,400 km apart by air.
Pakistan is to Islamabad as Japan is to ...?
Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan, and in the same way Tokyo is the capital of Japan.
Kyoto was the old imperial capital of Japan until 1868.
What is the meaning of the idiom 'burning issue'?
A very urgent and widely discussed problem
A burning issue is an important and urgent problem that people are talking about and that needs a solution now.
Similar phrases are 'hot topic' and 'pressing matter'.
What is the antonym of the word 'indigenous'?
Indigenous means native to a place, so its opposite is foreign or alien to that place.
On which date is the National Day (founding anniversary) of the People's Republic of China celebrated?
The People's Republic of China was proclaimed by Mao Zedong on 1 October 1949, and this day is its National Day.
China has no independence day in the usual sense because it was never formally a colony.
What is a square matrix called when its transpose is equal to the matrix itself?
A square matrix A is symmetric when A transpose equals A, that is, a(i,j) = a(j,i) for all entries.
In a skew-symmetric matrix the transpose equals the negative of the matrix, so all diagonal entries are zero.
For how many million Nanakshahi rupees was Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh by the British under the Treaty of Amritsar (1846)?
By the Treaty of Amritsar in 1846 the British sold Jammu and Kashmir to Gulab Singh for 75 lakh (7.5 million) Nanakshahi rupees.
Gulab Singh was a Dogra ruler, and his family ruled Kashmir until 1947.
Justice Rana Bhagwandas, who served as a judge and acting Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Pakistan, belonged to which religion?
Rana Bhagwandas was a Hindu and was the first Hindu to serve as acting Chief Justice of Pakistan.
He served as acting Chief Justice in 2007.
Who was the non-Muslim Chief Justice of Pakistan?
A. R. Cornelius, a Christian, was Chief Justice of Pakistan from 1960 to 1968.
Rana Bhagwandas was only an acting Chief Justice, and he was a Hindu.
In which year did Mustafa Kemal Ataturk abolish the Caliphate (Khilafat) in Turkey?
The Turkish Grand National Assembly abolished the Caliphate on 3 March 1924 under Mustafa Kemal.
The Sultanate had already been abolished in 1922.
Near which place in Pakistan does the Kabul River join the Indus River?
The Kabul River meets the Indus near Attock at Khairabad, where the clear Kabul water and the muddy Indus water can be seen side by side.
The Kabul River rises in Afghanistan and enters Pakistan near the Khyber area.
At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) marry Hazrat Khadija (RA)?
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was 25 years old when he married Hazrat Khadija (RA), who was about 40.
Hazrat Khadija (RA) passed away in the Year of Sorrow, three years before the Hijra.
Which thermodynamic cycle is used in a jet (gas turbine) engine?
A jet engine works on the Brayton cycle: air is compressed, heated by burning fuel at constant pressure, and expanded through a turbine.
Petrol engines use the Otto cycle and steam power plants use the Rankine cycle.
In which province is Dera Ismail Khan (DI Khan) located?
Dera Ismail Khan is a city and district in the south of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on the west bank of the Indus River.
DI Khan lies close to the borders of Punjab and Balochistan.
In which district is the tomb of Captain Karnal Sher Khan Shaheed (Nishan-e-Haider) located?
Karnal Sher Khan is buried in his home village in Swabi district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where a mausoleum marks his grave.
He was martyred in the Kargil conflict of 1999 and received the Nishan-e-Haider.
How many disbelievers (Quraish) marched to fight the Muslims in the Battle of Badr?
The Quraish army at Badr was about 1000 strong, while the Muslims were only about 313.
The Muslims won the battle, which took place in 2 AH.
Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal?
Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal at Agra as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
Construction began around 1632 and the main building was completed around 1643.
Who is known as the Gateway (Door) of Knowledge in Islamic tradition?
The Prophet (PBUH) is reported to have said that he is the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate, so Hazrat Ali (RA) is called Bab-ul-Ilm.
Hazrat Ali (RA) was the fourth Khalifa of Islam.
Which Prophet is known by the title Khalilullah (Friend of Allah)?
Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah because of his deep love and devotion to Allah.
Hazrat Musa (AS) is called Kaleemullah and Hazrat Ismail (AS) is called Zabihullah.
When was the first railway line in the Indian subcontinent opened, between Bombay and Thane?
The first passenger train in India ran from Bombay (Bori Bunder) to Thane on 16 April 1853.
The first railway line in what is now Pakistan was opened in 1861 between Karachi and Kotri.
The name Adam is a word of which language?
Adam is a Hebrew word that is linked with the meaning man or earth.
Hazrat Adam (AS) is regarded as the first human and the first prophet.
Choose the correct word to fill the blank: It is ___ late.
The word too means more than is wanted, and it fits before the adjective late in this sentence.
Too is also used in the sense of also, as in me too.
Shariah (Islamic law) is mainly based on which two sources?
The two primary sources of Shariah are the Holy Quran and the Sunnah (sayings and actions) of the Prophet (PBUH).
Ijma (consensus) and Qiyas (analogy) are the other two commonly listed sources.
Musaylima Kazzab, the false prophet, was the enemy leader in which battle?
Musaylima Kazzab claimed prophethood and led the Banu Hanifa against the Muslims. He was killed in the Battle of Yamamah in 632 AD during the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).
In the same battle many Huffaz of the Quran were martyred, which led to the first compilation of the Quran.
What is the meaning of the idiom 'at arm's length'?
At a safe distance, not too close
To keep someone at arm's length means to avoid becoming too close or familiar with them.
The idiom comes from the idea of stretching out your arm to keep a person away.
What is the literal meaning of the word Muhajireen?
Muhajireen is the plural of Muhajir, which means one who migrates. It is used for the Muslims who migrated from Makkah to Madina.
The Muslims of Madina who helped them are called Ansar, meaning helpers.
In which Surah is the command 'Stand up (to pray) at night, except a little'?
Surah Al-Muzzammil (73), verse 2, tells the Prophet (PBUH) to stand in prayer at night except for a small part.
Surah Al-Muzzammil is the 73rd Surah and was revealed in Makkah.
In whose room did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) spend his last days and pass away?
During his last illness the Prophet (PBUH) took permission from his wives and stayed in the room of Hazrat Aisha (RA) in Madina, where he passed away in 11 AH.
He is buried in the same room, which is now inside Masjid-e-Nabawi.
In which year did the Black Lives Matter movement begin?
The phrase Black Lives Matter started as a hashtag in 2013 in the USA after the acquittal of the man who shot Trayvon Martin.
The movement became worldwide in 2020 after the death of George Floyd.
What is the characteristic of the common logarithm of 2179?
The number 2179 has 4 digits in its whole part, so the characteristic is 4 - 1 = 3.
The decimal part of a logarithm is called the mantissa.
What is the approximate value of log 0.9 (base 10)?
Since 0.9 is less than 1, its common logarithm is negative. Log 0.9 = log 9 - log 10 = 0.9542 - 1 = -0.0458.
Log of 1 is 0 for every valid base.
Which country has the longest border with China?
China shares about 4,700 km of border with Mongolia, which is the longest, slightly more than its border with Russia.
China has land borders with 14 countries, the most in the world together with Russia.
We look forward to win the match.
We look forward to winning the match.
We look forward to won the match.
We look forward for win the match.
The phrase look forward to is followed by a gerund (verb plus ing), because to is a preposition here. So winning is correct.
Similar phrases are: used to doing, object to doing and in favour of doing.
What is the meaning of the idiom 'to lose heart'?
To lose heart means to lose hope or courage and become discouraged.
The opposite idiom is to take heart, meaning to become more hopeful.
What was the last major ghazwa of the Muslims against the Quraish of Makkah?
The Muslims conquered Makkah in 8 AH (630 CE), which ended the war with the Quraish.
The Prophet (PBUH) forgave the people of Makkah after the conquest.
In a class of 30 students, 2/3 are male. What is the percentage of males?
The remaining 1/3 are females, which is 33.33%.
According to the Holy Quran, killing one innocent person is like killing whom?
Surah Al-Maidah (5:32) says that whoever kills one innocent soul, it is as if he killed all of mankind.
The same verse says saving one life is like saving all of mankind.
What is the meaning of the idiom "man of straw"?
A person of no substance or strength
A man of straw is a weak person or an imaginary opponent with no real substance.
Straw is light and weak, which is why the idiom describes someone without real strength.
It is in Madinah, where the Prophet (PBUH) was leading prayer when the command came to turn towards the Kaaba.
The qibla was changed from Bait-ul-Muqaddas to the Kaaba in 2 AH.
What is the SI unit of mass?
The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram (kg).
Weight is a force and is measured in newtons.
What is the correct relation between the arithmetic mean (A.M), geometric mean (G.M) and harmonic mean (H.M) of positive numbers?
A.M is greater than or equal to G.M, which is greater than or equal to H.M
H.M is greater than or equal to G.M, which is greater than or equal to A.M
G.M is greater than or equal to A.M, which is greater than or equal to H.M
All three are always different and unrelated
For positive numbers, A.M is at least G.M, which is at least H.M, with equality only when all numbers are equal.
For two numbers a and b, G.M squared equals A.M times H.M.
What are the signs for greater than and less than called in mathematics?
Signs like greater than and less than show that two quantities are not equal, so they are inequality symbols.
Which word fills the blank: You have not seen me ___ we met last time?
The present perfect tense (have not seen) is used with since to show a starting point in the past, so since is correct.
For is used with a period of time, while since is used with a point in time.
What does the word Hidayah mean?
Hidayah is an Arabic word meaning guidance, especially guidance to the right path.
Al-Hadi, the Guide, is one of the names of Allah.
What does the word Hukm mean?
Hukm is an Arabic word meaning command, order or ruling (judgement).
Its plural Ahkam is used for the rules of Islamic law.
Fiqh literally means deep understanding and is the science of deriving Islamic rules from the Quran and Sunnah.
Imam Abu Hanifa is the founder of the Hanafi school of Fiqh.
Who are the Muhajirs in Islamic history?
Those Muslims who migrated from Makkah to Madina
Muhajir means one who migrates, and the term is used for the Companions who left Makkah and migrated to Madina.
The Muslims of Madina who helped them are called the Ansar.
What does the word Blind mean?
A blind person has no ability to see.
Louis Braille, who was blind, invented the Braille reading system.
What does the word Climb mean?
To climb means to go up something such as a hill, tree or ladder.
What is the meaning of the word aqua?
Aqua comes from Latin and means water.
An aquarium is a tank of water for fish.
What is the meaning of the word coarsest?
Coarse means rough and not smooth, so coarsest means the most rough.
The antonym of coarse is fine.
What is the meaning of the word decompose?
To rot or break down into simpler parts
To decompose means to break down into smaller parts, as dead plants and animals rot.
Bacteria and fungi are called decomposers in nature.
What is the meaning of the word expansive?
Wide-ranging or covering a large area
Expansive means covering a wide area or range, or friendly and open in manner.
What is the meaning of the word opaque?
Not allowing light to pass through
An opaque material blocks light, so one cannot see through it.
Glass is transparent, while wood is opaque.
What is the meaning of the word polite?
A polite person is courteous and shows good manners to others.
The antonym of polite is rude.
What is the meaning of the word spongy?
Soft and full of small holes like a sponge
Spongy means soft, springy and porous like a sponge.
A sponge can absorb a lot of liquid.
What is the meaning of the word stupid?
Stupid describes someone who shows poor judgement or lacks intelligence.
The antonym of stupid is intelligent.
What is the meaning of the word suspicious?
Feeling or causing doubt and distrust
A suspicious person doubts others, and a suspicious thing causes doubt.
How many delegates attended the first session of the Indian National Congress in Bombay in 1885?
The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay in December 1885 with 72 delegates.
It was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee.
In which game did Pakistan win its first Olympic medal?
Pakistan won its first Olympic medal, a silver in hockey, at Melbourne in 1956.
Pakistan has won three Olympic gold medals, all in hockey.
In which continent is Moscow, the capital of Russia, located?
Moscow lies on the Moskva River in the western part of Russia, which is in the European part of the country. So it is counted as a European city.
Moscow is the largest city entirely in Europe by population.
The Minto-Morley Reforms of 1909 were related to which country?
These reforms were the Indian Councils Act 1909, passed by the British government for British India. They gave Muslims separate electorates.
Lord Minto was the Viceroy and John Morley was the Secretary of State for India.
What is the minimum number of ayat (verses) in a surah of the Quran?
The shortest surahs, Al-Asr, Al-Kawthar and An-Nasr, each have 3 ayat. No surah has fewer.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah with 286 ayat.
Who is the current Foreign Minister of Pakistan (2026)?
Mohammad Ishaq Dar serves as Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Pakistan. He was still in office in August 2026 according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Bilawal Bhutto Zardari was Foreign Minister from 2022 to 2023 before Ishaq Dar took the post in 2024.
Who was the first Finance Minister of Pakistan?
Malik Ghulam Muhammad was Finance Minister in the first cabinet of Liaquat Ali Khan in 1947. He later became the third Governor General.
He presented the first budget of Pakistan in 1948.
In which year did Pakistan launch its first rocket into space, the Rehbar-1?
Rehbar-1 was launched from Sonmiani in Balochistan on 7 June 1962 by SUPARCO. It made Pakistan the third country in Asia and the tenth in the world to launch a rocket into space.
Find the missing number in the series: 66, 63, 56, 45, ?
The differences are minus 3, minus 7, minus 11, so the next difference is minus 15. Then 45 minus 15 equals 30.
The differences themselves fall by 4 each time.
What is the synonym of modesty?
Modesty means a humble and unassuming attitude. Humility has the same meaning.
Modesty can also mean decent behaviour in dress.
Who are called Ummul-Momineen (Mothers of the Believers)?
Female companions who fought in battles
The Quran calls the wives of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) the mothers of the believers. This is a title of respect.
Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the first of the Ummul-Momineen.
If the 1st day of a month is Monday, which day will the 16th be?
From the 1st to the 16th is 15 days. 15 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so the day is one day after Monday, which is Tuesday.
The 8th and 15th of that month would also be Mondays.
Which two cities does the M-2 motorway connect?
The M-2 is the Lahore-Islamabad Motorway, about 367 km long. It opened in 1997.
It is also known as the Salt Range Motorway because it passes through the Salt Range.
A train is moving at 45 km per hour. How far will it travel in 5 minutes?
5 minutes is 5/60 = 1/12 hour. Distance = 45 x 1/12 = 3.75 km.
Speed in km/h divided by 60 gives the distance covered in one minute.
Find the odd one out: Delhi, Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Sibbi.
Delhi, Ahmedabad and Mumbai are cities of India. Sibbi (Sibi) is a city of Balochistan, Pakistan.
Sibi is famous for its annual Sibi Mela and its very hot summers.
Which term comes next in the series: B5, D7, F9, H11, ?
Letters skip one letter each time: B, D, F, H, J. Numbers go up by 2: 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. So the next term is J13.
Skipping one letter means moving forward by 2 positions in the alphabet.
The series is made of odd numbers, each 2 more than the one before. 9 + 2 = 11.
The differences are -4, -3, -2, so the next difference is -1. 6 - 1 = 5.
Here the amount subtracted gets smaller by 1 each step.
The numbers are multiples of 19: 19 x 1, 19 x 2, 19 x 3, 19 x 4 = 76, 19 x 5 = 95.
Check the last term: 95 divided by 19 is 5, so the pattern fits.
The differences are 3, 4, 5, so the next difference is 6. 14 + 6 = 20.
When the differences increase by 1 each time, the series is quadratic.
The differences are -5, -4, so the next difference is -3. 13 - 3 = 10.
The following term would then be 10 - 2 = 8.
Each term is multiplied by 3: 3 x 3 = 9, 9 x 3 = 27, 27 x 3 = 81.
This is a geometric series with common ratio 3.
The differences are -6, -12, so the next is -24 (doubling each time). 45 - 24 = 21.
The next difference after that would be -48.
What is the mean of 6 and -9?
The mean of two numbers is their sum divided by 2.
In the commonly taught order of the five pillars of Islam, at which number does Namaz (Salah) come?
The usual order taught in Pakistan is Kalima (Shahada), Salah, Roza (Sawm), Zakat and Hajj. So Salah is the second pillar.
Some hadith narrations list the pillars in a slightly different order.
In which continent is the River Nile located?
The Nile flows through northeastern Africa, mainly Uganda, Sudan and Egypt, and ends in the Mediterranean Sea.
The Nile is generally counted among the longest rivers in the world.
The sum is 4(1^2+2^2+...+n^2) = 4 x n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 = 2n(n+1)(2n+1)/3. Since 2n+2 = 2(n+1), option (a) gives 2n(2n+1) x 2(n+1)/6, which is the same.
The sum of squares of the first n natural numbers is n(n+1)(2n+1)/6.
What is the antonym of the word notorious?
Notorious means known for bad deeds, so its opposite is reputable, meaning having a good name.
Infamous and scandalous are synonyms of notorious, not antonyms.
Asad is 3 times as old as Amna when Amna is 6 years old. Now Amna is 10 years old. What is Asad's age now?
When Amna was 6, Asad was 3 x 6 = 18, so Asad is 12 years older. Now Amna is 10, so Asad is 10 + 12 = 22 years.
The difference between two people's ages always stays the same.
Ali is 3 years older than his brother. What will be Ali's age when his brother is 11 years old?
The age gap stays 3 years. When the brother is 11, Ali is 11 + 3 = 14 years.
In age problems, the difference in ages never changes with time.
If you can see through an object but the view is blurry, what is the object called?
A translucent object lets some light pass but scatters it, so things look blurry. A transparent object shows a clear view.
Frosted glass is a common example of a translucent material.
In which year was the Objective Resolution passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
The Objective Resolution was passed on 12 March 1949 during the time of Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan.
It later became a preamble to the constitutions of Pakistan and is now part of the 1973 Constitution.
In which month was Namaz made obligatory during the Mairaj?
The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of Mairaj, which is traditionally dated 27 Rajab.
Dates of Mairaj differ slightly in sources, but Rajab is the common view.
In which year did the United States attack and occupy Afghanistan?
The US led an invasion of Afghanistan in October 2001 after the 9/11 attacks.
US forces left Afghanistan in August 2021.
Which is the odd one out: India, Pakistan, China, Spain?
India, Pakistan and China are Asian countries, while Spain is in Europe.
Which is the official language of Pakistan, used in government alongside the national language Urdu?
The 1973 Constitution makes Urdu the national language and keeps English as the official language for government use.
Urdu is the national language of Pakistan.
What is the official name of the legislature of Pakistan?
The Parliament of Pakistan is officially called Majlis-e-Shoora and has the National Assembly and the Senate.
The President is also a part of the Majlis-e-Shoora.
What was the old name of Beijing?
Beijing was long known in English as Peking.
Beijing is the capital of China.
Which word is the closest opposite of resentment?
Resentment is bitter anger over unfair treatment. Gratitude (thankfulness and goodwill) is its opposite feeling.
Other opposites of resentment are goodwill and forgiveness.
What is the opposite of the word clean?
Clean means free from dirt. The word with the opposite meaning is dirty.
Pure, neat and fresh are all close in meaning to clean.
What is the opposite of the word expensive?
Expensive means high in price. Cheap means low in price, so it is the opposite.
Costly, valuable and precious are synonyms of expensive.
What is the opposite of the word retain?
Retain means to keep or continue to have something. Release (let go) is the opposite.
Another opposite of retain is discard.
Which statement about the number 39 is correct?
It is an odd composite number
39 is not divisible by 2, so it is odd. 39 = 3 x 13, so it has factors other than 1 and itself and is composite, not prime.
The only even prime number is 2.
Which number cancels out 15 when the two are added together (the additive inverse of 15)?
The multiplicative inverse of 15 is 1/15, because 15 x 1/15 = 1.
What is the antonym of the word overt?
Overt means open and visible, while covert means hidden or secret.
A synonym of overt is open or obvious.
What is a synonym of the word pacifist?
A pacifist believes in peace and rejects war, so peace lover (peacemaker) is a synonym.
The dove is a common symbol of peace and pacifism.
In which city was the Pakistan-China boundary agreement of 1963 signed?
The agreement was signed in Beijing (then written Peking) on 2 March 1963 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Chinese Foreign Minister Chen Yi.
The agreement settled the border between Pakistan and the Xinjiang region of China.
On what basis is the Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chosen?
Elected by the members of the Provincial Assembly, as the leader of the majority
Elected directly by the people of the province
Under Article 130 of the Constitution, the Provincial Assembly elects the Chief Minister, who must command the confidence of the majority of members.
The Governor of the province appoints the person elected by the assembly.
Who first suggested the name Pakistan?
Chaudhary Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge student, proposed the name Pakistan in his 1933 pamphlet Now or Never.
Allama Iqbal gave the idea of a separate Muslim state in his 1930 Allahabad address.
What is the meaning of the word panic?
Panic is a sudden strong fear that makes people act without thinking.
The word comes from Pan, the Greek god of the wild.
Which book is generally regarded as the first book written in the Pashto language?
Khair-ul-Bayan, written by Bayazid Ansari (Pir Roshan) in the 16th century, is generally regarded as the first Pashto book.
Pata Khazana is a disputed anthology of early Pashto poets, so some sources name other early works.
A bus has 30 passengers and two thirds of them are boys, the rest are girls. How many girls are there?
The girls are 1/3 of the passengers, which is 33.33 percent.
Change the narration into indirect speech: She said to me, "Can you give me your pen?"
She asked me if I could give her my pen.
She told me that can I give her my pen.
She said me whether I can give her pen.
She asked me that I can give me my pen.
A question in direct speech becomes a reporting verb asked plus if, and the tense and pronouns change: can becomes could, you becomes I, me becomes her.
In indirect speech a yes or no question is joined with if or whether and has no question mark.
A car travels at 60 km per hour. How much distance will it cover in 20 minutes?
20 minutes is 20/60 = 1/3 of an hour. Distance = 60 x 1/3 = 20 km.
Approximately what percentage of Pakistan's population is non-Muslim according to the 2023 census?
The 2023 census gave Muslims 96.35 percent, which leaves about 3.65 percent non-Muslim.
Hindus (about 1.61 percent) and Christians (about 1.37 percent) are the largest minorities, and Ahmadis are listed separately.
What is 5/7 as a percentage (to two decimal places)?
5 divided by 7 = 0.714285. Multiplying by 100 gives 71.43 percent.
One side of a right-angled triangle is 8 and the perpendicular is 6. What is the length of the third side (hypotenuse)?
By Pythagoras, hypotenuse squared = 8 squared + 6 squared = 64 + 36 = 100, so the hypotenuse is 10.
3, 4, 5 and its multiples such as 6, 8, 10 are Pythagorean triples.
In a right-angled triangle, sine of an angle is the perpendicular divided by what?
Sin of an angle = perpendicular / hypotenuse.
Cos is base / hypotenuse and tan is perpendicular / base.
What is the correct thing to do with the engine of your vehicle at a petrol pump?
Petrol vapour can catch fire from sparks, so the engine must be switched off while refuelling.
Smoking and using mobile phones at a petrol pump are also unsafe.
In which year was the Pirpur Report on the grievances of Muslims in Congress provinces published?
The Pirpur Report, prepared by a committee of the Muslim League headed by Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur, came out in 1938.
It listed complaints against Congress rule in the provinces from 1937.
Change into passive voice: Let us play a game.
A game was played by us.
For a sentence beginning with Let, the passive form is Let + object + be + past participle.
Another example is Let the work be done.
What are the two parts of a common logarithm called?
A common logarithm has an integral part called the characteristic and a decimal part called the mantissa.
The mantissa is always kept positive.
Which is the deepest known point of the Earth's oceans?
Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench
Challenger Deep lies in the Mariana Trench in the western Pacific Ocean. It is about 10,900 metres deep.
The Mariana Trench is near Guam in the Pacific Ocean.
According to the 2023 census, about what percentage of Pakistan's population lives in Balochistan?
Balochistan has about 14.9 million people out of about 241.5 million in Pakistan. That is roughly 6 percent.
Balochistan is the largest province by area but the smallest by population.
What is the population of Balochistan according to the 2023 census of Pakistan?
The 2023 digital census recorded about 14.89 million people in Balochistan.
In the 2017 census Balochistan had about 12.3 million people.
What is the population of Sindh according to the 2023 census of Pakistan?
The 2023 digital census recorded about 55.7 million people in Sindh.
In the 2017 census Sindh had about 47.9 million people.
Yes, it has tested a bomb
No, it is not a nuclear power
Greece has no nuclear weapons. It is a NATO member but does not own an atomic arsenal.
The nine nuclear-armed states are the USA, Russia, UK, France, China, India, Pakistan, North Korea and Israel (undeclared).
Fill in the preposition: Do you agree ___ me?
We agree with a person and agree to a plan or proposal. Here the object is a person, so the correct word is with.
We say agree with someone, agree to a proposal, and agree on a matter.
Fill in the blank: I always face difficulty ___ prepositions.
The common phrase is difficulty with something. So the correct preposition is with.
Difficulty in doing something is used with a verb-ing form, for example difficulty in understanding.
In which year was Pakistan's first constitution enforced, and who became the first President under it?
The first constitution of Pakistan was enforced on 23 March 1956. Iskander Mirza became the first President under it.
Iskander Mirza had earlier been the last Governor General of Pakistan.
Yes, it is a prime number
19 is not divisible by 2, 3, 5, 7 or 11, and has no divisor other than 1 and itself. So it is prime.
The prime numbers below 20 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19.
Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan in 1973 when the new Constitution was adopted?
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto became Prime Minister in August 1973 and the 1973 Constitution came into force under him.
Bhutto was earlier President of Pakistan from 1971 to 1973.
What is the order of the product of a 3 x 2 matrix and a 2 x 3 matrix?
For a product AB, the inner orders (2 and 2) must match, and the result has the outer orders. So a 3 x 2 matrix times a 2 x 3 matrix gives a 3 x 3 matrix.
The product in the reverse order (2 x 3 times 3 x 2) would be a 2 x 2 matrix.
Which property of multiplication is shown by 9 x 7 = 7 x 9?
Changing the order of the numbers does not change the product, which is the commutative property.
Addition is also commutative, but subtraction and division are not.
Which type of tissue in the human body pumps blood regularly?
The walls of the heart are made of cardiac muscle, which contracts rhythmically without tiring.
Cardiac muscle is involuntary, meaning we cannot control it by will.
Which companion headed the committee that prepared copies of the Quran during the caliphate of Hazrat Usman (RA)?
Hazrat Usman (RA) appointed Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA) to lead the committee that wrote standard copies of the Quran and sent them to major cities.
Because of this work Hazrat Usman (RA) is called Jami ul Quran.
To which caste (community) did Raja Dahir, the ruler of Sindh at the time of Muhammad bin Qasim's invasion, belong?
Raja Dahir belonged to the Brahmin dynasty that ruled Sindh after the Rai dynasty.
Chach, the father of Dahir, had founded the Brahmin dynasty of Sindh.
Is mass a scalar quantity or a vector quantity?
Mass has only magnitude and no direction, so it is a scalar quantity.
Weight is a vector because it acts downward as a force.
What is one quarter of one third of 36?
One third of 36 is 36/3 = 12. One quarter of 12 is 12/4 = 3.
One quarter of one third is the same as 1/12 of the number.
Which one is different from the rest: Rawalpindi, Lahore, Sindh, Peshawar, Quetta?
Rawalpindi, Lahore, Peshawar and Quetta are cities, while Sindh is a province.
Quetta is the capital of Balochistan and Peshawar is the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
In which city did the Quraish tribe mainly reside?
The Quraish were the leading tribe of Makkah and looked after the Kaaba.
The Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself belonged to the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraish.
What is the diameter of a circle whose radius is 56?
Diameter is twice the radius. 2 x 56 = 112.
The circumference of a circle is pi times the diameter.
Ramiz Raja was a famous player of which game?
Ramiz Raja played for Pakistan in Tests and ODIs from 1984 to 1997.
He was later the PCB chairman (2021 to 2022) and is a well known commentator.
In which province are the Ras Koh Hills located?
The Ras Koh Hills lie in Chagai district of Balochistan.
Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests of May 1998 in the Chagai area.
A number that cannot be written as a fraction
A number that can be written as p/q where p and q are integers and q is not zero
A number with a non-repeating infinite decimal
A number that is only positive
A rational number is any number that can be expressed as the ratio p/q of two integers with q not equal to 0.
Terminating and repeating decimals are rational numbers.
How many rational numbers lie between 0 and 1?
Between any two rational numbers there is another one, for example their average, so the set between 0 and 1 is infinite.
Rearrange the letters of CHIKARA to make the name of a city. Which city is it?
The letters C H I K A R A can be arranged to spell KARACHI.
Karachi is the largest city of Pakistan.
Muammar Gaddafi was the long-time ruler of which country?
Muammar Gaddafi ruled Libya from 1969 until he was overthrown in 2011.
He was killed in October 2011 during the Libyan civil war.
How many countries are strictly counted as Scandinavian countries?
Scandinavia strictly means Denmark, Norway and Sweden.
The wider Nordic region also includes Finland and Iceland, making five countries.
Which symbol is commonly used to represent the common difference of an arithmetic sequence?
In an arithmetic sequence each term is found by adding a fixed number to the previous term. That fixed number is called the common difference and is written d.
The nth term of an arithmetic sequence is a + (n - 1)d, where a is the first term.
Which number is different from the rest: 5, 7, 9, 12?
5, 7 and 9 are odd numbers, while 12 is an even number.
A number is even if it is divisible by 2.
Which one is different from the rest: A4, B5, C5, D7?
A, B, C, D are the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th letters. The number is the letter position plus 3 in A4, B5 and D7 (1+3, 2+3, 4+3), but C5 breaks it because 3+3 is 6.
In letter-number odd-one-out questions, convert letters to their alphabet positions first.
Which one is different from the rest: X5, Y6, Z9?
The numbers follow the letters in order: X is followed by 5 and Y by 6, so Z should be followed by 7. Z9 breaks the pattern.
X, Y and Z are the 24th, 25th and 26th letters of the alphabet.
How many rings are there in the Olympic symbol?
The Olympic symbol has five interlocking rings coloured blue, yellow, black, green and red.
The rings represent the five inhabited continents joined together.
The Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 divided how many rivers between India and Pakistan?
The treaty covered six rivers: the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) went to India and the three western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) went to Pakistan.
The treaty was brokered by the World Bank and signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960.
Gwadar Port is situated on the coast of which sea?
Gwadar is a deep sea port in Balochistan and lies on the Arabian Sea coast.
Gwadar is the main port of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).
Which event is commonly called the First War of Independence against British rule in the subcontinent?
The uprising of 1857 against the East India Company is called the War of Independence by Muslims and Hindus of the subcontinent.
The British called the same event the Sepoy Mutiny.
A train runs at a speed of 99 km/hr. What distance does it cover in 12 minutes?
Distance = speed x time, with time in hours when speed is in km/hr.
What is the highest individual score by a Pakistani batter in Test cricket?
Hanif Mohammad scored 337 against the West Indies at Bridgetown in 1958.
Inzamam-ul-Haq scored 329, Younis Khan 313 and Azhar Ali 302 not out.
Which saint is buried in the city of Kasur?
The famous Punjabi Sufi poet Bulleh Shah is buried in Kasur.
Baba Farid rests at Pakpattan and Data Ganj Bakhsh at Lahore.
On which date was Pakistan's first satellite, Badr-1, launched?
Badr-1 was launched on 16 July 1990 from China.
Pakistan's space agency SUPARCO built Badr-1.
Where is the Yellow Sea located?
Between China and the Korean Peninsula
The Yellow Sea is an arm of the Pacific Ocean lying between mainland China and the Korean Peninsula.
It gets its name from the yellow silt carried into it by rivers such as the Yellow River.
Southern Europe and Asia Treaty Organization
SEATO stands for South East Asia Treaty Organization, a defence alliance led by the USA.
Pakistan was a member from 1954 until 1973.
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: I ___ to school.
With the subject I, the simple present verb is go.
With he, she or it the verb takes s, as in goes.
What comes next in the series: Z4, X8, V12, ?
The letters move back by two (Z, X, V, T) and the numbers go up by 4 (4, 8, 12, 16). So the next term is T16.
Skipping one letter each time gives the alphabet position falling by 2 each step.
What comes next in the series: Aa, Bb, Cc, Dd, ?
Each term has a capital letter and its small letter, moving one letter forward each time. After Dd comes Ee.
What comes next in the series: A2, D9, H16, M23, ?
The letters jump by 3, 4, 5 places (A, D, H, M) so the next jump is 6, giving S. The numbers increase by 7 each time (2, 9, 16, 23), giving 30. So the next term is S30.
M is the 13th letter, and 13 + 6 = 19, which is S.
By which symbol is the universal set usually represented in set theory?
The universal set, which contains all elements under consideration, is written with the capital letter U.
The empty set is written with the symbol phi or with empty braces.
A set with exactly one element
A singleton set has exactly one element, for example {5}.
A set with no element is called the empty or null set.
What does the idiom "cold shoulder" mean?
To treat someone in an unfriendly way and ignore them
To feel a pain in the shoulder
To give someone the cold shoulder means to deliberately ignore them or treat them coldly.
An idiom has a meaning different from the literal meaning of its words.
Ali is 10 years old and he is twice as old as his sister. How old will his sister be after 20 years?
His sister is 10 divided by 2 = 5 years old now. After 20 years she will be 5 + 20 = 25.
The age difference between two people never changes with time.
Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 8 years old. When Ali is 10 years old, how old will his sister be?
The age difference is 8 - 5 = 3 years. When Ali is 10, his sister is 10 + 3 = 13.
The sister is always 3 years older than Ali.
If my mother is your sister, what am I to you?
Your sister is my mother, so I am her child, which makes me your sister's child, that is your nephew or niece.
The child of your brother is also your nephew or niece.
According to the Quran, whom should a person respect and obey most (after Allah)?
The Quran commands good treatment of parents right after the command to worship Allah alone, and tells us not even to say 'uff' to them.
Surah Bani Israil (verses 23 to 24) gives the command about kindness to parents.
Fill in the blank: I go to sleep ____ I am tired.
'When' shows the time at which something happens, so 'I go to sleep when I am tired' is correct.
'Whenever' can also be used here to mean every time.
Which is the smallest Muslim country of the world by area?
The Maldives covers only about 300 square kilometres, less than Bahrain (about 780) and Brunei (about 5,770).
The Maldives is also the smallest country in Asia.
Father is to son as mother is to ____.
A father and his male child are father and son. In the same way a mother and her female child are mother and daughter.
Analogy questions test the same relationship in both pairs.
Which of the following was a son of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
Hazrat Qasim (RA) was the first son of the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA); he died as a small child.
Hasan and Husain were the grandsons of the Prophet (PBUH).
On which side of Pakistan does China lie?
Pakistan's northern border, through Gilgit-Baltistan, meets China's Xinjiang region.
The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with China.
Choose the correct word: The Arabian Sea is ____ in the southern part of Pakistan.
The sentence needs the past participle 'situated' after 'is' to mean 'located'.
'Is situated' is a passive form often used to describe locations.
The word is spelled d-i-v-e-r-s-i-t-y, from the Latin word diversus.
Who started the Khilafat Movement in the subcontinent?
Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan and Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk
Maulana Hasrat Mohani and Liaquat Ali Khan
The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was led by the Ali Brothers, Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali. It aimed to save the Ottoman Caliphate.
Mahatma Gandhi supported the movement for some time.
Who started the Shuddhi movement in India?
The Shuddhi (purification) movement to bring converts back to Hinduism was begun by the Arya Samaj of Swami Dayanand Saraswati.
It became very active in the 1920s under Swami Shraddhanand and angered Muslims.
As of 2026, has any woman been elected President of the United States?
No, no woman has been elected so far
Hillary Clinton lost in 2016 and Kamala Harris lost in 2024. No woman has yet held the office of US President.
The next US presidential election after 2024 is due in 2028.
Who is the author of the book The Story of the Pakistan Army?
The Story of the Pakistan Army was written by Major General Fazal Muqeem Khan and first published in 1963.
Shuja Nawaz wrote the books Crossed Swords and The Battle for Pakistan.
In set theory, a set that contains another set as its subset is called what?
If every element of A is also in B, then A is a subset of B and B is a superset of A.
The power set of a set is the set of all its subsets.
What is the sum of the first seven multiples of 5?
The sum of the first n natural numbers is n(n+1)/2.
CNG is natural gas, mostly methane, stored under high pressure and used as vehicle fuel.
CNG is cheaper and cleaner than petrol in most cases.
What does RAW stand for in the name of the Indian intelligence agency?
RAW is the external intelligence agency of India, called the Research and Analysis Wing.
RAW was formed in 1968 after the 1962 and 1965 wars.
Anniversary of Pakistan's nuclear tests of May 1998
Day of the passing of the Lahore Resolution
Anniversary of the independence of Pakistan
Youm-e-Takbeer is observed every year on 28 May to mark the five nuclear tests Pakistan carried out in the Chagai hills in 1998.
Takbeer means saying Allahu Akbar, and the tests made Pakistan the seventh nuclear power.
The word Olympic is taken from which ancient Greek place?
The word Olympic comes from Olympia, the town in ancient Greece where the original games were held.
Some sources link the name to Mount Olympus, the home of the Greek gods, but Olympia is the usual textbook answer.
What is the chemical symbol of gold in the periodic table?
The symbol Au comes from the Latin name aurum, meaning gold.
Ag is the symbol of silver, from the Latin argentum.
What is the chemical symbol of potassium?
The symbol K comes from kalium, the Latin name for potassium.
Sodium has the symbol Na, from the Latin natrium.
Against which team did Pakistan play its first Twenty20 International match?
Pakistan played its first T20I against England on 28 August 2006 at Bristol and won by five wickets.
The very first men's T20I in history was played between Australia and New Zealand on 17 February 2005.

What does the idiom 'out of temper' mean?
To be out of temper means to be in a bad mood and easily angered.
The opposite state is to be good-tempered, meaning calm and cheerful.
What does the idiom 'to keep one's temper' mean?
To remain calm and not lose control of anger
To keep a hot drink warm
To keep one's temper means to stay calm even when provoked.
The opposite idiom is 'to lose one's temper', meaning to become suddenly angry.

One tenth of 12 is 1.2. One quarter of 1.2 is 1.2 / 4 = 0.3.
A quarter of a number is the same as dividing it by 4.
Multiplying fractions means multiplying the numerators and the denominators.
One third of 10 = 10 / 3 = 3.33, which is 3 and 1/3.
Ten is not exactly divisible by 3, so the answer is a fraction.
Ali is 6 years older than his sister. When Ali's age was three times his sister's age, how old was the sister?
Let the sister be x. Then Ali is x + 6 = 3x, so 2x = 6 and x = 3. Ali was then 9.
The age difference between two people always stays the same.
In which country is the Three Gorges Dam located?
The Three Gorges Dam is built on the Yangtze River in Hubei province, China.
It is the largest hydroelectric power station in the world by installed capacity.
Khateeb ul Ambia (the orator among the prophets) is the title of which prophet?
Hazrat Shuaib (AS) was known for his powerful and eloquent speech, so he is called Khateeb ul Ambia.
Hazrat Musa (AS) is called Kalimullah, the one who spoke with Allah.

Each answer joins the squares of the two numbers: 2x2 gives 4 and 4, 2x3 gives 4 and 9, 3x4 gives 9 and 16. So 2x4 gives 4 and 16, which is 416.
The first digits come from the square of the first number and the rest from the square of the second.
In which province of Pakistan did the country carry out its nuclear tests in May 1998?
The tests were carried out in the Chagai Hills in Chagai district, Balochistan.
The Ras Koh Hills in the Chagai range was the site of the main tests of 28 May 1998.
What is the meaning of the idiom "to take to one's heels"?
The idiom "take to one's heels" means to run away quickly, usually from danger.
A similar idiom is "to show a clean pair of heels", which means to outrun someone.
What is a synonym of the word "total"?
"Total" means the whole amount after adding everything together, which is the same as "sum".
The opposite of total in this sense is "part" or "fraction".
What is the length of a marathon race in miles?
A standard marathon is 42.195 km. Dividing by 1.609 gives about 26.2 miles.
The marathon distance of 42.195 km was fixed by World Athletics after the 1908 London Olympics.
Complete the sentence: Our team ______ their track suits.
"Team" is treated here as one unit, so the singular verb "is wearing" is used.
In British English a collective noun like team can also take a plural verb, but the singular is the textbook answer.
If A transpose is equal to A, then the matrix A is called what?
A square matrix with A^T = A is called a symmetric matrix. If A^T = -A, it is skew symmetric.
The diagonal entries of a skew symmetric matrix are always zero.
A car travels 70 km in one hour. How much distance will it travel in 40 minutes at the same speed?
40 minutes is 40/60 = 2/3 of an hour. Distance = 70 x 2/3 = 46.67 km.
Distance equals speed multiplied by time.
Insulin is used for the treatment of which disease?
Insulin is a hormone that controls blood sugar, so it is used to treat diabetes.
Insulin is produced by the beta cells of the pancreas.

Hazrat Ali (RA) wrote the text of the Treaty of Hudaibiyah as dictated by the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
Suhail bin Amr represented the Quraish in the treaty.
What is the synonym of the word "trouble"?
"Trouble" means a problem or hardship, which is the same as difficulty.
Other synonyms include distress and worry.
If the 3rd day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 26th be?
From the 3rd to the 26th is 23 days. 23 divided by 7 leaves 2, so Tuesday + 2 = Thursday.
The 10th, 17th and 24th of this month are also Tuesdays.
If the 1st day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 21st be?
From the 1st to the 21st is 20 days. 20 divided by 7 leaves 6, so Tuesday + 6 = Monday.
The 22nd is exactly 3 weeks after the 1st, so it is a Tuesday.
Who was the leader of the Muslim army in the Battle of Uhud?
The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) himself commanded the Muslim army at Uhud.
He placed 50 archers on the Ainain hill under Abdullah bin Jubair.
Umm-ul-Masakeen (Mother of the Poor) is the title of which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaymah (RA) was known as Umm-ul-Masakeen because of her great generosity to the poor.
She died within a few months of marrying the Prophet (PBUH) and is among the wives who passed away in his lifetime, along with Hazrat Khadija (RA).
Which British queen was the first to visit Pakistan?
Queen Elizabeth II visited Pakistan in February 1961, the first reigning British monarch to do so.
She visited again in 1997 with Prince Philip.
In which year did the Soviet Union complete its withdrawal from Afghanistan?
The last Soviet troops left Afghanistan on 15 February 1989, after the 1979 invasion.
The Soviet Union entered Afghanistan in December 1979.
Under the Indus Waters Treaty, what is the position of Pakistan relative to India on the rivers?
The rivers rise in or pass through Indian-held territory before entering Pakistan, so Pakistan is the lower riparian (downstream) state.
The treaty was signed in Karachi in 1960 with World Bank mediation.
Who has taken the most wickets in One Day Internationals?
Muttiah Muralitharan of Sri Lanka took 534 ODI wickets, the highest ever.
Wasim Akram is second with 502 wickets, the most by a Pakistani.
In which country is the White Sea located?
The White Sea is an inlet of the Barents Sea on the north-west coast of Russia.
The port city of Arkhangelsk lies on it.
Complete the analogy: Man is to wallet as woman is to ____.
A man carries money in a wallet and a woman usually carries it in a purse.
Analogy questions test the relation between the first pair.

He told her that he wanted to meet her father.
He told her that I want to meet your father.
He told her that he wants to meet your father.
He told her that he had wanted to meet his father.

Say or tell with an object is changed to told in reported speech.
Which country has the second largest population in the world (2026)?
India is first and China is second according to 2026 estimates.
India overtook China as the most populous country in 2023, and before that China was first.
For which book is Gulbadan Begum, daughter of Babur, famous as a writer?
Gulbadan Begum wrote the Humayun-nama, a history of the reign of her brother Humayun.
She was one of the first Mughal women to write history.
Who wrote the work The Loyal Muhammadans of India?
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote it around 1860 to show that most Muslims were loyal to the British during the events of 1857.
Sir Syed also wrote Asar-us-Sanadid and founded the Aligarh movement.
What was the name of the mother of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS)?
Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS) and Rifqa (Rebecca).
Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) is also known as Israel.
What is the relation between Hazrat Zakariya (AS) and Hazrat Yahya (AS)?
Hazrat Yahya (AS) was the son of Hazrat Zakariya (AS), born in his old age by Allah's will.
Hazrat Yahya (AS) is mentioned in Surah Maryam.
What was the relation of Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) with the Holy Prophet (SAW)?
Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) was a freed slave whom the Prophet (SAW) adopted as his son before Islam.
He is the only Companion named in the Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab).
Is zero a natural number, according to the definition taught in Pakistani textbooks?
Yes, it is the first natural number
No, it is a whole number
No, it is a negative number
Yes, it is a prime number
Natural numbers are the counting numbers 1, 2, 3 and so on. Zero is added to them to form the whole numbers.
Some modern books include zero among the natural numbers, so definitions differ.
