Krone is the currency of which country?
The Danish krone is the currency of Denmark. Norway also uses a krone.
Sweden uses the krona and Finland uses the euro.
What is the boundary line between India and China called?
The McMahon Line was drawn in 1914 and is the boundary India claims with China in the east.
China does not accept the McMahon Line.
How many peaks above 8000 metres are located in Pakistan?
Pakistan has five peaks above 8000 m: K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Gasherbrum II and Broad Peak.
The whole world has 14 peaks above 8000 m, and K2 at 8611 m is the second highest.
In which province is the Lower Indus plain mostly located?
The Lower Indus plain lies in Sindh, from near Sukkur down to the Arabian Sea.
The Upper Indus plain lies mainly in Punjab.
Which country hosted the G20 summit in 2023 (New Delhi)?
The 2023 G20 summit was held in New Delhi, India, in September 2023. India held the G20 presidency that year.
Indonesia hosted in 2022 and Brazil in 2024.
Kiwi, a flightless bird, is the national symbol of which country?
The kiwi is the national bird of New Zealand, and New Zealanders are often called Kiwis.
The kiwi fruit is also linked to New Zealand but it originally came from China.
Who wrote the novel Ice Candy Man?
Ice Candy Man (1988) was written by the Pakistani novelist Bapsi Sidhwa. It tells the story of Partition through a Parsi girl in Lahore.
The novel was published in the USA as Cracking India and was filmed as 1947 Earth.
In which year did Pakistan play its first Test match?
Pakistan's first Test was played against India in Delhi in October 1952.
Pakistan's first Test win came against India at Lucknow in the same series.
Car is to wheel as sound is to what?
A car moves by its wheels in the same way that sound travels as waves.
Sound is a mechanical wave and cannot travel through a vacuum.
World War 2 began on 1 September 1939 when Germany invaded Poland.
It ended in 1945 with the surrender of Germany in May and Japan in September.
Who is credited with inventing the electric motor?
Michael Faraday demonstrated the first electric motor in 1821, and most textbooks credit him.
Other inventors such as Jedlik, Jacobi and Davenport also built early motors, so sources differ.
In which year was the Durand Line, the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, agreed?
The Durand Line agreement was signed in 1893 between Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan of Afghanistan.
Afghanistan has not formally accepted the Durand Line as an international border.
Who is the Prime Minister of Canada today (October 2026)?
Mark Carney became Prime Minister of Canada on 14 March 2025 and leads the Liberal Party. Canada has no president; the Prime Minister is head of government.
Justin Trudeau was Prime Minister before Carney (2015 to 2025), and King Charles III is Canada's head of state.
Who wrote the Urdu poetry book Bal-e-Jibreel (Gabriel's Wing)?
Bal-e-Jibreel was written by Allama Muhammad Iqbal and published in 1935.
Iqbal's other Urdu books include Bang-e-Dara and Zarb-e-Kaleem.
Which element is the most abundant in the universe?
Hydrogen makes up about 75 percent of the ordinary matter in the universe by mass.
Helium is the second most abundant element, and oxygen is the most abundant in the Earth crust.
In which year did Aligarh College (MAO College) become Aligarh Muslim University?
The MAO College was given university status in 1920 and became Aligarh Muslim University.
The MAO school began in 1875 and became a college in 1877, and sources differ slightly on these dates.
For what is the city of Multan famous?
Multan is known as the City of Saints (Madinat-ul-Auliya) because it has many famous shrines of Sufi saints.
Multan is also called the City of Pirs and is famous for its mangoes and blue pottery.
Muhammad bin Qasim, a young Arab general of the Umayyad caliphate, defeated Raja Dahir and conquered Sindh.
Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam, the Gateway of Islam, in the subcontinent.
Which word is closest to the opposite of envious?
Envious means wanting what others have. A content person is satisfied with what they have, so content is the opposite.
The noun envy is opposed by contentment.
Who was known as the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity in the subcontinent?
Muhammad Ali Jinnah worked for Hindu-Muslim unity in the early part of his career, including the 1916 Lucknow Pact. Sarojini Naidu gave him this title.
Jinnah was a member of the Indian National Congress before he led the Muslim League.
What was the first book of poetry of Allama Iqbal?
Asrar-e-Khudi, a Persian poetry book, was published in 1915 and is usually called his first poetry book.
His first prose book was Ilm-ul-Iqtisad (1903), so sources differ depending on the question.
A quarter of a number is the same as dividing it by 4.
Which is the hottest planet of the solar system?
Venus is the hottest planet, about 465 degrees Celsius, because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat.
Mercury is closer to the Sun but has almost no atmosphere to hold heat.
On which date did the full-scale 1965 war between Pakistan and India begin, according to Pakistani textbooks?
India attacked Lahore across the international border on 6 September 1965, which started the full-scale war. A ceasefire came on 23 September 1965.
Operation Gibraltar had begun earlier, in early August 1965, which is why some candidates remember 5 August.
Which ruler is known as the Tiger of Mysore (Sher-e-Mysore)?
Tipu Sultan fought the British in the Anglo-Mysore wars and is called the Tiger of Mysore.
He was martyred in 1799 defending Seringapatam in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.
Into how many main physical regions is Pakistan commonly divided in Pakistan Studies textbooks?
Textbooks usually list six regions: Northern Mountains, Western Mountains, Potohar Plateau, Balochistan Plateau, Indus Plains and Deserts.
Sources differ, and some books group these into five regions.
Who is regarded as the oldest (first) poet of the Pashto language?
Amir Kror Suri, a ruler of Ghor in the 8th century, is regarded as the earliest known Pashto poet.
Rahman Baba and Khushal Khan Khattak are famous later Pashto poets.
Which is the oldest sport in the world according to most textbooks?
Wrestling is usually named as the oldest sport, as cave paintings and ancient records show it thousands of years ago.
Sources differ, as some also name running, archery or chess among the oldest.
Where were all the Round Table Conferences (1930 to 1932) held?
The three Round Table Conferences were held in London to discuss constitutional reforms for India. They took place in 1930, 1931 and 1932.
The Muslim League was represented by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah and Allama Iqbal attended the second session.
In which region of Pakistan is the Shina (Sheena) language mainly spoken?
Shina is the main language of the Gilgit area and nearby valleys of Gilgit-Baltistan. It belongs to the Dardic group of languages.
Shina is also spoken in parts of Indian-administered Kashmir and in Kohistan.
Which vegetable is regarded as the national vegetable of Pakistan?
Okra, known locally as bhindi or lady finger, is commonly listed as Pakistan's national vegetable.
Lists of national symbols differ between sources because there is no well-known official notification.
The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared by a committee headed by whom?
The All Parties Committee that drafted the 1928 Nehru Report was chaired by Motilal Nehru.
Jawaharlal Nehru, his son, served as secretary of the committee.
Which building is shown on the back of the Pakistani 100 rupee note?
The reverse of the Rs 100 note shows the Quaid-e-Azam Residency in Ziarat, Balochistan.
The Rs 5000 note shows the Faisal Mosque on its back.
Approximately what percentage of Pakistan's area does Balochistan cover?
Balochistan has about 347,000 square km, which Pakistani textbooks give as roughly 44% of the country.
Sources differ slightly, as some give about 40 percent depending on the total area used.
Which person won two Nobel Prizes in his life, one of them the Nobel Peace Prize?
Linus Pauling won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1954 and the Nobel Peace Prize in 1962.
He is the only person to win two unshared Nobel Prizes.
Who built the Red Fort of Delhi?
The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built the Red Fort in Delhi, completed in 1648.
Shah Jahan also built the Taj Mahal and the Badshahi Mosque was built by Aurangzeb.
In which Amendment to the 1973 Constitution were Ahmadis declared non-Muslim?
The Second Amendment, passed in 1974, declared Ahmadis non-Muslim for the purposes of the Constitution.
It was passed during the government of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
Pablo Picasso, the famous painter, belonged to which country?
Pablo Picasso was born in Malaga, Spain, in 1881.
He spent most of his adult life in France and co-founded the Cubist art movement.
Which is the largest dam of Pakistan?
Tarbela Dam on the Indus River is the largest earth filled dam in Pakistan and one of the largest in the world.
Mangla Dam on the Jhelum is the second largest.
On which date did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan die?
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan died on 27 March 1898 at Aligarh. He was born on 17 October 1817.
He is buried in the compound of the Jama Masjid at Aligarh Muslim University.
Which mountain range lies in the north-west of Pakistan?
The Hindu Kush range lies in the north-west of Pakistan, along the border with Afghanistan.
Some sources also mention the Sulaiman Range, which lies to the west.
In which city was the second Islamic Summit Conference of the OIC held in 1974?
The second OIC Islamic Summit took place in Lahore in February 1974 and was hosted by Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
The first Islamic Summit was held in Rabat, Morocco, in 1969.
Who won the ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year (Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy) award for 2022?
Babar Azam of Pakistan won the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy for 2022.
Shaheen Shah Afridi won it for 2021.
What is the full form of ISPR?
ISPR stands for Inter Services Public Relations, the media wing of the Pakistan Armed Forces.
It is headed by a Director General, a serving army officer.
Which dam of Pakistan is made of earth and rock fill and is the largest earth-filled dam in the world?
Tarbela Dam on the Indus River is mostly built of earth and rock fill and is called the largest earth-filled dam.
BODMAS stands for Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.
Who was the Viceroy of India in 1911 when the partition of Bengal was annulled?
Lord Hardinge was Viceroy from 1910 to 1916. The annulment of the 1905 partition was announced at the Delhi Durbar in December 1911.
The capital was also shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911.
In a class of 500 students, 340 are boys. What percentage of the students are girls?
The percentage of boys here is 68%, and the two percentages add up to 100%.
On which date did the USA drop the atomic bomb on Hiroshima, Japan?
The first atomic bomb was dropped on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945.
A second bomb hit Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.
Humayun was defeated by which ruler, forcing him to leave India in 1540?
Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun at Chausa in 1539 and at Kannauj in 1540. Humayun then fled India.
Humayun regained his throne in 1555 after defeating the Suri ruler Sikandar Suri.
On which date did Israel declare its independence?
David Ben-Gurion declared the State of Israel on 14 May 1948, as the British Mandate ended.
Israel celebrates its Independence Day by the Hebrew calendar, so the Gregorian date changes each year.
Which city is known as the City of Light?
Paris is called the City of Light because it was an early centre of education and ideas and one of the first cities with gas street lighting.
Paris is the capital of France and stands on the River Seine.
Who is the author of the book Pakistaniat (What is Pakistaniat?)?
Pakistaniat is the idea of Pakistani national identity, and Javed Jabbar wrote a book on it titled What is Pakistaniat. He lists many elements that shape the identity of the Pakistani nation.
Javed Jabbar is a Pakistani politician, writer and former senator who also wrote Pakistan: Unique Origins, Unique Destiny.
Germany invaded which country first in World War II in September 1939?
Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. Britain and France then declared war on Germany.
The Soviet Union also invaded Poland from the east on 17 September 1939.
Butterfly is a technique (stroke) of which sport?
Butterfly stroke is one of the four main competitive swimming strokes.
The other strokes are freestyle, backstroke and breaststroke.
What does OS stand for in computing?
In computers, OS stands for Operating System, the main software that runs the computer.
Windows, Linux, macOS and Android are well-known operating systems.
The Wagah border connects Pakistan with which country?
Wagah, on the Grand Trunk Road between Lahore and Amritsar, is the main land crossing between Pakistan and India.
A daily flag-lowering ceremony is held there by both countries.
In 9/2 the numerator 9 is greater than the denominator 2, so it is an improper fraction. It equals the mixed number 4 and 1/2.
A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator, for example 2/9.
Which country is Pakistan's biggest trading partner today?
China is Pakistan's largest trading partner, mainly because of large imports from China.
The United States is Pakistan's largest single export market, but China leads in total trade.
Who is the head of state of Pakistan according to the 1973 Constitution (currently in office, 2026)?
The President is the head of state, and Asif Ali Zardari has held the office since 10 March 2024.
His predecessor was Arif Alvi (2018 to 2024); the Prime Minister is head of government.
What is the tenure of a member of the Senate of Pakistan?
A Senator is elected for six years. Half of the members retire every three years.
The Senate is a permanent house and cannot be dissolved.
How many Prime Ministers did Pakistan have between 1947 and 1958?
They were Liaquat Ali Khan, Khawaja Nazimuddin, Mohammad Ali Bogra, Chaudhry Mohammad Ali, H. S. Suhrawardy, I. I. Chundrigar and Feroz Khan Noon, which makes 7.
Martial law was imposed in October 1958 by Iskander Mirza and Ayub Khan.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah join the Indian National Congress?
Jinnah joined the Indian National Congress in 1906, when he attended its Calcutta session.
He joined the All India Muslim League later, in 1913.
In which year was the C. R. (Rajagopalachari) Formula put forward?
C. Rajagopalachari proposed the formula in 1944 as a basis for talks between Gandhi and Jinnah.
The Gandhi-Jinnah talks of September 1944 failed, partly because Jinnah rejected the formula.
Which sport is called the Game of Gentlemen?
Cricket is known as the Game of Gentlemen because of its tradition of fair play and sportsmanship. The phrase comes from its English origins.
Cricket began in England and its laws are kept by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC).
Who founded the Khudai Khidmatgar movement?
Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Bacha Khan) founded the Khudai Khidmatgar (Servants of God) movement around 1929 in the Pashtun areas.
Its members were known as Red Shirts and followed non-violence.
In which city is Paradise Point located?
Paradise Point is a famous rocky beach spot on the Arabian Sea coast in Karachi.
It is close to Cape Monze (Ras Muari) and has a natural arch in the rocks.
In which city of Pakistan is Iqbal Park located?
Iqbal Park in Lahore is the park where Minar-e-Pakistan stands and the Pakistan Resolution was passed in 1940.
It was earlier called Minto Park.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam return to India after his self-imposed exile in England?
Jinnah stayed in London for some years after the Round Table Conferences. He came back in 1934 at the request of Muslim leaders and was elected president of the Muslim League.
Some sources give 1935 for his final return, but 1934 is the common textbook year.
A train moves at a speed of 60 km/hour. How much time will it take to cover 150 km?
Who prepared the Pirpur Report of 1938 on the grievances of Muslims in Congress provinces?
Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur
The Pirpur Report was prepared by a Muslim League committee headed by Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur.
Fazlul Haq issued a separate report in 1939 called the Sharif Report.
Which constitution of Pakistan was enforced in 1962?
The second constitution, with a presidential system
The first constitution, with a parliamentary system
The third constitution, with a parliamentary system
The 1962 constitution was the second constitution of Pakistan and gave a presidential system with strong powers to the President.
It was given by President Ayub Khan and ended in 1969 when Yahya Khan imposed martial law.
Akbar is older than Khalid and Ahmed is younger than Khalid. Which statement is true?
The order from oldest is Akbar, Khalid, Ahmed. So Akbar is older than Ahmed.
Chaining two comparisons gives a third one.
What does the crescent on the flag of Pakistan represent?
According to the usual explanation, the crescent stands for progress.
The five pointed star stands for light and knowledge, and the white strip for minorities.
Who wrote the book 'Pakistan: The Heart of Asia'?
Pakistan: The Heart of Asia is a collection of speeches made by Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, during his 1950 visit to the USA.
Ayub Khan wrote the autobiography Friends Not Masters.
In which year did Pakistan become a member of the International Labour Organization (ILO)?
Pakistan has been an ILO member since 1947, the year of its independence.
The ILO headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland.
Between which latitudes does Pakistan lie?
Pakistan extends from about 24 degrees north in the south to about 37 degrees north in the north.
Pakistan's north-south extent is roughly 1,600 km.
In which district of Sindh is Ranikot Fort (Rani Fort) situated?
Ranikot Fort lies in the Kirthar foothills of Jamshoro district in Sindh.
Ranikot is often called the largest fort in the world because its wall is about 26 km long.
Which two countries are known for the greatest rivalry in Test cricket?
England and Australia play the Ashes series, the oldest and most famous rivalry in Test cricket.
The Ashes began in 1882 after Australia beat England at The Oval.
In which war was Captain Muhammad Sarwar Shaheed martyred?
Captain Muhammad Sarwar was martyred in the 1948 Kashmir war near Uri in October 1948.
He was the first recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider.
Who is called the Traveller of Islam?
Ibn Battuta, the Moroccan explorer, travelled about 120,000 km across Africa, Asia and Europe in nearly 30 years.
He wrote the famous travel book called the Rihla.
In which year was the Wavell Plan announced?
Lord Wavell, the Viceroy, announced his plan in June 1945, and it was discussed at the Simla Conference.
The Cripps Mission came earlier, in 1942.
On a farm, goats are double the cows and camels are double the goats. If there are 10 goats, how many animals are on the farm?
Goats are 10, so cows are 10 / 2 = 5 and camels are 10 x 2 = 20. Total is 5 + 10 + 20 = 35.
Always find the base quantity first, then work out the others.
Where is the National College of Arts (NCA) located?
The National College of Arts is a famous art and design institution in Lahore. It was founded in 1875 as the Mayo School of Art.
Its first principal was John Lockwood Kipling, the father of the writer Rudyard Kipling.
Who was the Finance Minister in the interim government of British India in 1946, before independence?
Liaquat Ali Khan held the finance portfolio in the interim government formed in October 1946. His budget was nicknamed the poor man's budget.
Liaquat Ali Khan later became the first Prime Minister of Pakistan.
Who wrote the book Pakistan: A Hard Country?
Pakistan: A Hard Country (2011) was written by the British author Anatol Lieven.
Ahmed Rashid wrote Taliban and Descent into Chaos.
If 7 books cost 3500 rupees, what is the price of 1 book?
Price of 1 book = 3500 divided by 7 = 500 rupees.
This is the unitary method: find the price of one item first.
In a bus, 2/3 of the passengers are men. What is the percentage of women?
Women are 1 minus 2/3 = 1/3 of the passengers. 1/3 of 100 = 33.33%.
Doomed means certain to meet a bad end or failure.
Doom also refers to death or destruction.
The platypus and the echidna are monotremes, the only mammals that lay eggs.
Monotremes live in Australia and New Guinea.
Which of the following books was written by Altaf Hussain Hali?
Altaf Hussain Hali wrote the long poem Musaddas, also called Madd-o-Jazr-e-Islam, in 1879. Bang-e-Dra and Shikwa are by Allama Iqbal, and Aab-e-Hayat is by Muhammad Hussain Azad.
Hali also wrote Hayat-e-Javed, Yadgar-e-Ghalib and Muqaddama Sher-o-Shayari.
Jabir bin Hayyan (Geber) is known as the father of which science?
Jabir bin Hayyan, a Muslim scientist of the eighth century, developed early laboratory methods such as distillation and crystallisation, so he is called the father of chemistry.
Ibn al-Haytham is known as the father of optics and Al-Khwarizmi as the father of algebra.
What is the date of Bangladesh's declaration of independence?
Bangladesh declared independence on 26 March 1971 and celebrates it as Independence Day. The war ended on 16 December 1971.
16 December is celebrated in Bangladesh as Victory Day.
What is the lowest point on the surface of the earth on land?
The shore of the Dead Sea, between Israel, Jordan and the West Bank, is about 430 m below sea level, the lowest land point.
The Dead Sea is also one of the saltiest lakes in the world.
The ancient Mehrgarh civilization site, one of the oldest farming settlements in South Asia, is located in which province of Pakistan?
Mehrgarh lies on the Kachhi plain near the Bolan Pass in Balochistan.
Mehrgarh dates back to about 7000 BC and came before the Indus Valley civilization.
What was the real (original) name of Shah Waliullah of Delhi?
Shah Waliullah was born as Qutbuddin Ahmad and later became known as Shah Waliullah.
He wrote the famous book Hujjat Allah al-Baligha.
Who is Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in New York as of October 2026?
Asim Iftikhar Ahmad heads the Pakistan Mission to the UN and issues its statements in 2026.
Munir Akram held this post before him.
Which place in Punjab is famous for its salt mountain and salt mine?
Khewra in the Salt Range of Jhelum district is famous for the world's second largest salt mine.
The Khewra salt mine was discovered in the time of Alexander the Great, according to local tradition.
In which city is the shrine of the Sufi poet Bulleh Shah located?
Bulleh Shah is buried in Kasur, in Punjab.
Bulleh Shah wrote his Sufi poetry (kafis) in Punjabi.
What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word spurn?
To spurn means to refuse something with scorn. Reject is the nearest meaning.
Spurn can also be used as a noun in old English for a kick, but the common meaning is to refuse.
If the 13th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 28th of that month?
28 - 13 = 15 days later. 15 = 14 + 1, so move 1 day forward from Monday, which is Tuesday.
Two full weeks (14 days) bring back the same weekday.
If the 27th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 9th day be?
From the 9th to the 27th is 18 days. 18 divided by 7 leaves 4, so Monday - 4 days = Thursday.
Saeed Anwar, famous in Pakistan, was a player of which sport?
Saeed Anwar was a left-handed opening batsman of the Pakistan cricket team.
He scored 194 against India in 1997, which was then the highest ODI score.
What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3 PM?
At 3 o'clock the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand is at 3. Three hour marks of 30 degrees each make 90 degrees.
Each hour mark on a clock face is 30 degrees apart.
Who is the head of the cabinet in a parliamentary system?
In a parliamentary system the Prime Minister leads the cabinet and the government.
In Pakistan the President is the head of state, not of the cabinet.
In which present-day country did Islam originate?
Islam began in Makkah in the Arabian Peninsula, in what is now Saudi Arabia.
The first revelation came to the Prophet (PBUH) in the Cave of Hira near Makkah.
Is the cosine function an even or an odd function?
cos(-x) = cos x for every x, which is the definition of an even function.
Sine and tangent are odd functions because sin(-x) = -sin x and tan(-x) = -tan x.
In which year was Prime Minister Khawaja Nazimuddin dismissed?
Khawaja Nazimuddin was dismissed on 17 April 1953.
He had become Prime Minister after the assassination of Liaquat Ali Khan in 1951.
Doomed means destined for misfortune, so its opposite is blessed or fortunate.
Fated and condemned are synonyms of doomed.
Which word is closest in meaning to furtive?
Furtive means done in a secret or sneaky way to avoid being noticed. Stealthy has the same meaning.
Other synonyms of furtive are secretive, sly and surreptitious.
A car travels 60 km. A train with double the speed of the car travels for half the time. What distance does the train cover?
Distance = speed x time. Doubling the speed and halving the time gives 2 x 1/2 = 1 times the car's distance, which is 60 km.
Speed doubled and time halved leaves the distance unchanged.
On which date is the Kargil conflict between Pakistan and India commonly said to have begun in 1999?
The conflict is commonly dated from 3 May 1999, when intrusions were first reported in the Kargil sector.
Indian sources mark 26 July 1999 as the end of the conflict, and sources differ slightly on exact dates.
In which year was Zulfikar Ali Bhutto hanged?
Bhutto was hanged on 4 April 1979, after being removed from power by General Zia ul Haq in July 1977.
He was the founder of the Pakistan Peoples Party.
Between which longitudes does Pakistan lie?
Pakistan lies approximately between 61 degrees east and 75 degrees east longitude.
Pakistan lies in the northern and eastern hemispheres.
Where is the Noor Mahal located?
Noor Mahal is a palace built by the Nawab of Bahawalpur in 1872 in the city of Bahawalpur.
It is now under the care of the Pakistan Army.
What is the full name of Imam Malik, founder of the Maliki school of fiqh?
Imam Malik is Malik ibn Anas, who lived in Madinah. He is also called Imam of Madinah.
Pakistan provides a sea route to the landlocked countries of which region?
Pakistan's ports, Karachi, Port Qasim and Gwadar, offer the shortest sea access for Afghanistan and the Central Asian states. These states have no coastline of their own.
Afghanistan has long used Karachi port under the Afghan Transit Trade agreement.
Under which constitution is Pakistan currently being run?
Pakistan is run under the Constitution of 1973, which came into force on 14 August 1973 and has been amended many times.
The earlier constitutions of 1956 and 1962 were abrogated.
What is the tenure (term) of the National Assembly of Pakistan, unless it is dissolved earlier?
Under the 1973 Constitution the National Assembly lasts five years from its first meeting. After that it stops working automatically.
The Senate is a permanent house and is never dissolved.
Who was the Governor General of India during the War of Independence of 1857 and became the first Viceroy in 1858?
Lord Canning was Governor General from 1856 to 1858. After the Government of India Act 1858 he became the first Viceroy.
Lord Dalhousie was his predecessor and introduced the Doctrine of Lapse.
Who was the President of Pakistan during the 1971 war with India?
General Yahya Khan was President from March 1969 until 20 December 1971, so he was President during the December 1971 war.
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto took over as President and Chief Martial Law Administrator on 20 December 1971.
Which country won the 1974 FIFA World Cup?
West Germany beat the Netherlands 2-1 in the final in Munich to win the 1974 FIFA World Cup.
West Germany had also won the World Cup in 1954.
In the point (3, 4), what is the number 3 called?
In an ordered pair (x, y) the first number x is the abscissa. The second number y is the ordinate.
The abscissa is measured along the x-axis.
Which province of the subcontinent did the British occupy first?
The British won the Battle of Plassey in 1757 and took control of Bengal first.
Sindh was conquered in 1843 and Punjab in 1849.
In which year was the Advisory Council of Islamic Ideology (Islamic Council) established in Pakistan?
The Advisory Council of Islamic Ideology was set up under the 1962 Constitution, on 1 August 1962.
In the 1973 Constitution it continued as the Council of Islamic Ideology under Articles 228 to 230.
Disastrous means causing great harm or damage, which is the same as catastrophic.
Doomed means destined to a bad outcome, which is the same as fated.
The noun doom means a terrible fate.
Which country is the largest exporter of tea in the world by volume?
Kenya exports more tea by volume than any other country. India is second, and Sri Lanka and China follow.
China is the largest tea producer, but it keeps much of its tea for home use, and sources differ if ranked by value.
In which country was FIFA founded in 1904?
FIFA was founded in Paris, France, on 21 May 1904 by seven European associations.
FIFA headquarters are today in Zurich, Switzerland.
Which is the largest glacier of Pakistan according to most Pakistani textbooks?
Pakistani textbooks name the Siachen Glacier, about 76 km long, as the largest in the Karakoram and in the region.
Sources differ because Siachen is under Indian control, and Biafo and Baltoro are the longest glaciers inside Pakistan-administered areas.
The Gobi Desert lies in southern Mongolia and in which other country?
The Gobi Desert stretches across southern Mongolia and northern China.
It is a cold desert and the largest desert in Asia.
What is the currency of Hungary?
Hungary uses its own currency, the forint (HUF). It has not adopted the euro.
Poland uses the zloty and the Czech Republic uses the koruna.
The United States entered World War II after which event?
The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor
Japan attacked the US naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, on 7 December 1941. The US declared war on Japan the next day.
Germany and Italy then declared war on the US a few days later.
Which group of gases is mainly responsible for damaging the ozone layer?
CFCs release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere, and these break down ozone molecules.
The Montreal Protocol of 1987 phased out the use of CFCs.
What is the antonym of the word liberty?
Liberty means freedom, so its opposite is slavery or bondage.
Captivity and servitude are also antonyms of liberty.
In a bus of 30 passengers, 2/3 are male. How many are female?
Females are 1/3 of the total, which is about 33.33 percent.
What is the name of the force that opposes the motion between two bodies in contact?
Friction acts between touching surfaces and opposes their relative motion.
Under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, a Federal Minister must be a member of which body?
Article 92 says Federal Ministers are appointed from the members of Majlis-e-Shoora, which means the National Assembly or the Senate.
Not more than one-fourth of the Federal Ministers can be taken from the Senate.
Where is the Pakistan Navy War College located?
The Pakistan Navy War College is in Lahore.
The Pakistan Navy headquarters is in Islamabad.
What is a synonym of oppression?
Oppression means cruel and unjust use of power, which is the same as tyranny.
Persecution is another synonym of oppression.
In which constitutional amendment were Qadianis declared non-Muslim in Pakistan?
The Second Amendment to the 1973 Constitution, passed in 1974, declared Qadianis (Ahmadis) non-Muslims. It was passed under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
The amendment added clause 3 to Article 260.
The product of two real numbers is always which kind of number?
Real numbers are closed under multiplication, so multiplying two real numbers always gives a real number.
Real numbers are also closed under addition and subtraction.
Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points of 1929 were presented in reply to which report?
The Nehru Report of 1928 rejected separate electorates and other Muslim demands. Quaid-e-Azam answered it with his Fourteen Points in March 1929.
The Fourteen Points also demanded the separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency.
Shahbaz Ahmed Senior is a renowned Pakistani player of which game?
Shahbaz Ahmed Senior was a famous Pakistani hockey midfielder and captain. He was part of the team that won Olympic gold in 1984.
Pakistan has won the Olympic hockey gold medal three times.
In a class of 33 students, the boys outnumber the girls by 7. How many girls are there?
Let girls = g, then boys = g + 7. So g + g + 7 = 33, 2g = 26 and g = 13.
There are 20 boys in this class.
Who was the father of the Mughal emperor Humayun?
Humayun was the second Mughal emperor and the son of Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire.
Humayun's son Akbar became the third Mughal emperor.
Which word is pronounced differently from the rest: white, wait, wrong?
In wrong the w is silent and the word begins with the r sound. In white and wait the w is pronounced.
Other words with a silent w are write, wrist and wrap.
Which Muslim leader was given the title of knighthood (Sir) by the British in 1888?
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was awarded the title KCSI (Knight Commander of the Star of India) in 1888.
Allama Iqbal was knighted later, in 1923.
Who was the Speaker (President) of the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan from 1948, after Quaid-e-Azam?
Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan became President (Speaker) of the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan in 1948 and held the post until 1954.
In 1954 Tamizuddin Khan challenged the dissolution of the Assembly by Governor General Ghulam Muhammad in court.
Who was the President of Pakistan under the 1962 constitution in 1962?
Field Marshal Ayub Khan was President of Pakistan from 1958 to 1969, and he introduced the 1962 constitution.
Ayub Khan was the first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army.
What is shown on the back of the Pakistani 5000 rupee note?
The State Bank of Pakistan describes the back of the Rs 5000 note as showing the Faisal Mosque, Islamabad.
The front of the note carries the portrait of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
What is the antonym of the word sympathetic?
Sympathetic means feeling pity and care for others, so its opposite is callous or unfeeling.
Merciless and heartless are also opposites.
What was the date of birth of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan?
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was born on 17 October 1817 in Delhi.
He founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875.
Which of these countries has a coastline on the Black Sea?
The Black Sea is bordered by Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia and Georgia. Ukraine is the only one among the options.
The Black Sea connects to the Mediterranean through the Bosphorus and the Dardanelles.
In which language did Baba Bulleh Shah write his poetry?
Bulleh Shah, the Sufi poet of Kasur, wrote mainly in Punjabi (kafis).
Bulleh Shah lived from about 1680 to 1757.
Which region of China borders Pakistan in the north?
The Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region of China touches Gilgit-Baltistan in the north of Pakistan.
The Karakoram Highway crosses the Khunjerab Pass to link Pakistan with Xinjiang.
In which city is Clifton Beach located?
Clifton Beach, also called Sea View, is on the Arabian Sea coast in Karachi.
Karachi is the capital of Sindh province.
What is the process called in which a gas changes directly into a liquid?
Condensation is the change of a gas or vapour into a liquid, for example water vapour forming water drops.
Condensation is the opposite of evaporation.
What is the currency of Bhutan?
Bhutan's currency is the ngultrum, which is pegged to the Indian rupee.
The Indian rupee is also accepted in Bhutan.
Which word is a synonym of efficiency?
Efficiency means doing a job well with little waste, which is the same as competence.
In which year was the draft constitution of the European Union presented?
The European Convention presented the draft Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe in 2003.
The treaty was signed in 2004 but was never enforced, because France and the Netherlands rejected it in 2005.
Change the voice: By whom is the child being fed?
Who is being fed by the child?
The sentence is in the present continuous passive. The active form is "Who is feeding the child?", with the same tense.
For "by whom" questions in passive voice, the active form starts with "who".
Which river do Hindus in India regard as sacred?
Hindus consider the Ganges (Ganga) the holiest river and bathe in it at places like Varanasi and Haridwar. It is worshipped as the goddess Ganga.
The Ganges flows from the Himalayas to the Bay of Bengal.
Who is the current President of Iraq (as of October 2026)?
Iraq's parliament elected Nizar Amidi (Amedi) as President on 11 April 2026.
His predecessor Abdul Latif Rashid held the office from October 2022 to 2026.
In which country are the Olympic Mountains located?
The Olympic Mountains are in the state of Washington in the north-west United States.
They are on the Olympic Peninsula and contain Olympic National Park.
Who was the Governor-General of India at the time of the War of Independence of 1857?
Lord Canning was Governor-General from 1856 and became the first Viceroy of India in 1858.
Gypsum is the main source of which two elements?
Gypsum is hydrated calcium sulfate (CaSO4.2H2O), so it supplies calcium and sulfur.
Heated gypsum gives plaster of Paris.

A train moves at twice the speed of a car, and the car moves at 60 km/h. How far will the train go in 12 minutes?
Train speed is 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. In 12 minutes (12/60 = 0.2 hour) it covers 120 x 0.2 = 24 km.
To change minutes to hours, divide by 60.
What was the Tashkent Pact (Declaration) of 1966?
A peace agreement between Pakistan and India after the 1965 war
A trade treaty between Pakistan and China
A defence pact between Pakistan and the USA
A water treaty on the Indus rivers
It was a peace agreement signed on 10 January 1966 in which both sides agreed to withdraw to pre-war positions.
The Soviet Union mediated the agreement.
Who signed the Tashkent Declaration on behalf of India?
Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri signed it and died in Tashkent the next day.
Ayub Khan signed it for Pakistan.
If 5 men type 5 pages in 5 minutes, how long will 1 man take to type 1 page?
5 men type 5 pages in 5 minutes, so each man types 1 page in 5 minutes.
Work equals number of workers multiplied by time, divided by the number of pages.
Peshawar has traditionally been known as the city of what?
Peshawar was traditionally called the City of Flowers because of its many gardens.
Peshawar is also called the City of Grain and is one of the oldest living cities in South Asia.
In which constitution of Pakistan were Islamic provisions first included?
The 1956 Constitution was the first constitution of Pakistan and made the country an Islamic Republic. It included Islamic provisions.
The Objectives Resolution of 1949 was made its preamble.
Which team won the PSL trophy two times in a row?
Lahore Qalandars won PSL 7 in 2022 and PSL 8 in 2023, back to back. No other team has won consecutive titles.
Lahore Qalandars also won in 2025, and Peshawar Zalmi won PSL 11 in 2026.
In which year did Quaid-e-Azam go into self-imposed exile in London?
After the Round Table Conferences, Jinnah was disappointed with Indian politics and settled in London around 1930. He returned in 1934.
Some sources say 1931; most Pakistani textbooks give 1930.
In which game is a free throw used?
A free throw is an unopposed shot at the basket given to a player after a foul in basketball. It is worth one point.
A basket scored from inside the three-point line in open play is worth two points.
What is the height of the Eiffel Tower in Paris, including antennas, in metres?
The Eiffel Tower is about 330 metres tall including its antenna, which is about 1,083 feet.
Sources differ slightly: the older figure of 324 m was used before antenna changes.
Who is generally regarded as the first poet of the Urdu language?
Amir Khusrow (1253-1325) is commonly taught as the first poet who used early Urdu (Hindavi) in verse.
Sources differ, and some name Wali Deccani as the first major Urdu poet.
On what date was the Wavell Plan announced?
Lord Wavell broadcast his plan on 14 June 1945. The Simla Conference to discuss it started on 25 June 1945.
The Simla Conference ended without agreement in July 1945.
In which city is the shrine of Hazrat Bahauddin Zakariya located?
The shrine of the Sufi saint Hazrat Bahauddin Zakariya is in Multan.
Multan is known as the City of Saints.
Percent of 100 is always the same number as the percent itself.
Which battle was fought in 1757 between Nawab Siraj ud Daula and the British East India Company?
The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 in Bengal, where Robert Clive defeated Siraj ud Daula.
Mir Jafar's betrayal helped the British win Plassey, and the Battle of Buxar followed in 1764.
Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan during the December 1971 war?

Who was the fifth Mughal emperor of India?

What is the square root of 900?
30 x 30 = 900, so the square root of 900 is 30.

What is the absolute value of a number?
Its distance from zero, always non-negative

The absolute value of zero is zero.

Which organization runs the world's largest volunteer ambulance service, founded by Abdul Sattar Edhi?
The Edhi Foundation, founded by Abdul Sattar Edhi in Pakistan, is recognised by Guinness World Records as having the largest volunteer ambulance service.

What is the antonym of the word mighty?
Mighty means very strong, so its opposite is weak.

What is the antonym of the word opaque?
Opaque means that light cannot pass through, so its opposite is transparent.

Choose the correct word: We are going to the beach ___ car.

Was the Constitution of Pakistan of 1956 bicameral or unicameral?
Bicameral with a National Assembly and a Senate
Unicameral with a single National Assembly

Pakistan was created on the basis of the Two-Nation Theory, and the common religion Islam binds its diverse peoples together.

What are the approximate length and breadth of Pakistan?
Pakistan stretches about 1,600 km from north to south and about 885 km from east to west at its widest.

In which years were the modern Olympic Games cancelled because of the world wars?
The 1916 Games were cancelled due to World War 1, and the 1940 and 1944 Games due to World War 2.

Hazara is the name of an ethnic group mainly found in which country?
The Hazara are a Persian-speaking ethnic group living mostly in central Afghanistan (Hazarajat).

In which district of Punjab is the main part of the Kala Chitta Range located?

On which two Japanese cities did the USA drop atomic bombs in August 1945?
The USA dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945 and another on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.
Japan announced its surrender soon after, ending World War 2.
What is the closest meaning of the word tenure?
Tenure means the period or term during which a person holds an office or position.

Which letter completes the series: L, _, N, O?
The letters are in alphabetical order, and M comes between L and N.
The alphabet has 26 letters from A to Z.
What does the Parliament of Pakistan consist of?
Under Article 50 of the 1973 Constitution, Parliament consists of the President, the National Assembly and the Senate.
The National Assembly is the lower house and the Senate is the upper house.

sin 0 = 0 and cos 90 = 0, so the product is 0 x 0 = 0.

Which constitution is currently in force in Pakistan?
The Constitution of 1973 is the current constitution of Pakistan.

Who is the current Director General of ISI (Pakistan)?
Lt Gen Muhammad Asim Malik has been DG ISI since September 2024.
He also serves as National Security Adviser; his predecessor was Nadeem Anjum.
Who is the current Prime Minister of Pakistan?
Shehbaz Sharif has been Prime Minister since March 2024.
Anwaar ul Haq Kakar was caretaker PM from August 2023 to March 2024.
Which is the lowest point on land in Asia, about 430 metres below sea level?
The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest land elevation on Earth, about 430 metres below sea level. It lies between Jordan and Israel or the West Bank.
Death Valley is the lowest point in North America, not Asia.
What type of democracy does Pakistan have under the 1973 Constitution?
The 1973 Constitution set up a federal parliamentary system. The Prime Minister heads the government and the President is the head of state.

What is the derivative of 9 with respect to x?
9 is a constant and the derivative of any constant is zero.
What is the Tour de France?
The Tour de France is an annual multi-stage men's bicycle race held mainly in France. It usually lasts about three weeks in July.
The winner wears the famous yellow jersey.
In which continent is the Cape of Good Hope located?
The Cape of Good Hope is a rocky headland on the Atlantic coast of South Africa.
Vasco da Gama rounded it in 1497 on the sea route to India.
Choose the correct word: He was good ___ math.
The correct preposition after the adjective good, when talking about a skill or subject, is at.
We also say bad at, clever at and expert at.
Who proposed the heliocentric (sun-centred) model of the solar system?
Nicolaus Copernicus proposed in 1543 that the Sun is at the centre and the planets move around it. Ptolemy and Aristotle supported an Earth-centred model.
Galileo later supported the Copernican model using telescope observations.
What is the approximate range of Pakistan's short-range ballistic missile Hatf-I?
Hatf-I is Pakistan's first short-range, solid-fuel missile with a range of about 70 km, later improved to about 100 km in the Hatf-IA version.

Justice Musarrat Hilali took oath in 2023 as the first woman Chief Justice of which high court?

Justice Tahira Safdar of the Balochistan High Court was the first woman chief justice of any high court in Pakistan (2018).
Iota is the imaginary unit and is defined as i = square root of -1, so i squared = -1.
Numbers of the form a + ib are called complex numbers.

'Much' and 'a little' are also used with uncountable nouns.
In which city was Zulfikar Ali Bhutto hanged?
Bhutto was hanged in Rawalpindi Central Jail, and he was buried at Garhi Khuda Bakhsh near Larkana.
What is the LCM of 3 and 8?
3 and 8 have no common factor, so LCM = 3 x 8 = 24.
For two numbers, LCM x HCF equals their product.
Which is the largest lake of North America by area?
Lake Superior is the largest of the Great Lakes and the largest freshwater lake in North America by surface area.
Lake Michigan is the largest Great Lake lying wholly inside the USA.

The event happened last year, so the simple past form went is correct.
A time word like last year needs a past tense verb.
What is the smallest unit of life?
The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living things.
Robert Hooke first observed and named cells in 1665.
Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan served as President (Speaker) of Pakistan's Constituent Assembly from 1948 until which year?
He held the office from 1948 until the Assembly was dissolved by Governor General Ghulam Muhammad in 1954.

What is the meaning of the word 'Hadith'?
A saying or tradition of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)

The Sunnah and Hadith are the second main source of Islamic law after the Quran.
What is the meaning of the word obscure?
Obscure means hard to understand or see, or not well known.

Which number is different from the others: 3, 5, 7, 11, 12, 13, 17, 19?
All the numbers except 12 are prime numbers. 12 is divisible by 2, 3, 4 and 6.
2 is the only even prime number.
Which scientist won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences, Physics and Chemistry?
Marie Curie won the Physics prize in 1903 (shared) and the Chemistry prize in 1911. She is the only person to win in two different sciences besides Linus Pauling, who won Chemistry and Peace.
Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.
Who wrote the folk romance Sassi Punnu in verse?
Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai told the tale of Sassui Punhun in his Shah Jo Risalo.
It is one of the seven tragic romances of Sindh.
In which city is Shalimar Bagh (Shalimar Gardens) located?
The Shalimar Gardens are in Lahore, Pakistan. They were built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan around 1641.
The Shalimar Gardens and Lahore Fort are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Sine of 270 minus theta lies in the third quadrant where sine is negative, and the function changes to cosine at 270. So the result is minus cos theta.
Sin(90 minus theta) is equal to plus cos theta.
What is the currency of Spain?
Spain uses the Euro, which replaced the peseta in 2002.
The Euro is used by 20 or more European Union countries known as the Eurozone.
Who was the Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan at the time of the 1956 Constitution?
Abdul Wahab Khan was the Speaker from 1955 and was in office when the 1956 Constitution came into force.
Tamizuddin Khan was the earlier President of the Constituent Assembly; sources differ on the numbering of the Speakers.
Which city of Pakistan is world famous for sports goods?
Sialkot is the centre of Pakistan's sports goods industry, especially footballs.
Sialkot made the footballs used in several FIFA World Cups.

Which part of Asia is called the subcontinent?
The subcontinent means South Asia, the region of Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and nearby countries.

Which symbol denotes the union of two sets?
The symbol ∪ means union, the set of all elements that are in A or in B or in both.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'console'?
To console means to give comfort to someone who is sad.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'consumer'?
A consumer is a person who buys and uses goods or services, like a customer.
The opposite of consumer in economics is producer.
When did the Gandhi-Jinnah talks take place in Bombay?
Gandhi met Quaid-e-Azam Jinnah at his house in Bombay from 9 to 27 September 1944. The talks failed because they did not agree on the Pakistan demand.
Gandhi's proposal was based on the Rajagopalachari formula.
What is Pakistan's top export product group?
Textiles and clothing make up more than half of Pakistan's total exports.
Rice is Pakistan's biggest food export.
Ernest Hemingway was a writer of which country?
Ernest Hemingway was an American novelist who wrote The Old Man and the Sea.

Which word is the opposite of zeal?
Zeal means strong enthusiasm, while apathy means lack of interest.

One hour has 60 minutes, so distance in one minute is 200 divided by 60 = 3.33 km (10/3 km).
Speed is distance divided by time.

Mian Saqib Nisar was Chief Justice of Pakistan from December 2016 until January 2019, which covers all of 2018.

A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

From the 2nd to the 27th is 25 days later. 25 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4, so move 4 day(s) forward from Friday to reach Tuesday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.
In a class of 1000 students, 850 are present. What is the percentage of absentees?
Present students are 85% of the class.

The Geneva Accords were signed on 14 April 1988 by Pakistan, Afghanistan, the USA and the USSR.

What is the antonym of the word industrious?
Industrious means hardworking, so its opposite is lazy.

Maulana Zafar Ali Khan, editor of the daily Zamindar, is most commonly given this title in Pakistani textbooks.

To avoid coming to the main point

Japan attacked Pearl Harbor in December 1941

The mode is the value that is repeated the most times in the data.

Lahore Qalandars won the PSL in 2022 and again in 2023.

March has 31 days and December has 31 days. So 31 + 31 = 62.

Pakistan came into being in 1947 and East Pakistan separated in December 1971, which is 24 years later.

Haemoglobin contains iron, and the iron binds oxygen in the red blood cells. Lack of iron causes anaemia.

Which Egyptian footballer is famous as Mo Salah?
Mohamed Salah is the well known Egyptian forward who plays for Liverpool and is nicknamed the Egyptian King.

Tipu Sultan fought the Anglo-Mysore wars against the British East India Company and was martyred defending Seringapatam in 1799.

The 1956 Constitution made Pakistan an Islamic Republic with a federal, parliamentary system and a single-house legislature.

Where was the United Nations founded in 1945?

The Strait of Gibraltar is a narrow channel between Spain and Morocco that joins the Mediterranean Sea to the Atlantic Ocean.

Who is the Federal Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination of Pakistan (health minister) as of 2026?

What is the capital of Hungary?

Peshawar, at the entrance of the Khyber Pass

It is often described as the oldest mosque in northern Pakistan, near Raja Gira Castle.
In which year was the Nishan-e-Haider awarded to Major Aziz Bhatti?
Major Aziz Bhatti was martyred in the 1965 war near the BRB canal at Lahore and was honoured with the Nishan-e-Haider for it that year.
He is one of the recipients of Pakistan's highest military award for gallantry.
Who was the first Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan in 1958?
Martial law was imposed on 7 October 1958 by President Iskander Mirza, who made General Ayub Khan the Chief Martial Law Administrator.
Ayub Khan became Pakistan's first Field Marshal in 1959.
What is the geometric mean of 4 and 16?
GM = square root of (4 x 16) = square root of 64 = 8.
For positive numbers, GM is never greater than the arithmetic mean.
How many member countries does SAARC have?
SAARC has eight members: Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan.
Afghanistan joined as the eighth member in 2007.
What is the mode of the numbers 3, 3, 4, 5, 6?
The mode is the value that appears most often. The number 3 appears twice and all others appear once.
The median of this set is 4.
To which age do the people of the Indus Valley Civilization belong?
The Indus Valley people used copper and bronze tools, so the civilization belongs to the Bronze Age.
The civilization is also called the Harappan Civilization.
For what were the people of Mohenjo-daro and Harappa famous?
Well-planned cities with a drainage system
Their cities had straight streets, brick houses and covered drains. This shows advanced town planning.
The Great Bath is a famous building of Mohenjo-daro.
If the first day of a month is Monday, what day will the 21st day be?
The 21st is 20 days after the 1st. 20 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6, and Monday plus 6 days is Sunday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days.
Suo motu notice by the Supreme Court of Pakistan is taken under which article of the Constitution?
Article 184(3) gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction on matters of public importance involving fundamental rights.
Suo motu is a Latin term meaning on its own motion.
On which date was NATO founded?
The North Atlantic Treaty was signed in Washington on 4 April 1949.
The Warsaw Pact was formed in 1955 as the Soviet response to NATO.
In 1999 General Pervez Musharraf replaced Nawaz Sharif and became what?
After the coup of 12 October 1999 Musharraf took the title Chief Executive.
Which was the first battle of the Muslims against a non-Arab power?
The Battle of Muta in 8 AH (629 CE) was fought against the Byzantine (Roman) army, a non-Arab power.
Zaid bin Haritha was the first commander of the Muslim army at Muta.
Which word is a synonym of obvious?
Obvious means easy to see or understand, which is the same as evident.
Other synonyms are clear, plain and apparent.
In which year did the Third Battle of Panipat take place?
The Third Battle of Panipat was fought in 1761 between the Marathas and the Afghan ruler Ahmad Shah Abdali.
Ahmad Shah Abdali won the battle, which ended Maratha power in North India.
About what percent of the total area of Pakistan is covered by Balochistan?
Balochistan has about 347,190 square km out of about 796,095 square km, which is about 43.6 percent.
Balochistan is the largest province by area but the smallest by population share.
What is the value of 3P2 (permutation of 3 things taken 2 at a time)?
Permutations count ordered arrangements, so order matters.
In which type of cricket match is the pink ball used?
Only one-day matches played in the morning
The pink ball is easier to see under floodlights, so it is used in day-night Test matches.
The first day-night Test was played in Adelaide in 2015 between Australia and New Zealand.
On which date was the first cricket World Cup played (started)?
The first Cricket World Cup, the Prudential Cup, began on 7 June 1975 in England.
West Indies won the first World Cup, beating Australia in the final at Lord's.
What is the capital of Poland?
Warsaw is the capital and largest city of Poland. It lies on the Vistula river.
Krakow was the capital of Poland until the late 16th century.
Which building is shown on the back of the Pakistani 5000 rupee note?
The State Bank of Pakistan states that the reverse of the Rs 5000 note carries a picture of Faisal Mosque, Islamabad.
The portrait of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah is on the front of all Pakistani banknotes.
Under which article of the 1973 Constitution is the definition of a Muslim and non-Muslim given, as added by the Second Amendment?
The Second Amendment added clause 3 to Article 260 and defined who is a Muslim. Qadianis were thus declared non-Muslim.
Article 2 declares Islam the State religion.
In which year was the Radcliffe Award announced?
The Radcliffe Boundary Commission award was announced on 17 August 1947, after independence. It fixed the Punjab and Bengal boundaries.
Sir Cyril Radcliffe headed the commission.
Who received the first Nobel Prize in Physics, awarded in 1901?
The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in 1901, and the Physics prize went to Wilhelm Rontgen for discovering X-rays.
Marie Curie won the Physics prize in 1903 and was the first woman Nobel winner.
In which province is the Rekodiq mining project (copper and gold) located?
Rekodiq is a copper-gold deposit in Chagai district of Balochistan.
Saindak and Reko Diq are both in Chagai district.
For what work did Dr Abdus Salam win the Nobel Prize?
Unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces
Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for the electroweak unification theory.
He was the first Pakistani Nobel laureate.
Which phrase does the Quran use for the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as a mercy for all?
Surah Al-Anbiya says the Prophet was sent as Rahmatul lil Alamin, a mercy for all the worlds.
Khatam-un-Nabiyyin means Seal of the Prophets.
What is the gap in years between the first (1956) and second (1962) constitution of Pakistan?
The first constitution came into force in March 1956 and the second in June 1962. 1962 minus 1956 is 6 years.
The 1973 Constitution is the third and current constitution of Pakistan.
Which letter is used to denote the set of rational numbers?
Rational numbers are written as quotients (fractions) of integers, so the set is denoted by Q.
N is natural numbers, Z is integers and R is real numbers.
What is the domain of the function sin x?
Sine is defined for every real value of x. Its range, not its domain, is from minus 1 to 1.
The period of sin x is 360 degrees (2 pi).
What is the determinant of a singular matrix?
A square matrix is called singular exactly when its determinant is zero. Such a matrix has no inverse.
A matrix with non-zero determinant is called non-singular and has an inverse.
If the sum of two angles of a triangle is 90 degrees, what is the third angle?
The three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees. So the third angle is 180 - 90 = 90 degrees.
A triangle with one 90 degree angle is called a right-angled triangle.
Ship is to captain as car is to what?
A captain is the person who controls a ship. In the same way a driver controls a car.
How many countries are there in South Asia (the SAARC region)?
South Asia has eight countries: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
Afghanistan joined SAARC in 2007 as its eighth member.
Spain is located in which continent?
Spain lies in the south-west of Europe on the Iberian Peninsula.
Spain and Portugal share the Iberian Peninsula.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'strength'?
Strength means the quality of being strong, which is the same as power or force.
The opposite (antonym) of strength is weakness.
What is the sum of 2 and 8?
Addition is commutative, so 2 + 8 gives the same answer as 8 + 2.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'momentary'?
Momentary means lasting only a very short time, which is the same as brief.
The opposite (antonym) of momentary is permanent.
Which word is closest in meaning to 'fragile'?
Fragile means easily broken, which is the same as delicate.
Glass is a common example of a fragile material.
In which district and province is the Tanda Dam located?
Tanda Dam is a small dam built near Kohat in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It supplies drinking and irrigation water.
Kohat is also known for its tunnel, the Kohat Pass and its cantonment.
In which district of Punjab is Tandlianwala located?
Tandlianwala is a city and tehsil in Faisalabad district of Punjab.
Tarbela Dam construction began in 1968 during whose rule?
Work on Tarbela Dam started in 1968 when Field Marshal Ayub Khan was President. It followed the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960.
The dam was completed in 1976 during the time of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
Fill in the blank: He is too weak ___ walk.
The pattern is too + adjective + to + verb, so the correct word is to.
The sentence means that he is so weak that he cannot walk.
Which PSL team won the title in two consecutive seasons, 2022 and 2023?
Lahore Qalandars won the PSL final in 2022 and again in 2023, the only back-to-back titles in PSL history.
Peshawar Zalmi are the champions of the 2026 season; Lahore also won in 2025.
Which tribe of Pashtuns did Sher Shah Suri belong to?
Sher Shah Suri belonged to the Sur tribe of the Pashtuns, which is why he is called Suri.
His birth name was Farid Khan.
Sher Shah Suri belonged to which ethnic group?
Sher Shah Suri was a Pashtun (Afghan) from the Sur tribe.
He defeated the Mughal emperor Humayun and ruled India from 1540 to 1545.
Who was the leader of the hypocrites (Munafiqeen) in the Battle of Uhud?
Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul withdrew with about 300 men before the battle began.
This left the Muslims with about 700 men.
What does the expression Bird's Eye View mean?
A view from a high point looking down
A bird's eye view means a wide view from high above, as a bird would see it.
The phrase is also used for a general overview of a subject.
Which famous book was written by the Punjabi poet Waris Shah?
Waris Shah wrote the Punjabi romantic epic Heer (Heer Ranjha) around 1766.
Saif-ul-Malook was written by Mian Muhammad Bakhsh.
On what date did Pakistan win the Cricket World Cup final in 1992?
Pakistan beat England in the final at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on 25 March 1992 under Imran Khan.
It is Pakistan's only ODI World Cup title.
Fill in the blank: He writes ____ blue ink.
We say write in ink, writing in blue ink, when the colour of the writing is meant. With is also used for the pen, but in is the standard choice here.
We say write with a pen but write in ink.
Who wrote the book Pakistan: The Formative Phase?
Pakistan: The Formative Phase was written by the political scientist Khalid B. Sayeed.
The book covers the early years of Pakistan from 1857 to 1948.
A number divided by itself equals 1.
Zero divided by any non-zero number is 0.
9/2 is an improper fraction, equal to 4 1/2.
A train covers 20 km in 100 minutes. How long will it take to cover 1 km?
100 minutes divided by 20 km gives 5 minutes for each km.
At this pace the train's speed is 12 km per hour.
103, 104, 105 and 106 are consecutive numbers, but 116 does not fit in the sequence.
Today is Monday and it is the 12th day of the month. What day will the 10th of the same month be?
The 10th is 2 days before the 12th. Two days before Monday is Saturday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days.

In alternating series, look at odd and even positions separately.

If the 3rd day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 12th of that month?
12 - 3 = 9 days later. 9 = 7 + 2, so move 2 days forward from Sunday, which is Tuesday.
Only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.
If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 13th of that month?
13 - 1 = 12 days later. 12 = 7 + 5, so move 5 days forward from Sunday, which is Friday.
Sunday plus 5 days: Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri.
If the 24th date of a month is Friday, what day is the 14th of that month?
24 - 14 = 10 days earlier. 10 = 7 + 3, so go back 3 days from Friday: Thursday, Wednesday, Tuesday.
Going back 3 days equals going forward 4 days in a week.
If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day is the 14th of that month?
14 - 4 = 10 days later. 10 = 7 + 3, so move 3 days forward from Friday: Saturday, Sunday, Monday.
The 11th and 18th would also be Monday if the 4th is Friday.

483 is missing from the list but the 111 pattern still holds.
Which reforms were introduced in British India in 1919?
The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms were enacted as the Government of India Act 1919 and introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
The Morley-Minto Reforms were earlier, in 1909.
Who launched the Quit Kashmir Movement in 1946 against the Dogra Maharaja?
Sheikh Abdullah and his National Conference launched the Quit Kashmir Movement in May 1946 against Maharaja Hari Singh.
He was arrested soon after the movement began.
Which constitution of Pakistan was made in 1956?
The Constituent Assembly passed the first constitution of Pakistan in 1956, which made the country an Islamic Republic.
It was abrogated by President Iskander Mirza in October 1958.
What was the first amendment to the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan about?
Recognition of Bangladesh by changing the definition of the territories of Pakistan
Allowing the President to dissolve the Assembly
Changing the name of the country
The First Amendment of 1974 changed Article 1 so that the territories of Pakistan no longer included East Pakistan, after Bangladesh was recognized.
The Second Amendment of 1974 declared Ahmadis non-Muslims for the purposes of the Constitution.
Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan during the 1999 Kargil conflict?
Nawaz Sharif was Prime Minister from 1997 until October 1999, so he was in office during the Kargil conflict.
General Pervez Musharraf removed him in a coup on 12 October 1999.
On which date was the first Cricket World Cup final played in 1975?
The first Cricket World Cup was played in England in June 1975 and its final was held at Lord's on 21 June 1975.
West Indies won that final by beating Australia.
A plane uses 60 gallons of fuel to cover 90 km. How many gallons are needed to cover 200 km?
Fuel per km is 60/90 = 2/3 gallon. For 200 km: 200 x 2/3 = 133.33 gallons.
Fuel needed is directly proportional to the distance covered.
Who won the 2014 ICC World Twenty20 (T20 World Cup)?
Sri Lanka beat India by six wickets in the final at Dhaka in April 2014.
Pakistan's only T20 World Cup win was in 2009.
Who won the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup?
Australia beat hosts India by six wickets in the final at Ahmedabad on 19 November 2023.
It was Australia's sixth World Cup title.

By BODMAS, multiplication comes first: 2 x 3 = 6. Then 2 + 6 = 8.
Brackets, orders, division and multiplication, then addition and subtraction is the correct order of operations.
If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 19th of that month be?
From the 2nd to the 19th is 17 days later. 17 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3, so move 3 day(s) forward from Monday to reach Thursday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.
If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 20th of that month be?
From the 4th to the 20th is 16 days later. 16 divided by 7 leaves remainder 2, so move 2 day(s) forward from Monday to reach Wednesday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.
If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 20th of that month be?
From the 2nd to the 20th is 18 days later. 18 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4, so move 4 day(s) forward from Friday to reach Tuesday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.
If the 31st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 25th of that month be?
From the 31st to the 25th is 6 days earlier. 6 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6, so move 6 day(s) backward from Monday to reach Tuesday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.
If the 12th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 29th of that month be?
From the 12th to the 29th is 17 days later. 17 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3, so move 3 day(s) forward from Monday to reach Thursday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.
If the 31st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 20th of that month be?
From the 31st to the 20th is 11 days earlier. 11 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4, so move 4 day(s) backward from Monday to reach Thursday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.
If the 31st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 2nd of that month be?
From the 31st to the 2nd is 29 days earlier. 29 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so move 1 day(s) backward from Monday to reach Sunday.
A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.
In a class of 450 students, 350 are male. What is the percentage of females?
The male percentage in this class is 350 / 450 x 100 = 77.78%.
In a class of 500 students, 350 were present. What is the percentage of absent students?
Present students are 70% of the class.
Out of 4500 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students (to two decimal places)?
Present students are only 340 / 4500 x 100 = 7.56% of the total.
Out of 4500 students, 3400 are present. What is the percentage of absent students (to two decimal places)?
If 260 out of 500 students are present, what is the percentage of absent students?
Present students are 52% of the total.
A class has 600 students and 420 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
Present students are 70% of the class.
In a school 500 students study and 320 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
Present students are 64% of the total.

The 3rd June Plan, which announced the partition of British India, was announced in which year?
Lord Mountbatten announced the plan on 3 June 1947. It decided the partition of India into India and Pakistan.
It is also called the Mountbatten Plan, and India Independence Act followed in July 1947.
Who was the third wife of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), in order of marriage?
In order of marriage the wives were Khadija, Sawda, then Aisha (RA). So Aisha (RA) was the third.
Hazrat Aisha (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA); sources may differ on later order.
If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 14th day be?
From the 4th to the 14th is 10 days. 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Monday + 3 days = Thursday.
Dates that differ by 7 fall on the same weekday.
If the 15th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 4th of that month?
From the 4th to the 15th is 11 days. 11 divided by 7 leaves 4, so Monday - 4 days = Thursday.
Going back 4 days is the same as going forward 3 days in a week.
If the 5th day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 18th of the month?
From the 5th to the 18th is 13 days. 13 divided by 7 leaves 6, so Sunday + 6 days = Saturday.
The 12th of this month would be Sunday too.
If the 9th of a month is Sunday, what day is the 26th of the month?
From the 9th to the 26th is 17 days. 17 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Sunday + 3 days = Wednesday.
The 23rd of this month would be Sunday.
What is the abscissa of a point also called?
The abscissa is the horizontal distance of a point, which is its x-coordinate.
The y-coordinate is called the ordinate.
Where did Maulana Syed Abul Ala Maududi die?
Maududi died in Buffalo, New York, USA, on 22 September 1979 while seeking medical treatment.
He founded Jamaat-e-Islami in 1941 and was buried in Lahore.
If the force on an object is doubled while its mass stays the same, what happens to its acceleration?
By Newton's second law, F = ma, so a = F / m. Acceleration is directly proportional to force when mass is fixed.
If the mass is doubled instead, the acceleration halves.
Acceleration is how fast the velocity of an object changes with time, a = change in velocity / time.
The SI unit of acceleration is metre per second squared.
What is the additive identity of 5?
The additive identity is the number which leaves a number unchanged when added. 5 + 0 = 5.
What is the additive inverse of 65?
The additive inverse is the number which gives zero when added. 65 + (-65) = 0.
On which date was the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan adopted by the National Assembly?
The National Assembly adopted the Constitution on 10 April 1973. It was enforced later, on 14 August 1973.
The Constitution was framed under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

'Bravely' tells how he fought, so it modifies a verb. Words that modify verbs and end in -ly like this are adverbs.
The adjective form of this word is 'brave'.
What type of adverb is the word 'often'?
'Often' tells how many times something happens. Adverbs that answer 'how often' are adverbs of frequency.
Other adverbs of frequency are always, never, sometimes and rarely.

Ahmad is 3 x 4 = 12 years old now. After 10 years he will be 12 + 10 = 22 years old.
Age problems are solved by first finding the present age, then adding the years.

Double of 4 is 2 x 4 = 8, so the sister is 8 years old.

Akbar is older than both Ahmed and Bilal, so he is the oldest.
Comparison questions are easiest with a line of names from oldest to youngest.
Which airline belongs to Italy and is its national flag carrier since 2021?
ITA Airways is the national airline of Italy. It took over from Alitalia in October 2021.
Alitalia was the former national airline of Italy.
Which is the intelligence agency of Israel?
Mossad is the national intelligence agency of Israel, responsible for foreign intelligence.
RAW is the foreign intelligence agency of India and ISI is that of Pakistan.
Abul Ala Maududi, the founder of Jamaat-e-Islami, was born in which city?
Maududi was born in 1903 in Aurangabad in the Deccan, British India.

In which year did Abul Ala Maududi die?
Maududi died in 1979 in Buffalo, USA, and was buried in Lahore.
In which country is the city of Allahabad (now Prayagraj) located?
Allahabad is in the state of Uttar Pradesh in India. Its name was changed to Prayagraj in 2018.
Allama Iqbal gave his famous address at the Muslim League session held here in 1930.
Allama Iqbal did his graduation (BA) from which college?
Iqbal passed his BA in 1897 from Government College Lahore, and later his MA there in 1899.
He later got a PhD from Munich in Germany.

Altaf Hussain Hali was a famous poet of which language?
Altaf Hussain Hali (1837-1914) was a well-known Urdu poet and critic.
His long poem Musaddas-e-Hali is famous in Urdu literature.
Ali is older than Hammad but younger than Amir. Hammad is younger than Amir. Who is the youngest of the three?
Amir is older than Ali, and Ali is older than Hammad. So the order from oldest is Amir, Ali, Hammad, and Hammad is the youngest.

Muhammad Amir is a famous fast bowler of which country?
Muhammad Amir is a left-arm fast bowler who plays cricket for Pakistan.

The British East India Company, under General Charles Napier, defeated the Talpur Mirs at Miani in 1843 and annexed Sindh.
Sindh was made part of the Bombay Presidency and separated from it in 1936.
From which ruling family did the British annex Sindh in 1843?
The Talpur Mirs ruled Sindh when Charles Napier defeated them in the Battle of Miani in 1843.
The Talpurs had replaced the Kalhoras in the 1780s.
What is the antonym of the word intricate?
Intricate means very complicated, so its opposite is simple.
Complicated is a synonym of intricate.
What is the antonym of the word solitude?
Solitude means being alone, so its opposite is company.
Solitude is a noun meaning the state of being alone.
What is the antonym of the word elegant?
Elegant means graceful and stylish, so its opposite is clumsy or awkward.
Graceful is a synonym of elegant.
What is the antonym of the word generous?
Generous means ready to give freely, so its opposite is stingy.
Miserly is another opposite of generous.
What is the antonym of the word pleasant?
Pleasant means enjoyable, so its opposite is unpleasant.
Disagreeable is a synonym of unpleasant.
What is the antonym of the word terrible?
Terrible means very bad, so its opposite is wonderful or excellent.
Awful is a synonym of terrible.
What is the antonym of the word vicious?
Vicious means cruel and violent, so its opposite is gentle.
Civilized and kind are also opposites in some tests.
What is the antonym of the word wide?
Wide means large from side to side, so its opposite is narrow.
Broad is a synonym of wide.
What is another name of Tipu Sultan, the ruler of Mysore?
Tipu Sultan was known as the Tiger of Mysore because of his bravery against the British.
He was killed in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War at Seringapatam in 1799.
What was the old name of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia before 1932?
Abdulaziz Ibn Saud ruled the Kingdom of Hejaz and Najd, which was renamed Saudi Arabia in September 1932.
Saudi Arabia is named after the House of Saud.
Argentina is located in which continent?
Argentina lies in the southern part of South America. It shares borders with Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay, Brazil and Uruguay.

The Global Firepower index ranks the USA first because of its budget, technology, air power and navy. Russia and China follow.

What percentage of Pakistan's total area does Balochistan, the largest province, cover?

The Spanish expedition that Ferdinand Magellan led was the first to sail around the Earth. Magellan was killed in the Philippines in 1521 and Juan Sebastian Elcano completed the voyage.
Vasco da Gama found the sea route from Europe to India in 1498.
What was the name of the dog that stayed with the Companions of the Cave (Ashab-e-Kahf)?
Muslim tradition names the dog of the Ashab-e-Kahf as Qitmir (Kitmir). The dog is mentioned in Surah Al-Kahf of the Quran, though its name is given in commentaries.

Akbar is older than Ahmad and Aslam. Ahmad is younger than Aslam. Which statement is true?

Average is the sum of the values divided by how many values there are.
What is the average of 30 and 42?
For two numbers the average is exactly halfway between them.

Sir Donald Bradman of Australia scored 6,996 runs at an average of 99.94 in Tests. No other player is close to this average.

Who was the first Pakistani to win a Nobel Prize, and in which field?
