The preposition towards shows the direction of movement, so 'He walked towards school' is correct.
The preposition to is also used with walk, as in 'walked to school'.
In which years did the two World Wars take place?
World War I was fought from 1914 to 1918 and World War II from 1939 to 1945.
World War II began with the German invasion of Poland in September 1939.
Change into passive voice: She said to me that she was watching TV.
I was told by her that she was watching TV.
I told her that she was watching TV.
She was told by me that she was watching TV.
TV was being watched by her to me.
In the passive form the object (me) becomes the subject, and said to becomes was told by. The reported clause stays the same.
The verb tell is used in the passive instead of say for reported speech.
A plan to reconstitute the Viceroy's Executive Council with equal Hindu and Muslim representation
A plan to partition India into two states
A plan to give India dominion status immediately
A plan to hold elections for a Constituent Assembly
Wavell proposed an Executive Council in which all members except the Viceroy and Commander-in-Chief were Indians, with parity between caste Hindus and Muslims.
The plan failed because Congress and the Muslim League disagreed over who could nominate Muslim members.
Choose the correct word: She is ___ weak in maths.
The adverb very is used before an adjective such as weak to give strength. Much, many and more do not fit here.
Very is an adverb of degree.
Which symbol is used for the set of whole numbers?
The set of whole numbers (0, 1, 2, 3, ...) is written W.
N is for natural numbers, Z for integers and Q for rational numbers.
What is the synonym of the word widely?
Widely means over a large area or among many people, which is the same as extensively.
Narrowly is the opposite of widely.
What is the area of a rectangle with length 5 and width 4?
Area of a rectangle is length times width, so 5 x 4 = 20 square units.
The perimeter of this rectangle would be 2 x (5 + 4) = 18 units.
What is the synonym of the word wildly?
Wildly means in an uncontrolled or fierce way, which is close to violently.
What is the antonym of the word wildly?
Wildly means in an uncontrolled way, so the opposite is calmly.
If 1 man writes 5 pages in 5 minutes, how many pages will 5 men write in 25 minutes?
One man writes 1 page per minute. So 5 men write 5 pages per minute, and in 25 minutes they write 5 x 25 = 125 pages.
Work problems are solved by first finding the rate of one worker.
If yesterday was Sunday, what day is it today?
The day after Sunday is Monday.
Monday is the first working day after the weekend in many countries.
What is the chemical symbol of zinc?
The symbol of zinc is Zn.
Zinc is used to galvanise iron to prevent rusting.
BODMAS says division comes before addition.
BODMAS says division comes before addition.
What is 3x + 3y written in factor form?
Both terms have the common factor 3, so 3x + 3y = 3(x + y).
Taking out a common factor is called factorisation.
10% of 70 is 7, so 60% is 42 and 5% is 3.5.
10% of 80 is 8, so 70% is 56 and 2% is 1.6.
8 x 8 = 64, and two zeros are added, giving 6400.
9 x 9 = 81, and two zeros are added, giving 8100.
KG is the short form of kilogram, the SI unit of mass.
What is the H.C.F of 4 and 16?
Factors of 4 are 1, 2, 4. All of these divide 16, so the highest common factor is 4.
If one number divides the other, it is the HCF.
What was the Islamic date of the independence of Pakistan (14 August 1947)?
14 August 1947 fell on 27 Ramadan 1366 AH, the blessed night of Laylat ul Qadr as commonly believed.
Because of this date, Pakistan is often called a gift of the holy month of Ramadan.
Arrange the letters of PLOEADR to make the name of an animal.
The letters P, L, O, E, A, D, R make the word LEOPARD, a big cat. It uses all seven letters once.
The leopard is a spotted big cat found in Asia and Africa.
On what date did the Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) receive royal assent?
The Act got royal assent on 23 December 1919 and the reforms started in 1921. They introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
The 20 August 1917 date is Montagu's announcement in the House of Commons.
What is the value of 3 factorial (3!)?
In which province of Pakistan is the ancient site of Kot Diji located?
Kot Diji is in Khairpur district of Sindh, near the Indus River. Its fort and Indus Valley site are well known.
The Kot Diji culture is an early phase of the Indus Valley civilization, before Mohenjo-daro.
Qantas is the national airline of which country?
Qantas is the flag carrier of Australia. The name comes from Queensland and Northern Territory Aerial Services.
According to grammar, what part of speech is the word 'between'?
'Between' shows the relation of a noun or pronoun to another word, as in 'between the two trees'. A word that does this is a preposition.
'Between' is normally used for two things, while 'among' is used for more than two.
Who is the author of the book India, My Love?
India, My Love is a book by the French author Dominique Lapierre about his travels in India. The French title is India Mon Amour.
Lapierre also wrote City of Joy and, with Larry Collins, Freedom at Midnight; a different book called India My Love: A Spiritual Journey also exists.
What is the commonly stated range of Pakistan's Nasr (Hatf-IX) short-range ballistic missile?
Nasr is a short-range, nuclear-capable missile with a reported range of 60 to 70 km, with the upgraded version given as 70 km. It is meant as a battlefield weapon.
Early reports gave 60 km, so sources differ depending on the variant.
Which planet is called the sister planet of the Earth because of its similar size?
Venus is almost the same size and mass as Earth, so it is called Earth's sister.
Venus is the hottest planet of the solar system.
A car is used for what purpose?
A car is a road vehicle used to travel from one place to another.
The first practical petrol car was built by Karl Benz in 1885.
About how many litres of blood does an average adult human body contain?
An average adult has about 5 litres of blood, which is roughly 7 to 8 percent of body weight.
Blood is pumped around the body by the heart.
Which ancient city is regarded as the centre of Buddhist learning in Pakistan?
Taxila, in the Gandhara region near Rawalpindi, was a famous centre of Buddhist learning and art.
Taxila was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.
Hawaii is a state of the USA. What is its capital?
The capital of Hawaii is Honolulu, on the island of Oahu.
Hawaii became the 50th US state in 1959.
In which year did the first All Pakistan Educational Conference take place in Karachi?
The conference was held in Karachi from 27 November to 1 December 1947, just after independence. It was opened by Quaid-e-Azam's message on education policy.
Its date is the 27th of November 1947 as the start of the conference.
Mahatma Gandhi was the leader of which political party?
Gandhi led the Indian National Congress in the freedom movement against British rule. He led campaigns such as Non-Cooperation and Civil Disobedience.
Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah led the All India Muslim League.
What is the average life span of a red blood cell in the human body?
Red blood cells live for about 120 days and are then broken down in the spleen and liver.
Red blood cells are made in the bone marrow.
Approximately how many litres of blood does an average adult human body contain?
An average adult has roughly 4.5 to 5.5 litres of blood, usually given as about 5 litres. This is around 7 percent of body weight.
Women usually have slightly less blood volume than men.
The famous Leaning Tower of Pisa is located in which country?
The Leaning Tower stands in the city of Pisa in Tuscany, Italy.
It is the bell tower of Pisa Cathedral and its construction started in 1173.
Which British commander defeated Tipu Sultan in the Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-92)?
Lord Cornwallis led the British forces and Tipu had to sign the Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792.
Tipu Sultan was finally killed in 1799 in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War, when Lord Wellesley was Governor-General.
If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, which day will the 17th be?
From the 3rd to the 17th is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. So the 17th is also a Monday.
A gap that is a multiple of 7 days gives the same weekday.
The 24th of January is celebrated as the day of what?
The UN General Assembly declared 24 January the International Day of Education in 2018.
The day highlights the role of education in peace and development.
A helicopter needs 50 gallons of fuel to cover 320 km. How many gallons does it need to cover 700 km?
Fuel per km = 50/320 = 0.15625 gallons. For 700 km: 0.15625 x 700 = 109.375, about 109.4 gallons.
Fuel used is directly proportional to the distance covered.
What part of speech is the word 'against' in the sentence 'He leaned against the wall'?
'Against' shows the relation between 'leaned' and 'the wall', so it is a preposition.
A preposition is normally followed by a noun or pronoun.
What part of speech is the word 'eat' in the sentence 'Children eat fruit'?
'Eat' names an action, so it is a verb.
A verb expresses an action, a state or an occurrence.
Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi is a famous Pakistani player of which sport?
Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi is Pakistan's best-known tennis player, famous for doubles.
He reached the US Open men's doubles final in 2010 with Rohan Bopanna.
How did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah respond to the Nehru Report of 1928?
He rejected it and later presented his Fourteen Points
He asked the British to enforce it
He ignored it and left politics
The Nehru Report did not protect Muslim rights such as separate electorates, so Jinnah rejected it. In 1929 he gave his Fourteen Points as the Muslim demands.
Jinnah's earlier Delhi Muslim Proposals of 1927 had been turned down by the Congress.
What is the logarithm of unity (1) to any base?
Any base raised to the power 0 gives 1, so log of 1 to any base is 0.
The logarithm of a negative number is not defined in real numbers.
Peshawar is associated with which ancient civilisation?
Peshawar, once called Purushapura, was a capital of the Gandhara civilisation in Kushan times. Gandhara art blended Greek and Buddhist styles.
Taxila was another important Gandhara city.
The Principal has accepted my application.
The Principal have accepted my application.
The Principal has accept my application.
Principal is singular, so it takes has, and the present perfect needs the past participle accepted.
Principal means head of a school, while principle means a rule.
What is the date of birth of Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar?
Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar was born on 10 December 1878 in Rampur, India.
He edited the newspapers Comrade and Hamdard and was a leader of the Khilafat Movement.
Which disease is caused by the bite of an infected dog?
Rabies is a viral disease passed to humans through the saliva of an infected animal, usually a dog.
Rabies can be prevented by vaccination given soon after a bite.
On which date is World Hepatitis Day observed every year?
World Hepatitis Day is observed on 28 July, the birthday of Dr Baruch Blumberg who discovered the hepatitis B virus.
World Health Day is on 7 April and World AIDS Day is on 1 December.
Under the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan, the office of Governor General was replaced by which office?
The Constitution of 1956 made Pakistan a republic, so the post of Governor General was replaced by the President.
Iskander Mirza, the last Governor General, became the first President of Pakistan in 1956.
Fill in the blank: She sits ___ the tree.
The preposition under shows she is below the tree, which gives a meaningful sentence.
Under is a preposition of place, like above, beside and near.
Which comes next in the series: 1Z, 3X, 5V, ?
Numbers go up by 2 (1, 3, 5, 7) and letters go back by 2 (Z, X, V, T). So the next term is 7T.
Z is the 26th letter and T is the 20th.
Numerators increase by 3, 4, 5, 6 (3, 6, 10, 15, 21). Denominators double (2, 4, 8, 16, 32). So the next term is 21/32.
What is the total number of members of the UN Security Council?
There are 5 permanent members and 10 non-permanent members, so 5 + 10 = 15.
Non-permanent members are elected for two years.
Choose the correct verb: My mother ___ at the hospital.
The subject my mother is third person singular, so the simple present verb takes -s: works.
In simple present tense, he, she and it take a verb ending in -s or -es.
What is iota (i) in mathematics called, and what is its value?
The imaginary unit, equal to the square root of -1
Iota i is the imaginary unit defined by i squared = -1, so i is the square root of -1.
Powers of i repeat in a cycle of four: i, -1, -i, 1.
Change into passive voice: The pilot landed the aeroplane safely.
The aeroplane was landed safely by the pilot.
The aeroplane is landed safely by the pilot.
The aeroplane has been landed safely by the pilot.
The pilot was landed safely by the aeroplane.
The sentence is in simple past tense, so the passive uses was plus the past participle: the object becomes the subject.
Passive voice is formed as: object + form of be + past participle + by + subject.
How many centimetres are there in one inch?
By international definition, one inch is exactly 2.54 centimetres.
One foot is 12 inches, which is about 30.48 centimetres.
PEMRA is the regulatory authority for which type of media in Pakistan?
PEMRA is the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority. It regulates and licenses television and radio channels.
If one person writes one page in one minute, how many pages will 5 persons write in 5 minutes?
One person writes 1 page per minute. 5 persons write 5 pages per minute, so in 5 minutes they write 25 pages.
Rate times people times time gives the total work.
According to the 2023 digital census, what is the population of Pakistan (approximately)?
The 2023 census, approved by the CCI, recorded 241.49 million people.
What is the value of 1 raised to any power n?
1 multiplied by itself any number of times is always 1.
Any non-zero number raised to power zero is also 1.
If the diameter of a circle is 35, what is its radius?
Radius is half of the diameter, so 35 divided by 2 = 17.5.
The diameter is twice the radius and the longest chord of a circle.
When did the United Nations General Assembly adopt the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
The General Assembly adopted the Declaration in Paris on 10 December 1948.
10 December is celebrated every year as Human Rights Day.
What is the common short form (abbreviation) of Saudi Arabia?
Saudi Arabia is officially the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, so its short form is KSA.
SAR is the code for the Saudi riyal, the currency of Saudi Arabia.
What is the value of cosec x multiplied by sin x?
Cosec x is 1 divided by sin x, so cosec x times sin x equals 1 over sin x times sin x, which is 1.
Similarly sec x times cos x is 1 and cot x times tan x is 1.
Which place in Pakistan is famous for making small arms (weapons) in home industry?
Darra Adam Khel, south of Peshawar in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, is well known for its local small arms workshops.
Sialkot is instead famous for sports goods and surgical instruments.
Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'affection'?
The Victoria Cross is the highest military award of which country?
The Victoria Cross is the highest British award for bravery in the face of the enemy. It was created by Queen Victoria in 1856.
The highest American military award is the Medal of Honor.
What is the meaning of the word wild?
Untamed or living in a natural state
Wild describes animals or plants living in their natural state, not tamed or cultivated.
The opposite of wild is tame or domestic.
Who wrote the book Kitab ul Umm?
Kitab ul Umm is a major work of fiqh written by Imam Muhammad bin Idris al-Shafi'i.
Imam Malik wrote Al-Muwatta and Imam Ahmad compiled the Musnad.
Percent means per hundred, so any percent of 100 equals the same number.
The population of a town in the year 2000 is 1600 and it doubles every 5 years. What was the population in 1980?
From 1980 to 2000 is 20 years, which is 4 doublings. So the 1980 population = 1600 / 2 / 2 / 2 / 2 = 100.
Going back in time with doubling means halving at each step.
If the 14th day of a month is Monday, which day will the 24th be?
From the 14th to the 24th is 10 days. 10 = 7 + 3, so move 3 days ahead of Monday: Thursday.
Divide the gap by 7 and move forward by the remainder.
If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, which day will the 24th be?
From the 4th to the 24th is 20 days. 20 = 14 + 6, so move 6 days ahead of Sunday: Saturday.
Moving 6 days ahead is the same as moving 1 day back.
If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, which day will the 28th be?
From the 2nd to the 28th is 26 days. 26 = 21 + 5, so move 5 days ahead of Monday: Saturday.
If the 16th day of a month is Sunday, which day is the 5th of the same month?
From the 5th to the 16th is 11 days. 11 = 7 + 4, so the 5th is 4 days before Sunday: Saturday, Friday, Thursday, Wednesday. So it is Wednesday.
For earlier dates, move backwards by the remainder of the gap divided by 7.
If the 5th day of a month is Friday, which day is the 23rd?
From the 5th to the 23rd is 18 days. 18 = 14 + 4, so move 4 days ahead of Friday: Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday. So it is Tuesday.
Two full weeks bring the same weekday back.
Akbar and Khalid were born in 1970 and 1975 respectively, and Ikram is older than Khalid. Who is the youngest of the three?
Khalid (1975) is younger than Akbar (1970), and Ikram is older than Khalid. So Khalid is younger than both and is the youngest.
In age puzzles, a later birth year means a younger person.
A bus carries 500 passengers, of which 350 are men and the rest are women. What percentage of the passengers are women?
Men are 70% and women 30%, so the two add up to 100%.
Out of 1200 students, 800 boys are present. What percentage of the students are present?
In which year CE did Abu Jahal die?
Abu Jahal was killed in the Battle of Badr, fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, which is March 624 CE.
Badr was the first major battle between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.
In which year was the national flag of Pakistan adopted?
The Constituent Assembly adopted the flag on 11 August 1947, a few days before independence.
The flag was designed on the basis of the Muslim League flag, with a white stripe for minorities.
An adverb is a word that mainly modifies a what?
An adverb mainly modifies a verb. It can also modify an adjective or another adverb.
Adjectives, in contrast, modify nouns and pronouns.
Which name of Allah means the Most Merciful?
Ar-Rahim means the Most Merciful (the Ever-Merciful).
Ar-Rahman is usually translated as the Most Gracious or the Beneficent.
Ahmed is 5 years old and Sara is three times his age. How old will Sara be when Ahmed is 11?
Sara is 3 x 5 = 15 now. Ahmed becomes 11 after 6 years, so Sara will be 15 + 6 = 21.
The age difference between two people always stays the same.
Akbar is 3 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Akbar is 8?
The sister is 3 x 3 = 9 now. Akbar becomes 8 after 5 years, so she will be 9 + 5 = 14.
Both people age by the same number of years.
Why did the United States enter World War II in December 1941?
Japan attacked its naval base at Pearl Harbor
Japan carried out a surprise air attack on Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, on 7 December 1941. The US declared war on Japan the next day.
Germany and Italy then declared war on the United States a few days later.
What is the spread of cultural traits from one society to another called?
Cultural diffusion is the transfer of ideas, customs and technology from one society to another. Cultural diversity only means many cultures exist together.
Cultural lag means material culture changes faster than beliefs and values.
Delight means great pleasure, so its opposite is sorrow or misery. The other options are synonyms.
Another opposite of delight is displeasure.
Fragile means easily broken, so the opposite is sturdy or strong. Delicate, brittle and weak are close in meaning to fragile.
The word fragile comes from the Latin fragilis, meaning easily broken.
Secret means kept hidden from others, so the opposite is public or open. The other options are synonyms.
Overt is another opposite of secret in formal English.
Terrifying means causing great fear, so the opposite is comforting or soothing. The others are synonyms.
Reassuring is another good opposite of terrifying.
Condensed means made shorter or more compact, so the opposite is expanded. The other options mean the same as condensed.
In science, condensation is the change of a gas into a liquid.
Idleness means doing no work, so the opposite is industry, meaning hard work. Laziness and sloth are synonyms.
The proverb says an idle mind is the devil's workshop.
The Arabian Sea is a part of which ocean?
The Arabian Sea is the north-western part of the Indian Ocean. It lies between India, Pakistan, Iran and the Arabian Peninsula.
Pakistan's coastline along the Arabian Sea is about 1000 kilometres long.
The separation of Bangladesh in 1971 benefited which neighbouring country the most?
India supported the separation and fought the 1971 war, which weakened its rival Pakistan. India therefore gained strategically.
The 1971 war ended with the surrender of about 90000 Pakistani personnel.
ADB is the Asian Development Bank, which lends money to Asian countries for development. Pakistan is one of its members.
The ADB headquarters is in Manila, Philippines.
What is the logarithm of a number to its own base?
By definition, log base a of a equals 1 because a raised to the power 1 is a. For example, log 10 to base 10 is 1.
The logarithm of 1 to any base is 0.
Under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, who is the head of government?
The Speaker of the National Assembly
Pakistan has a parliamentary system. The Prime Minister heads the government and the President is the head of state.
The Prime Minister is elected by the National Assembly.
On which date of Ramadan was the Battle of Badr fought?
The Battle of Badr took place on 17 Ramadan, 2 AH, which is March 624 CE.
How many population censuses had Pakistan held up to the 2023 census, including it?
Censuses were held in 1951, 1961, 1972, 1981, 1998, 2017 and 2023, which makes seven.
The 2023 census was the first fully digital census of Pakistan.
Salman said that Ali ___ ill. Which option correctly completes this reported speech sentence?
In reported speech, a past reporting verb (said) changes the present tense of the original statement to the past tense, so is becomes was.
Direct speech: Salman said, "Ali is ill"; reported speech: Salman said that Ali was ill.
Which event led the United States to enter World War 2 in December 1941?
The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor
On 7 December 1941 Japan attacked the US naval base at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii, and the US declared war on Japan the next day.
The war in Europe had already begun in September 1939 when Germany invaded Poland.
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: I hate being laughed ___.
The phrasal verb is laugh at, so the passive form is being laughed at.
Similar verb and preposition pairs are look at, listen to and depend on.
When was Chaudhry Rahmat Ali, who coined the name Pakistan, born?
Chaudhry Rahmat Ali was born on 16 November 1897 in Balachaur, in East Punjab.
He published the pamphlet Now or Never in 1933 in which the name Pakistan was proposed.
In linear programming, what is a point of the solution region where two of its boundary lines intersect called?
A vertex of the feasible region, where two boundary lines meet, is called a corner point.
The maximum or minimum of the objective function always occurs at a corner point of the feasible region.
Fill in the blank: Go there ___ bus.
We use by with a means of transport when no article is used, as in by bus, by train, by car.
With an article we say on the bus or in the car.
What is the capital of Gambia?
Banjul is the capital of Gambia, a small West African country.
Gambia is surrounded on land by Senegal.
What is the capital of Switzerland?
Bern is the federal city and seat of the Swiss government, although many people wrongly think Geneva or Zurich is the capital.
Geneva hosts many international organisations such as the UN European office.
Fill in the blank: That was ___ I was born.
The year is correct because the sentence refers to one specific year, so the definite article is needed.
The article an is used only before a vowel sound, so an year is always wrong.
On which date did Makkah fall to the Muslims in the Conquest of Makkah (Fath Makkah)?
Most Pakistani textbooks give 20 Ramadan 8 AH (January 630 AD) for the conquest. The Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah peacefully.
Sources differ slightly, some give 10 or 17 Ramadan 8 AH.
On which date did Pakistan come into being according to the Islamic calendar?
Pakistan was created on 14 August 1947, which was 27 Ramadan 1366 AH, a Friday. It was also the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) in many accounts.
The date 27 Rajab is Shab-e-Miraj, not Pakistan's birth.
Each number is double the previous one: 3x2=6, 6x2=12, 12x2=24, so 24x2=48.
This is a geometric series with common ratio 2.
The differences are -10, -8, -6, so the next difference is -4. Thus 56 - 4 = 52.
The differences themselves form an arithmetic series.
A helicopter covers 240 km using 50 gallons of fuel. How many gallons are needed for the next 400 km?
Fuel per km is 50/240 gallons. For 400 km: 400 x 50 / 240 = 83 1/3 gallons.
This is a direct proportion question.
Who is the Supreme Commander of all the armed forces of Pakistan?
The Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee
Under the Constitution of Pakistan, the President is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces. The Prime Minister runs the government.
The President appoints the service chiefs on the advice of the Prime Minister.
In which continent is the Sahara Desert located?
The Sahara lies across North Africa. It is the largest hot desert in the world.
It covers an area of about 9 million square kilometres.
Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning a person who does something for pleasure and not as a job?
The correct spelling is amateur. It comes from the French word for lover.
In which part of Pakistan is K2 located?
K2 is in the Karakoram range in Gilgit-Baltistan, on the border with China. It is 8611 metres high.
K2 is the second highest peak in the world.
What is the currency of North Korea?
North Korea uses the North Korean won. South Korea uses the South Korean won.
Change into passive voice: I take exercise daily.
Exercise is taken by me daily.
Exercise was taken by me daily.
Exercise is being taken by me daily.
Exercise has been taken by me daily.
The sentence is in the simple present, so the passive uses is or are plus the past participle. So it becomes Exercise is taken by me daily.
The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive.
The Darling is a famous what, located in Australia?
The Darling is a river in Australia that joins the Murray River. It is about 1,500 km long.
The Murray-Darling basin is Australia's main river system.
A is the father of B, but B is not a daughter. What is B to A?
B is a child of A and is not a daughter, so B is a son.
The relation of A to B is father.
Who wrote the book Daughter of Destiny?
Daughter of Destiny is the autobiography of Benazir Bhutto, published in 1989. It was later reissued as Daughter of the East.
Benazir Bhutto was the first woman Prime Minister of Pakistan.
Between which two countries was the Tashkent Declaration signed in 1966?
It ended the 1965 war between India and Pakistan. The Soviet Union mediated it.
Who was the first woman Chief Minister of a province of Pakistan?
Maryam Nawaz became Chief Minister of Punjab in February 2024, the first woman to hold the post in any province. She belongs to PML-N.
Benazir Bhutto was the first woman Prime Minister.
Which is the largest river of China?
The Yangtze is about 6,300 km long and is the longest river in China and Asia. The Yellow River is second.
It flows into the East China Sea near Shanghai.
Lyallpur is the old name of which Pakistani city?
Lyallpur was renamed Faisalabad in 1979 in honour of King Faisal of Saudi Arabia. It was named after Sir James Lyall.
The city of Savannah is located in which country?
Savannah is a historic port city in Georgia, United States. It lies on the Savannah River.
A savannah is also a type of grassland.
What is the term for a line that meets another line at an angle of 90 degrees?
Two lines that meet at a right angle (90 degrees) are called perpendicular lines. Parallel lines never meet.
Perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is minus 1.
In a geometric progression, the constant ratio between consecutive terms is denoted by which letter?
In a geometric progression each term is the previous term multiplied by a fixed number called the common ratio, written r. The nth term is a times r to the power n minus 1.
In an arithmetic progression the common difference is denoted by d.
What is the derivative of cos(2x) with respect to x?
By the chain rule, the derivative of cos(u) is -sin(u) times du/dx. With u = 2x, du/dx = 2, so the answer is -2 sin(2x).
The derivative of sin(2x) is 2 cos(2x).
A decimal number that ends after a finite number of digits (for example 0.25) is called what?
A decimal with a finite number of digits after the point is a terminating decimal. It can always be written as a fraction.
A recurring decimal such as 0.333... has digits that repeat forever.
Change into direct speech: He told me that he was playing a game.
He said to me, "I was playing a game."
He said to me, "He is playing a game."
He said to me, "I am playing a game."
He said to me, "I will play a game."
In direct speech the reported past continuous tense changes back to the present continuous, and 'he' becomes 'I'. So the sentence is: He said to me, "I am playing a game."
When changing indirect to direct speech, 'told' usually becomes 'said to'.
Change into direct speech: She said to me that she was watching TV.
She said to me, "I am watching TV."
She said to me, "She was watching TV."
She said to me, "I will watch TV."
She said to me, "I have watched TV."
The past continuous 'was watching' goes back to the present continuous 'am watching', and 'she' becomes 'I'.
Direct speech is always written inside quotation marks.
Rearrange the jumbled letters 'EBAUYT' to make a meaningful English word.
The six letters E, B, A, U, Y, T can be arranged to spell BEAUTY.
Beauty is a noun meaning the quality of being pleasing to the eye or mind.
A car moves at 60 km/h and a train moves twice as fast as the car. How much time will the train take to cover 30 km?
Speed of train = 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. Time = 30 / 120 = 1/4 hour = 15 minutes.
Time equals distance divided by speed.
Which gas is mostly named as the main greenhouse gas causing global warming in textbooks?
Carbon dioxide released by burning fossil fuels is the main greenhouse gas added by human activity. It traps heat in the atmosphere.
Water vapour is the most abundant greenhouse gas, but its amount is controlled by temperature, so sources can differ on which is primary.
There are 24 students in a class and the number of boys is double the number of girls. How many girls are there?
Let girls = x, then boys = 2x, so 3x = 24 and x = 8. There are 8 girls and 16 boys.
Ratio boys to girls here is 2:1, so girls are one third of the class.
The total number of students is 1500 and 340 of them are boys. What is the percentage of girls?
Boys are 340/1500 x 100 = 22.67%, and the two percentages add up to 100.
If the 7th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 21st day of that month be?
From the 7th to the 21st is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. After whole weeks the day stays the same, so it is Friday.
Dates that differ by a multiple of 7 always fall on the same weekday.
Perpendicular divided by hypotenuse gives which trigonometric ratio?
In a right-angled triangle, sin of an angle = perpendicular / hypotenuse. Cos = base / hypotenuse and tan = perpendicular / base.
A memory aid is SOH CAH TOA: Sin = Opposite/Hypotenuse, Cos = Adjacent/Hypotenuse, Tan = Opposite/Adjacent.
On the number line, a number further to the right is greater. -15 lies to the right of -20, so -15 is greater.
Among negative numbers, the one closer to zero is the greater number.
Arrange the letters AGRMYNE to form the name of a country.
The letters A, G, R, M, Y, N, E can be rearranged to spell GERMANY, a country in Europe.
The capital of Germany is Berlin.
Who started the FIFA World Cup, as the FIFA president who proposed the tournament?
Jules Rimet, a Frenchman and FIFA president from 1921 to 1954, drove the idea of the World Cup. The first tournament was held in Uruguay in 1930.
The original World Cup trophy was named the Jules Rimet Trophy.
According to grammar, what part of speech is the word 'hey'?
'Hey' is a word used to express sudden feeling or to get attention, so it is an interjection.
A car runs at half the speed of a train that travels at 60 km/h. How far will the car go in 30 minutes?
Car speed = 60 / 2 = 30 km/h. Distance in 30 minutes (half an hour) = 30 x 1/2 = 15 km.
Distance = speed x time, so time must be in hours when speed is in km/h.
Taking half of a fraction doubles its denominator.
The Hazara people of Afghanistan and Pakistan are commonly said to be descended from whom?
The most common view is that the Hazara descend from Mongol (and Turkic) troops of Genghis Khan who settled in central Afghanistan in the 13th century.
Sources differ on exact origins, and the Hazara speak Hazaragi, a dialect of Persian.
The second highest civil award of Pakistan
The highest military gallantry award of Pakistan
The highest civil award of Pakistan
Hilal-e-Imtiaz is the second highest civil award of Pakistan, given for excellence in fields such as arts, sports, science and public service.
The highest civil award of Pakistan is Nishan-e-Pakistan.
Which city is considered the hottest city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
Dera Ismail Khan in the southern plains of KPK regularly records the highest summer temperatures in the province, around 45 to 50 degrees Celsius.
The hottest city of Pakistan overall is usually given as Jacobabad in Sindh.
What is 24 minutes past 10 pm in 24-hour format?
10 pm = 22:00 in 24-hour time. Adding 24 minutes gives 22:24, written 2224.
To convert pm time to 24-hour format, add 12 to the hour (except 12 pm).
A Kashmiri poetess known as the Nightingale of Kashmir
A queen of the Mughal Empire
Habba Khatoon was a 16th century Kashmiri poetess and the wife of Sultan Yusuf Shah Chak. She is known for her songs of love and longing.
She is called the Nightingale of Kashmir.
What is the date of Independence Day of Pakistan?
Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947 as a result of the Indian Independence Act 1947.
India celebrates its Independence Day on 15 August.
What is the antonym (opposite) of the word justice?
Justice means fair treatment, so its opposite is injustice, which means unfair treatment.
The prefix in- is often added to a word to make its opposite.
On which date did the 1999 Kargil conflict between Pakistan and India end?
The fighting in the Kargil sector began in early May 1999 and ended on 26 July 1999 when the last operations were over.
26 July is observed in India as Kargil Vijay Diwas.
Mount Godwin-Austen is another name of which mountain?
K2 was named Mount Godwin-Austen after the British surveyor Henry Haversham Godwin-Austen who explored the area.
K2 is the second highest mountain in the world at about 8611 metres.
Which country is called the Land of the Midnight Sun?
In summer, parts of northern Norway have daylight all night, so it is called the Land of the Midnight Sun.
Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun.
Which country has the largest number of islands in the world?
Sweden has about 267,000 islands, the most of any country, though most are very small.
Indonesia has the most islands among large island nations, about 17,000.
Which is the largest city of Japan?
Tokyo is the capital and the most populous city of Japan.
Osaka and Yokohama are other large Japanese cities.
According to the Economic Survey of Pakistan 2025-26, what is Pakistan's literacy rate (population aged 10 and above)?
The Economic Survey 2025-26, released in June 2026, gave the literacy rate as 63 percent, up from about 61 percent the year before.
Older reports gave around 60 percent in 2023 and 53 percent in earlier years; Punjab has the highest provincial rate.
The Margalla Hills of Islamabad are an extension of which mountain range?
The Margalla Hills are the foothills at the western end of the Himalayas.
Margalla Hills National Park lies in the north of Islamabad.
What is a matrix called in which all the entries are zero?
A matrix whose every entry is zero is called a zero matrix or null matrix. It is the additive identity for matrices of the same order.
Adding a zero matrix to any matrix of the same order leaves it unchanged.
In statistics, what is the difference between the maximum value and the minimum value of a data set called?
Range is the largest value minus the smallest value in the data. For example, in 3, 7, 12 the range is 12 - 3 = 9.
Range is the simplest measure of how spread out data is.
What does the idiom 'call it a day' mean?
To call it a day means to stop what you are doing and finish for the time being. It is used when one has done enough work.
A similar idiom is 'call it a night'.
What is an interjection in English grammar?
A word that expresses sudden emotion, such as Wow or Alas
A word that names a person or place
A word that describes a noun
A word that joins two sentences
An interjection is a word or short phrase that shows sudden feeling like surprise, joy or pain. Examples are Oh, Hurrah and Alas.
An interjection is usually followed by an exclamation mark.
If the 12th day of a month is Monday, which day is the 25th of that month?
From the 12th to the 25th is 13 days. 13 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6, so Monday plus 6 days is Sunday.
Any two dates 7 days apart fall on the same weekday.
If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, which day is the 15th of that month?
From the 3rd to the 15th is 12 days. 12 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5, so Monday plus 5 days is Saturday.
The 10th and 17th of that month are also Mondays.
Who built the Mohabbat Khan Mosque in Peshawar?
Nawab Mohabbat Khan, Mughal governor of Peshawar
The mosque was built around 1630 by Nawab Mohabbat Khan, the Mughal governor of Peshawar under Emperor Shah Jahan.
It is one of the best known Mughal-era mosques of Peshawar.
On which date was the Quit India resolution passed by the Indian National Congress in 1942?
The Quit India resolution was passed at Bombay on 8 August 1942 and the movement began the next day. It demanded an end to British rule in India.
Gandhi gave the call Do or Die during this movement.
Which countries are the five permanent members of the United Nations Security Council?
USA, UK, France, Russia and China
USA, UK, France, Germany and Japan
USA, UK, Russia, India and China
USA, France, Germany, Russia and China
The five permanent members (P5) are the United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia and China. Each has the power of veto.
Pakistan has been elected a non-permanent member of the Security Council several times, most recently for 2025-2026.
Which country has won the most Olympic medals of all time?
The United States has the highest total of medals in the history of the Summer Olympic Games, well ahead of any other country.
Some tables count the former Soviet Union separately, but it still stays behind the United States.
What was the capital of the Ottoman Empire after 1453?
Sultan Mehmed II conquered Constantinople in 1453 and made it the Ottoman capital. It remained the capital until the empire ended in 1922.
Ankara became the capital of the Republic of Turkey in 1923.
Choudhry Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge student, coined the name Pakistan in 1933 in his pamphlet Now or Never.
Allama Iqbal had given the idea of a separate Muslim state in his 1930 Allahabad address.
What is negative two divided by negative two?
A negative number divided by a negative number gives a positive result. So (-2) divided by (-2) = 1.
Any non-zero number divided by itself is equal to 1.
What is the scattering (spread) of a set of numbers called in statistics?
Dispersion means how much the values are spread out. Range, variance and standard deviation are measures of dispersion.
Mean, median and mode are measures of central tendency.
A function in which different elements of the domain have different images in the range is called what?
In a one-one function, no two different inputs give the same output. Such a function is also called injective.
A function that is both one-one and onto is called bijective.
Hens and cows together have 48 heads and 140 legs. How many hens are there?
Let hens be h and cows c. h + c = 48 and 2h + 4c = 140, so h + 2c = 70. Subtracting gives c = 22, so h = 48 - 22 = 26.
Check: 26 hens have 52 legs and 22 cows have 88 legs, which total 140.
In which mountain range is Broad Peak located?
Broad Peak (8,051 m) lies in the Karakoram range on the Pakistan-China border, near K2.
Broad Peak is the 12th highest mountain in the world.
If 40 percent of a number is 56, what is the number?
40 percent of x = 56, so x = 56 times 100 divided by 40 = 140.
A period of ten years is also known as what?
A century is 100 years and a millennium is 1000 years.
How many Pakistanis have won the Nobel Prize in Physics?
Only Dr Abdus Salam won it, in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg.
Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014.
From which substance do plants obtain hydrogen for making food?
In photosynthesis, water splits and gives hydrogen, which is used with carbon dioxide to make glucose.
Plants take in water through their roots.
Between which two teams was the first Test cricket match played?
The first Test was played at Melbourne in 1877 between Australia and England.
Australia won that match by 45 runs.
What is the lowest point of Pakistan?
Sea level at the Arabian Sea coast
The lowest point is the coast of the Arabian Sea at 0 m.
The highest point of Pakistan is K2.
What is the probability of getting a tail when a fair coin is tossed once?
There are 2 equally likely outcomes and one is a tail, so probability is 1/2.
The probability of a sure event is 1.
Which Prophet (AS) was swallowed by a whale (big fish)?
The Quran tells that Hazrat Yunus (AS) was swallowed by a big fish and he prayed to Allah for forgiveness.
He is also called Dhun-Nun, the one of the fish.
Which authority provides water supply and sewerage services in big cities such as Lahore?
WASA is the Water and Sanitation Agency of the city development authorities.
WAPDA looks after water and power development at national level.
A book is bought for 40 rupees and sold for 40 rupees. What is the profit?
Profit = selling price minus cost price = 40 - 40 = 0.
When selling price equals cost price there is no profit and no loss.
In which year did Queen Victoria die?
She became Empress of India in 1876.
Which pass connects Quetta with Sibi?
The Bolan Pass lies in Balochistan between Quetta and Sibi.
Khojak Pass connects Quetta with Kandahar in Afghanistan.
Who was the first woman pilot of Pakistan?
Shukriya Khanum earned a commercial pilot licence in 1959 and was the first Pakistani woman pilot.
Ayesha Farooq became the first woman fighter pilot of the PAF in 2013.
The Hunza River is located in which region of Pakistan?
The Hunza River flows through the Hunza valley in Gilgit-Baltistan and joins the Gilgit River.
The Karakoram Highway runs along the Hunza valley up to the Khunjerab Pass.
Who presides over the sessions of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
The Speaker is the presiding officer who runs the business and sessions of the National Assembly.
In the absence of the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker presides.
Change into passive voice: Mary said that she was sorry.
It was said by Mary that she was sorry.
Mary was said that she was sorry.
That she was sorry has said Mary.
For reported speech, the passive form starts with It was said by, followed by the that clause unchanged.
The reporting verb said changes to was said in the passive.
What is the meaning of the name Muhammad (SAW)?
Muhammad comes from the Arabic root h-m-d and means the one who is praised again and again.
Ahmad, another name of the Holy Prophet (SAW), also comes from the same root.
On which date did Pakistan become a full member of the SCO?
Pakistan, along with India, became a full member at the Astana summit on 9 June 2017.
Pakistan had been an observer since 2005.
How many full member countries does the SCO have after Belarus joined in 2024?
The members are China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India, Pakistan, Iran and Belarus, which makes ten.
Iran joined in 2023 and Belarus in July 2024.
Who scored the first Test double century for Pakistan?
Wicketkeeper Imtiaz Ahmed scored 209 against New Zealand at Lahore in October 1955.
Hanif Mohammad later made 337 against West Indies in 1958.
According to the 1973 Constitution, how many seats in the National Assembly are reserved in total (women and non-Muslims)?
60 seats are reserved for women and 10 for non-Muslim minorities, so 60 plus 10 = 70.
Reserved seats are filled through proportional representation of the parties.
Which legislative assembly in Pakistan has the highest number of seats?
The Punjab Provincial Assembly has 371 seats, more than the National Assembly (336) and all other assemblies.
Which of the following is NOT one of the five senses of a human being?
The five traditional senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch. Balance is not counted in them.
Balance is sensed by the inner ear.
What comes next in the series: X1, YY3, ZZZ5, ?
The letters go X, Y, Z, A in order and each letter is repeated one more time (1, 2, 3, 4 times). The numbers go up by 2: 1, 3, 5, 7, so the next term is AAAA7.
After Z the alphabet starts again from A in such series.
What comes next in the series: Z1, X3, U6, Q10, L15, ?
Letters move back by 2, 3, 4, 5 and then 6 places: Z, X, U, Q, L, F. Numbers go up by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, so the next term is F21.
The numbers 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21 are called triangular numbers.
How many sides does a pentagon have?
The word pentagon comes from the Greek penta meaning five, so it has five sides.
The sum of the interior angles of a pentagon is 540 degrees.
Ali is 6 years old and his sister is twice his age. How old is the sister?
The age difference between them is 6 years and it never changes.
Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'embellish'?
Its opposite is a word such as 'disfigure'.
Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'specify'?
'Specify' means almost the same as 'state clearly'.
Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'weird'?
Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'contemporary'?
It can also mean living or existing at the same time.
Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'dearth'?
Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'absolute'?
An absolute monarch has complete power.
Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'spontaneous'?
Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'supervision'?
The person who supervises is called a supervisor.
On which river is the Tanda Dam (Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) built?
Tanda Dam is in Kohat District and is filled with water of the Kohat Toi stream. It supplies irrigation water to nearby villages.
Tanda Dam was declared a Ramsar wetland site in 1976.
Find the next term in the series: 3/6, 6/9, 10/15, 15/24, ?
Numerators 3, 6, 10, 15 increase by 3, 4, 5, so next is 15 + 6 = 21. Denominators 6, 9, 15, 24 increase by 3, 6, 9, so next is 24 + 12 = 36. The term is 21/36.
The numerators 3, 6, 10, 15, 21 are called triangular numbers.
Ali is 5 years old and Ayesha is twice his age. What will be Ayesha's age when Ali is 15 years old?
Ayesha's present age = 2 x 5 = 10 years. Ali becomes 15 after 10 years, so Ayesha will be 10 + 10 = 20 years.
Ayesha is 5 years older than Ali, so she is always 5 years older.
In which year did Turkey become a republic and gain its modern independent status under Mustafa Kemal Ataturk?
The Treaty of Lausanne was signed in July 1923, and the Republic of Turkey was proclaimed on 29 October 1923.
Mustafa Kemal Ataturk was the first President of Turkey and died in 1938.
What type of equation is 2y = 1 + x?
Both x and y have power 1 only, so the highest degree is one. Such an equation is linear and its graph is a straight line.
A quadratic equation has a highest power of 2.
Which is considered the oldest university in the world still in operation?
Al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco was founded in 859 AD by Fatima al-Fihri. UNESCO and the Guinness World Records recognise it as the oldest.
Some sources name Al-Azhar (970 AD) or Bologna (1088) depending on the definition used.
When did the Indus Valley Civilization flourish, according to commonly taught dates?
Pakistani textbooks give the period of the Indus Valley Civilization as about 2500 BC to 1500 BC. Its main cities were Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro.
Some modern sources give the mature phase as 2600 BC to 1900 BC, so dates differ between sources.
Between which two values does probability always lie?
Probability of an impossible event is 0 and of a certain event is 1. Every other event lies between these two values.
Probability is often also written as a percentage between 0 percent and 100 percent.
What is the range of the values 15, 7, 11, 10, 2, 3?
Range = largest value minus smallest value = 15 - 2 = 13.
Range is a measure of spread of data.
Could is a modal auxiliary (helping) verb. It is the past form of can and shows ability or possibility.
Other modal verbs are can, may, might, must, shall, should, will and would.
Choose the correct word: This jacket is very ___.
Very is followed by an adjective, and expensive is the correct adjective here. Much cheap and high do not fit the sentence.
Much is normally used with uncountable nouns, not directly before adjectives.
How many vowels are there in the letters: A E Z Y U A W O L U E?
The vowels are A, E, U, A, O, U, E. That makes 7 vowels.
The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.
How many vowels are there in: A G I F O M E J I U Y X E?
The vowels are A, I, O, E, I, U, E. That makes 7 vowels.
Y is counted as a consonant in such counting questions.
Under whose government was the Indus Waters Treaty signed in 1960?
The treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960 by President Ayub Khan of Pakistan and Prime Minister Nehru of India.
The World Bank was a signatory as the broker of the treaty.
Which bowler has taken the most wickets for Pakistan in international cricket (all formats combined)?
Wasim Akram took 414 Test and 502 ODI wickets, about 916 in international cricket, which is the most by any Pakistani bowler.
Wasim Akram is a left-arm fast bowler who captained Pakistan to the 1992 World Cup win as a key player.
Which movement launched in 1920 asked Indians to refuse to cooperate with British rule?
The Non-Cooperation Movement, led by Gandhi with Khilafat support, asked people to boycott British schools, courts and goods.
The Quit India Movement came later, in 1942.
Who wrote the famous travel book Rehla?
Ibn Battuta, the Moroccan traveller, dictated his travels in the Rihla (Rehla) around 1355.
Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq.
Ammar is older than Amjad, and Ali is younger than Ammar. Who is the oldest of the three?
Ammar is older than both Amjad and Ali, so Ammar is the oldest.
The order of Amjad and Ali cannot be known from this information.
Saba is twice as old as her sister, and her sister is 8 years younger than Saba. How old will Saba be when her sister is 15?
Let sister be x, so Saba is 2x and 2x - x = 8, giving x = 8 and Saba = 16. Sister reaches 15 after 7 years, so Saba is 16 + 7 = 23.
The age gap between two people always stays the same.
What is the result when zero is multiplied by any number?
Any number multiplied by zero gives zero.
This is called the zero property of multiplication.
Any non-zero number divided by itself is 1.
Division of a number by 1 gives the same number.
